body.text: Ācāryakamalaśīlaviracito Madhyamakālokaḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>Madhyamakāloka</s> (Illumination of the Middle Way), composed by Ācārya <s>Kamalaśīla</s>.

children.translated_text: Those who are ignorant here, with perverted views, and who, through the power of the great seizure of attachment to [real] entities (<s>bhāvas</s>),

children.text: vaśena grastā hi praṇaṣṭaprajñā nāgārjunādīṃśca mahāmahimnaḥ /
children.translated_text: are grasped and whose wisdom is destroyed — they revile even <s>Nāgārjuna</s> and other [masters] of great glory.
Therefore, for the pacification of the great spirit-seizure (<s>bhūtagraha</s>) of those whose very self-destruction [results],
a beneficial method is now undertaken here by me, relying on compassion.

body.text: bhāvābhiniveśa eva tāvat samastasaṅkleśajālamūlam, atastatparihṛtya niḥśreyasapadābhilāṣiṇāṃ sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatāvyutpādanārthamidamārabhyate /
body.translated_text: The obsessive clinging to [real] entities (<s>bhāvābhiniveśa</s>) is indeed the root of the entire web of afflictions (<s>saṅkleśa</s>). Therefore, for those who desire the state of the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>), having abandoned that [clinging], this [work] is undertaken in order to generate understanding of the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) (<s>sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatā</s>).

body.text: paramārthagambhīrodadhinayamanavagāhya atra kecidāhuḥ - yuktyāgamābhyāṃ sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatā sidhyatīti cet?
body.translated_text: Without having plunged into the deep ocean of the ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>), some here say: "If [you claim that] the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s> is established by reasoning (<s>yukti</s>) and scripture (<s>āgama</s>)?"

body.text: nāgamastāvacchaktaḥ, kenāpi tathābhyupagamābhāvād, vivakṣādhīnatvād vacanānāṃ tadvastusambandhābhāvācca na prāmāṇyam / syādapi sambandhastathāpyarvāgdarśibhiravadhārayituṃ na śakyate
body.translated_text: Scripture, to begin with, is not capable [of establishing this], because no one has acknowledged it as such, because statements depend on the speaker's intention (<s>vivakṣā</s>), and because there is no connection of those [statements] with the [alleged] reality — therefore [scripture] has no validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>). Even if there were a connection, it cannot be ascertained by those of limited vision.

body.text: prekṣakāstatpravacanamata - mabhyupagamyamānebhyo 'pi niḥsaṃśayaṃ sarvabhāvānāṃ niḥsvabhāvatāpratipādakaṃ kimapi vacanamupadarśayituṃ na śaknuvanti /
body.translated_text: Those who examine [the matter] — even when accepting his [the Buddha's] teaching — are unable to point to any statement whatsoever that indubitably demonstrates the essencelessness of all entities.

body.text:
sūtreṣu keṣucit - 'niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmāḥ, anutpannāḥ, ādiśāntāḥ prakṛtiparinirvṛtā ityādīni [vacanāni] āgacchanti, tānyapi neyārthānyeva veditavyāni, nānābhisandhidvāreṇa bhagavato deśanayā avatāraṇāt / trayāṇāṃ svabhāvānāṃ parikalpitaparatantrapariniṣpannānāṃ kramaśaḥ lakṣaṇata utpattitaḥ paramārthataḥ niḥsvabhāvatāṃ sandhāya sarvadharmā niḥsvabhāvā uktāḥ, tena niḥsvabhāvatvādanutpannā, tata ādiśāntāḥ, tena prakṛtiparinirvṛtāḥ /
tathaiva bhagavatā āryasandhinirmocanasūtrādau sūtrārthābhiprāyayogo deśitaḥ /
body.translated_text:
In certain <s>sūtras</s>, [statements such as] 'All <s>dharmas</s> are essenceless, unborn, primordially peaceful, and by nature in <s>Nirvāṇa</s>' and so forth occur. But these too should be understood as having a provisional meaning (<s>neyārtha</s>), since the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s teaching leads [beings] through various intentions (<s>abhisandhi</s>). Having in view the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s> with respect to the three natures — <s>parikalpita</s> (imagined), <s>paratantra</s> (dependent), and <s>pariniṣpanna</s> (perfected) — respectively in terms of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), arising (<s>utpatti</s>), and ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>), it was said that all <s>dharmas</s> are essenceless; therefore, being essenceless, they are unborn; therefore primordially peaceful; therefore by nature in <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.
In precisely this way, the <s>Bhagavān</s> taught the intended meaning of the <s>sūtras</s> in the noble <s>Saṃdhinirmocana Sūtra</s> and elsewhere.

body.text: dvaitābhāsivijñānamātreṇa sarvadharmāṇāmutpattyādayo vibhajyante, na tu svasaṃvedanamātreṇa / dvaitābhāso 'pi mithyā, tena sarvabhāvā api mṛṣā eva vyavasthāpyante / parikalpitasya lakṣaṇaniḥsvabhāvatvāt sarvadharmānutpādādayo deśitāḥ, na tu paramārthataḥ / ato nāgamadvārā [sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatā] sādhayituṃ śakyate /
body.translated_text: The arising and so forth of all <s>dharmas</s> are distinguished only by consciousness-only (<s>vijñānamātra</s>), which appears as duality — not by mere self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>). The appearance of duality is also false; therefore all entities are established as ultimately unreal. Because the imagined [nature] (<s>parikalpita</s>) lacks essence in terms of characteristics, the non-arising and so forth of all <s>dharmas</s> were taught, but not in the ultimate sense. Therefore, the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s> cannot be established through scripture.

body.text: nāpi yuktidvārā / na khalu sarve bhāvāḥ pratyakṣata evaṃ viviktāḥ [śūnyāḥ] anubhūyante / vastutvāttasya viṣayāṇām / abhāvāya tāvad nīrūpatayā na kathamapi svarūpopadarśanena vijñānajanakatvaṃ yujyate, janakatve sati vastutvaprasaṅgaḥ, arthakriyāsamarthyatvād vastulakṣaṇasya / yat pratyakṣaṃ tadapi yadi sasvabhāvam, tadā sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatāpratijñāyā hāniprasaṅgaḥ / yadi tanniḥsvabhāvam, kathaṃ tena sarvadharmāṇāṃ viviktatānubhūyate / atha kaiścid arthāntarā viviktateti pakṣo gṛhyate, tadā itareṇa tāvat pratyakṣeṇa śūnyatā grāhyā syāt /
body.translated_text: Nor [can it be established] through reasoning. Indeed, not all entities are directly experienced through perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) as thus distinguished [i.e., as empty] — because of the reality of its objects. For a non-existent thing (<s>abhāva</s>), being formless, showing its own form in any way whatsoever cannot logically produce cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>); and if it does produce [cognition], the absurd consequence of it being a real entity (<s>vastu</s>) follows, since the defining characteristic of a real entity is the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsamarthya</s>). If that which is perceptual also has intrinsic nature, then the thesis that all <s>dharmas</s> are essenceless would be abandoned. If it is essenceless, how can the distinctness of all <s>dharmas</s> be experienced through it? And if some maintain the position that [things are] distinct through some other [means], then emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) would have to be grasped by yet another perception.

body.text: sarvadharmaḥsvabhāvavādiṣu ye kecana [dharmāḥ] pratyakṣeṇa upalabhyante [te] sarve dharmā viviktāḥ pratīyeran / sarvadharmāṇāṃ svabhāvaviviktatā tāvannāsti kimapi vastu, tasyā api sarvadharmāntargatatvāt / na cedantarbhāvaḥ, svapratijñāhāniḥ /
body.translated_text: Among those who hold that all <s>dharmas</s> have intrinsic nature, whatever [<s>dharmas</s>] are apprehended by perception would all be experienced as distinct [i.e., empty]. But there is in fact no real thing whatsoever that is the distinctness of intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s>, since that [distinctness] too would be included among all <s>dharmas</s>. And if it is not included, the thesis itself is abandoned.

body.text: ayaṃ tāvad [viṣayaḥ] sarvajñādīnāṃ yogināṃ pratyakṣeṇa sugamya ityucyamāne 'pi na khalu vidvadbhyastṛptimāsādayati, yuktyabhāvāttatra / yadi tad yogijñānamapyasaditi ced? tadā kathaṃ tasya prāmāṇyam / yadi tat sat, tadā pratijñāhāniḥ /
body.translated_text: Even when it is said that this [matter] is easily grasped through the perception of omniscient beings (<s>sarvajña</s>) and other <s>yogins</s>, this does not produce satisfaction among the learned, due to the absence of reasoning in support. If that <s>yogic</s> cognition too is unreal, then how can it be valid (<s>pramāṇa</s>)? If it is real, then the thesis is abandoned.

body.text: nāpyanumānenāpi 'sarve bhāvāḥ śūnyāḥ' iti sādhayituṃ śakyate, kasyāpyādhārasya dharmiṇa evābhāvāt, hetudṛṣṭāntādīnāmapyanupapannatvāt / svabhāvāśrayarahitaiḥ sarvahetubhiḥ kathaṃ sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatā sādhayituṃ śakyate /
body.translated_text: Nor can it be established through inference (<s>anumāna</s>) that 'all entities are empty (<s>śūnya</s>),' because there is no basis (<s>ādhāra</s>) — indeed no subject (<s>dharmin</s>) at all — and because the logical reason (<s>hetu</s>), example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>), and so forth are also untenable. How can the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s> be established by any reason whatsoever that is devoid of a basis in intrinsic nature?

body.text: paraiḥ siddhatvāt parābhyupagatahetvādibhiḥ svapakṣaḥ prasidhyediti cet tadāpi na yujyate,sādhanadūṣaṇayorubhayaprasiddhatvenābhimatatvāt / ithaṃ yadā parābhyupagatahetvādayo yadi na vāstavikāḥ, mohena kalpitamātrasattākāḥ, tadā kathaṃ taiḥ svapakṣaḥ prasidhyet / yadi te bhāvarupeṇa sanmātrāḥ, tadā na kevalaṃ te paraprasiddhamātrāḥ, tavāpi tatprasiddhatvāt / bhāvānāṃ siddhayasiddhayo na puruṣavivakṣādhīnāḥ / parābhyupagatasādhanādayo yadi sanmātrā evābhyupeyante tadā bhāvā api sasvabhāvāḥ kathaṃ nābhyupeyante?
body.translated_text: If [you say] that your own position would be established by reasons and so forth accepted by the opponent, since [they are] established for them — even so, this is not tenable, because both proof (<s>sādhana</s>) and refutation (<s>dūṣaṇa</s>) are intended to be established for both [parties]. Furthermore, if the opponent's accepted reasons and so forth are not real but merely have the status of being fabricated through delusion, then how could your own position be established through them? If they exist as mere beings of real nature, then they are not merely accepted by the opponent alone — they would be accepted by you as well, since they would be established for you too. The establishment or non-establishment of entities does not depend on a person's intention to speak. If the means of proof accepted by the opponent and so forth are accepted as mere existents, then how can entities too, as possessing intrinsic nature, not be accepted?

body.text: sarvadharmaśūnyatā kutrāpi kenāpi hetunā na sambaddhā, atyantaparokṣatvāt / yadi [sambandhaḥ] siddhaḥ syāt tadā sarve tattvadarśinaḥ syuriti prasaṅgaḥ / pūrvata eva siddhatvād yuktyanusaraṇamapi nirarthakaṃ syāt /
body.translated_text: The emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> is not connected with any reason anywhere, due to its being utterly beyond [ordinary] perception (<s>atyantaparokṣa</s>). If the connection were established, then the absurd consequence would follow that everyone would be a seer of truth. Since it would already be established beforehand, even the pursuit of reasoning would be pointless.

body.text: api ca, na tāvat kāryasvabhāvaliṅgābhyāṃ śakyate sādhayituṃ sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatā / teṣāṃ khalu bhāvasādhanatvāt / tvanmate tu etau [kāryasvabhāvau] na sambhavataḥ tathā hi - sarveṣāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpannatvena kasyāpi kenāpi saha kāryakāraṇabhāvasyānabhyupetatvāt kāryahetustāvanna sambhavati /
body.translated_text: Moreover, the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s> cannot be established by the [logical reasons of] effect (<s>kārya</s>) and intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), since these [reasons] serve to establish [real] entities. In your view, however, these two [kārya and svabhāva] are impossible, for since all <s>dharmas</s> are unborn, the causal relation (<s>kāryakāraṇabhāva</s>) between anything whatsoever is not accepted — therefore the reason of effect cannot apply.

body.text: sarvadharmāṇāṃ niḥsvabhāvatvena kasyāpi ātmanaḥ svabhāvasyāsattvāt kutastāvat svabhāvahetuḥ /
body.translated_text: Since all <s>dharmas</s> are essenceless, no self-nature (<s>ātman</s>) or intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) of anything exists — so whence the reason of intrinsic nature?

body.text: anupalabdhirapi tāṃ sādhayituṃ na śaktā / svabhāvānupalabdhiryā khalu asadvyavahāraṃ sādhayati, sā taditaraviviktasya vastunaḥ pratyakṣataḥ pratītau satyāmapi asacchāstraśravaṇavimūḍhamanasā kenacit taditaravivekavyavahāre 'pravṛttānāṃ tadvyavahāraprasādhanāya prayujyata iti / tava tu sādhyamānasarvadharmābhāvavyavahārasya pratyakṣataḥ jñānārthaṃ kiñcidapi nāstyeva, svapakṣahāniprasaṅgādityuktapūrvam /
body.translated_text: Non-apprehension (<s>anupalabdhi</s>) too is unable to establish it. The non-apprehension of intrinsic nature, which establishes the convention of non-existence (<s>asadvyavahāra</s>), is employed — when the direct perception of a real thing distinct from that [alleged entity] is obtained — for those who have not yet engaged in the convention of distinguishing that [thing] from the other, due to their minds being confused by hearing incorrect treatises, in order to facilitate that convention. But for you, who seek to establish the convention of the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s>, there is absolutely nothing [available] for perceptual knowledge — as already stated, since abandoning your own thesis would follow.

body.text: viruddhopalabdhyādayo 'pi [tava mate abhāvasādhanārthaṃ] na sambhavantyeva / atyantaparokṣāt sarvadharmavivekāt sahānavasthānavirodhenāpi na kiñcidapi sidhyati / yadi sidhyet tadā tadviruddhādayo bhāvatvenaiva sidhyeyurityanabhyupetā na syuḥ / bhāvānāṃ virodho dvidhā vyavasthāpyate, tadyathā - sahānavasthānalakṣaṇaḥ parasparaparihāralakṣaṇaśca / ye tatrāvikalakāraṇāni tebhyo niyataṃ yasminna bhavati, tayoḥ prathamo virodho vyavasthāpyate, śītoṣṇasparśavat / yad yasmin parihriyate yanna vicchidyate tayorubhayorabhāvayordvitīyo virodho vyavasthāpyate, ekasmin dharmiṇi yugapat sadasattvavat / tathāvidhau dvāvapi virodhau sarvadharmāniḥsvabhāvavādiṣu naiva sambhavataḥ / gaganāravindādiṣu na santi avikalakāraṇānyapi tathā nāsti atadvyāvṛttyā paricchedo 'pi bhāvaparyantavāt / sattāvyavacchena yadyapi paricchedo vyavasthāpyate tathāpi kutracit kācit, sattā vyavacchinnā sidhyet, kintu bhavantastāvat kutrāpi kasyāpi vyavacchedaṃ kathamapi naivābhyupagacchanti /
body.translated_text: The apprehension of what is contradictory (<s>viruddhopalabdhi</s>) and so forth too are simply impossible [in your view for establishing non-existence]. From the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>, being utterly beyond [perception], nothing whatsoever is established even through the contradiction of mutual non-coexistence. If it were established, then those contradictory entities and so forth would be established as real entities — which you do not accept. The contradiction of [real] entities is established in two ways: (1) characterized by mutual non-coexistence, and (2) characterized by mutual exclusion. The first contradiction is established for those [entities] that are invariably absent where there are unimpeded causes — like cold and hot touch. The second contradiction is established for both absences [of two things] — where one is excluded from the other and neither is interrupted — like being existent and non-existent simultaneously in a single subject. Both such types of contradiction are simply impossible for those who hold the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>. In [entities] like sky-lotuses and the like, there are no unimpeded causes; likewise there is no delimitation through exclusion of what is other, since [your theory] terminates in [real] entities. Although delimitation might be established through the exclusion of existence, even so, some particular existence would be established as excluded somewhere — but you [Mādhyamikas] do not accept any delimitation of anything anywhere.

body.text: yadi sarve dharmā niḥsvabhāvatāpratyāsannāstadā yuṣmāsu kimapyavikalakāraṇasattvaṃ na sidhyet / yadi sidhyettadā tānyavikalakāraṇānyeva bhāvāḥ sidhyeyuḥ / yadi sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatāvyavacchedana kecana bhāvāḥ paricchidyante, tadā ta evāsmāsu vastusantaḥ sidhyeyuḥ tadviruddhopalabdhyasambhavāt /
body.translated_text: If all <s>dharmas</s> approximate essencelessness, then no unimpeded causal conditions would be established in your [system]. If they were established, then those very unimpeded causes would be established as [real] entities. If some entities are delimited through the exclusion of the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, then those very [entities] would be established in our [system] as real things — because the apprehension of what is contradictory [with them] would be impossible.

body.text: yadyasambhavastadā vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhyādayo 'pi na sambhaveyuḥ / viruddhopalabdhyasiddhestā api na sambhavanti, viruddhopalabdhiprabhāvitatvāttāsām /
body.translated_text: If [the apprehension of contradictories] is impossible, then the apprehension of what contradicts the pervader (<s>vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhi</s>) and so forth would also be impossible. Due to the non-establishment of the apprehension of contradictories, those too cannot apply, since they are brought about by the apprehension of contradictories.

body.text: vyāpakānupalabdhirapi vyāpyavyāpakabhāvasiddhau vyāpyaniṣedhāya yadi prayujyate tadā sarvadharmasvabhāvaśūnyatvaṃ tu tāvanna kasyāpi vyāpyaṃ sidhyatīti / yadi sidhyatīti cet tad vyāpyameva hi vastutayā siddhaṃ syāt /
body.translated_text: The non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>) too — if it is employed to negate the pervaded (<s>vyāpya</s>) when the relation of pervaded and pervader is established — then the complete emptiness of intrinsic nature of all <s>dharmas</s> is not established as the pervaded of anything. If it were established, then that very pervaded would be established as a real thing.

body.text: kāraṇānupalabdhirapi kāryakāraṇabhāvasiddhau kāryatvaniṣedhāya yadi prayujyate tadā sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatāyāṃ tu kāryakāraṇabhāva eva siddho na bhavati / yadi siddhastadā yat kāraṇaṃ yaccāpi vā kāryaṃ tadeva vastu syāt /
body.translated_text: The non-apprehension of the cause (<s>kāraṇānupalabdhi</s>) too — if it is employed to negate the effect-nature when the causal relation is established — then in the [doctrine of] essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, the causal relation itself is not established. If it were established, then whatever is the cause and whatever is the effect — that very thing would be a real entity.

body.text: sarvadharmeṣu kasyāpyekasya niṣedhād eteṣāṃ niḥsvabhāvatāsiddhayarthaṃ nāsti kimapyekaṃ kāraṇam /
body.translated_text: By negating any single one among all <s>dharmas</s>, there is no single cause whatsoever for establishing the essencelessness of these [remaining dharmas].

body.text: kenāpi īścarādyekanimittābhyupagamaniṣedhe 'pi neme niḥsvabhāvatve sidhyanti, sarveṣāṃ svanimittotpannatvāt / eteṣāṃ pratisvaṃ nimittānyapi niṣeddhuṃ na śakyante, teṣāṃ prasiddhatvāt /
body.translated_text: Even by negating the acceptance of a single cause such as God (<s>Īśvara</s>) and the like, these [dharmas] are not established as essenceless, because all [dharmas] arise from their own respective causes. Nor can their individual causes be negated, since those [causes] are well-established.

body.text: api ca, nairātmyaṃ yadi sarvadharmagocaratāyāṃ sādhyate, tadā na dṛṣṭāntaḥ prasiddhayati / pratibimbādayo ye 'pi dṛṣṭāntāsteṣvapi kecit bāhyavastusvabhāvāḥ, anye tāvajjñānasvabhāvā abhyupagamyante, ataste vastusvabhāvā eva svīkṛtāḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, if selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) is to be proved with respect to all <s>dharmas</s>, then no example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) is forthcoming. Even the examples such as reflections and the like — among them, some are accepted as having the nature of external objects, while others are accepted as having the nature of cognition — therefore, they are accepted as having the nature of real entities.

body.text: yadi prādeśikaṃ nairātmyaṃ sādhayitumiṣyeta, tatra yadi tairthikaparikalpitāḥ pradhānādayaḥ niṣidhyante, tadā siddhasādhanamātrameva /
body.translated_text: If it is desired to prove selflessness only partially, and if [in that case] the imagined [entities] such as <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) etc. posited by the non-Buddhist schools (<s>Tīrthikas</s>) are negated, then it is merely a case of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>).

body.text: yadi lokaprasiddhā rupādayastadā dṛṣṭānta eva tāvannopalabhyate, pratijñāyāścāpi pratyakṣavirodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: If [selflessness is proved of] commonly known [entities] such as form (<s>rūpa</s>) and the like, then to begin with no example can be found, and there is also a contradiction of the thesis with perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>).

body.text: yadyanumānasya pratibandhasādhanārthaṃ pratyakṣapramāṇamabhayupagamyate, tadā siddha eva tāvad bhāvaḥ / tadyathā - kalpanāpoḍhamabhrāntamiti pratyakṣalakṣaṇam / abhrāntajñānena nirūpito 'pi bhāvasvabhāvaḥ kathamanumānenāpahnotuṃ śakyate / yadi sa nirākriyate tadā pratyakṣasyaiva bādhaprasaṅgaḥ / yadi sa badhyate tadā nānumānasyāpi sausthityam / pratyakṣasambandhādanuprāptānumānenāpi sa eva kathaṃ bādhayituṃ śakyate / yadi pratyakṣasiddho 'rtho na bādhyate tadā vastuvādināmeva sausthityam, prāpyasya prāptatvāt /
body.translated_text: If, for the purpose of proving the invariable connection (<s>pratibandha</s>) of inference, perception as a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is accepted, then a [real] entity is already established. For the definition of perception is: 'free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>) and non-erroneous (<s>abhrānta</s>).' How can the intrinsic nature of an entity, established by non-erroneous cognition, be denied through inference? If it is negated, then the absurd consequence of invalidating perception itself follows. If perception is invalidated, then inference too has no standing. How can that very [entity] be invalidated by inference derived from the connection with perception? If the object established by perception is not invalidated, then the position of the <s>Realists</s> (<s>vastuvādins</s>) alone stands firm, since what was to be attained has been attained.

body.text: api ca, sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatvaṃ sādhayitu yadi kaścid bhāvasvabhāvo hetuḥ pradarśyate, tadā viparītasādhyasādhako heturviroddho bhavati /
body.translated_text: Moreover, if some reason with the nature of a [real] entity is adduced to prove the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, then the reason becomes contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), as it proves the opposite of what is to be proved.

body.text: yadi abhāvasvabhāvastadā asadabhavayoḥ parasparasambandhāabhāvāt kathaṃ sādhayiṣyati?
body.translated_text: If [the reason has] the nature of non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>), then since there is no mutual connection between non-existence and non-being, how will it prove [anything]?

body.text: yadyubhayasvabhāvaḥ, so 'pyaniyata eva, vipakṣe 'pi sattvāt / yato hi tat sādhayituṃ nānyat kimapi pramāṇamiti /
body.translated_text: If [the reason has] a dual nature (<s>ubhayasvabhāva</s>), even that is inconclusive (<s>aniyata</s>), since it is present also in the counter-instance (<s>vipakṣa</s>). For there is no other means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) to establish it.

body.text: śabdamātrato 'pi na tat sidhyati, sarvataḥ sarvasiddhiprasaṅgāt / śabdo 'pi viruddhaḥ, yato hi yadi niḥsvabhāvastadā kathaṃ sa siddhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Nor can it be established through mere words (<s>śabda</s>) alone, since the absurd consequence would follow that everything could be established from everything. Words too are contradictory, for if they are essenceless, how are they themselves established?

body.text: prasaṅgatvena siddhe 'pi neṣṭārthasiddhiḥ,tathāvidhaprasaṅgasyaivāsiddhatvāt / prasaṅgena tāvat parapakṣo bādhayituṃ śakyate, tathāpi svapakṣastu na sidhyati, ubhayasiddhahetvantarāpekṣatvāttasya /
body.translated_text: Even if [something] is established through a <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio ad absurdum), the desired conclusion is not thereby established, because such a <s>prasaṅga</s> itself is not established. Through a <s>prasaṅga</s>, the opponent's position can be refuted; however, one's own position is not thereby established, since it requires a further reason established for both [parties].

body.text: svato notpadyate bhāvaḥ, yaścānutpannastasyāsattvena kutrāpi hetutvenānupapatteḥ / utpannānāṃ punarutpāde nairarthakyam, vidyamānatvāt / yadyaviśiṣṭastadā kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'pi na yujyate, viśiṣṭasyaiva hetutvāt /
body.translated_text: An entity does not arise from itself; and that which is unborn, being non-existent, is inapplicable as a cause anywhere. And if already-arisen [things] were to arise again, that would be pointless, since they already exist. If [cause and effect] are undifferentiated, then even the causal relation is not tenable, since only what is differentiated can be a cause.

body.text: parato 'pi notpadyate bhāvaḥ, parasyaivāsiddhatvāt / api ca nityabhūtādapi tāvat parānnotpadyate, nityasya kramayaugapadyābhyāmarthakriyāvirodhāt / anityādapi tāvad vinaṣṭānna, tasyāvidyamāanatvāt / avinaṣṭādapi na, kāryakāraṇayostutvaprasaṅgāt / samakālikayostāvat kāryakāraṇabhāvo na yujyate, niṣpannavasthāyāṃ dvayorvidyamānasvabhāvatvena parasparopakārakatvābhāvāt / aniṣpannavasthāyāṃ tu dvayorasattvād upakārakatvātyantābhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text: An entity does not arise from an other either, because the 'other' itself is not established. Moreover, from an eternal other, things do not arise, because eternality contradicts causal efficacy whether sequentially or simultaneously. Nor from a non-eternal [other] that has perished, because that is non-existent. Nor from an unperished [other], because there would be the absurd consequence of simultaneity of cause and effect. When both exist simultaneously, the cause-effect relation is not possible, because in the accomplished state both have established natures and thus there is no mutual assistance. In the unaccomplished state, however, since both are non-existent, there is a complete absence of assistance.

body.text: ubhayato 'pi notpadyate,yathoktobhayadoṣaprasaṅgāt, ekasmin dvitvavirodhācca /
body.translated_text: Nor does [an entity] arise from both [self and other], because of the absurd consequence of the faults stated for both, and because of the contradiction of duality in a single [thing].

body.text: ahetuto 'pi notpadyate bhāvaḥ kādācitkatvāt, naivaṃ kathanaṃ yujyate / yanna svato nobhayato nāpi vinaṣṭāddhetornāpyahetuto nābhīṣṭānnityāddhetoḥ kāryotpattirbhavatīti tathāvādinastat [sarvaṃ] yujyate, kintvanityatvenābhīṣṭāttaditarādavinaṣṭāddhetoḥ kāryotpattau kastāvad virodhaḥ, kena hetunā tataḥ kāryotpattirniṣidhyate, nāsti tadbādhakaṃ kimapi pramāṇam /
body.translated_text: An entity does not arise without a cause either, because of occasional occurrence. Such a statement is not valid. Those who maintain that an effect does not arise from self, not from both, not from a perished cause, not without a cause, and not from a desired eternal cause — everything is consistent for them. But what contradiction is there in the arising of an effect from a cause that is non-eternal, desired, different from it, and unperished? For what reason is the arising of an effect from that denied? There is no <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) whatsoever that contradicts it.

body.text: parabhūtasya bhāvamātrasyāpyasiddhiriti na, yato hi yadanantaraṃ kāryamutpadyate tadeva 'para'ḥ ityabhidhīyate / kāryotpādāt prāk pareti nāmro 'siddhatve 'pi bhāvasya tu naiva hāniḥ /
body.translated_text: It should not be said that the 'other' as mere entity is also not established, because whatever immediately precedes the arising of an effect is called 'other.' Even though the name 'other' is not established before the arising of the effect, there is no loss to the entity itself.

body.text: kecit paratvāditi bādhakaṃ pramāṇaṃ vadanti, tadapyanaikāntikameva, parātvajanakatvayoravirodhāt / sa tāvavirodhanayo 'pi niṣeddhuṃ na śakyate, atiprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: Some say that 'because of otherness' is a contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s> (proof). But that too is merely inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because there is no contradiction between being other and being a generator. That very non-contradiction also cannot be denied, because of over-extension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>).

body.text: yadyevamasti tadā kasmiṃścidaparasmin drāridrayamūḍhatvādidharmāṇāṃ dṛśyatvena paratvahetoḥ sarvajagaddāridrayādidharmopādānaṃ syāt /
body.translated_text: If that is so, then since qualities such as poverty, stupidity, and others are observed in some other [entity], the reason of otherness would lead to the absurd consequence that the entire world must take on poverty and similar qualities.

body.text: avyavahitādavinaṣṭāt parāt kāryotpattau kāryakāraṇasamakālikatvaprasaṅgo bādhakapraṇamiti yadi kaścidevaṃ manyate, tadapyayuktameva / avyavahikāryotpādenāpi kāryakāraṇasamakālikatvaṃ na prasajyate, kṣaṇikatvena kāryasattve kāraṇasyāsattvāt /
body.translated_text: If someone thinks that the arising of an effect from an unperished, unmediated other leads to the absurd consequence of simultaneity of cause and effect, which is a contradicting proof — that too is not valid. Even with unmediated arising of an effect, simultaneity of cause and effect does not follow, because when the effect exists, the cause does not exist, due to <s>kṣaṇikatva</s> (momentariness).

body.text: yadā kāryamutpadyate tadaiva kāraṇaṃ nirudhyate, tulādaṇḍonnāmāvanāmavaditi kutaḥ samakālikatvaprasaṅgaḥ / kāraṇāvasthāyāmapi kāryasya vidyamānatvād nairarthakyameva / yathā avyavahitavinaṣṭo bhāva uttarakṣaṇabhāvinā bhāvena saha yugapad vyavasthāpyo na bhavati, evameva kāryasyāpi tatsadṛśatvādaviruddhataiva, chāyātapavat / yathā ca pūrvāparāvyavadhānena pravahamānajaladhārāyāṃ viṣayaikatvaṃ na bhavati, tathaiva asyāpi tatsadṛśatvāt samakālikatvaṃ na bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: When the effect arises, at that very moment the cause ceases, like the rising and falling of a balance-beam — so how can there be the absurd consequence of simultaneity? If the effect already exists in the state of the cause, there would only be purposelessness. Just as an entity that has perished in the immediately preceding [moment] cannot be established as simultaneous with the entity existing in the subsequent moment, in the same way the effect too, being similar to that, is not contradicted — like shadow and sunlight. And just as in a flowing stream of water without interruption between earlier and later there is no identity of objects, similarly for this too, being similar, there will be no simultaneity.

body.text: vidyamānasyāpi kāryasya naivotpādaḥ, utpādavaiyarthāt, nāpyavidyamānasya, śaśaśṛṅgadīnāmapyutpattiprasaṅgād ityapi kathanaṃ naiva yujyate / yadi vidyamānakāryasyotpattinirṣidhyate tadā tava [pakṣe] ubhayasiddho heturdṛṣṭāntaśca na syātām / yadyasti tadā niḥsvabhāvatvapratijñāyā hāniḥ /
body.translated_text: 'There is no arising of an existing effect, because arising would be purposeless; nor of a non-existing one, because there would be the absurd consequence of the arising even of hare's horns' — this statement too is not valid. If the arising of an existing effect is denied, then in your own position there would be neither a commonly established reason nor an example. If [the effect] exists, then there is a loss to the thesis of <s>niḥsvabhāvatva</s> (essencelessness).

body.text: sāṃkhyādiparikalpitasatkāryavādo yadyapyayuktastathāpyasatkāryotpāde kiṃ nāma viruddhatvam, kimarthaṃ ca tanniṣidhyate / naiva ca syāt śaśaśṛṅgādyutpattiprasaṅgaḥ tattathāvidhahetūnāmabhāvādanutpatteḥ na tvabhāvāddhetoḥ /
body.translated_text: Although the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and others' theory of <s>satkāryavāda</s> (existent-effect doctrine) is unjustified, still what contradiction is there in the arising of a non-existent effect, and why is that denied? There would not be the absurd consequence of the arising of hare's horns and such, because those things do not arise due to the absence of their specific causes — not because of the absence of a cause [in general].

body.text: sarvataḥ sarvotpattiprasaṅgo 'pi naiva; kāraṇapratiniyatasāmarthasya vyavasthitatvāt / pratiniyatakāraṇasāmarthyamapyaśyamabhyupeyam, anyathā sāṃvṛtike 'pi kāryakāraṇabhāve kathaṃ na sarvataḥ sarvotpattirbhavatīti /
body.translated_text: The absurd consequence of everything arising from everything also does not follow, because the specific capacity restricted to its [particular] cause is well established. This specific capacity of the cause must necessarily be admitted; otherwise, how would everything not arise from everything even in the conventional (<s>sāṃvṛtika</s>) cause-effect relationship?

body.text: api ca, yadi vinaṣṭāvinaṣṭādayo vikalpāḥ pāramārthikīmutpattiṃ bādhante, tadā kathaṃ na sāṃvṛtikīmapi bādhante? vastubalapravṛttasya hetorviṣasya puruṣecchāvaśena vibhāgo na yuktarūpaḥ / yadi patyakṣabādhitatvāśaṅkayā tasmin hetutvaṃ na pravartata ityucyeta tarhi sa hetureva nāsti, bādhayogyatvāt /
body.translated_text: Moreover, if the alternatives such as perished, unperished, etc. contradict ultimate arising, then how do they not also contradict conventional arising? It is not proper to divide the domain of a reason that operates by the force of reality according to a person's wish. If it is said that the reason does not apply there because of the suspicion that it is contradicted by perception, then that very reason does not exist at all, because it is capable of being contradicted.

body.text: na hyekena hetunā anekakāryotpattiryujyate, na cānekenāpyekotpattiryujyate, anyathā hetubhedena bhedo na syāt / ata eva nānekebhyo 'pyanekakāryotpattirbhavatīti / yadyekaṃ kāryaṃ sarve hetovo 'bhinirvartayanti, tadā bhinnānāṃ hetūnāmabhedaḥ syāt, anekebhya ekaikasyotpatteḥ / yadhekaikaṃ nābhinirvartayanti tadā kathaṃ nāmānekebhyo 'nekotpattirapi /
body.translated_text: For the arising of many effects from one cause is not possible, nor is the arising of one [effect] from many [causes], for otherwise there would be no difference due to difference in causes. For this very reason, the arising of many effects from many causes also does not occur. If all causes together produce one effect, then the distinct causes would be non-distinct, since one [effect] arises from many. If each one does not produce [the effect], then how can there be the arising of many from many?

body.text: na hyekenāpi ekasyotpattiḥ, cakṣurādīndriyebhyastadvijñānasyotpatteḥ / tadanantaraṃ yadi sajātīyakṣaṇotpattirna bhavettadā sarveṣāmandhabadhiratvādiprasaṅga ityapi kathanaṃ tāvannaiva yujyate / evaṃ yastāvadandhabadhiratvādiprasaṅgo 'bhihita sa naiva sambhavati, anabhyupagatatvāt, sāmagryā utpatteḥ, na hi kācidekena ekasyotpattiriti /
body.translated_text: For there is no arising even of one [effect] from one [cause] — since consciousness arises from the eye and other sense organs. 'If after that, the arising of a homogeneous moment does not occur, then there would be the absurd consequence of everyone being blind and deaf' — this statement too is not valid. The stated absurd consequence of blindness, deafness, etc. does not obtain, because it is not accepted [that a single cause produces a single effect], since arising is from the aggregate of conditions (<s>sāmagrī</s>). For there is no arising of one from one alone.

body.text: yenaikasmādanekotpattiḥ, anekasmād vā ekasyotpattiḥ [tataḥ sa] viruddho hetusvabhāvātikrānto janakatvenānabhyupagato bhavati, tathāpi vidyamānamātrādanekasvabhāvāt pradīpādeḥ anekasvabhāvaṃ kāryamutpadyamānaṃ dṛśyate /
body.translated_text: Even when the arising of many from one, or of one from many, being contrary to the nature of cause, is not accepted as generative — nevertheless, from a mere existent [cause] of multiple natures such as a lamp, a multi-natured effect is seen to arise.

body.text: hetubhedo bhedako na bhaviṣyatīti na syāt, hetuviśeṣeṇa kāryaviśeṣasyotpatteḥ / hetuviśeṣeṇa kāryaviśeṣotpāda iti yadeva kathanaṃ tadeva hetubhedasya bhedakatvapratipādakamiti /
body.translated_text: 'Difference of causes will not be a differentiator' — this should not be said, because a specific effect arises from a specific cause. The very statement 'a specific effect arises from a specific cause' demonstrates that difference of cause is indeed a differentiator.

body.text: yaḥ pratītyasamutpannaḥ sa prakṛtyā śānta ityetadanaikāntikatvam, pratītyasamutpannasya sasvabhāvatvena virodhābhāvāt, pratītyasamupādasya sasvabhāvatve prasiddhatvād / hetorviruddhatvamapi, ajātānāṃ khapuṣpādīnāṃ sasvabhāvatvenānanubhūyamānatvāt /
body.translated_text: That 'what is dependently arisen (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>) is peaceful by nature' — this is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), because there is no contradiction with the dependently arisen having its own nature, since the dependently arisen is well-known as having its own nature. The reason is also contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), because unborn things like sky-flowers are not experienced as having their own nature.

body.text: yo hi paramārthato 'san sa saṃvṛtāvapi svabhāvato 'nutpanno dṛśyate, yathā - vandhyāputraḥ / tulye 'pi niḥsvabhāvatve yathā rupādayo 'vabhāsante, tathā śaśaśṛṅgādayaḥ kathaṃ nāvabhāsante? avabhāsaviśeṣasyāsya nāsti kimapi kāraṇam /
body.translated_text: What is ultimately non-existent is seen as conventionally unarisen from its own nature too, like a barren woman's son. If [both are] equal in essencelessness, then just as forms and other [entities] appear, how do hare's horns and such not appear? There is no cause whatsoever for this difference in appearance.

body.text: 'sarve dharmā niḥsvabhāvāḥ, ekānekasvabhāvarahitatvāt' ityevamabhidadhānā ye prasaṅgaṃ sādhayanti teṣāmapi tathā parairanaṅgīkārād heturasiddha eva, ekānekasvabhāvarahitatvasya na kenāpyabhyupagatatvāt / ataḥ svataḥ siddhāvapi heturayaṃ parato 'siddhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Those who establish through <s>prasaṅga</s> (reductio) that 'all <s>dharmas</s> are essenceless, because they are devoid of one-or-many natures' — for them too, since others do not accept [the reason], the reason is indeed unestablished, because the property of being devoid of one-or-many natures is not accepted by anyone. Therefore, even if this reason is established for oneself, it is unestablished for the other.

body.text: anyacca, sādhyasādhane paryudāsātmake prasajyātmake vā? yadi paryudāsātmake tadā ekānekasvabhāvarahitātvasya bhāvasvabhāvatvenābhyupetatvāttadapyanabhyupagataṃ na bhavet / yadi prasajyātmake tadā nāsti gamyagamakabhāvaḥ, tayorniḥsvabhāvatvād anyo 'nyāsambaddhatvād abhinnatvācca /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, is the proof-to-be-proved (<s>sādhya-sādhana</s>) in the form of exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>) or in the form of simple negation (<s>prasajya-pratiṣedha</s>)? If in the form of exclusion, then since being devoid of one-or-many natures would be accepted as the nature of entities, that too would not be unaccepted. If in the form of simple negation, then there is no relation of the understood and the instrument of understanding, because both being essenceless, they are mutually unrelated and non-different.

body.text: yacca sarvābhilāpavirahalakṣaṇaṃ tanna kiñcid gamyaṃ gamakaṃ vā, yathā - aśvaśṛṅgam / yathoktasādhyasādhane api sarvābhilāpavirahalakṣaṇe /
body.translated_text: And that which has the characteristic of being free from all verbal expression — that is neither something to be understood nor an instrument of understanding, like a horse's horn. The said proof and what is to be proved also have the characteristic of being free from all verbal expression.

body.text: yau hyanyo 'nyāsambaddhau tayornāsti gamyagamakabhāvaḥ, yathā vindhyahimālayau / sādhyasādhane cāpyanyo 'nyāsambaddhe /
body.translated_text: For two things that are mutually unrelated have no relationship of the understood and the instrument of understanding, like the <s>Vindhya</s> and <s>Himālaya</s> mountains. The proof and the proved are also mutually unrelated.

body.text: yadyubhe abhāvasvabhāvatvena tādātmyalakṣaṇāpanne eveti manyase cet, tadapyuktam, tadātmano bhāve vyavasthitatvāt /
body.translated_text: If one thinks that both are characterized by identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) because both have the nature of non-existence — that too has been stated [to be refuted], because identity is established only in existing things.

body.text: yo yasmānna bhinnasvabhāvastayornāsti gamyagamakabhāvaḥ, vṛkṣadrumavat / yathoktasādhyasādhane api na bhinnasvabhāve / nāyaṃ kṛtakatvānityatvābhyāmanaikāntiko 'pi, vyāvṛttyā bhinnatvāttayoḥ /
body.translated_text: That which is not of a different nature from something else — between those two there is no relation of the understood and the instrument of understanding, like 'vṛkṣa' (tree) and 'druma' (tree). The said proof and proved are also not of different natures. This is not inconclusive like 'produced' and 'impermanent,' because those two are different through exclusion (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>).

body.text: atrāpi vyāvṛttyā bheda iti manyate cet? tadapyayuktam / yadyevaṃ svād bhāva eva te syātām, nīlapītavat /
body.translated_text: If one thinks 'here too there is difference through exclusion' — that too is not valid. If so, they would be positive entities for you, like blue and yellow.

body.text: api ca yathā kenāpi ekānekasvabhāvaviyuktatvahetunā bhāvānāṃ niḥsvabhāvatā sādhyate, tathā dharmiṇo 'pyabhāvaḥ sādhyate tadā dharmivyāvṛttatvasiddheḥ / heturviruddhaḥ syāt, tathā niḥsvabhāvatvasiddhau nāsti kimapi pramāṇam /
body.translated_text: Moreover, just as the essencelessness of entities is proved by the reason of being devoid of one-or-many natures, the non-existence of the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) is also proved, since the absence of the subject is established. The reason would be self-contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>); thus there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) whatsoever for establishing essencelessness.

body.text: api ca, yadi vijñānamapyanyadharmavat paramārthato niḥsvabhāvaṃ syāttadā tadanupādeyaṃ syād vitathatvādanyadharmavat / yadyevaṃ syāttadā na syuryogino 'pi, naiva yogijñānamapi syānna ca taistattvapratibodhaḥ syāt / naiva teṣāṃ bhagavatāṃ buddhānāmapratiṣṭhitanirvāṇaṃ syānna ca sarvākāraṃ jñānaṃ syāt / phalataḥ sarvavyavasthāvilopaḥ syāditi /
body.translated_text: Moreover, if consciousness too, like other <s>dharmas</s>, were ultimately essenceless, then it too should not be accepted, because it would be false like other <s>dharmas</s>. If so, there would be no <s>yogins</s> either, nor would there be yogic knowledge, nor would they realize reality. There would be neither the non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhita-nirvāṇa</s>) of the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> nor omniscient knowledge. In effect, there would be the destruction of all conventions.

body.text: saṃvṛtau yogijñānādīnāmabhyupagamād buddhā api viparyastā bhaveyuriti prasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: Because yogic knowledge and such are accepted in the conventional [level], there would be the absurd consequence that even the <s>Buddhas</s> would be deluded.

body.text: api cāsti bhavatāṃ sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatvapratijñāyāṃ yuktyāgamābhyāṃ virodho 'pi / yathā rupādayastāvat sasvabhāvatve eva niyatā, deśakālāvasthābhedena sphuṭamavabhāsamānatvāt / ata ādau tāvat pratyakṣavirodhaḥ suspaṣṭaḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, in your thesis that all <s>dharmas</s> are essenceless, there is a contradiction with both reasoning and scripture. For instance, forms and such are determined as having their own nature, because they appear clearly according to differences of place, time, and condition. Therefore, first of all, the contradiction with perception is quite clear.

body.text: agnyādayo ye bhāvāḥ parokṣarvenābhyupagatāste 'pi abhrāntena niyatadhūmādihetunā anumānapramāṇena satsvabhāvātmakā eva / bhāvānāmutpādo 'pi khalu hetupratyayasāpekṣa eva siddhaḥ, kādācitkatvāt / ahetukasya tu kādācitkatvamapi na yujyate, nirapekṣatvāt / ataḥ pratijñāyāmanumānabādhāpi /
body.translated_text: Those entities such as fire etc. that are accepted as beyond direct perception — they too, through the inference based on undeluded, invariable signs such as smoke, are of the nature of having real existence. The arising of entities is also established as dependent on causes and conditions, because of occasional occurrence. But for what is without a cause, even occasional occurrence is not possible, because of its being independent. Therefore, there is also a contradiction with inference in the thesis.

body.text: yāni trāyastriṃśānāṃ nagarādīnyatyantaparokṣāṇi, tānyapi samastalokaikacakṣurbhūtena tāyinā svakīyenānāvṛtena jñānacakṣuṣā pratyakṣīkṛtya anyebhyo 'pi samprakāśitāni, ato viścastāgamena sattāyāḥ siddherāgamavirodho 'pi, asatāmākāśapuṣpādīnāṃ tathā darśanasamprakāśanayorayuktvāt /
body.translated_text: Those things that are completely beyond perception, such as the cities of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> [gods] — they too were directly perceived through the unobscured eye of knowledge by the <s>Tāyin</s> (<s>Buddha</s>), the unique eye of the entire world, and were revealed to others. Therefore, since their existence is established by a trustworthy scripture (<s>āgama</s>), there is also a contradiction with scripture, since it is not possible to directly perceive and reveal things that are absolutely non-existent like sky-flowers.

body.text: bhagavatā khalu ye āntarabahyavastūnāmanekavidhāḥ pratītyasamutpādāḥ samupadiṣṭāste 'pi svabhāvavirahitāḥ kathaṃ yujyante, atyantābhāvānāmākāśapuṣpādīnāṃ naivātyantikī utpattiriti /
body.translated_text: The many types of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) of inner and outer entities taught by the Blessed One — how can they be justified as devoid of nature, since for things that are absolutely non-existent like sky-flowers there is never any ultimate arising?

body.text: kuśalākuśalamarmaṇāṃ phalabhūtā devanarakādigatayo bhavantīti svayambhuva upadeśāt kathaṃ na virodhaḥ, naiva yujyate atyantāsadbhūtakūrmaromādibhirvastranirmāṇopadeśaḥ /
body.translated_text: From the teaching of the Self-born (<s>Svayambhū</s>, i.e., <s>Buddha</s>) that the destinies of gods, hells, etc. are the fruits of wholesome and unwholesome <s>karmic</s> patterns — how is there no contradiction? It is not valid to teach the weaving of cloth from utterly non-existent turtle-hairs and the like.

body.text: ataḥ karmaṇāmiṣṭāniṣṭaphalāpavādāt saṃkleśapakṣāpavādaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, from the denial of the desirable and undesirable fruits of actions, there would be the denial of the defilement side (<s>saṃkleśa-pakṣa</s>) [of practice].

body.text: sūtrādiṣu āryāṇāṃ mārgābhyāsabalena yā uttarottaralokottarajñānaphalavyavasthā sāpi na syāt, gatigamyagamakādyabhāvāt / śaśaśṛṅgakṛtasopānamārge pādau nidhāya
body.translated_text: Also, the hierarchy of progressively higher supramundane knowledges as fruits, attained through the power of practice of the Noble Path as stated in the <s>sūtras</s> and other [texts], would also not exist, because of the absence of path, destination, what is to be traversed, and what makes one traverse. Having placed one's feet on a stairway made of hare's horns,

body.text: vandhyāputrasya aścaṅgasamucchritottuṅgaviśālaprāsādārohaṇaṃ na sambhavatītyato vyavadānapakṣāpavādo 'pi syāt /
body.translated_text: the climbing of a barren woman's son up to a tall, lofty, spacious palace elevated to its full height is not possible — therefore there would also be the denial of the purification side (<s>vyavadāna-pakṣa</s>) [of practice].

body.text: ityevamubhayapakṣāpavādamanutiṣṭhantaścatvāryāryasatyānyapi niṣedhanti bhavantaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, maintaining the denial of both sides, you also deny the <s>Catvāry Āryasatyāni</s> (Four Noble Truths).

body.text: bījādiṣu janyajanakabhāvastāvad āgopāṅganāprasiddhaḥ, ataḥ pratijñāyāḥ prasiddhivirādho 'pi /
body.translated_text: The cause-and-effect relationship in seeds and such is well-known even to cowherd women. Therefore, there is also a contradiction with common knowledge (<s>prasiddhi</s>) in the thesis.

body.text: hetuprayogeṇa pareṣu niścayotpādābhyupagamāt svavacanavirodho 'pi /
body.translated_text: Since you accept that applying a reason produces certainty in others, there is also a contradiction with your own words (<s>svavacana-virodha</s>).

body.text: yaśca bhagavatā pratyakṣādipramāṇairbhāvānāṃ sattānirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ, tasyāpi bādhā syāt / yato hiḥ
body.translated_text: The Blessed One's teaching of the existence of entities based on perception and other <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) would also be contradicted. For indeed,

body.text: "cakṣurvijñānasamaṅgī nīlaṃ vijānāti, no tu nīlam" ityādinā tāvannīlādayo bhāvāḥ kalpānāpoḍhalakṣaṇena pratyakṣapramāṇena jñāyanta iti pratipāditam, naiva hi gaganotpalavartīni nīlādīni cakṣurvijñānenānubhūyanta iti /
body.translated_text: through the statement 'One who possesses visual consciousness cognizes blue, but not [merely] blue' and so forth, it has been demonstrated that blue and other entities are cognized by perception (<s>pratyakṣa-pramāṇa</s>) whose defining characteristic is the exclusion of conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>). For blue and other things present in sky-lotuses are not experienced by visual consciousness.

body.text: "yatkiñcit samudayadharmakam, tat sarvatra nirodhadharmakam" anena sādhyavyāptahetunānumānapramāṇenopadarśitāḥ kṣaṇasthitadharmiṇo bhāvāḥ prasiddhā iti spaṣṭamupadarśitam / anena tāvadupadarśanena te [bhāvā] sasvabhāvatāyāṃ nirucyante, atyantāsadbhūtākāśapuṣpādīnāmutpādāvyayadharmāyogāt /
body.translated_text: 'Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of cessation' — through this inference (<s>anumāna-pramāṇa</s>) whose reason pervades what is to be proved, it has been clearly demonstrated that entities characterized by momentary existence are well-established. By this demonstration, those [entities] are determined to have their own nature, because for things that are absolutely non-existent like sky-flowers, the properties of arising and ceasing do not apply.

body.text: "dhūmena jñāyate vahniḥ salilaṃ ca balākayā" iti / agnyādayo bhāvāḥ kāryaliṅgena niyataṃ jñāyamānatvānniyataṃ svabhāvamavadhārayantīti suspaṣṭaṃ nirdiśyate / balākādihetūnāṃ darśanānmarīcikādyabhāvānumānasyotpatterabhāvāt /
body.translated_text: "Fire is known by smoke, and water by the crane" — it is clearly indicated that entities such as fire, being invariably known through the inferential mark of their effects, ascertain a fixed nature. For from the observation of reasons such as cranes and the like, no inference of the non-existence [of things] such as mirages arises — because [such inference] does not occur.

body.text: abhidharmādau ye ṣaḍ hetavaścatvāraśca pratyayā abhihitāste 'pi sarvadharmānutpādavāde tāvatkathaṃ yujyante, utpādyasya kasyacidabhāvena hetvādīnāmayuktatvāt /
body.translated_text: The six causes and four conditions taught in the <s>Abhidharma</s> and other [texts] — how can they be consistent with the doctrine of the non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s>? For since there is no thing to be produced, causes and the like would be unjustified.

body.text: sūtreṣu sarve dharmāḥ skandhadhātvāyataneṣu saṅgṛhītāḥ samupadiṣṭāḥ / skandhādīnāṃ bhagavatā kāryakāraṇasvabhāvatvasamprakāśanāt kathaṃ te sarvedharmānutpādatāyāṃ saṅgṛhītāḥ syuḥ /
body.translated_text: In the <s>Sūtras</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are classified and taught under <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases). Since the Blessed One illuminated the <s>skandhas</s> and the like as having the nature of cause and effect, how could they be included in the non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s>?

body.text: yadi skandhadivyatiriktasya kasyacid dharmasya anutpādaḥ sādhyate tadā nāsti [kaścit] vivādaḥ, vayamapi tadvyatiriktaṃ dharmaṃ nāṅgīkurmahe /
body.translated_text: If the non-arising of some <s>dharma</s> other than the <s>skandhas</s> and the like is being established, then there is no dispute, for we too do not accept a <s>dharma</s> other than those.

body.text: yadyevaṃ manyate yatsaṃvṛtau pramāṇādīnāmabhyupagamānnaiva eṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ dūṣaṇānāmavakāśo yujyata iti cet? tadā [saṃvṛtau] bhāvābhyugama evāṅgīkṛtaḥ syāt, yato hi yāni pramāṇādīni saṃvṛtāvabhyupetāni tāni niścayena sarvābhilāpavidhuralakṣaṇaśaśaśṛṅgādibhyo vyāvṛttasvabhāvānyeva vyāhatāni syuḥ / yadyevaṃ na syāttatadā lokavirodha āgamavirodhaśca kathaṃ parihataḥ syāt / vayaṃ tu yat sarvasāmarthyavirahalakṣaṇaśaśaśṛṅgādiviparītaṃ tadeva 'vastu' ityabhidadhmahe / yadi bhavantastānapi saṃvṛtisaditi nāmamātramupacāramātraṃ vyavahāramātramiti pravyāharanti, tadā kāmaṃ tathābhilapantviti / na hi nāmamātreṇa bhāvastathāvidhaṃ svabhāvamanusaratītyatiprasaṅgāt /
body.translated_text: If one thinks thus: "Since <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) and the like are accepted in the conventional [level], none of these objections should have any scope" — then the acceptance of entities in the conventional [level] itself would be conceded. For whatever <s>pramāṇas</s> and the like are accepted in the conventional, they must necessarily be of a nature distinct from hare's horns and the like, which are characterized by being devoid of all expression — otherwise they would be contradicted. If it were not so, how would the contradiction with the world and the contradiction with scripture be resolved? We, however, designate as 'real thing' (<s>vastu</s>) precisely that which is the opposite of hare's horns and the like, which are characterized by the absence of all capacity. If you declare them too as 'conventionally existent' — merely a name, merely a figurative expression, merely a designation — then let them declare so as they please. For a thing does not follow such a nature merely by [giving it] a name — because of the absurd consequence [that anything could be anything].

body.text: api ca, kā nāma saṃvṛtirityapi vaktavyam / yadi sarvamasaditi kathyate, tadapi na yuktam, parasparavirodhāt / tathāvidhā saṃvṛtistāvadasamarthaivocyeta / yadi utpādayatīti tadā sāmarthyamevaitat / tadā kathamekasmin parasparaviruddhayoḥ sāmarthyāsāmathyayoryoga iti / kathamasatā sanniṣpādayituṃ śakyate /
body.translated_text: Moreover, one must also state what exactly is <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional reality). If it is said that everything is non-existent, that too is not correct, because of mutual contradiction. Such a <s>saṃvṛti</s> would then be called incapable. If [one says] "it produces," then that itself is capacity. Then how can mutually contradictory capacity and incapacity be conjoined in one [entity]? How can the existent be produced by the non-existent?

body.text: na hi sarvamasaditi / tatkathamiti cet? bhāvasvabhāvaiva saṃvṛtiriti / tadā nāsti vivādaḥ, bhavataḥ pratijñāyā eva hāniḥ bhavo 'pyutpadyata eva, ataḥ saṃvṛtyā tadutpadyata iti kathamevamucyeta? tadā tvanutpanna utpadyata ityuktaṃ syāt / saṃvṛtiviparītasyānutpādasya paramārthatvāt tadā paramārthato 'nutpāda eva syādityasambaddhabhidhānaṃ syāt / upayato 'nubhayata ityeṣāpi kalpanā naiva sambhavati, parasparaviruddhatvāt /
body.translated_text: [If it is said:] "It is not that everything is non-existent" — then how? [If the answer is:] "<s>Saṃvṛti</s> is the very nature of entities (<s>bhāvasvabhāva</s>)" — then there is no dispute, [but] your own thesis is destroyed. Moreover, existence (<s>bhāva</s>) does arise; so how can it be said that "it arises conventionally"? That would be saying that the unarisen arises. Since non-arising, which is the opposite of the conventional, is the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>), then there would be non-arising in the ultimate sense — which would be an incoherent statement. The conception that [it is] "from one side but not from both" is also impossible, because of mutual contradiction.

body.text: yadyanityārthaḥ saṃvṛtyartha ityevaṃ cet? tadā kiṃ tāvadanityam? yadi nityābhāvamātram? tadā kathaṃ talloke pratītaṃ syāt / yadi nityaditaraṃ kimapyanityamiti nigadyeta? tadā nityasya vikalpātmakatvāttat [itaraṃ] tāvat sāmarthyānnirvikalpaṃ jñānamityatasyadavasthāyāṃ 'saṃvṛtisat' - iti kathanaṃ tu nirvikalpakajñānena tatpratīyata ityabhihitaṃ syāt /
body.translated_text: If [one says] the meaning of <s>saṃvṛti</s> is 'impermanent' — then what exactly is impermanent? If it is merely the absence of the permanent, how would that be cognized in the world? If something other than the permanent is said to be impermanent — then since the permanent is of the nature of conceptual construction (<s>vikalpa</s>), that other [thing] would be non-conceptual cognition (<s>nirvikalpaka-jñāna</s>) by its very capacity, and to call it 'conventionally existent' in that state would amount to saying that it is cognized by non-conceptual cognition.

body.text: yadyevaṃ syāttadā kimiva bhāvasvabhāvo nābhyupeyate / [tathātve ca] anumānakalpanāyā api tāvat parihāraḥ syāt savikalpakatvāttasyāḥ /
body.translated_text: If it were so, then why would the nature of entities not be accepted? [Moreover, in that case,] even the device of inference would be eliminated, since it is of the nature of conceptual cognition (<s>savikalpakatva</s>).

body.text: atha lokapratītyarthaḥ saṃvṛtyartha ityevaṃ cet? kastāvalloka iti? śāstrakārā vā prākṛtā vā janāḥ prathame vikalpe bhāvo hyanekaparasparaviruddhasvabhāvaḥ syāt, śāstrakāraikasyāpi bhāvasya nānākāreṇādhyāropaṇāt / dvitīye vikalpe nairātmyakarmaphalādīni nābhyupetāni syuḥ, prākṛtakairapratītatvāt /
body.translated_text: If [one says] the meaning of <s>saṃvṛti</s> is 'what is cognized by the world' — then first one must ask: who is this 'world'? Is it the authors of treatises, or ordinary people? In the first alternative, an entity would have many mutually contradictory natures, since even a single entity is superimposed upon in various forms by different treatise-authors. In the second alternative, <s>Nairātmya</s> (selflessness), <s>Karma</s> (action), <s>Phala</s> (result), and the like would not be accepted, since they are not cognized by ordinary people.

body.text: atha māyārthaḥ saṃvṛtyartha iti cet tadā ko hi nāma māyārtha iti vaktavyam / yadi sarvamasaditi, tadā pūrvadoṣa eva samāpadyeta, saṃkleśavyavadānāni ca kathaṃ syuriti ca / atha bhrāntijñānena māyeti cet tadā ābhyantarikajñeyanayena ko hi viśeṣaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: If [one says] the meaning of <s>saṃvṛti</s> is 'illusion' (<s>māyā</s>) — then one must ask: what exactly is 'illusion'? If everything is non-existent, then the same fault as before would apply, and how would affliction (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>) be possible? If [one says] 'illusion by deluded cognition' — then what difference would there be from the approach of internal cognizable objects?

body.text: atha saṃvṛtirnāmamātramiti tadā subhāṣitadurbhāṣitayorbhedo 'śakyaḥ syāt, asatyabhidheye śabdamātre bhedābhāvāt /
body.translated_text: If [one says] <s>saṃvṛti</s> is merely a name — then the distinction between what is well-spoken and what is ill-spoken would be impossible, since there would be no difference in mere words when the referent is unreal.

body.text: atha śabdārtha iti cettadā kathabhedaḥ syāt, pratyātmādhigamyā ye sukhādayaste kutra saṃgṛhītāḥ syuḥ? na hi tāvat saṃvṛtau, teṣāmanirvacanīyatvāt, saṃvṛtisatāṃ vyavahāraprajñapyamānatvācca / sūtre 'pyevamuktamḥ "kiṃ nāma saṃvṛtisatyam? yāvanto lokavyavahārāḥ ye 'kṣarapadaniruktibhirnidiśyanta iti" / anena hi saṃkṣepataḥ saṃvṛtiśabdārtho 'bhihitaḥ /
body.translated_text: If [one says it is] the meaning of words — then how would the distinction [between categories] be made? Where would happiness and the like, which are cognized by each person's own experience, be classified? Not in the conventional, since they are inexpressible, and since conventionally existent things are designated through conventional usage. In the <s>Sūtra</s> too it is stated thus: "What is conventional truth? Whatever worldly usages are indicated by syllables, words, and etymologies." By this, the meaning of the word <s>saṃvṛti</s> is stated in brief.

body.text: athaivaṃ manyate yadābhāsaparikalpyau vyāmiśrya sāmānyākārena gṛhyanta iti? tadā paramārthe 'pyeṣa prasaṅgaḥ syāt, tasyāpi vacanīyasvābhāvye vyavasthitatvena abhidheyatvāt / na ca paramārthasatye 'pi saṅgṛhyante, tadvastusattayāḥ sattvāt / satyāntaraviśeṣapūrakākārā api te na bhavanti / yadi pratītyotpannā rupādayaḥ, pratyāmādhigamyāḥ sukhādayaścāpi 'saṃvṛtisatyam' it nāmrā prajñapyante, tadā mudā tathā kuryuriti, kulmāṣamapi dātavyamiti, katipayenāvirpayayeṇāvivādaśceti /
body.translated_text: If one thinks that appearances (<s>ābhāsa</s>) and constructs (<s>parikalpya</s>) are grasped in a mixed, general form — then this consequence would apply to the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>) too, since it too is expressible insofar as it is established as having a nature that can be spoken of. Nor are they included in ultimate truth, since the reality of that entity exists [as it is]. Nor are they forms that fill up the distinction with another truth. If form (<s>rūpa</s>) and the like, which arise from dependent origination, and happiness and the like, which are cognized by each person, are designated as 'conventional truth' — then let them gladly do so; even <s>Kulmāṣa</s> (boiled grain) should be given [as offering]; with a few non-inversions, there would be no dispute.

body.text: atha kṣaṇamātrānantarānavasthānena asthirārthaḥ saṃvṛtyarthastadviparītaśca nityārthaḥ paramārtha iti siddhasādhanamevaitat, bhavadbhirevaṃ vastunaḥ kṣaṇikatvasvīkarāt, vayamapyevamabhyupagacchamaḥ / ato nāsti vivādaḥ tathā sāṃvṛtikānāṃ vastusāmānyalakṣaṇāmāṃ yā nairātmyarupā dharmatā sāsti paramārthataḥ / sāpi utpādād vā tathāganāmanutpadād vā sarvakālamavikāratayā nityābhyupeyate /
body.translated_text: If [one says] the meaning of <s>saṃvṛti</s> is 'unstable' — i.e., not enduring beyond a single moment — and the meaning of <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate truth) is the opposite, i.e., 'permanent' — then this is merely establishing what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>), since you yourselves accept the momentariness of things. We too accept this very [position]. Therefore there is no dispute. Thus, the <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality), which is the <s>Nairātmya</s> (selflessness) character of the general characteristics of conventionally real things — that exists ultimately. And that too, whether by virtue of the arising of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> or their non-arising, is accepted as permanent since it is unchanging at all times.

body.text: atha asatyārthaḥ saṃvṛtyartha iti tadā kathaṃ sā satyamiti parasparaviruddhayoḥ satyāsatyayoraikātmyānupapatteḥ bhāvasvabhāvaiva kācana saṃvṛtirabhyupagantavyā, anyathā kathaṃ jagat tathā satyaṃ sidhyet, yadi tadabhyupagamyate, tadā [bhavataḥ] pratijñātārthahāniḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: If [one says] the meaning of <s>saṃvṛti</s> is 'unreal' — then how is it 'truth' (<s>satya</s>)? Since the identity of the mutually contradictory — real and unreal — is impossible, some <s>saṃvṛti</s> of the nature of entities must be accepted. Otherwise, how would the world be established as such a truth? If that is accepted, then there would be the loss of your asserted thesis.

body.text: anyacca saṃvṛtiḥ pramāṇamapramāṇaṃ vā? yadi pramāṇaṃ kathaṃ sā saṃvṛtiḥ? athāpramāṇaṃ tadā kathaṃ nairātmyaṃ sādhayituṃ śakyeta?
body.translated_text: Furthermore, is <s>saṃvṛti</s> a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge) or not? If it is a <s>pramāṇa</s>, how is it conventional? If it is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>, then how could <s>Nairātmya</s> (selflessness) be established?

body.text: avaśyamataḥ saṃvṛtibījāni vijñānādīni paramārthataḥ santītyaṅgīkartavyāni, ṛte bījaṃ saṃvṛtyanutpatteḥ, yad bijaṃ tadeva vastutaḥ saditi /
body.translated_text: Therefore it must necessarily be accepted that the seeds of the conventional — consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) and the like — exist in the ultimate sense (<s>paramārthataḥ</s>), since without a seed the conventional does not arise. And what is a seed is indeed real (<s>sat</s>) in truth.

body.text: api ca, yadi bhāvasvabhāvā abbhyupagamyante tadā teṣvāropito mithyāsvabhāvaḥ saṃvṛtisatyam, anāropitastu bhāvasvabhāvaḥ paramārthasatyam / paramārthasatyam / tataśca satyadvayavibhājanaṃ tāvad yujyate / yadi nābhyupagamyante, tadā saṃvṛtirapi vitathā syāt paramārtho 'pyaśakyavyavasthānaḥ syāt, vyavasthākārāṇānāmasattvāt /
body.translated_text: Moreover, if entities with inherent nature are accepted, then the false nature superimposed upon them is conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>), while the non-superimposed inherent nature of entities is ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>). In that case, the division into two truths is indeed consistent. If [entities] are not accepted, then the conventional would be false, and the ultimate would be impossible to establish, since the bases of establishment would be non-existent.

body.text: yadi yathākathañcana kañcidekaḥ paramārthaḥ syāttadā kimarthaṃ sa sādhayate? sa naiva paramārthaḥ kathaṃ sa jñānenāvadhārayituṃ śakyate, na ca paramārthaśabdenāpyabhidhātumarhaḥ evaṃ tāvannāyaṃ paramārthaḥ, na cārtho 'pi paramaḥ, nāpi paramasya jñānasyāyamarthaḥ, sādhāraṇatvāt / yadi yathākathañcana kiścidekaḥ paramārthaḥ syāt tadā paramārthato 'sadbhāvasyaikasya yathākathañcana nirākaraṇād bhāvasattāyā evābhyupagamaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: If, by some means, there were some single ultimate — then why would one need to establish it? It would not be the ultimate; how could it be ascertained by cognition? Nor would it deserve to be designated by the word 'ultimate' (<s>paramārtha</s>). Thus, this is not the ultimate, nor is it the supreme object (<s>parama artha</s>), nor is it the object of supreme cognition — since it would be common [to all]. If, by some means, there were some single ultimate, then by refuting in some way the single non-existence in the ultimate sense, the acceptance of the existence of entities would result.

body.text: api ca, yadi saṃvṛtiparamārthāvabhinnāviti manyate, tadā satyadvayavyavasthānāṃ kathaṃ syāt, dvayorekatarasya parityāgāt / atha bhinnau tadobhayoḥ pṛthaksiddhatvād bhāvaprasaṅgaḥ / atha bhinnabhinnau, tadā kathamekasmin parasparaviruddhatvam / ataḥ pakṣo 'yam 'na bhinno nāpyabhinnaḥ' iti na yujyate, viruddhatvāt / evaṃ bhinnābhinnatvasya anyo 'nyaparihārasthitalakṣaṇatvena ekasya pratiṣedhe 'parasya vidhānaṃ na bhavettadā asattvameva / sa tadā pratiṣeddhumapi kathaṃ śaktaḥ ekasmin yugapatparyudāsaprasajyayorvirodhāt /
body.translated_text: Moreover, if one thinks that <s>saṃvṛti</s> and <s>paramārtha</s> are non-different — then how would the establishment of the two truths be possible, since one of the two would be abandoned? If they are different, then since both would be independently established, the consequence of [real] existence would follow. If they are both different and non-different, how could there be mutual contradiction in a single [entity]? Therefore this position — 'neither different nor non-different' — is untenable, because of contradiction. Since the difference and non-difference are characterized by the elimination of each other, if one is negated, the establishment of the other would not occur — then there would be non-existence itself. How then could one even negate it? Because of the contradiction of exclusion (<s>paryudāsa</s>) and implicative negation (<s>prasajya</s>) occurring simultaneously in one [entity].

body.text: anyacca, bhavatāmanusāreṇa tu puṇyajñānasambhārau duṣparipūraṇau syātām, tadabhāve ca buddhatvamapi duṣprāpaṃ syāt / pūjānugrahakāmyayā yad dīyate tad dānaṃ tvatyantaṃ prasādamabhinirvartayati, tacca nāsti deyadāyakapratigrāhakānupalambhāśritatvāt / sa cānupalambhaḥ kiṃ deyābhāvād vā viṣayābhāvād vā bhavati? prathame tāvat pakṣe na ko 'pi kimapi dadātīti puṇyasyaivābhāvaḥ prasajyate, sattvābhāvācca yo hi bodhisattvānāṃ sattvārthapariśramaḥ sa nirarthaka eva syāt, ato 'sattvaṃ tu nāstyeva / viṣayābhavo 'pi tāvannāsti, bhagavatā deyādivastūnāṃ paridṛṭatvāt / yadyevaṃ na syāuttadā bhagavatā bodhisattvāvasthāyāṃ kathamarthibhyaḥ putrādidānaṃ kṛtam? bhavantastvālambanāśritaṃ dānādikaṃ 'viśuddham' iti nābhyupagacchanti, ataḥ sambhārapāripūristāvadasambhavaiva / tadabhāve hetvabhāvād buddhātvamapi dūre 'pāstaṃ syāt /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, according to your [system], the accumulations of merit and knowledge (<s>puṇya-jñāna-sambhāra</s>) would be difficult to complete, and without them, Buddhahood (<s>buddhatva</s>) too would be difficult to attain. A gift given out of desire for worship and favor produces the utmost grace — but that does not exist, since it relies on the non-apprehension of the gift, the giver, and the recipient. Does that non-apprehension arise from the absence of the gift-object or from the absence of the object [of cognition]? In the first alternative, no one gives anything to anyone, and therefore the very absence of merit would follow. And since sentient beings (<s>sattva</s>) do not exist, the effort of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> for the welfare of sentient beings would be utterly purposeless — therefore, the non-existence of beings simply does not hold. Nor is there absence of the object, since the Blessed One has perceived things such as gifts and the like. If it were not so, how could the Blessed One, while in the stage of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, have given his sons and other [things] to suppliants? You, however, do not accept that giving and the like, which depend on an object of support (<s>ālambana</s>), are 'pure' — therefore the completion of the accumulations is simply impossible. Without them, since the cause is absent, Buddhahood too would be far removed.

body.text: api ca, 'sarve dharmā niḥsvabhāvāḥ' ityettasya tāvat ko hyarthaḥ? yadi svayambhāvasya abhāvānniḥsvabhāvā ityabhidhīyante tadā siddhasādhanameva, hetupratyayādhīnavṛttitvāt sarvavastūnām, na tānyahetukānīti vayamapyabhyupagacchāmaḥ / yadyevaṃ na syāttadā nirapekṣatvānnityaṃ sattvamasattvaṃ vā syāt / yadyucyeta - vinaṣṭā bhāvāḥ svasvabhāvenānutpannatvāt svasvabhāvena na santīti niḥsvabhāvāḥ? ityetadapi siddhasādhanameva, asmākamapi vinaṣṭotpatteranabhyupetatvāt / yadi cābhidhīyeta - tatsvabhāvenaiva sarvakālānavasthānānniḥsvabhāvā manyante, tadapi siddhasādhanameva, yasmādutpattisamanantaravināśasadbhāvāt kṣaṇikā eva / kṣaṇikasya khalu vastuno dvitīye kṣaṇe 'vasthānaṃ nābhyupeyate /
body.translated_text: Moreover, what is the meaning of 'all <s>dharmas</s> are without own-nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>)'? If they are called <s>niḥsvabhāva</s> because of the absence of self-nature (<s>svayambhāva</s>) — then this is merely establishing what is already established, since all things depend on causes and conditions for their operation. We too accept that they are not without cause. If it were not so, then, being independent, there would be either eternal existence or eternal non-existence. If it is said — 'destroyed entities are <s>niḥsvabhāva</s> because they are not arisen by their own nature, and do not exist by their own nature' — this too is merely establishing what is already established, since we too do not accept arising from what has been destroyed. And if it is said — 'they are considered <s>niḥsvabhāva</s> because they do not endure at all times in that very nature' — this too is merely establishing what is already established, since [all things] are indeed momentary (<s>kṣaṇika</s>), due to the reality of destruction immediately upon arising. For the endurance of a momentary thing in a second moment is not accepted.

body.text: yadyucyeta yathā bālapṛthagjanaiḥ parikalpitasya grāhyagrāhakabhāvasya paramārthena svabhavato 'sattvād sasattvaṃ tathā niḥsvabhāvatvamiti tadapi siddhasādhanam, asmābhirapi parikalpitātmano niḥsvabhāvatvasyābhyupagamāt / yadyevaṃ na syāttadā sarve 'pi tattvadarśinaḥ syuḥ /
body.translated_text: If it is said that just as the nature of the grasped-and-grasper (<s>grāhya-grāhaka</s>) superimposed by childish ordinary people is <s>niḥsvabhāva</s> (without own-nature) in the ultimate sense because it is non-existent by its own nature — so too is all non-own-nature to be understood — this too is merely establishing what is already established, since we too accept the non-own-nature of the superimposed self (<s>parikalpitātman</s>). If it were not so, then everyone would be a seer of truth.

body.text: paramārthataḥ sarve bhāvā bālapṛthagjanaiḥ parikalpitena grāhyagrahakāreṇa virāhitā api āryajñānasya advaitātmanā gocaratvena sthitā eva / yadyevaṃ na sthitāḥ, tathāpyasattvena niḥsvabhāvāstadā saṅkleśavyavadānau na syātām /
body.translated_text: Although all entities are, in the ultimate sense, devoid of the grasped-and-grasper form superimposed by childish ordinary people, they are established as the non-dual (<s>advaita</s>) object of noble cognition (<s>āryajñāna</s>). If they were not thus established — if they were <s>niḥsvabhāva</s> by virtue of non-existence — then affliction (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>) would not be possible.

body.text: tathaiva sarvadharmānutpādo 'pyabhihitaḥ / kiṃ tadanutpadatāyāstāvadarthaṃ manyase? yadyucyeta ādito 'nutpannatvāt sarve bhāvā anutpannā iti tadapi siddhasādhanameva, vayamapi saṃsāramanādiṃ manyāmahe / atha pūrvamutpannasya vastunaḥ punaranupattyā sarve dharmā anutpannā iti tadapi siddhasādhanameva, vayamapi pūrvamatpannasya punarutpattiṃ nābhyupagacchāmaḥ, tasya vinaṣṭatvāt / atha apūrvotpādābhāvādanutpādo 'bhidhīyate, tasya vinaṣṭatvāt / atha apūrvotpādābhāvādanutpādo 'bhidhīyate, tadapi nāniṣṭasādhakam, saṃsāre 'pūrvasattvānabhyupagamāt, sarvadā ca pūrvavinaṣṭānāṃ sajātīyotpatteḥ atha bālapṛthagjanaparikalpitasya svalakṣaṇato 'nutpādādanutpāda ucyate, tadāpi nāsti virodhaḥ, kalpitasya svabhāvata utpettaranabhyupagamāt /
body.translated_text: Similarly, the non-origination of all <s>dharmas</s> has also been stated. What do you think is the meaning of that non-originatedness? If one were to say: "All entities are non-arisen because they are non-arisen from the very beginning" — that too is merely proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>), for we too consider <s>saṃsāra</s> to be beginningless. Or if [one says]: "All <s>dharmas</s> are non-arisen because an entity that has previously arisen does not arise again" — that too is merely proving what is already established, for we too do not accept the re-arising of what has previously arisen, since it has perished. Or if non-origination is spoken of as the absence of unprecedented origination, since it has perished — or if non-origination is spoken of as the absence of unprecedented origination, that too does not prove what is undesired, because unprecedented beings are not accepted even in <s>saṃsāra</s>, and because those of similar type always arise from those previously perished. Or if non-origination is spoken of as non-origination from own-characteristic (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) of what is imagined by childish ordinary persons (<s>bālapṛthagjana</s>), even then there is no contradiction, since we do not accept that what is imagined arises from its own nature.

body.text: atha svato 'nutpādād anutpāda ityucyeta tadāpi nāsti virodhaḥ, hetupratyayādhīnatvāt sarvavastūnām, yathā pūrvamuktam / yadi sarvaśaḥ sarvānutpādād anutpāda ucyate tadā darśanādivirodho durnivāraḥ syāt / yadi parasparaviśeṣānutpādād anutpādo 'bhidhīyate tadā [yadi] tathatāsvabhavatāmupādāyocyate tadā nāsti doṣaḥ,[kintu] yadi lokaprasiddhasvabhāvatāmupādāyocyate tadā kena darśanādivirodho nivārayituṃ śakyate / yadi svabhāvetarakriyālakṣaṇaviyogād anupāda iti? tadāpi nāsti doṣaḥ, sarvabhāveṣu kriyāyā abhāvāt / atheścarādibhiritarairanutpādād [anutpāda] ucyate, tadāpi nāniṣṭam, [asmābhirapi] īśvarāderanabhyupagamāt / evamādibhirākāraiḥ 'ādiśāntāḥ, prakṛtiparinirvṛttāḥ' ityādiśabdānāmapyarthā vicāraṇīyāḥ / api ca, anyairanekasūtraiścāpi virodhaḥ saṃllakṣyate, tathā hi āryasandhinirmocanasūtre hyuktaṃ
body.translated_text: Or if one says non-origination means non-origination from self (<s>svataḥ</s>), even then there is no contradiction, because all things are dependent on causes and conditions (<s>hetupratyaya</s>), as stated earlier. If non-origination in every respect means the non-origination of everything, then the contradiction with perception and the like would be unavoidable. If non-origination means the non-origination of mutual distinctions — if this is said with reference to the nature of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), there is no fault; but if said with reference to conventionally established nature, who could ward off the contradiction with perception and the like? If non-origination means the separation from the characteristic of action that is other than <s>svabhāva</s> — even then there is no fault, since action is absent in all entities. Or if non-origination means non-origination by <s>Īśvara</s> and others — even then it is not undesirable, since we too do not accept <s>Īśvara</s> and the like. By such and other forms, the meanings of terms such as "primordially quiescent" (<s>ādiśānta</s>), "naturally in <s>nirvāṇa</s>" (<s>prakṛtiparinirvṛtta</s>), and so forth should also be investigated. Moreover, contradiction is observed with other numerous <s>sūtras</s> as well. For in the <s>Ārya-Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra</s> it is stated:

body.text: "ato lakṣaṇaniḥsvabhāvatāmabhisandhāya mayā sarvadharmaṇāmanutpādḥparikīrtitaḥ /"
body.translated_text: "Having aimed at the essencelessness of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇa-niḥsvabhāvatā</s>), I have proclaimed the non-origination of all <s>dharmas</s>."

body.text: parikalpitasvabhāve hi lakṣaṇaniḥsvabhāvatā vyavasthāpyate /
body.translated_text: For the essencelessness of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇa-niḥsvabhāvatā</s>) is established in relation to the imagined nature (<s>parikalpita-svabhāva</s>).

body.text: mahāyānaprasādaprabhāvane [nāma mahāyānasūtre] coktamḥ
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Mahāyāna-prasāda-prabhāvana</s> [<s>sūtra</s>] it is stated:

body.text: "kulaputra, bodhisattvaḥ dharmamayoniśaḥ śabdaśaḥ pravicayya mahāyānaprasadāyatano na bhavati / śabdaśo 'nabhipretya yoniśo manasi kṛtvā mahāyānaprasādāyatano bhavati / evaṃ kulaputra, bodhisattvo 'yoniśaḥ śabdaśo dharmān pravicayya aṣṭāviṃśatimasaddṛṣṭīrutpādayati, tadayathā - nimittadṛṣṭiḥ, adṛṣṭidarśanadṛṣṭiḥ, vyavahārāpavādadṛṭiḥ, saṃkleśāpavādadṛṣṭiḥ, tattvāpavādadṛṣṭiśceti" ityevamādikaṃ vistareṇābhidhāya ḥ
body.translated_text: "Son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who investigates <s>dharmas</s> unsystematically, word by word, does not become a vessel of faith in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Not grasping at mere words, [but] reflecting systematically in mind, one becomes a vessel of faith in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Thus, son of good family, a <s>bodhisattva</s> who investigates <s>dharmas</s> unsystematically, word by word, generates twenty-eight wrong views, namely: the view of signs (<s>nimitta-dṛṣṭi</s>), the view of seeing what is not seen (<s>adṛṣṭi-darśana-dṛṣṭi</s>), the view of denying conventions (<s>vyavahārāpavāda-dṛṣṭi</s>), the view of denying affliction (<s>saṃkleśāpavāda-dṛṣṭi</s>), and the view of denying reality (<s>tattvāpavāda-dṛṣṭi</s>)" — and so forth, [the sūtra] states at length.
