body.text: "kulaputraṃ, kā hi tāvannimittadṛṭiḥ? sāṃyogikasya svabhāvamabhisandhāya mayā sarvadharmāṇāṃ yadasattvaṃ samprakāśitaṃ tacchabdaśo 'bhiniviśya [ye] sāṃkleśikadharmāṇāṃ vaiyavadānīkadharmāṇāṃ cāpyasattve 'bhiniviśante, asannimittopādānena [teṣu] asaddṛṣṭirupajāyate, ataḥ [saiva] nimittadṛṣṭiruktā / [ataḥ] bodhisattvasya śabdaśo 'bhiniviṣṭāyāmasaddṛṣṭi saiva tasya mahatī dṛṣṭiriti, ata eva sā adṛṣṭidarśanadṛṣṭirityucyate / tato vyavahārāpavādadṛṣṭisaṃkleśāpavādadṛṭitattvāpavādadṛṣṭa yastāvajjāyante / tato vyavahārāpavādadṛṣṭisaṃkleśāpavādadṛṣṭitattvāpavādadṛṣtayastāvajjāyante yadā nimittadṛṣṭyā sarvāpavādaḥ [yadā] kriyate tadā vyavahārāpavādadṛṣṭerapyabhiniveśo jāyate, saṃkleśāpavādadṛṣṭerapyabhiniveśo jāyate tattvāpavādadṛṣṭerapyabhiniveśo jāyate" ityevamuktam /
body.translated_text: "Son of good family, what then is the view of signs? Having aimed at the nature of what is conditioned (<s>sāṃyogika</s>), I have revealed the non-existence (<s>asattva</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>. Those who, grasping at mere words, cling to the non-existence of both defiled <s>dharmas</s> and purifying <s>dharmas</s> — through grasping at the sign of non-existence, the wrong view arises in them; hence it is called the view of signs. [Therefore], when the <s>bodhisattva</s> clings to the word, this wrong view itself becomes his great [wrong] view; for this very reason it is called the view of seeing what is not seen. From this, the views of denying conventions, denying affliction, and denying reality arise. When through the view of signs all is negated, attachment to the view of denying conventions arises, attachment to the view of denying affliction arises, and attachment to the view of denying reality arises" — thus it is stated.

body.text: laṅkāvatārasūtre 'upuktamḥ
body.translated_text: In the <s>Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra</s> it is also stated:

children.translated_text: The imagined entity does not exist, but the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>) does exist;
those who conceptualize in terms of superimposition and negation perish.
All <s>dharmas</s> are without cognition by imagined nature;
depending on the dependent [nature], conceptualization wanders among people.

body.text: ataḥ pratītyasamutpannaḥ paratantrasvabhāvaḥ paramārthataḥ san, tatra parikalpitasvabhāvo 'nutpādinābhihitaṃ ityeva tāvannirdekṣyate / punastatroktamḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore, the dependent nature (<s>paratantra-svabhāva</s>), being dependently arisen (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>), exists in the ultimate sense; the imagined nature (<s>parikalpita-svabhāva</s>) is what is spoken of as "non-arisen" — this much will be demonstrated. Again, in the same [text] it is stated:

children.text: na hyātmā vidyate skandhe skandhāścaiva hi nātmani /
children.translated_text: The self does not exist in the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), nor do the aggregates [exist] in the self;

children.text: na te yathā vikalpyante na ca vai na santi ca //
children.translated_text: they are not as they are conceptualized, yet they are not non-existent either.

body.text: ābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ pratiṣedhābhyāṃ skandhānāṃ sattaiva tāvannirdiṣṭā / mahāśūnyatāsūtre 'pi yaduktamḥ
body.translated_text: By these two negations, the very existence of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) is indicated. In the <s>Mahāśūnyatā-sūtra</s> too, it is stated:

body.text: "asti karma asti vipākaḥ kārakastu nopalabhyate" anena tāvad vacanena virodho 'pi samupajāyate / evaṃ yadi paramārthataḥ karmāpyasti vipāko 'pyasti tadā sarve dharmā niḥsvabhāvā bhavituṃ nārhanti / yadi saṃvṛtau santīti cet tadā karturapi saṃvṛtau sadbhāvāt "kārakastu nopalabhyate" ityevaṃ na vaktavyam / āryalaṅkāvatārasūtre coktamḥ
body.translated_text: "There is action, there is result, but no agent is apprehended." By this statement, indeed, contradiction also arises. Thus, if both action and result exist in the ultimate sense, then all <s>dharmas</s> cannot be without own-nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>). If [they are said to] exist conventionally (<s>saṃvṛtau</s>), then since the agent too exists conventionally, one should not say "the agent is not apprehended." And in the <s>Ārya-Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra</s> it is stated:

children.translated_text: The existence of all entities, as conceptualized by the childish —

children.text: yadi te bhaved yathā dṛṣṭāḥ sarve syustattvadarśinaḥ //
children.translated_text: if they were as perceived, all would be seers of reality.
Due to the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s>, there is no conjunction from [mere] thought;

children.text: na te tathā yathā dṛṣṭā na ca te vai na santi ca //
children.translated_text: they are not as perceived, yet they are not non-existent either.

body.text: anena yadi sarvadharmāṇāmasattvaṃ tadā saṃkleśavyadānayorapavādadoṣaḥ prasajyata iti nirdiṣṭam / punastatraivoktamḥ
body.translated_text: By this, it is indicated that if all <s>dharmas</s> were non-existent, then the fault of denying both defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>) would follow. Again, in the same [text] it is stated:

children.translated_text: The perception of external objects is false; there is no [external] object — it is mind alone.
For those who observe correctly, the grasper and the grasped (<s>grāha-grāhya</s>) are extinguished.

children.text: bāhyo na vidyate hyartho yathā bālairvikalpyate /
children.translated_text: External objects do not exist as conceptualized by the childish;
the mind, agitated by latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), produces the appearance of objects.

body.text: āryadaśabhūmakasūtre 'pyuktam "cittamātraṃ yaduta traidhātukam" iti / tathaiva āryasandhinirmocanalaṅkāvatāraghanavyūhādiṣvapi sarvadharmāṇāṃ cittamātraśarīratvaṃ nirdeṣṭuṃ 'cittamātrameva paramārthasat, netarathā' iti sampradarśitam / ataḥ sarve dharmā niḥsvabhāvatvena na sidhyanti / āryātakūṭe 'pyullikhitamḥ
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Daśabhūmaka-sūtra</s> too it is stated: "The three realms are mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>)." Likewise, in the <s>Ārya-Saṃdhinirmocana</s>, <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s>, <s>Ghanavyūha</s>, and other <s>sūtras</s>, in order to indicate that all <s>dharmas</s> have the nature of mind-only, it has been shown that "mind-only is ultimately real, not otherwise." Therefore, all <s>dharmas</s> are not established as being without own-nature. In the <s>Ārya-Kāśyapaparivarta</s> too it is stated:

body.text: "astīti kāśyapa, ayameko 'nta, nāstīti kāśyapa, ayameko 'ntaḥ, yadenayorantayormadhyam, tadarupyanidarśanamapraṣṭhimanābhāsamaniketamavijñaptikam, iyamucyate kāśyapa, madhyatā pratipad bhūtapratyavekṣā" iti /
body.translated_text: "O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, 'it exists' — this is one extreme. 'It does not exist,' O <s>Kāśyapa</s> — this is the other extreme. That which is the middle between these two extremes — that is formless, without indication, without foundation, without appearance, without abode, without cognition. This, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is called the middle path (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>), the investigation of things as they truly are."

body.text: anena tāvad vijñānameva paramārthasattvānidarśanatvādiguṇopetaṃ śāścatocchedāntadvayavinirmuktamiti nirdiṣṭam / etadadhikṛtyaivāryaratnamedhe 'pyuktamḥ
body.translated_text: By this, it is indicated that consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) alone, being endowed with qualities such as being without indication in the ultimate sense, is free from the two extremes of eternalism (<s>śāśvata</s>) and annihilationism (<s>uccheda</s>). With reference to this, in the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s> too it is stated:

body.text: "kulaputra, yadi [vijñānaṃ] paramārthato nāsti, tadā brahmacaryādīni nirarthakāni syuḥ" iti / āryaratnakūṭe hyuktamḥ
body.translated_text: "Son of good family, if consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) does not exist in the ultimate sense, then the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) and the like would be meaningless." In the <s>Ārya-Ratnakūṭa</s> it is stated:

body.text: "ye paramārthasato 'pi vijñānasyāpavādaṃ kṛtvā sarvadharmaśūnyatāyāmabhiniviśya śūnyatādṛṣṭikāste 'cikitsyāḥ" iti /
body.translated_text: "Those who, having negated even ultimately real consciousness, cling to the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s>, holding the view of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā-dṛṣṭi</s>) — they are incurable."

body.text: tathā coktamḥ
body.translated_text: And it is also stated:

body.text: "varaṃ khalu kāśyapa, sumerumātrā pudgaladṛṣṭirna tvevābhimānikasya śūnyatādṛṣṭiriti" /
body.translated_text: "O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, better a view of self (<s>pudgala-dṛṣṭi</s>) as great as Mount <s>Sumeru</s> than the view of emptiness of one who is conceited."

body.text: āryasandhinirmocane cāpi śūnyatālakṣaṇamudbhāvitamḥ
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Ārya-Saṃdhinirmocana</s>, the characteristic of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) has been elaborated:

body.text: "paratantralakṣaṇaṃ maitreya, pariniṣpannalakṣaṇaṃ ca saṃkleśo vyavadānaṃ ca / sarvathātyantaviyuktaṃ parikalpitalakṣaṇaṃ yattanna tenopalabhyata idaṃ śūnyatālakṣanamuktaṃ bhavati" /
body.translated_text: "O <s>Maitreya</s>, the characteristic of the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>) and the characteristic of the perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>) are defilement and purification [respectively]. That which is completely and utterly separated from the imagined characteristic (<s>parikalpita-lakṣaṇa</s>) — that which is not apprehended by that — this is called the characteristic of emptiness."

body.text: āryāṇāṃ pratyātmavedyamavaśyameva paramārthato vastusat, anyathā āryasandhinirmocanoktāni vacanāni tāvādasadarthakānītī naiva / yadyucyeta kiṃ khalu vastu? yadāryajñānena āryadarśanena vānirvacanīyatvena parijñātam / anirvacanīyadharmatāvabodhena saṃskārāsaṃskārābhyāṃ prajñaptamiti yaduktaṃ tena virodhaḥ syāditi /
body.translated_text: What is directly experienced by the noble ones (<s>āryas</s>) must certainly be ultimately real; otherwise the statements in the <s>Ārya-Saṃdhinirmocana</s> would be meaningless. If one asks: "What indeed is the real thing?" — [it is] that which is known through noble wisdom (<s>āryajñāna</s>), through noble vision (<s>āryadarśana</s>), as inexpressible (<s>anirvacanīya</s>). Through understanding the nature of inexpressibility, what has been designated by both conditioning and non-conditioning — there would be contradiction with that which is stated.

body.text: ekameva yānaṃ paramārthato mahāyānalakṣaṇaṃ, nāvaśiṣṭamiti yad bhavatābhihitaṃ tadapi yuktyāgamābhyāṃ viruddham, vipratipattināṃ sandarśanāt / sattveṣu tāvad vividhādhimuktikā upalabhyante / tathā hi kecana parahitāśayā eva pravartante / athāpare niṣkāraṇaṃ paraduḥkheṣu spṛhante / kecittvalpamātra evātmano hitasukhe āsajyāyeṣu drahyanti / tathaivānye svasukhasampattisādhanatatparā anyavyāghātaṃ kṛtvā tadduḥkhavinivṛttito virajyate / kecana saṃsārasukhamātrasyaivābhilāṣeṇa puṇyādīni sampādayanti / tathaivetare tāvad bhavāntarakhecchato viramya svamuktyarthaṃ prayatante / aye tu kevalaṃ paravimuktimevānucintayanti saṃbodhinidānāṃ ca dānādipāramitāpravṛttimālambante / ityevamaprameyapratipattyālambanāt sattvānāṃ chandalakṣaṇo hetuviśeṣo 'numīyate, phalaviśeṣo 'pihetuviśeṣākṣiptavāttasya / svābhilāṣadvāreṇaiva pravṛttidarśanād śraddhaiva hi pravṛttiheturiti niścitam / sattvānāmayaṃ śraddhāviśeṣo 'pi gotraviśeṣeṇāvinābhūtaḥ, ato nānāgotratvāt sattvānāṃ tulyajātīyagotrakairvidhīyamānapratipattiviśeṣānurūpaṃ phalalakṣaṇayānamapi nānā bhavatīti yuktibhirnānāyānataiva niścīyate /
body.translated_text: That there is only one vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>), with the characteristic of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> in the ultimate sense, and no others — what you have stated is contradicted by both reasoning and scripture, because of the observation of differences in understanding among beings. Among beings, indeed, various dispositions are observed. For some engage [in action] solely out of benevolence toward others. Others, without reason, delight in the suffering of others. Some, attached to only a slight degree of their own benefit and happiness, are hostile toward others. Similarly, others, intent on achieving their own happiness and prosperity, harm others and are detached from averting their suffering. Some accumulate merit and the like merely out of desire for <s>saṃsāric</s> happiness. Similarly, others, having turned away from even the desire for another existence, strive for their own liberation. Yet others contemplate solely the liberation of others and engage in the practice of generosity and other <s>pāramitās</s> as the foundation for awakening. Thus, from the immeasurable differences in the objects of spiritual practice among beings, a specific causal difference characterized by disposition is inferred, and a specific result [is inferred] because it is entailed by the specific cause. Since engagement is observed through the door of one's own aspiration, it is determined that faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) alone is the cause of engagement. This specific difference in faith among beings is invariably accompanied by a specific difference in spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>); therefore, because of the diversity of <s>gotras</s> among beings, the vehicles too — whose characteristics are results corresponding to the specific practices performed by those of similar lineage — become diverse. Thus by reasoning, the diversity of vehicles is established.

body.text: bahudhātukasūtre 'pi bahudhātukāḥ sattvā vinirdiṣṭāḥ / bhagavātā yatkhalu dhātujñānabalānāṃ nānātvamabhihitam, tadapi nānādhātutvaṃ kimiva asat syāt / āryakaṅkavatārasūtre 'pi pañca abhisamayotrāṇyabhihitāni / āryākṣayamatinirdeśasūtre 'pyuktam - trīṇi tāvatrairyāṇikayānāni, yaduta - śrāvakayānaṃ pratyekabuddhayānaṃ mahāyānaṃ ceti / evamevānekeṣu sūtreṣvapi śrāvakādiyānatrayanirdeśād āgamato 'pi tāvannānā yānāni sidhyantīti /
body.translated_text: In the <s>Bahudhātuka-sūtra</s> too, beings of many elements are indicated. The fact that the Blessed One stated the diversity of the power of element-knowledge — how could that diversity of elements be non-existent? In the <s>Ārya-Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra</s> too, five types of spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>) for awakening are stated. In the <s>Ārya-Akṣayamatinirdeśa-sūtra</s> too it is stated: there are three vehicles for those of the three [types], namely the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle, and the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Thus, since the indication of three vehicles beginning with the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle is found in many <s>sūtras</s>, from scripture too the diversity of vehicles is established.

body.text: āryasaddharmapuṇḍarīkādiṣu yaddhi ekaṃ hi yānamiti vyapadiṣṭam, tadābhiprāyikamiti draṣṭavyam samatābhiprāyādipradarśanāt / dharmadhātulakṣaṇatayā yānānāṃ bhedābhāvād ekameva yānamiti tadabhiprāyaḥ / athavā yānīkṛtaṃ yānamiti yānikurvatāṃ śrāvakādipudgalānāṃ nairātmye 'tulyatvābhāvād ekameva yānam / athavā ye vimuktāsteṣāmabhinnatvād ekameva yānam / athavā aniyatagotrakāṇāṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ mahāyānenaiva niryāṇād ekameva yānaṃ deśitam / athavā sarvasattveṣvātmādhyāśayena mahākaraṇāmayā bhagavantaḥ, pūrvaṃ samudānītabodhisambhārāḥ śrāvakagotrīyāścāpi buddhatvaprāptyadhyāśayāḥ, ato 'bhinnādhyāśayād ekameva yānam / athavā bhagavatā svayamanekadhā śrāvakayānādibhirniryāṇadvāraiḥ parinirvāṇasandarśanād ekameva yānam / athavā nāsti mahāyānād viśiṣṭataraṃ yānāntaramiti tadadhikārād ekameva yānamiti, tadevaṃvidhābhiprāyeṇa ekameva yānamiti deśitam / athavā aniyatānāṃ śrāvakagotrīyāṇāmākarṣaṇārthaṃ bodhisattvagotrīyāṇāṃ ca
body.translated_text: What has been designated as "there is only one vehicle" in the <s>Ārya-Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> and other texts should be understood as having a special intention (<s>ābhiprāyika</s>), since it demonstrates the intention of sameness and so forth. Since there is no distinction among vehicles from the perspective of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>-characteristic, there is only one vehicle — that is the intention. Or: "vehicle" means "that which serves as a vehicle"; since there is no difference in selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) among persons of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and others who make it a vehicle, there is only one vehicle. Or: since those who are liberated are non-different, there is only one vehicle. Or: since <s>Śrāvakas</s> of indeterminate lineage (<s>aniyata-gotra</s>) also proceed by the <s>Mahāyāna</s> alone, only one vehicle has been taught. Or: the Blessed Ones, out of compassion with the aspiration of self (<s>ātmādhyāśaya</s>) in all beings, having previously accumulated the provisions for awakening (<s>bodhisambhāra</s>), and even those of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> lineage having the aspiration for attaining Buddhahood — hence, due to non-difference of aspiration, there is only one vehicle. Or: since the Blessed One himself, through the doors of various vehicles such as the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, displayed [final] <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in many ways, there is only one vehicle. Or: since there is no vehicle more excellent than the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, by virtue of its supremacy, there is only one vehicle. Thus, with such various intentions, "only one vehicle" has been taught. Or: for the purpose of attracting <s>Śrāvakas</s> of indeterminate lineage and

body.text: sandhāraṇārthamityabhiprāyo bhagavataiva āryadaśadharmakasandhinirmocanalaṅkāvatārādiṣu sūtreṣu spaṣṭīkṛtaḥ /
body.translated_text: for the purpose of sustaining <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> lineage — this intention of the Blessed One has been made clear in the <s>Ārya-Daśadharmaka</s>, <s>Saṃdhinirmocana</s>, <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s>, and other <s>sūtras</s>.

body.text: anyacca, naikabhavaparamparāyāṃ sambhārān paripūrya bodhisattvā buddhatvapadamadhigamiṣyanti / śrāvakā aśeṣabhavasaṃyojanaṃ prajahantīti teṣāṃ naikajanmasādhyaṃ buddhātvadhigantuṃ ko 'pi bhavapratīsandhirnaiva sambhavati, tathā hi - mūlaṃ bhavasyānuśayāḥ yaduktaṃ so 'pyātmagrahaprabhava eveti niyatam abhīṣṭaṃ ca / āryairātmadṛṣṭiviparītayā nairātmyamārgabhāvanayā sarvānuśayāḥ samūlamucchināḥ, tatsamucchedena teṣāṃ janmano 'pyādhārarasyābhāvāt tad [janma] api samucchidyate / phalataḥ kutasteṣāmanekabhavaparamparāsādhyo buddhātvalābho bhaviṣyatīti / āryāsaddharmapuṇḍarīke bhagavatā yacchrāvakebhyo buddhātvādhigatervyākaraṇaṃ kṛtaṃ tattu nirmitaśrāvakāṇāṃ nirmāṇasya, yairbodhau pariṇāmanā kṛtā, teṣāṃ vābhiprāyeṇa kṛtamiti draṣṭavyam / idaṃ tāvad bhagavatā āryalaṅkavatārasūtrādiṣu nirdiṣṭameva / āryasamādhirājasūtre yattāvaduktamḥ
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will attain the state of <s>Buddhahood</s> by completing the accumulations over a succession of many existences. Since <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers) abandon all fetters of existence, no rebirth-connection whatsoever is possible for them to attain <s>Buddhahood</s>, which requires many lifetimes. For it has been stated that the root of existence is the latent dispositions (<s>anuśaya</s>), and that too arises from grasping at a self (<s>ātmagraha</s>) — this is certain and accepted. The Noble Ones, through cultivating the path of selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) which is the opposite of the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>), have uprooted all latent dispositions along with their root; through their elimination, since the basis of their birth is also absent, that [birth] too is eliminated. Consequently, how will the attainment of <s>Buddhahood</s>, which requires a succession of many existences, be possible for them? The prophecy of attaining <s>Buddhahood</s> made by the Blessed One to the <s>Śrāvakas</s> in the <s>Āryasaddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> should be understood as [made] for emanated <s>Śrāvakas</s> as an emanation, or with the intention [of addressing] those who had dedicated [their merit] toward enlightenment. This has been stated by the Blessed One in the <s>Āryalaṅkāvatārasūtra</s> and other texts. In the <s>Āryasamādhirājasūtra</s>, it is stated:

body.text: atra nāsti ko 'pi sattvo 'bhavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Here there is no being whatsoever who is incapable [of awakening].

body.text: sampūrṇo 'yaṃ sattvaloko buddho bhaviṣyati //
body.translated_text: This entire world of beings will become <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.text: tadapyucyamānamupagatānabhipretyābhihitamiti jñātavyam / katipayeṣu [sūtreṣu] - "tathāgatagarbhāḥ sarve sattvāḥ" iti yaduktaṃ tadapi tathatālakṣaṇāyāstathatāyā abhiprāyeṇa vyapadiṣṭam / ataḥ paramārthatastrīṇyeva yānāni, sarve dharmāśca sasvabhāvā ityabhidhīyate / ityayaṃ pūrvapakṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: That too should be understood as stated with the intention of those who have attained [the path], not [taken] literally. The statement in some [sūtras] that 'all beings have the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> (embryo of the <s>Tathāgata</s>)' — that too is stated with reference to <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), which has the characteristic of suchness. Therefore, it is stated that ultimately there are three vehicles only, and all <s>dharmas</s> have their own nature. This is the prior position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>).

body.text: tataścāyaṃ pratyavasthīyate / tatra tāvad 'nāgamataḥ sarve dharmā niḥsvabhāvatvena sādhayituṃ śakyāḥ, kenāpi tathābhyupagamābhāvād' ityādyuktaṃ tannirucyate / kiṃ kenāpyanabhyupetatvādāgama ekāntenānupādeya eva bhavatyuta utadeyo 'pīti? prathamastāvat pakṣo na yuktaḥ / tathā sati na ko 'pi kamapyāgamamāśrayiṣyati, kenacidapi tadanabhtupetatvāt / tatra kaścid abhimānitayā vā, anarthitayā vā, pāpamitrasaṃsargeṇa vā, vimūḍhacittatayā vā, sukalyāmitrānupalambhena vā, parapratyaneyatayā vā, śraddhendriyādivaikalyena vā? tadvidāṃ sudhiyāṃ viraheṇa bhagavata ādimadhyaparyavasānakalyāṇaṃ pravacanaratnamanāśritā api kiṃ tāvadadhigatasvaparahitasampādanonopāyaṃ tarkanipuṇaṃ vidvāṃsamapi nāśrayiṣyante?
body.translated_text: Now this is responded to. First, regarding the statement 'all <s>dharmas</s> cannot be established as essenceless from scripture, because no one accepts it thus,' etc. — this is analyzed. Is it the case that because no one accepts it, scripture should absolutely not be relied upon, or can it still be relied upon? The first position is not valid. In that case, no one would ever rely on any scripture, because no one accepts it. Among those, some [do not accept it] due to conceit, some due to lack of interest, some due to association with evil friends, some due to confused mind, some due to not finding good spiritual friends, some due to being dependent on others, some due to deficiency in the faculty of faith and other [faculties]. Will even those who, not relying on the jewel of the Blessed One's teaching which is excellent in the beginning, middle, and end, fail to rely on a learned person who is skilled in reasoning and who has mastered the means of accomplishing benefit for self and others?

body.text: athavā, ajñā vaṇijo yathā vimugdhatayānarghaṃ ratnamapi parityajanti tathā suvijñāstarkanipuṇā api vaṇijastanna parigṛhṇantīti na / tāpāccedācca nikaṣāt suvarṇamiva pratyakṣānumānapūrvaparāviruddhāgamairaviruddhātvāt pareṣāñcāgamānāṃ tadviparītatvād ābhyudayikanaiḥśreyasikanaiḥśreyasikaphalamāptukāmā aśeṣasampadamadhigantukāmā vipaścitastaṃ [viparītāgamaṃ] parityajya yadekāntakuśalaṃ tatpravacanaratnamevāśrayantīti yaḥ pakṣaḥ, sa cet samyagiti tadā bhavanto 'pi yadi bhagavatpravacanaṃ suparīkṣyaivābhyupayantītyato bhagavatā prajñāpārāmitādiṣu yo hi madhyamo mārgaḥ suspaṣṭamādiṣṭastaṃ kinnāśrayiṣyantīti?
body.translated_text: Or, just as ignorant merchants, due to confusion, discard even a priceless gem — do well-informed merchants skilled in reasoning likewise not accept it? No. Like gold [tested] by burning, cutting, and rubbing on a touchstone, because [the teaching] is not contradicted by perception, inference, and mutually non-contradictory scripture, and because the scriptures of others are contrary to that — those wise ones who desire the fruit of worldly prosperity and ultimate liberation, who wish to attain all excellences, discarding that [contrary scripture], rely upon precisely that jewel of teaching which is exclusively wholesome. If that position is correct, then if you too accept the Blessed One's teaching only after thorough examination, then why would you not rely on the Middle Path that the Blessed One has clearly taught in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and other [texts]?

body.text: yadi svayaṃ tamāśrayituṃ na śaktāstathāpyāryanāgātjunapādairyo hyanekayuktipradīpaprakāraiḥ suspaṣṭaṃ nirdiṣṭastadbalenāpi kimiva nābhyupagacchanti? yato hi sa ācāryastāvad bhagadvacananirdiṣṭatvena prathamāṃ bhūmimāsāditatvena cāryalaṅkāvatārādau vyākṛtaḥ / tasyāpi yadi nirdeśo viparyastaḥ syāttadā naiva tāvad bhagavatā tathā vyākṛtaḥ syāt / ato yadayācāryavacānaṃ tyajyate bhagavadvacanamapi nūnaṃ parityaktaṃ bhavet / phalata āryanāgārjunapādapratipadītaṃ mārgaṃ parityajya anāryapudgalapradarśitapathāśrayaṇaṃ tāvānnaiva yujyate /
body.translated_text: Even if you yourselves are unable to rely on it, the Venerable <s>Nāgārjuna</s> has clearly taught it through various kinds of illumination by means of reasoning — why do you not accept it even on his authority? For that teacher has been prophesied in the <s>Āryalaṅkāvatāra</s> and other [texts] as having been designated by the Blessed One's word and as having attained the first <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). If his teaching too were mistaken, then the Blessed One would not have prophesied him thus. Therefore, when this teacher's words are rejected, the Blessed One's words too are surely rejected. Consequently, it is not at all proper to abandon the path taught by the Venerable <s>Nāgārjuna</s> and take refuge in a path shown by a non-noble person.

body.text: na vayaṃ śabdānāṃ bhāvikaḥ kaścana sambandha iti manyāmahe / atastanniṣedhato na [te] anabhyupagatā bhaviṣyantīti / te tāvat [śabdāḥ] saṅketābhijñānena vyavahāre vakturicchāṃ dyotayante arthāvasthādibhirabhrāntapuruṣairabhihitāḥ śabdāḥ vivakṣitārthāsambaddhā iti na sarvathā niścetuṃ śakyate, anyathā sarvavyavahāroccheda eva syāditi /
body.translated_text: We do not think that there is any inherent connection of words [with their referents]. Therefore, from denying that, [you] will not become non-acceptors. Those [words] indicate the speaker's intention in usage through familiarity with convention. Words uttered by non-deluded persons in accordance with the state of affairs and other [conditions] cannot be definitively [determined to be] unconnected with the intended meaning, for otherwise there would be the complete cessation of all convention.

body.text: kṣīṇarāgadveṣamohānāṃ śabdā aviparītārthā iti pratipādanena sarveṣāṃ śabdā viparītārthā evati na, svasantatau viniyatatvātteṣām / atastrirupapaliṅgāni parikṣaṇapariśuddhāni ādimadhyāntakalyāṇaniyatāni tāvad vacanāni avisaṃvādakatvād vidvadbhiḥ samāśrayaṇīyānyeva /
body.translated_text: By demonstrating that the words of those whose passion, hatred, and delusion are exhausted are not of mistaken meaning, it does not follow that the words of everyone are of mistaken meaning, because those [words] are restricted to their own continuum. Therefore, words that have been purified through investigation by the three kinds of evidential marks, that are determined to be excellent in the beginning, middle, and end — these should indeed be relied upon by the wise, because they are non-deceptive.

body.text: na vayaṃ tathāgatavacanapratihatebhyastīrthikebhyastātsiddhaye bhagavadvacanaprāmāṇyaṃ pratipādayāmāstathāpi yadā āgamārthaṃ vinintayāmastadā vyākaraṇapramāṇatvena sampradarśayāmaḥ / tatpratipādakaṃ bhagavadvacanaṃ nāstītyetadapi kathanaṃ nocitam / bhagavatāpyevameva nītārthasūtrasamāśrayaṇamevābhihitam, na neyārthasūtrasamāśrayaṇamiti /
body.translated_text: We do not establish the authority of the Blessed One's words for <s>Tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist teachers) who are opposed to the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s words. Nevertheless, when we investigate the meaning of scripture, we demonstrate it through the authority of [<s>Buddha</s>'s] prophecy. The statement that there is no word of the Blessed One that demonstrates this is also not appropriate. The Blessed One himself has stated that one should rely on sūtras of definitive meaning (<s>nītārtha</s>), not on sūtras of provisional meaning (<s>neyārtha</s>).

body.text: yadyucyeta ko 'yaṃ paramārtho nāmeti cet? pramāṇopapatraḥ paramārthādhikṛtaśceti / athavā yadartho nānyatra netuṃ śakyata iti / sarvadharmānutpādāstāvat pramāṇopannārthaḥ,ato yuktyanvitatvāt sa paramārtha ityucyate / āryadharmasaṃgītāvuktam - anutpādaḥ satyam, utpādādayo 'nye dharmā asatyāḥ, mṛṣā moṣadharmakatvāt / āryasatyadvayanirdeśe 'pyuktam "devaputra, artho hi paramārthato 'nutpādaḥ, ayaṃ tāvat sarvasaṃkleśavyavadānadharmeṣu vyavasthāpyate, na katipayeṣu" avameva punastatraivoktam - "tadyathāpi nāma devaputra, yacca mṛdbhājanasyābhyantaramākāśam, yacca ratnabhājanasyākāśam ākāśadhātureva eṣaḥ / tatra paramārthano na kiñcinnānākaraṇam / evameva devaputra, yaḥ saṃkleśaḥ, sa paramārthato 'tyantānutpādatā / yadapi vyavadānaṃ tadapi paramārthato 'tyantānutpādatā / saṃsāro 'pi paramārtha 'tyantānutpādatā / yāvannirvāṇamapi paramārthato 'tyantānutpādatā / nātra kiñcit paramārthato nānākaraṇam / tat kasmāddhetoḥ? paramārthato 'tyantānutpādatvāt sarvadharmāṇāmiti" / evamayamanutpādo 'pi paramārthānukulatvāt paramārtha ucyate, na vastutaḥ, sarvaprapañcitītatvāddhi vastutaḥ paramārthasya / ato yāni ca yāvanti ca paramārthamadhikṛtya anutpādīni lakṣaṇāni nirdiṣṭāni tāni sarvāṇi nītārthatvena grahītavyāni, ato viparītāni neyārthāniti / āryākṣayamatinirdiśasūtre tāvanneyanītārthalakṣaṇaṃ nirdiṣṭam, tathāhi -
body.translated_text: If it is asked, 'What is this ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>)?' — it is that which is supported by <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) and pertains to the ultimate. Or alternatively, it is that whose meaning cannot be led elsewhere. Non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s> is a meaning supported by <s>pramāṇa</s>; therefore, because it accords with reasoning, it is called ultimate. In the <s>Āryadharmasaṃgīti</s> it is stated: 'Non-arising is truth; arising and other <s>dharmas</s> are untrue, false, because they have the nature of being deceptive.' In the <s>Āryasatyadvayanirdeśa</s> too it is stated: 'O Son of the Gods, the meaning is that ultimately [there is] non-arising; this is to be established with respect to all <s>dharmas</s> of defilement and purification, not just some.' Again in that same [text] it is stated: 'O Son of the Gods, just as the space inside an earthen vessel and the space inside a jeweled vessel are both just the space-element — there is ultimately no differentiation between them — in the same way, O Son of the Gods, defilement is ultimately absolute non-arising. Purification too is ultimately absolute non-arising. <s>Saṃsāra</s> too is ultimately absolute non-arising. Even <s>nirvāṇa</s> is ultimately absolute non-arising. There is nothing here that is ultimately differentiated. Why? Because ultimately all <s>dharmas</s> are absolutely non-arising.' Thus this non-arising too is called ultimate because it accords with the ultimate, not in reality, because the ultimate in reality transcends all conceptual elaboration (<s>prapañca</s>). Therefore, whatever and however many characteristics of non-arising have been taught with reference to the ultimate — all those should be taken as of definitive meaning; those contrary to this are of provisional meaning. In the <s>Āryākṣayamatinirdeśasūtra</s>, the defining characteristics of provisional and definitive meaning have been taught. Thus —

body.text: ke sūtrāntā neyārthāḥ?
body.translated_text: Which sūtras are of provisional meaning (<s>neyārtha</s>)?

body.text: yāvad ye sūtrāntā saṃvṛtipratipattaye nirdiṣṭāsta ucyante neyārthāḥ yāvad ye sūtrāntāḥ paramārthapratipattaye nirdiṣṭāsta ucyante nītārthāḥ /
body.translated_text: Those sūtras that are taught for the understanding of conventional [truth] (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) are called of provisional meaning. Those sūtras that are taught for the understanding of the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>) are called of definitive meaning (<s>nītārtha</s>).

body.text: yāvad ye sūtrāntā nānāpadavyañcanāni nirdiśanti, ta ucyante neyārthāḥ, yāvad ye sutrāntā gambhīradurdarśadurjñeyāni nirdiśanti, ta ucyante nītārthāḥ /
body.translated_text: Those sūtras that teach with various words and expressions are called of provisional meaning. Those sūtras that teach what is profound, difficult to see, and difficult to understand are called of definitive meaning.

body.text: yāvad ye sūtrāntā ātmasattvajīvapuruṣapudgalamanujamānavakāravedakān anekarutairasvāmikān svāmina iva nirdiśanti, ta ucyante neyārthāḥ / yāvad ye sūtrāntāḥ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitānabhisaṃskārājānutpādābhāvanirātmaniḥsattvanirjīvaniḥpudgalāsvāmikavimokṣamukhā nirdiṣṭāsta ucyate nītārthāḥ - iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: Those sūtras that teach, using many expressions, ownerless [<s>dharmas</s>] as if they had an owner — [using terms like] self, being, life-force, person, individual, human, youth, doer, and experiencer — are called of provisional meaning. Those sūtras that teach the doors of liberation such as emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), signlessness (<s>animitta</s>), wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>), non-conditioning, non-arising, non-production, non-existence, selflessness, beinglessness, lifelessness, personlessness, and ownerlessness — are called of definitive meaning. Thus in detail.

body.text: sutrāntareṣu 'tāvadanutpādādinirdeśā abhiprāyāntareṇa nītārtha ityabhihitāḥ' - iti yaduktam, tadapi na samyak / ekaṃ hi sthitau ātmādinirdeśā api nītārthāḥ syuḥ / ataḥ paramārthābhidhāyako nītārthastadviparīto neyārtha ityavaboddhavyam / āryasarvabuddhaviṣayāvatārajñānālokālaṅkāre 'pyuktam - 'yo hi nītārthāḥ, sa paramārtha iti" / āryākṣayamatinirdeśasūtre ca anutpādādayo nītārthā uktāḥ / ataścaivamanutpādādaya eva paramārthā iti niyatam /
body.translated_text: The statement in certain sūtras that 'the teachings of non-arising etc. are of definitive meaning with a different intention' is also not correct. For on that basis, even the teachings of self etc. would be of definitive meaning. Therefore, one should understand that what expresses the ultimate is of definitive meaning, and what is contrary to that is of provisional meaning. In the <s>Āryasarvabuddhaviṣayāvatārajñānālokālaṅkāra</s> too it is stated: 'That which is of definitive meaning — that is the ultimate.' And in the <s>Āryākṣayamatinirdeśasūtra</s>, non-arising and others are stated to be of definitive meaning. Therefore, it is certain that non-arising and others alone are the ultimate.

body.text: yadyevaṃ tadā kathaṃ bhagavatā āryasandhinirmocanasūtre trividhasya svabhāvasya trividhāṃ niḥsvabhagavatāmabhipretya sarve dharmā niḥsvabhāvāḥ, proktā iti ced?
body.translated_text: If so, then how did the Blessed One state in the <s>Āryasaṃdhinirmocanasūtra</s> that 'all <s>dharmas</s> are essenceless,' having intended three types of essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatā</s>) of three types of nature (<s>svabhāva</s>)?

body.text: nāsti doṣaḥ / ye tāvat kecit saṃvṛtisvabhāvamapyapavadanti, atha cāsacchastraśravaṇābhiniśavaśād viparyastamatayaḥ saṃvṛtau asantamanṛtamapi nityādivasturupatayā samāropya yathā rūpapratibhāsaṃ tathaiva parigṛhṇanti, te āropāpavādāntadvayapatitatamatitayā antadvayarahite paramagambhīre paramārthanayasāgare nānupraviśanti / ataeva tāvad bhagavān 'anutpādādinirdeśaḥ paramārthādhikṛtaḥ' iti nirucya trividhaniḥsvabhāvatābhiprāyapratipādakamantadvayarahitaṃ0 madhyamapathaṃ madhaymapathaṃ prakāśayituṃ nītārthameva mataṃ pratiṣṭhāpitavān / na ca mādhyamikāstrividhaniḥsvabhāvatāvyavasthānaṃ nābhyugacchantīti, anyathā darśanādiviparītaṃ kathaṃ parihareyuriti /
body.translated_text: There is no fault. Some deny even the conventional nature (<s>saṃvṛtisvabhāva</s>), while others, due to hearing wrong teachings and through the force of habitual attachment, with mistaken minds, superimpose upon things that are conventionally non-existent and untrue the appearance of permanent entities and the like, and grasp them just as they appear as forms. They, having fallen into the two extremes of superimposition and denial, do not enter the supremely profound ocean of the ultimate approach that is free from both extremes. For this very reason, the Blessed One, having determined that 'the teaching of non-arising etc. pertains to the ultimate,' established his own definitive-meaning position by illuminating the middle path free from both extremes, which demonstrates the intent of the three types of essencelessness. And the <s>Mādhyamikas</s> do not fail to accept the framework of the three types of essencelessness; otherwise, how would they avoid the error of [wrong] views and such?

body.text: tatravicāritaṃ tāvad vastu yathāpratibhāsaṃ māyāvat pratītyasamutpannam, tacca paratantrasvabhāvam / tatrāpi saṃvṛtau māyāvat parapratyayena tasyotpādaḥ, na tu svayaṃbhāvaḥ / ata eva utpattiniḥsvabhāvatāyāṃ tad vyavasthāpyate / 'yaḥ prattyasamutpannaḥ sa svabhāvataḥ śūnya iti vidvāṃso nirdhārayanti / na hi svabhāvo nāma kṛtrimaḥ / abhūtvā bhāvaḥ bhūtvā cābhāvo 'pi tāvannasti, krameṇāpyekasya sadasattvāmyāṃ viruddhatvāt /
body.translated_text: When investigated, an entity that appears conventionally is, like an illusion, dependently arisen (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>), and that is the dependent nature (<s>paratantra-svabhāva</s>). Even in that [case], its arising in the conventional is, like an illusion, through other conditions, not through its own being. For this very reason, it is established in the essencelessness of arising (<s>utpatti-niḥsvabhāvatā</s>). 'What is dependently arisen — that, the wise determine, is empty of own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>).' For own-nature is by definition not produced. 'First non-existent and then existent, and [then] non-existent after being existent' — this is not [possible], because it is contradictory for one thing to be both existent and non-existent, even sequentially.

body.text: yaduta -
body.translated_text: As it is said —

children.translated_text: The arising of own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) from causes and conditions is not proper,
for an own-nature arisen from causes and conditions would be produced.

children.text: svabhāvaḥ kṛtako nāma bhaviṣyati punaḥ katham //
children.translated_text: How can there be something called a produced own-nature?

body.text:
akṛtrimaḥ svabhāvo hi nirapekṣaḥ paratra ca /
kutaḥ svabhāvasyābhāve parabhāvo bhaviṣyati /
body.translated_text: For own-nature is by definition unproduced and independent of other things. Where own-nature is absent, how can there be other-nature (<s>parabhāva</s>)?

body.text: bhagavatāpi āryānavataptanāgarājaparipṛcchāsūtre nirdiṣṭam -
body.translated_text: The Blessed One too has taught in the <s>Āryānavataptanāgarājaparipṛcchāsūtra</s> —

children.text: yaḥpratyayairjāyati sa hyajāto na tasya utpādu svabhāvato 'sti /
children.translated_text: What arises from conditions is indeed unborn; its arising does not exist by own-nature.

children.text: yaḥpratyayādhīnu sa śūnya ukto yaḥśūnyatāṃ jānati so 'pramattaḥ //
children.translated_text: What depends on conditions is called empty; one who knows emptiness is heedful.

body.text: āryasāgararājaparipṛcchasūtre 'pyuktam -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Āryasāgaranāgarājaparipṛcchāsūtra</s> too it is stated —

children.translated_text: What is dependently arisen is empty of own-nature;

children.text: yacca śūnyaṃ svabhāvena na hi taccasti kutracit //
children.translated_text: and what is empty of own-nature — that does not exist anywhere.

body.text: etadarthameva āryapitāputrasamāgamasūtre 'pi pratītyasamutpādapravṛttyā dharmadhātupravṛttirnidiṣṭā, yaduta - "tatra bhagavan, avidyā tu avidyātvenaivāsatī / tatkathamityucyeta tarhyevamavidyā tu svabhāvena virahitā / yasmin dharme nāsti svabhāvaḥ sa na tāvad vastu / yacca nāsti vastu tadapariniṣpannam, yadapariniṣpannaṃ tadanutpannamaniruddhaṃ ca / yadanutpannamaniruddhaṃ tad 'atītam' iti prajñaptuṃ naiva śakyate, na ca tadanāgataṃ pratyatpannamityapi vā prajñaptuṃ śakyate / yacca kālatraye 'pyanupapannaṃ tannāma lakṣaṇaṃ nimittaṃ prajñaptamiti vā na bhavati, yato hi tat sattvānāṃ grahaṇārthaṃ nāmamātrasaṃketamātravyavahāramātrasaṃvṛtimātrābhidheyamātraprajñaptimātrebhyo 'tiriktaṃ nāsti / avidyā tāvat paramārthato 'nupalabdhā / yaśca dharmaḥ paramārthato 'nupalabdhaḥ, na tat prajñaptaḥ, na vyavahāryaḥ, nābhidheyaśca / ato hi bhagavan yacca nāmamātraṃ saṃketamātraṃ na tattathyamiti" vistareṇābhihitam / ata eva paratantrasvabhāvo na tathyatve yujyate, anyathā māyādīnāmapi vastutvaprasaṅgaḥ, tānyapi pratyayasāpekṣatāyāṃ na santi bhinnāni / ata eva māyābhinnatvena paratantrasvabhāvastāvadutpattiniḥsvabhāvatāyāṃ vyavasthāpyate /
body.translated_text: For this very purpose, in the <s>Ārya-Pitāputrasamāgama-sūtra</s> (Noble Father-Son Meeting Sūtra) also, the operation of <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) is indicated through the operation of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), as follows: "In that regard, Blessed One, <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) is indeed non-existent as ignorance itself. How then can it be said? Thus, <s>avidyā</s> is devoid of <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature). That <s>dharma</s> in which there is no <s>svabhāva</s> is not even an entity. And what is not an entity is not fully accomplished. What is not fully accomplished is unborn and unceased. What is unborn and unceased — that cannot be designated as 'past,' nor can it be designated as 'future' or 'present.' And what is not established even in the three times — that is not a name, characteristic, sign, or designation, because that does not exist beyond the mere name, mere convention, mere conventional usage, mere <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional truth), mere denotation, mere conceptual designation for the apprehension of beings. <s>Avidyā</s> is ultimately unapprehended. And whatever <s>dharma</s> is ultimately unapprehended, that is not designated, not conventionally used, and not denotable. Therefore, Blessed One, whatever is mere name, mere convention — that is not real." This has been stated in detail. Therefore, the <s>paratantra-svabhāva</s> (dependent nature) is not justified as being real; otherwise there would be the absurd consequence that even illusions etc. would be real entities, since they too are not different in their dependence on conditions. Therefore, being non-different from illusion, the <s>paratantra-svabhāva</s> is first established as <s>utpatti-niḥsvabhāvatā</s> (essencelessness regarding arising).

body.text: āryasandhinirmocanasūtre cābhihitam - yathā māyākṛtaṃ tathaivotpattiniḥsvabhāvatāyāmupalakṣaṇīyam / māyādito 'bhinno yo hi paratantrasvabhāvaḥ sa eva nityānityādibhiḥ paramārthata upacaritaḥ sa eva ca parikalpitasvabhāvaḥ so 'pi yathā parikalpyate tathā lakṣaṇenāsiddhatvāllakṣaṇaniḥsvabhāvatāyāṃ vyavasthāpyate / sāpi niḥsvabhāvatā vastutaḥ paratantrasvabhāve eva sthitā / yato hi tasminneva [parikalpitaḥ] sa lakṣaṇairupacaryate / ata eva yathā anityādibhiḥ parikalpitāḥ sarve dharmāḥ paramārthato lakṣaṇaśūnyatvena anutpannāḥ, ata eva cāniruddhāḥ, ata eva ādiśāntāḥ, ata eva hi prakṛtiparinirvṛtāḥ āryasandhinirmocane 'pi yathoktam -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Sandhinirmocana-sūtra</s> (Noble Sūtra Unraveling the Intention) also it is stated: just as what is produced by illusion, so too it should be recognized as <s>utpatti-niḥsvabhāvatā</s>. The <s>paratantra-svabhāva</s> which is non-different from illusion and such — that very [nature] which is superimposed upon as permanent, impermanent, etc. ultimately — that very [nature] is the <s>parikalpita-svabhāva</s> (imagined nature). That too, because it is unestablished by the characteristics as it is imagined, is established as <s>lakṣaṇa-niḥsvabhāvatā</s> (essencelessness regarding characteristics). That essencelessness too is actually situated in the <s>paratantra-svabhāva</s> itself, because in that very [dependent nature] the imagined is superimposed with characteristics. Therefore, just as all <s>dharmas</s> imagined as permanent, impermanent, etc. are ultimately unborn due to being empty of characteristics, and therefore also unceased, and therefore primordially peaceful, and therefore naturally fully liberated — as also stated in the <s>Ārya-Sandhinirmocana</s>:

body.text: ye tāvat svalakṣaṇenāsantaste 'nutpannāḥ, ye hyanutpannāste 'niruddhāḥ, ye cāniruddhāsta ādiśāntā, ādiśāntā, ye hyādiśāntāste prakṛtiparinirvṛtā iti /
body.translated_text: "Those that do not exist by their own characteristics are unborn; those that are unborn are unceased; those that are unceased are primordially peaceful; those that are primordially peaceful are naturally fully liberated (<s>prakṛti-parinirvṛta</s>)."

body.text: ata evāhaṃ lakṣaṇaniḥsvabhavātābhisandhāya 'sarve dharmā anutpannāḥ' iti yadupadiśāmi, tadapi yathāśabdamarthaparikalpanaṃ nirākaroti / paratantrasvabhāvaśca yathā saṃvṛtau hyuktastathā parikalpitātmanā virahitatvena prasidhya saṃvṛtisvabhāvasyānapavādamapi nirdiśati, na tu paramārthatvena / alakṣaṇasvabhāvastu na kaścana yujyate / yathoktamḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore, intending <s>lakṣaṇa-niḥsvabhāvatā</s>, when I teach that 'all <s>dharmas</s> are unborn,' that too refutes the literal conceptual construction of meaning. And the <s>paratantra-svabhāva</s>, as stated in the conventional level, being well-known as devoid of the imagined self, also indicates the non-negation of the conventional nature, but not as ultimate. However, a nature without any characteristics is not justified. As stated:

body.text: alakṣaṇo na kaścicca bhāvaḥ saṃvidyate kvacit /
body.translated_text: "No entity exists anywhere that is without characteristics."

body.text: sarve dharmāḥ paramārthataḥ sadā bhāvaniḥsvabhāvatāyāmeva pratiṣṭhitā bhavanti / ayameva tāvat pariniṣpatraḥ svabhāvaḥ, nityaṃ tasyānāropitatvena sthitatvāt / sa hi pramāṇaiḥ samyugupapatrannasvabhāvatayā paramārtha ityucyate, niḥsvabhāvatāprabhāvitātvācca niḥsvabhāvo 'pi / ato 'yaṃ [pariniṣpannaḥ] paramārthaniḥsvābhāva iti /
body.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> ultimately abide always in <s>bhāva-niḥsvabhāvatā</s> (essencelessness regarding existence) alone. This indeed is the <s>pariniṣpanna-svabhāva</s> (perfected nature), because it always abides as that which is never superimposed upon. For it is called <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate reality) because its essencelessness is well established by the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge), and also 'essenceless' because it is influenced by essencelessness. Therefore, this [perfected nature] is <s>paramārtha-niḥsvabhāva</s> (essenceless regarding the ultimate).

body.text: āryasandhinirmocane 'pyuktam -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Sandhinirmocana</s> also it is stated:

body.text: "sa ca paramārtho 'pi dharmaniḥsvabhāvatāprabhāvito 'pītyataḥ paramārthaniḥsvabhāvaḥ" iti /
body.translated_text: "That <s>paramārtha</s> too is called <s>paramārtha-niḥsvabhāva</s> because it is influenced by <s>dharma-niḥsvabhāvatā</s> (essencelessness of <s>dharmas</s>)."

body.text: yannidānamanena niḥsvabhāvena sarve niḥsvabhāvāḥ, tannidānamanutpādādideśanā nītarthā / paramārthābhiprāyanirdeśāt sa na tāvad darśanādiviruddhaḥ, na ca yathāśabdaṃ parikalpitaśca / ata eva nābhiprāyanirdeśo 'pi nītārthaviruddhaḥ, parigrahītavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Because all [<s>dharmas</s>] are essenceless through this essencelessness — on that basis, the teaching of non-arising etc. is of definitive meaning (<s>nītārtha</s>). Because it is a teaching from the standpoint of the ultimate, it does not contradict perception etc., nor should it be imagined literally. Therefore, the teaching from the standpoint is also not contradictory to the definitive meaning; it should be accepted.

body.text: ataśca abhiprāyanirdeśo 'pi na nītārthaviruddho bhavatīti / phalataḥ anutpādideśanāṃ nītārthāṃ sādhayituṃ darśanādivirodhaṃ parihartuṃ yathāśabdaparikalpanaṃ ca nirākartum āryasandhinirmocane tāvadabhihitam -
body.translated_text: And therefore the teaching from the standpoint is also not contradictory to the definitive meaning. In effect, to establish the teaching of non-arising etc. as definitive, to remove the contradiction with perception etc., and to refute literal conceptual construction, it is stated thus in the <s>Ārya-Sandhinirmocana</s>:

body.text: api ca, paramārthasamudgat, paramārthaniḥsvabhāvaṃ dharmanairātmaprabhāvitamityabhipretya mayā sarve dharmā anutpannāḥ sarve dharmā aniruddhāḥ, ādiśāntāḥ, prakṛtiparinivṛttāśva deśitāḥ /
body.translated_text: "Moreover, O <s>Paramārthasamudgata</s>, intending <s>paramārtha-niḥsvabhāva</s>, influenced by <s>dharma-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>), I have taught that all <s>dharmas</s> are unborn, all <s>dharmas</s> are unceased, primordially peaceful, and naturally fully liberated."

body.text: yadyevaṃ mahāśraddadhāsūtre "prayogajaṃ svabhāvamabhipretya yanmayā 'sarve dharmā asantaḥ' iti yaduktaṃ tatra yathāśabdamabhiniviśca saṃkleśavyavadānadharmāṇāmapyabhāvamātramabhiniviśca asannimittagrahaṇād asaddarśanaṃ tad bhavedityato nimittadarśanaṃ taducyate / evaṃ vistareṇa yadabhihitaṃ tatkathaṃ grāhyamiti?
body.translated_text: If this is so, then [regarding the passage] in the <s>Mahāśraddadhā-sūtra</s>: 'Intending the produced nature (<s>prayogaja-svabhāva</s>), what I have said — "all <s>dharmas</s> are non-existent" — if one clings literally to that, and clings to the mere non-existence of the <s>dharmas</s> of defilement and purification also, then from grasping the sign of non-existence, there would be the view of non-existence. Therefore, the view of signs is to be stated.' Thus, what has been extensively stated — how should that be understood?

body.text: ayamapi yathoktaḥ paratantrasvabhāva eva, yo hi saṃvṛtau hetupratyayabalasambhūtatvena māyāvannisvabhāvatvena ca 'prayogajaḥ' ityuktaḥ /
body.translated_text: This too is the very <s>paratantra-svabhāva</s> (dependent nature) as described, which is called 'produced' (<s>prayogaja</s>) because in the conventional level it arises through the power of causes and conditions, being essenceless like an illusion.

body.text: prajñāpāramitāyāmapyuktam -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) also it is stated:

body.text: "prayogajaḥ svabhāvastāvadasat pratītyasamunpannatvād" iti /
body.translated_text: "The produced nature is indeed non-existent, because it is dependently arisen."

body.text: etadarśaṃ yo hi parikalpitasvabhāva uktaḥ so 'pyāgantuka eva kalpanābhinirhatatvāt / ata eva saḥ [paratantraḥ] prayogaja ityuktaḥ / svabhāvo 'yaṃ dvidhāpi paramārthato naiva yujyate / ataḥ sarve dharmāḥ svabhāvenānena paramārthato niḥ svabhāvāḥ / na hyabhāvāt saṃvṛtisvabhavo bhavati / yadi sa tāvadasat svāttadā saṃkleśavyadānadharmā naiva vyavasthāpayituṃ śakyeran, yato hi tatprabhāvitā hi te, na tu paramārthena [prabhāvitāḥ] / evaṃ hi sūtrānteṣvapi pratipāditamiti / ato ye paramārthābhiprāyaṃ naiva jānanti, te pūrvasvabhāvamapi vasturupeṇa parigṛhya paścāttasyāpyabhāvaṃ matvā anutpannādideśanānāṃ śabdaśo 'rthābhiniveśaṃ kurvanti / te cābhāvādinimittagrahaṇena nimittādidṛṣṭayo bhavanti / atastanniṣedhāyaiva etaduktam, na tu mādhyamikebhya etaduktamiti / te tu tathatāṃ sarvanimittagrāhapratipakṣāṃ pracakṣate / atasteṣvabhāvādinimittagrāho naiva sambhavati / tathā hiḥ
body.translated_text: That which is of this nature — what is called the <s>parikalpita-svabhāva</s> (imagined nature) is also indeed adventitious, because it is produced by conceptual construction. Therefore that [dependent nature] is called 'produced.' This nature, in both [its aspects], is not justified ultimately. Therefore, all <s>dharmas</s> by this nature are ultimately essenceless. For the conventional nature does not come from non-existence. If that were indeed non-existent, then the <s>dharmas</s> of defilement and purification could not be established at all, because they are influenced by that [conventional nature], not by the ultimate. Thus it has been demonstrated also in the <s>sūtrāntas</s>. Therefore, those who do not understand the standpoint of the ultimate, having grasped even the former nature as a real entity, then thinking it too is non-existent, cling literally to the meaning of the teachings of non-arising etc. And they, through grasping the sign of non-existence, become holders of views of signs and such. Therefore, this is said precisely to refute them, not against the <s>Mādhyamikas</s>. For they proclaim <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) as the antidote to all grasping of signs. Therefore, the grasping of signs such as non-existence is indeed impossible for them. As indeed:

children.translated_text: "Not dependent on another, peaceful, not elaborated by conceptual proliferations,
Free from conceptual construction, without diversity — this is the characteristic of reality (<s>tattva</s>)."
Furthermore, "'It exists' is the eternalist grasp; 'It does not exist' is the nihilistic view;
Therefore the wise one should not resort to existence or non-existence."

body.text: yeṣu bhāvābhāvādayo nimittagrāhā bhavanti, teṣu naiva sambhavati tattvadarśanāvakāśo 'pi, tathā coktam -
body.translated_text: For those in whom there are graspings of signs such as existence and non-existence, there is no opportunity even for the seeing of reality. As it is stated:

children.text: svabhāvaṃ parabhāvaṃ ca bhāvaṃ cābhāvameva ca /
children.translated_text: "Those who see <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature) and <s>parabhāva</s> (other-nature), and existence and non-existence —

children.text: ye paśyanti na paśyanti te tattvaṃ buddhaśāsane //
children.translated_text: They do not see the truth (<s>tattva</s>) in the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s>."

body.text: yo 'yaṃ bhāvābhāvābhiniveśaḥ, sa tāvad bhāvābhiniveśapūrvaka iti sūtreṣu pratipāditam / tathā hi laṅkavatārasūtre proktam -
body.translated_text: This clinging to existence and non-existence is preceded by the clinging to existence — thus it is demonstrated in the <s>sūtras</s>. As indeed it is stated in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra</s>:

children.translated_text: "Non-existence is preceded by [the view of] existence; existence is preceded by [the view of] non-existence;

children.text: ato nāsti na gantavyamastitvaṃ na ca kalpayet //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should not go to non-existence, nor should one construct existence."

body.text: ato ye khalu bhāvābhiniveśaparaśāste tāvat paratantraṃ sanimittaṃ paśyanti / ye tu vyapagatabhāvagrāhāste tathā na kurvanti, kutrāpyanavasthitatvāt / tathā hyuktam -
body.translated_text: Therefore, those who are devoted to clinging to existence see the dependent [nature] as having signs. But those who have abandoned the grasping of existence do not do so, because they are not established anywhere. As indeed it is stated:

children.translated_text: "Those who desire in reality the accomplishment of entities that have been resorted to —

children.text: tatra nityādayo doṣāḥ sambhavanti na vā katham //
children.translated_text: For them, faults of permanence etc. arise — or how could they not?
But for entities that have been resorted to, whether they are non-existent or existent —
Those who do not desire [to determine this], like the moon in water — seeing [thus], they are not deceived.

body.text:
rāgadveṣodbhavastīvraduṣṭadṛṣṭaparigrahaḥ
vivādāstatsamutthāśca bhāvābhyupagame sati //
body.translated_text: The holding of fierce, evil views arising from attachment and aversion, and disputes arising therefrom — [all arise] when entities are accepted."

body.text: ato ye 'nutpādādideśanāsu śabdaśo 'bhiniviśante, tān pratiṣeddhuṃ nimittādidṛṣṭayo vigarhaṇīyāḥ / mādhyamikābhidhāstu anutpādādideśanāsu nābhiniviśante,paramārthato 'nutpādādīnāmabhyupagamāt saṃvṛtyotpādādīnāmapi vyāharaṇāt / tathā hi -
body.translated_text: Therefore, to refute those who cling literally to the teachings of non-arising etc., the views of signs and such are to be censured. But the <s>Mādhyamika</s> position does not cling to the teachings of non-arising etc., because of accepting non-arising etc. ultimately and also speaking of arising etc. conventionally. As indeed:

children.translated_text: "At the commencement of investigating reality, let everything be declared to exist;
After knowing the meanings, truly, in [the stage of] dispassion, distinctions are examined later.
Having entered merely into what is heard, without understanding the definitive meaning,

children.text: ye puṇyāni na kurvanti narāste kutsitā hatāḥ //
children.translated_text: Those people who do not perform meritorious deeds — they are condemned and destroyed.
Actions endowed with fruits and the destinies have been well taught;
Knowledge of their true nature — non-arising too has been taught.
Just as 'mine' and 'I' have been proclaimed by the Victorious Ones as required by the task,
So too the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and <s>dhātus</s> (elements) have been proclaimed as required by the task."

body.text: yadyevaṃ cet? āryalaṅkāvatārasūtre -
body.translated_text: If this is so, then [regarding the passage] in the <s>Ārya-Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra</s>:

children.translated_text: "The imagined entity does not exist, but the dependent does exist;
The one who constructs superimposition and denial perishes."

body.text: yaddhi proktaṃ tatkathamiti cintāyāmatrāpi yathā kathitasya parikalpitasvabhāvasya samāropo bhavati, tasya parihārārthaṃ "nāsti vaikalpito bhāvaḥ" ityuktam / yathoktaḥ paratantrasvabhāvāstu saṃvṛtiniṣedhakaraṇāt parāyattavṛtitayā 'san' ityevamuktaḥ / ucyamānamidaṃ dvayaṃ ye antadvayarupeṇa parikalpiyanti, te naiva madhyamamārge pravṛttā bhaviṣyanti, prapātasthānasthitaskandhasadṛśatvāt / ataḥ - "samāropāpavādaṃ hi vikalpanto vinaśyati" ityuktam / ata eva ca -
body.translated_text: What has been stated there — regarding this inquiry too: just as there is superimposition of the stated imagined nature, for its removal it is said 'the imagined entity does not exist.' The stated <s>paratantra-svabhāva</s>, because of not negating the conventional, being dependent on others, is said to be 'existent.' This duality being stated — those who construct it in the form of the two extremes will never enter upon the middle path, because they are like one standing on the edge of a precipice with a burden on one's shoulder. Therefore: 'The one who constructs superimposition and denial perishes.' And therefore also:

children.translated_text: "All <s>dharmas</s> are imagined by <s>svabhāva</s>, [yet] the unknowing [think otherwise];
Depending on the dependent [nature], conceptual construction wanders among humans."

body.text: yaduktaṃ tenāpi tannirākaraṇaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: What has been stated by that — by that [statement] a refutation is made.

body.text: anenāpi coktayoḥ samāropāpavādāntayoḥ nirākaraṇaṃ kriyate / tathā hiyathā vikalpyate tathā paramārthataḥ paratantrasyānutpannatvāt parikalpitātmanā anutpanna eva / tadanena samāropāntasvāvannirākriyate / saṃvṛtyā paratantratayā samutpannatvāt tadāśritā anye vikalpā nirmāṇanirmitasadṛśā samutpadyante / ata eva -
body.translated_text: By this too, a refutation of the stated extremes of superimposition and denial is made. For just as it is imagined, the dependent, being ultimately unborn, is indeed unborn as its imagined self. By this, the extreme of superimposition is refuted. Conventionally, because of arising through dependent [conditions], other conceptual constructions dependent on that arise, similar to what is created by a magical creation. Therefore:

body.text: paratantraṃ samāśritya vikalpo bhramate nṛṇām / ityevamuktaṃ / anena tāvadapavādānto nirākriyate, saṃvṛtyotpādasyānapavādāt / atastatra tatra yā paratantrasvabhāvāstitatvadeśanā yāśca bhāvotpatyādideśanāstāḥ sarvāḥ deśanāḥ bālapṛthagjanānāṃ bhayahetuparivarjanārthaṃ saṃvṛtyotpādāśayena abhiprāyataḥ pravṛttā ityavagamāya, na tu paramārthataḥ / tanniṣedhastu sūtre kṛtaḥ / yathoktaṃ laṅkāvatārasūtre -
body.translated_text: "Depending on the dependent [nature], conceptual construction wanders among humans" — thus it is stated. By this, the extreme of denial is refuted, because conventional arising is not negated. Therefore, wherever there is the teaching of the existence of the <s>paratantra-svabhāva</s> and wherever there are the teachings of the arising of entities etc. — all those teachings should be understood as proceeding from the intention based on conventional arising, for the purpose of removing the cause of fear for childish ordinary beings, and not from the ultimate. The negation of that, however, has been made in the <s>sūtras</s>. As stated in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra</s>:

children.text: buddhayā vivecyamānaṃ hi na tantraṃ nāpi kalpitam /
children.translated_text: "When examined by wisdom, there is neither the dependent nor the imagined;

children.text: niṣpanno nāsti vai bhāvaḥ kathaṃ buddhayā prakalpyate //
children.translated_text: The perfected entity does not exist indeed — how is it constructed by wisdom?

children.text: na svabhāvo na vijñaptirna vastu na ca ālayaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no own-nature, no consciousness, no entity, and no <s>ālaya</s> (storehouse consciousness);
These are imagined by the childish, who are in the power of bad reasoning."

body.text: āryadharmasaṅgītau cāpyuktam -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Dharmasaṅgīti</s> (Noble Assembly of Dharmas) also it is stated:

body.text: kulaputra, loko 'yaṃ jātinirādhayoradhyavasāyena tiṣṭhati, ato mahākaruṇāmayena tathāgatena lokabhayaviṣayaparivarjanārthaṃ vyavahāravaśena tasya utpattinirodhau bhavata ityupadiṣṭam / kulaputra, nātra kaścid dharma utpadyata iti /
body.translated_text: "O son of the family, this world abides through the conviction of arising and cessation. Therefore, out of great compassion, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, for the purpose of removing the domain of worldly fear, has taught by the force of convention that there is arising and cessation for that [world]. O son of the family, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever arises here."

body.text: āryaprajñāpāramitāsūtre 'pi -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Prajñāpāramitā-sūtra</s> (Noble Perfection of Wisdom Sūtra) also:

body.text: "āyuṣman śāradvatīputra, evaṃ rūpaṃ svabhāvena śūnyam, yacca svabhāvena śūnyaṃ tannotpadyate, na ca niradhyate / yasya natpattinirādhau tannānyathā bhavatīti / evaṃ yāvad vedanāto vijñānaparyantam" - iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: "Venerable <s>Śāradvatīputra</s>, thus form is empty by <s>svabhāva</s>. And what is empty by <s>svabhāva</s> does not arise, nor does it cease. That which has no arising and no cessation — that does not become otherwise. Thus [it continues] in detail from feeling up to consciousness."

body.text: nātra parikalpitasya svabhāvo yuktataraḥ, āgantukatvād bhāvabahirbhūtatvācca tasya, evaṃ śabdārtho 'pi nopapadyate / yadyapi rupādayaḥ paramārthato 'nutpannastathāpi bālapṛthagjanaiste utpādādisvabhāve parikalpyante / ityevaṃ tairyadi tatsvabhāve parikalpitatvāt svabhāvaśabdenocyante, tadā na doṣaḥ, iṣṭārthāviruddhatvāt / sūtrāntare 'pi -
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>svabhāva</s> of the imagined is not more justified, because of its being adventitious and external to [true] existence; thus the meaning of the word [<s>svabhāva</s>] also does not apply. Although forms etc. are ultimately unborn, nevertheless childish ordinary beings imagine them as having the nature of arising etc. Thus, if they are called by the word '<s>svabhāva</s>' because their nature is imagined, then there is no fault, because it does not contradict the intended meaning. In another <s>sūtra</s> also:

body.text: "kulaputra , yo bodhisattvaḥ dharmān ayoniśo manasikṛtya śabdaśaḥ pravicinoti, sa mahāyānaśraddhāyatano na bhavati / yaśca aśabdaśo 'bhisandhyarthaṃ yoniśo manasikaroti, sa mahāyānaśraddhāyatano bhavati" / yaduktaṃ tattu ye paramārthābhiprāyānabhijñāḥ saṃvṛtisvabhāvamapyapavadante te 'yoniśo dharmān pravicinvantītihetormahāyānaśraddhāyatanā na bhavantītyatastanniṣedhārthamidamityuktam /
body.translated_text: "O son of good family, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who, having attended to <s>dharmas</s> unsystematically, investigates them merely by their words, does not become a vessel of faith in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. But one who, going beyond words, attends systematically to the intended meaning, becomes a vessel of faith in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>." What was stated there — that those who, not knowing the intention of the ultimate, negate even the conventional nature, are 'investigating <s>dharmas</s> unsystematically' and therefore do not become vessels of faith in the <s>Mah��yāna</s> — was stated for the purpose of refuting that [error].

body.text: nikhileṣvapi sūtreṣu śabdaśo 'rthābhiniveśapariharāya abhipretārthāvabodhāya ca samyag yatnotpādārthaṃ sarveṣu cādhimaktyupādārthamevābhihitam, na tu mādhyamikamataniṣedhārtham, na hi mādhyamikāḥ śabdaśo 'rthaṃ parikalpayantīti pūrvamevoktatvāt / āryaratnameghasūtre 'pyuktam, yathā -
body.translated_text: In all <s>sūtras</s> without exception, [such teachings] are stated for the purpose of removing attachment to meanings merely by words, for the purpose of understanding the intended meaning, for the purpose of generating proper effort, and for the purpose of producing aspiration in all — but not for the purpose of refuting the <s>Mādhyamika</s> view. For the <s>Mādhyamikas</s> do not construct meanings merely by words, as has been stated previously. In the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha-sūtra</s> too it is stated, as follows —

body.text: "kathamiva bodhisattvaḥ paramārthanipuṇo na bhavati? kulaputra, bodhisattvaḥ samyak prajñayā rūpapratyavekṣaṇaṃ yāvd vijñānapratyavekṣaṇaṃ pratyavekṣate / yadā sa rūpaṃ pratyavekṣate, tadā na rupotpādamupalabhate, na samudayamupalabhate, na ca nirodhamupalabhate yāvad vijñānaparyantaṃ yathāvadutpādaṃ nopalabhate, yato hi so 'pi tāvad [anupalambhaḥ] paramārthato 'nutpādapravṛttayā prajayā bhavati, na tu sāṃvyāvahārikasvabhāvena" ityevaṃ nirdiṣṭam /
body.translated_text: "How does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> become skilled in the ultimate? O son of good family, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> examines with correct <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) the examination of <s>rūpa</s> (form) up to the examination of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). When he examines <s>rūpa</s>, then he does not apprehend the arising of <s>rūpa</s>, does not apprehend its origination, and does not apprehend its cessation — up to <s>vijñāna</s>, he does not apprehend arising as it is. For that non-apprehension too is [produced] by <s>prajñā</s> operating through non-arising in the ultimate sense, but not through the conventional nature" — thus it is taught.

body.text: āryalaṅkāvatāre 'pi -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Laṅkāvatāra</s> too —

body.text: sarvaṃ vidyati saṃvṛtyāṃ paramārthe na vidyate / dharmāṇāṃ niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ paramārthe 'pi dṛśyate // ityuktam / ye tāvadanutpādādinirdeśān 'sarve dharmāḥ paramārthata utpadyante saṃvṛtisvabhābhāvataśca notpadyante' ityetasmin mate sthāpayanti, te sarve āryaratnameghādinirdiṣṭaiḥ samastavacanairvirudhyante, vipratipannatvāt teṣām / teṣu [sūtreṣu] tu rupādayaḥ sarve [dharmāḥ] paramārthato 'nutpannāḥ, saṃvṛtitaścotpannā iti nirdiṣṭāḥ satyadvayanirdeśādiṣu tāvad - devaputra, sarve dharmāḥ śāntāḥ, paramārthato 'nutpannatvād
body.translated_text: "Everything exists in the conventional; in the ultimate, nothing exists. The non-own-nature of <s>dharmas</s> is seen even in the ultimate." Thus it is stated. Now, those who, based on teachings of non-arising and the like, establish the position that 'all <s>dharmas</s> arise in the ultimate sense but do not arise through the conventional nature' — they all contradict the statements taught in the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s> and other [sūtras], since they are confused. In those [sūtras], <s>rūpa</s> and all other [dharmas] are taught as unarisen in the ultimate, but arisen conventionally. In the teaching of the two truths and the like — 'O son of the gods, all <s>dharmas</s> are peaceful, because they are unarisen in the ultimate' —

body.text: ityevamādikaṃ yaduktaṃ tenāpi [saha] virudhyante / punaśca āryalaṅkāvatare 'bhihitam -
body.translated_text: what was stated in this manner — they contradict that too. Furthermore, in the <s>Ārya-Laṅkāvatāra</s> it is stated —

children.text: bhāvā vidyanti saṃvṛtyā paramārthe na bhāvakāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Entities exist conventionally; in the ultimate, there are no entities.
The delusion regarding things without own-nature — that truth would be the conventional."

body.text: āryaprajñāpāramitāyāmapi -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Prajñāpāramitā</s> too —

body.text: "subhūte, viparyayamatiricya bālapṛthagjanāḥ kutrāvatiṣṭhante? karmārbhisaṃskāravastu tāvat keśāgratulyamapi na vidyate"
body.translated_text: "O <s>Subhūti</s>, beyond inversion, where do childish ordinary beings abide? There does not exist even as much as the tip of a hair of the substance of actions and <s>abhisaṃskāras</s> (formations)" —

body.text: ityādikā yā deśānā, tayāpi virudhyante, vastutaḥ ātmano 'tisūkṣmasvabhāvasyāpi niṣiddhatvāt / yadi viparyayasyāpratiṣedhād asti viparyayaṃ vastu, tatraiva tathā proktatvāditi cet? tathā hiḥ
body.translated_text: they contradict this teaching too, since even the extremely subtle nature of the self is negated in reality. If, because inversion is not negated, there exists an inverted thing — since it is spoken of thus in that very [context] — [they might say]. For indeed:

body.text: niḥsvabhāveṣu yā bhrantistatsatyaṃ saṃvṛtirbhavet / iti / tadapi naivopapadyate / viparyastaṃ vastu yadi vidyeta, tadā atisūkṣmabhāvasvabhāvaniṣedhavacanaṃ kathaṃ nāmopapadyeta /
body.translated_text: "The delusion regarding things without own-nature — that truth would be the conventional." But even that is not tenable. If an inverted thing existed, how could the statement negating even the extremely subtle nature of entities be justified?

body.text: asatīṣvapi samastabhāvavāsanāsu bālapṛthagjanāḥ asadviparyayopakalpitānāṃ bhāvasvabhāvānāmabhiniveśena kamāṇyabhisaṃskurvantīti yadaivaṃ sūtrārtho vivecyeta tadā evaṃvidhena tāvad vivecanena [bhavadabhyupagataṃ] abhyupagantuṃ śakyeta /
body.translated_text: Even when all dispositions of entities are non-existent, childish ordinary beings, through attachment to the entity-natures constructed by unreal inversion, produce actions — if the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> is analyzed thus, then by such analysis, [your objection would be refuted].

body.text: āryasamādhirājasūtre -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Samādhirāja-sūtra</s> —

children.text: svabhāvaśūnyāḥ sada sarvadharmāḥ vastuṃ vibhāventi jinānaputrāḥ /
children.translated_text: "All <s>dharmas</s> are always empty of own-nature; the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors) discern the real.

children.text: sarveṇa sarvaṃ bhavasarvaśūnyaṃ prādeśikī śūnyatā tīrthikānām //
children.translated_text: Everything in existence is empty of everything; the emptiness of the non-Buddhists is partial."

body.text: iti yaduktam tadapi abhyuddhartuṃ śakyate / anyatrāpi sūtreṣu tāvad -
body.translated_text: What is stated there can also be cited [in support]. In other <s>sūtras</s> too —

children.translated_text: "The three realms of existence are merely designation; no entity exists by its own nature.
Logicians will construct the status of entities through designation alone."

body.text: iti yaducyate tadapyuddhariṣyate / viparyayādayo hi vastutvena tāvannaiva yaujyante /
body.translated_text: What is stated there will also be cited. For inversions and the like are simply not justified as real entities.

body.text: ityevaṃ bhavadbhiścittacaittātmakasya traidhātukasya yadasamyaktvaṃ parikalpyate tadapi asamyagākāropagrahaṇāvabhāsatvena viparyayāditayā procyate / mithyāsvabhāvenopagrahaṇād yastasyātmatvenāvabhāsaḥ sa kathaṃ samyag bhāva iti bhavet, tattvānyatvayoḥ parasparahārasthitalakṣaṇatvāt / tattvasya tāvadanyātmakatvaṃ hi viruddham /
body.translated_text: Thus, what you impute as the incorrectness of the three realms, which consist of mind (<s>citta</s>) and mental factors (<s>caitta</s>) — that too is called 'inversion' and the like because it appears as the apprehension of incorrect forms. Due to the apprehension with a false nature, whatever appearance of that as a self —

body.text: yadyevaṃ nāsti tadā sāṃkhyādiparikalpiteṣu pradhānādivikāreṣu bhavatāṃ ko dveṣaḥ svād, bhavadbhisteṣāmanabhyupagamāt / ata evaḥ kasya syādanyathābhāvaḥ svabhāvo yadi vidyate /
body.translated_text: if it is not so, then what aversion would you have toward the transformations of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and the like constructed by the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> and others? Since you do not accept those [either]. Hence: "If own-nature exists, of what would there be change?"

body.text: ityevamuktam / āryasatyadvayanirdeśe 'piḥ
body.translated_text: Thus it is said. In the <s>Ārya-Satyadvaya-nirdeśa</s> too:

body.text: "devaputra, yathā ātmā, nānti paramārthata ātmā, tathaiva devaputra, kleśā api,paramārthato na santi kleśāḥ / devaputra, yadyātmā paramārthatastattvaṃ svāttadā devaputra, anenaiva hetunā kleśā api paramārthatastattvāni syuḥ /"
body.translated_text: "O son of the gods, just as the self — in the ultimate, there is no self — so too, O son of the gods, the afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) — in the ultimate, there are no afflictions. O son of the gods, if the self were reality in the ultimate, then, O son of the gods, by this very reasoning, the afflictions too would be real in the ultimate" —

body.text: ityevaṃ kathitam / anena tāvad ātmādīnāṃ mithyākāropagrahaṇena pravṛttatvād ātmādivat kleśā api sarve mithyākāropagrahaṇena pravṛttatvād ātmādivat kleśā api sarve mithyāsvabhāvā evetyevaṃ tāvannirdiśyate /
body.translated_text: thus it is stated. By this, it is first taught that, since the self and the like have arisen through the apprehension of false forms, the afflictions too — just like the self and the like — all have a false nature, since they have arisen through the apprehension of false forms.

body.text: ityevaṃ traidhātukāḥ khalu cittacaitasikā mithyākāragraharaṇapravṛttatvāt svākāra iva tadabhinnatvācca mithyāsvabhāvā eveti nirdiṣṭāḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, the mind and mental factors of the three realms — since they operate through the apprehension of false forms, and since their own forms are not different from that [false apprehension] — are taught as being of false nature only.

body.text: bodhisattvebhyustu viśeṣataḥ kliṣṭatvāt sarvaparikalpānāṃ te mithyā evātaḥ "mithyā sarvavikalpāḥ" ityevaṃ tāvat pratipāditam /
body.translated_text: For <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in particular, since all constructions are afflicted, they are simply false. Therefore, "all conceptualizations are false" — thus it is first taught.

body.text: yadi nāsti paramārthato vastunāṃ svakīyaḥ kaścana svabhāvastadā -
body.translated_text: If there is no own nature whatsoever belonging to entities in the ultimate, then —

children.text: na hyātmā vidyate skandhe skandhāścaiva hi nātmani /
children.translated_text: "The self does not exist in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), nor indeed are the <s>skandhas</s> in the self.

children.text: na te yathā vikalpyante na ca te vai na santi ca //
children.translated_text: They are not as they are conceptualized, nor is it that they simply do not exist."

body.text: yadi yaduktaṃ tad yadyevamuddhriyate yadanena nioṣedhamukhena svandhādīnāṃ tāvat sattaiva nirdiśyata iti cet? tanna pramāṇayogyamiti / yato hyatra "na te yathā vikalpyante" iti yaduktaṃ tena sattayā niṣedho vidhīyate / "na ca vai na santi ca" ityamunā ca ye yathā saṃvṛtavavabhāsante, te tathaiva saditi nirdiśyante / phalataśca tairthikaparikalpitasyātmanaḥ saṃvṛttavapyasattvam / skandhādīnāṃ tāvad vyavahāre sattvam, na tu tathatāyāmiti vispaṣṭamādiṣṭam / yadyevaṃ na bhavettadaikasminnasattvabhidhāya punaḥ sattvena nirdeśaḥ kathaṃ sambadhyeta / āryabrahnaparivartasūtre coktaṃ yaduta -
body.translated_text: If what was stated is cited thus — [and the opponent says:] 'By this negation, the very existence of the <s>skandhas</s> and the like is being taught' — that is not acceptable as valid. For what is stated here, "they are not as they are conceptualized," by that, not through existence —

children.translated_text: "By whom the arising and non-arising of the <s>skandha</s> is known,

children.text: samudācarati talloke na ca loke sthitaśca saḥ //
children.translated_text: he operates in the world, yet he is not established in the world."

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: āryaratnameghe 'pi na skandhāḥ paramārthataḥ santi, saṃvṛtyaiva te santīti apaṣṭatayā nirdiṣṭamḥ
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha</s> too, it is clearly taught that the <s>skandhas</s> do not exist in the ultimate, but exist only conventionally:

body.text: "kulaputra, daśadharmasamanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ saṃvṛtisatye kuśalo bhavati, ke ca daśeti? tadyathā - rūpaprajñaptiṃ karoti, na ca paramārthato rūpamupalabhate, nābhiniveśaṃ karoti / vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānanyapi tadvaditi vistaraḥ /"
body.translated_text: "O son of good family, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> endowed with ten <s>dharmas</s> becomes skilled in conventional truth. What are the ten? Namely — he designates <s>rūpa</s> (form), but does not apprehend <s>rūpa</s> in the ultimate, and does not attach to it. Likewise <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) —

body.text: āryaratnākare 'piḥ
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Ratnākara</s> too:

body.text: "sūryadatta, evamasti, yathā vyomni citrāṅkanaṃ na bhavati, na bhaviṣyati, yato hi tadabhūtamaniruddhamanāgamamanirgamamanutpannamacyumanabhiniṣpannam anirvacanīyatvād vyavahāramātraṃ saṃvṛtimātraṃ bhavati / sūryadatta, tathaiva rupādivijñānaparyantaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati, ita ārabhya...... saṃvṛtimātraṃ bhavati" ityetatparyantaṃ yad vistareṇābhihitaṃ tadarthasambaddhaṃ karaṇīyamiti /
body.translated_text: "O <s>Sūryadatta</s>, it is thus: just as in the sky there is no painting, there was not, and there will not be — for it is unreal, unceased, un-come, un-gone, unarisen, unfallen, unaccomplished, inexpressible — a mere convention, a mere designation —

body.text: nanu mahāparamārthaśūnyatāyāṃ 'asti karma, asti vipākaḥ kartā tu nopalabhyate' yadevamuktaṃ tattāvad etadviruddhaṃ syāt, yato hi yadā karmādayaḥ paramārthataḥ santi, tadā na bhavanti sarve dharmā niḥsvabhāvāḥ, yadi saṃvṛtitaste santi tadā karturapi saṃvṛtitaḥ satvāt 'kartā tu nopalabhyate' ityetatkathanaṃ na yuktisaṅgataṃ syāditi cet?
body.translated_text: Now, in the <s>Mahā-paramārtha-śūnyatā</s>, the statement 'there is <s>karma</s> (action), there is <s>vipāka</s> (result), but no agent is apprehended' — that would contradict this, since when <s>karma</s> and the like exist in the ultimate, all <s>dharmas</s> would not be without own-nature —

body.text: yadyevamucyeta tadātrāpi nāsti virodhaḥ pūrvavadeva, karmaphalayoḥ saṃvṛtāveva sattvāt, tairthikaparikalpitasya ca kartuḥ saṃvṛtāvapyasattvāt / ityevaṃvidhanirdeśataḥ kutastāvad virodhāvasaraḥ /
body.translated_text: If it is stated thus, then here too there is no contradiction, just as before, since <s>karma</s> and its result exist only conventionally, and since the agent constructed by non-Buddhists does not exist even conventionally. From such a teaching, where is there room for contradiction?

body.text: yadyevaṃ ced anyeṣu sūtreṣuḥ
body.translated_text: If so, then in other <s>sūtras</s>:

children.translated_text: "The existence of all entities, as conceptualized by the childish —

children.text: yadi te bhaved yathādṛṣṭāḥ sarve syustattvadarśinaḥ //
children.translated_text: if they were as they are seen, all would be seers of truth.
Due to the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s>, there is no affliction from purity.

children.text: na te tathā yathā dṛṣṭā na ca te vai na santi ca //
children.translated_text: They are not as they are seen, nor is it that they simply do not exist."

body.text: yaduktaṃ tatkathamiti cet?
body.translated_text: If [one asks] how what was stated [is to be understood] —
