body.text: idamapi purvamaktameva / atrāpi 'yadi sarvāṇi vastūni yathāvabhāsante tathaiva paramārthato vidyante' iti tadā 'sarve 'pi tattvadarśinaḥ syuḥ' iti syāt / ato 'nenāpi tāvat paramārthataḥ sarvadharmānutpādamatameva saṃsthāpyate / yaddhi 'abhāvāt sarvadharmāṇām' ityuktaṃ tena vastūnāṃ saṃvṛtisattvaṃ pratipāditam 'na te tathā yathā dṛṣṭāḥ' iti vacanāt / prajñāpāramitāyāmapi saṃkleśavyavadānavyavasthā khalu vyavahārasatyamāśrityaiva kṛteti, tadyathāḥ "subhūte, prāptirabhisamayo jātirnirodhaḥ saṃkleśo vyavadānamiti vyavahārata eva saṃvidyante, na tu paramārthataḥ iti /"
body.translated_text: this too has been stated previously. Here too, 'if all things exist in the ultimate just as they appear' — then 'all would be seers of truth.' Therefore, by this too, the non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s> in the ultimate [is established].

body.text: yadyevaṃ tarhi tatraivaḥ
body.translated_text: If so, then in that very [context]:

body.text:
"bāhyārthadarśanaṃ mithyā nāstyarthaṃ cittameva tu /
'yuktyā vipaśyamānānāṃ grāhagrāhyaṃ virudhyate /
'bāhyo na vidyate hyartho yathā bālairvikalpyate /"
"vāsanairlulitaṃ cittamarthābhāsaṃ pravartate /"
body.translated_text: "The perception of external objects is false; there is no [external] object, but only mind. By those who examine with reasoning, the grasped and grasper are contradicted. For no external object exists as conceptualized by the childish." "The mind, stirred by latent impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>), operates with the appearance of objects —"

body.text: "cittamātraṃ bho jinaputra, yaduta traidhātukam" iti yaduktaṃ tatkathaṃ nīyate?
body.translated_text: "O sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), what is called the three realms is mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>)" — how is this statement to be interpreted?

body.text: evameva āryāndhimirmocane āryaghanavyūhādiṣvāpi sarvadharmāṇāṃ cittamātra kāyatvena nirdiṣṭatvāccittameva hi tāvat paramārthataḥ sat, nānyaditi sādhyate / ataśca sarve dharmāḥ niḥsvabhāvatvena na sādhyituṃ śakyante / yadyevamucyeta, tadapi na samucitaṃ kāraṇam, yato hi yathā cittasattā nirdiṣṭā tathaiva rūpasyāpi sattāyā nirdeśastattatsūtreṣvanekadhā kṛto vidyate /
body.translated_text: Likewise, since in the <s>Ārya-Saṃdhinirmocana</s>, the <s>Ārya-Ghanavyūha</s>, and other [sūtras] too, all <s>dharmas</s> are taught as being of the nature of mind-only — it is established that mind alone exists in the ultimate, and nothing else. Therefore, all <s>dharmas</s> cannot be established as without own-nature —

body.text: atha pramānabādhitatvāt suttrāntareṣu ca niṣiddhatvāta paramārthataḥ sattvena vyavasthāpayituṃ na śakyate, tadā pudgalanairātmyamātrapraveśābhisandhinā tathāvidhavineyajanāśayāpekṣayā kathanamātramevaitaditi?
body.translated_text: If [one says:] since [mind-only] is contradicted by <s>pramāṇas</s> (valid means of knowledge) and is negated in other <s>sūtras</s>, it cannot be established as existing in the ultimate; therefore [the mind-only teaching] was merely a statement made out of consideration for the disposition of trainees to be guided, with the intention of introducing them only to the selflessness of persons (<s>pudgala-nairātmya</s>) —

body.text: yadyevamucyeta tadā cittamapi vakṣyamāṇapramāṇairbādhitaṃ bhavati / sūtrāntareṣvapi niḥsvabhāvatvena nirdiṣṭatvāt paramārthato 'gṛhītāpi sā cittamātratā kramaśaḥ paramārthanayasamudrāvagāhanahetumātratayā nirdiṣṭetyevaṃ grahaṇanīyamiti /
body.translated_text: If it is stated thus, then mind too is contradicted by the <s>pramāṇas</s> to be stated. Since it is also taught as without own-nature in other <s>sūtras</s>, even that mind-only, not grasped as ultimately [real], is merely a cause for gradually entering into the ocean of the ultimate method (<s>paramārtha-naya</s>) —

body.text: ityevaṃ ye tāvat sarvadharmān niḥsvabhāvatayā yugapajjñātumakṣamāste kadācana cittamātratāmāśritya kramaśo bāhyārthaniḥsvabhāvatāyāṃ praviśanti / ata eva
body.translated_text: Thus, those who are unable to know all <s>dharmas</s> simultaneously as without own-nature, at some point, relying on mind-only, gradually enter into the non-own-nature of external objects. Hence —

body.text: yuktyā nirīkṣamāṇānāṃ grahyagrāho nirudhyate /
body.translated_text: "For those who examine with reasoning, the grasped and grasper cease."

body.text: ityuktam /
body.translated_text: Thus it is stated.

body.text: tadanantaraṃ yadi krameṇa cittasvabhāvaḥ pratyavekṣyate, tadā tamapi niḥsvabhāvatvenāvabudhya nitarāṃ gambhīranaye praviśanti / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā -
body.translated_text: Thereafter, if the nature of mind is gradually examined, then, understanding that too as without own-nature, one enters fully into the profound method. As the Blessed One stated —

children.translated_text: "Having mounted upon mind-only, one should not construct external objects.
Abiding in the support of suchness (<s>tathatā</s>), one should transcend mind-only.
Having transcended mind-only, one should transcend the absence of appearance (<s>nirābhāsa</s>).
The <s>yogī</s> established in the absence of appearance sees the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.
The effortless course is peaceful, purified by aspirations (<s>praṇidhānas</s>).
The supreme selfless (<s>anātmaka</s>) knowledge — in the absence of appearance, one does not see [it]."

body.text: anye tu bruvate - cittamātratā hi tavat svaprasiddhasvabhāvā, ataḥ saṃvṛtyaiva sthitā / bāhyārthāstu na khalu saṃvṛtyāpi, cittakāramatiricya na sidhyanti / ata eva bhagavatā tatpradarśanārthaṃ vastūni cittamātratāyāṃ nirdiṣṭāni, sāpi na paramārthataḥ sidhyati, sūtrāntareṣvapi niḥsvabhāvatāyāmeva nirdiṣṭatvād, yathoktam āryasarvabuddhaviṣayāvatārajñānalokākaṅkāre -
body.translated_text: Others say: Mind-only (<s>cittamātratā</s>) is indeed self-evidently established in its own nature; hence it exists only in conventional [truth]. External objects, however, do not exist even conventionally, since they are not established beyond the aspect of mind. For this very reason, the Blessed One indicated things as mind-only for the purpose of demonstrating this. But even that [mind-only] is not established ultimately, since in other <s>sūtras</s> it is indicated as being without own-nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>). As stated in the <s>Ārya-Sarvabuddhaviṣayāvatāra-jñānālokālaṅkāra</s>:

children.text: sarve buddhāḥ sadā sarvān dharmān jānanti sarvathā /
children.translated_text: All <s>Buddhas</s> always know all <s>dharmas</s> in every way;
not finding mind anywhere, we bow to the one who makes non-apprehension.

body.text: āryaratnakuṭasūtre 'pi -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Ratnakūṭa-sūtra</s> too:

body.text: cittaṃ hi kāśyapa, parigaveṣyamāṇaṃ na labhyate / yanna labhyate tannopalabhyate / yannopalabhyate tannaiva atītaṃ na anāgataṃ na pratyutpannam / yannaivātītaṃ nānāgataṃ na pratyutpannaṃ tat trikālātītam / yat trikālātītaṃ tasya sadasattvamapi nāsti / yasya nāsti sadasattvaṃ tasya nāstyutpādaḥ / yasya nāstyutpādastasya nāsti svabhāvaḥ yasya nāsti svabhāvastasya nāstyutpādaḥ, yasya nāstyutpādastasya nāsti nirodhaḥ / yasya nāsti nirodhastasya nāsti viyogaḥ / yasya nāsti viyogastasya nāstyāgamaḥ, nirgamaḥ, cyutiḥ, jātiḥ / yasya nāstyāgamo nirgamaścyutirjātistasya na santi saṃskārāḥ / yasya na santi saṃskārāḥ tadasaṃskṛtāḥ / yadasaṃskṛtaṃ tadāryairviditamiti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: "Mind, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, when sought, is not found. What is not found is not apprehended. What is not apprehended is neither past, nor future, nor present. What is neither past, nor future, nor present transcends the three times. What transcends the three times has neither existence nor non-existence. What has neither existence nor non-existence has no origination. What has no origination has no own-nature. What has no own-nature has no origination. What has no origination has no cessation. What has no cessation has no separation. What has no separation has no coming, no going, no falling away, no birth. What has no coming, no going, no falling away, no birth — for that there are no conditioned formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>). What has no conditioned formations is unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>). What is unconditioned is known by the noble ones" — and so forth at length.

body.text: punaśca tatraiva -
body.translated_text: And again in the same [text]:

body.text: "nitya iti kāśyapa, ayameko 'ntaḥ, anitya iti kāśyapa, ayameko 'ntaḥ / tathā astīti kāśyapa, ayameko 'ntaḥ, nāstīti kāśyapa, ayameko 'ntaḥ / yadanayorantayormadhyam, tadarupyamanidarśanamapratiṣṭhamanābhāsamaniketamavijñaptikam / iyamucyate kāśyapa, madhyamā pratipad bhūtapratyavekṣā" - iti /
body.translated_text: "'Permanent,' O <s>Kāśyapa</s> — this is one extreme. 'Impermanent,' O <s>Kāśyapa</s> — this is the other extreme. Likewise, 'it exists,' O <s>Kāśyapa</s> — this is one extreme. 'It does not exist,' O <s>Kāśyapa</s> — this is the other extreme. That which is the middle between these two extremes — that is formless, without indication, without foundation, without appearance, without abode, without cognition. This, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is called the middle path (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>), the investigation of things as they truly are."

body.text: yadevamuktaṃ tanmadhyabhūtam, na tasya vastusatā vijñānasvabhāvena sattvasiddhiḥ / dharmadhāturhi dvābhyāmantābhyāṃ vinirmuktaḥ sarvadharmanisvabhāvalakṣaṇaḥ niṣprapañca iti vacanīyaḥ / sa cāpi dharmadhātuḥ 'ayaṃ saḥ - ityākāreṇa nirupayitumaśakyatvād arupyaḥ, parebhyo nidarśayitusamarthatvād anidarśanaḥ, ādhyātmike dhātau āyatane vānavasthitatvād apratiṣṭhaḥ, bāhyānāṃ dhātūnāmāyatanānāmiva anavabhāsitatvād anābhāsaḥ, cakṣurvijñānādidhatusvabhāvātikrāntatvād avijñaptikaḥ, rāgādisamastakleśānāmāśrayābhāvād aniketaḥ - ityevamuktam /
body.translated_text: What is thus stated as the middle — its reality is not established through having the nature of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>). For the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, being free from both extremes, should be called "without conceptual elaboration" (<s>niṣprapañca</s>), characterized by the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>. And that <s>dharmadhātu</s> is: "formless" because it cannot be determined in the form "this is that"; "without indication" because it is incapable of being shown to others; "without foundation" because it does not abide in the inner element or sense-faculty; "without appearance" because it does not manifest like external elements and sense-faculties; "without cognition" because it transcends the nature of the eye-consciousness and other elements; "without abode" because there is no basis for the totality of afflictions such as passion — thus it is stated.

body.text: yadi madhye cittasvabhāvatāyāḥ ko 'pyaṃśaḥ paramārthasan syāttadā tatsattayā nityānityābhiniveśaḥ khalu kathaṅkārameko 'ntaḥ syād, yato hi yathā vastutattvaṃ tathā yathāvadanugamya manaskaraṇaṃ patanasthānamiti naiva yujyate /
body.translated_text: If some aspect of the nature of mind were ultimately real in the middle, then through its reality, how could attachment to permanence and impermanence be an extreme? For attending to [things] in exact conformity with the nature of reality is precisely not a place of falling — this is not tenable.

body.text: nityādisvaruopamatirijya vastubhūtaḥ kaścidanyo vastvākāro 'sambhavī madhye hi vastu khalu svasvabhāvasyāsattvād abhūtamiti grahaṇaṃ nāsti tāvad anta ityevaṃ yadi cintyeta, tadapi na yuktam / asaditi graḥaṇaṃ sattagrahaṇābhāve 'bhāva eva / viṣayābhāvaniṣedhastu na tāvat san bhavati, ataḥ yasyābhāvagrahaṇaṃ st, niyataṃ tasya sattāgrahaṇamapi sadeva / tato dvāvapyantau bhavataḥ /
body.translated_text: If one thinks: "Beyond the nature of permanence and the like, there is some other real aspect of the thing in the middle — but the thing, because of the non-existence of its own nature, is not truly existent, so there is no grasping as 'it is unreal,' hence it is not an extreme" — that too is not tenable. For the cognition 'it is non-existent' is nothing but the absence of the cognition of existence. The negation of the absence of the object does not make it existent. Hence, for one who has the cognition of non-existence, the cognition of existence is certainly also present. Therefore both extremes obtain.

body.text: yadi madhye vastunaḥ sattvaṃ tadā tatsattvagrahaṇaṃ kena tatsattvagrahaṇaṃ kena niṣiddhaṃ syāt? āryasamādhirājasūtre madhye sataḥ paramārthasthitasya vastuno niṣedhāya yaduktam, tenāpi saha virodhaḥ syāt -
body.translated_text: If the thing exists in the middle, then by what is the cognition of its existence prohibited? There would also be a contradiction with what is stated in the <s>Ārya-Samādhirāja-sūtra</s> for the purpose of negating a really existing thing established as ultimate:

children.translated_text: "It exists" and "it does not exist" — both are extremes.
"Pure" and "impure" — these too are extremes.
Therefore, having abandoned both extremes,
the wise one does not take a stand even in the middle.

body.text: ityevamuktam /
body.translated_text: Thus it is stated.

body.text: ayaṃ tāvat sūtrārthaḥ - āśrayaṇīye madhye yadi vastusatāṃ nāsti kimapi svarūpaṃ tadaiva 'madhye 'pi sthānaṃ na karoti panḍitaḥ' iti yaduktaṃ tad yuktaṃ syādityucyate yadyasti kimapi vastu tadā kathaṃ na paṇḍitastasmin sthānaṃ na grahīṣyatīti / āryalokottaraparavarte tāvaduktam -
body.translated_text: This is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>: If in the middle that is to be relied upon there is no nature whatsoever as really existing, then the statement "the wise one does not take a stand even in the middle" would be appropriate — this is what is said. [But] if there is some real thing, then how would the wise one not take a stand in that? In the <s>Ārya-Lokottaraparivarta</s> it is stated:

body.text: api ca, he jinaputrāḥ, trayaḥ khalu dhāvato vijñaptimātratāyāṃ pracaranti, yato hi adhvatrayaṃ cittavat pratibudhyate, tadapi tāvaccittaṃ madhyāntarahitameva pravartate / idaṃ tāvat sūtrasya tātparyam - utpādabhaṅgayoḥ sthitilakṣaṇe ca madhye paramārthato 'sattvāccittaṃ tāvanmadhyārahitaṃ sat pravartate pratibudhyate cetyucyate /
body.translated_text: "Moreover, O sons of the Conqueror, the three times indeed operate in mere representation (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>). Since the three times are awakened to as being like mind, that mind too operates devoid of middle and extremes." This is the purport of the <s>sūtra</s>: Since in the middle between origination and destruction, that is, in the characteristic of persistence, there is no ultimate existence, mind is said to operate and to be awakened to as devoid of middle.

body.text: apere khalvabhidadhate - saṃvṛtau hi vijñānavad bāhyārthā api saṃvidyanta iti / anyathā daśabhūmakasūtre - aṣṭabhyāṃ hi bhūmau saṃsthitā bodhisattvā lokadhātvantargatānāṃ paramāṇvādīnāṃ saṃkhyāṃ parijānanti - iti yaduktam, tena saha virodhaḥsyāditi / tathā hi -
body.translated_text: Others again state: Even in convention (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), external objects exist just as consciousness does. Otherwise, there would be a contradiction with what is stated in the <s>Daśabhūmaka-sūtra</s> — that <s>bodhisattvas</s> established on the eighth stage know the number of atoms and so forth within world-realms. For:

body.text: "sa paramāṇurajaḥsūkṣmatāṃ ca prajānāti, mahadgatatāṃ ca apramāṇatāṃ ca vibhaktiṃ ca prajānāti / apramāṇaparamāṇurajovibhaktikauśalyaṃ ca prajānāti / asyāṃ ca lokadhātau yāvanti pṛthvīdhātoḥ paramāṇurajāṃsi tāni prajānāti / yāvanti abdhātoḥ, tejodhātoḥ, vāyudhātoḥ prajānāti" / iti vastaraḥ / vijñānavad bāhyārthānāmapi prasiddhatvāt pratītivirodhaḥ, yato hi yuktibhirvicāraṇāyāṃ satyāmubhāvapi naiva parīkṣāṃ sahete, atastau avtusthitimapi na kṣamete / vyavahārasatye [saṃvṛtau] tvāgopālāṅganāṃ yāvat prasiddhau / vijñaptimātratākathanasya tāvat phalaṃ tu paraparikalpitānāṃ kartubhoktrādīnāṃ niṣedha eva, vyavahāre 'pi cittatiriktānāṃ teṣāṃ kartrādīnāṃ saṃsiddherabhāvāt /
body.translated_text: "He knows the subtlety of the atom, and he knows the great extent, the immeasurability, and the division. He knows the skill in the division of immeasurable atoms. And he knows however many atoms of the earth-element there are in this world-realm. [He knows] however many of the water-element, fire-element, [and] wind-element" — and so forth at length. Since external objects are also well-known just like consciousness, there is a contradiction with established convention. For when examined by reasoning, neither of the two withstands scrutiny; hence neither can endure even as being conventionally established. But in conventional truth, they are well-known even to cowherd women. The purpose of stating mind-only is merely the negation of the agent, experiencer, and so forth, as conceptualized by others — since even in convention, those agents and the like, separate from mind, are not established.

body.text: athavā - sarvadharmeṣu pūrvaṅgamatvāccittaṃ sarvadharmāpekṣayā pradhānaṃ sidhyate / yāvad yathā "nāstyarthaṃ cittameva tu" iti yaduktam, yathā vā "vāsanairlulitaṃ cittamārthābhāsaṃ pravartate" ityādi yaduktam, yathā vā "vāsanairlulitaṃ cittamārthābhāsaṃ pravatate" ityādi yaduktam, tadapi nirākāreṇa cittena viṣayagrahaṇaṃ kathamapi na yujyata ityavaśyaṃ tat sākārameva mantavyam / ataścittākāraṃ vyatiricya arthākārāvabhāsābhāvāt tanniṣedhena sākāracittameva tāvannirdiśyate, na tu tena bahyārthā bhāvo 'vabodhyate /
body.translated_text: Or: Because mind is foremost among all <s>dharmas</s>, mind is established as primary with respect to all <s>dharmas</s>. As to what is stated — "there is no object, it is mind alone," and "the mind, agitated by latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), produces the appearance of objects" — since the apprehension of an object by a formless (<s>nirākāra</s>) mind is in no way tenable, mind must necessarily be conceived as having form (<s>sākāra</s>). Therefore, since there is no appearance of the form of an object apart from the form of mind, by negating that [external object], mind with form (<s>sākāra-citta</s>) alone is indicated; but by that, the existence of external objects is not thereby understood.

body.text: athavā ātmadisattānirdeśa iva tadvineyajanāpekṣayā yathā sadvaidya āturān puṣṇāti tathā bhagavanto nānavidyā deśānāḥ pravartayanti / yathoktaṃ laṅkāvatārasūtre -
body.translated_text: Or: Just as in the teaching of the existence of a self — with reference to the disciples to be trained, just as a good physician nourishes the sick, so the Blessed Ones set forth various teachings. As stated in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra</s>:

children.text: āture āture yadvad bhiṣag dravyaṃ prayacchati /
children.translated_text: Just as a physician gives medicine to each sick person,

children.text: buddhā hi tadvat sattvānāṃ cittamātraṃ vadanti vai //
children.translated_text: so too the <s>Buddhas</s> proclaim mind-only to beings.

body.text: nānyān visaṃvādayatīti vineyajanānāṃ hitasukhakaratvāt sārthakaṃ vacanam / parahitaṃ tāvadekāntatayā satyamiti heturbhagavatsu tāvannāsti mṛṣāvādo 'pi / ata uktam -
body.translated_text: [This] does not deceive others, since the statement is meaningful because it brings benefit and happiness to the disciples. Since benefiting others is absolutely true, there is no false speech in the Blessed Ones. Hence it is stated:

children.translated_text: What is untrue is deceptive; what is not false is conducive to meaning.
What is certainly beneficial to others is proper; what is not beneficial is otherwise.

body.text: ityevaṃ kiṃ sṃvṛtāvasti bāhyārthasattvan / varaṃ tāvaccittamatratā, kintu niḥsandigdhaṃ sūkṣmavastusvabhāvaṃ samyak sādhayituṃ nāsti sarvathā ko 'pi āptāgamaḥ / āryaratnameghasūtre tāvat -
body.translated_text: Thus, does the reality of external objects exist in convention? Mind-only is indeed preferable; but there is certainly no authoritative scripture whatsoever that correctly establishes the subtle nature of the thing beyond doubt. In the <s>Ārya-Ratnamegha-sūtra</s>:

body.text: "kulaputra, yadi bhavet paramārthato 'sattvam, tadā nirarthakaṃ brahmacaryam" iti yaduktaṃ tatkiṃ nāsti sat?
body.translated_text: "Son of good family, if there were non-existence in the ultimate sense, then the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) would be meaningless" — it is stated. Then is there nothing real?

body.text: yadyevamucyeta tannaiva yujyate, yato hi tatpramāṇabhūtaṃ paramārthaṃ ko hi nāma tyajet / ayaṃ tāvat sūtrārthaḥ - iyaṃ hi pudgaladharmanairātmyalakṣaṇā tathataiva paramārthaśabdavācyā paramasya jñānasya gocaratvāt,yuktimattvācca saiva svayaṃ parameti / yadi tadapyasat syāttadā yathā pudgalo dharmāśca bālapṛthagjaneṣu prasiddhāstathaiva syuḥ, tathā sati sarve janā anāyāsena ādita eva tattvadarśinaḥ syuḥ, tattvadarśanārthaṃ ca prayatno 'pi nirarthakaḥ syāditi suspaṣṭameva / ato nāstīdaṃ pramāṇopapannamiti /
body.translated_text: If one says so, that is not tenable, for who would abandon what is ultimately authoritative? This is the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>: This very <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), characterized by the selflessness of persons and <s>dharmas</s> (<s>pudgala-dharma-nairātmya</s>), is what is denoted by the word "ultimate" (<s>paramārtha</s>), because it is the object of supreme knowledge and because it possesses reasoning — it itself is supreme. If even that were non-existent, then persons and <s>dharmas</s> as they are well-known to childish ordinary persons would remain just as they are; in that case, all people would be seers of reality effortlessly from the very beginning, and effort for seeing reality would also be meaningless — this is quite clear. Therefore, this is not supported by valid means of knowledge.

body.text: āryaratnakūṭasūtre tāvataḥ "kāśyapa, varaṃ khalu sumerumātrā pudgaladṛṣṭiḥ, nābhimānikasya śūnyatādṛṣṭiḥ"
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Ratnakūṭa-sūtra</s>: "O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, better a view of self (<s>pudgala-dṛṣṭi</s>) as great as Mount <s>Sumeru</s> than the view of emptiness of one who is conceited" —

body.text: iti uaduktaṃ tena kathaṃ na virodhaḥ syāditi cet? tarhi nāsti virodhaḥ / ye khalu paramārthasat vastvabhyupagamya punastasyāsattvaṃ parikalpayanti, evañca yeṣāṃ vināśārthaṃ śūnyatādeśānā, teṣāṃ rāgādīnāṃ samyak sattvameveti parikalpayanti, te pūrvaṃ sattvaṃ parikalpya paścāt tadasattvaṃ parigṛhṇanti / ataḥ sadasadantayoḥ patitatvāt te antadvayarahitaṃ sarvaprapañcapaśamaṃ śūnyatārthaṃ naivādhigacchantīti "abhimāninaḥ' ata eva bhagavantastathāvidhāyā dṛṣṭerniṣedhena paramārthataḥ sadasatsarvaprapañcajālavirahitasya jñānārthaṃ niyojayantīti / anyairapi sūtreḥ svayaṃ bhagavatā etannirdhāryate / laṅkāvatārasūtre 'piḥ
body.translated_text: if one asks how there is no contradiction with this statement — there is no contradiction. Those who, having accepted ultimately real things, then again conceptualize their non-existence — and those for whose destruction the teaching of emptiness [is given], who conceptualize that their passions and the like are truly real — they first conceptualize existence and then grasp non-existence. Hence, having fallen into the two extremes of existence and non-existence, they never attain the meaning of emptiness which is the pacification of all conceptual elaboration, free from both extremes — they are "conceited." For this very reason, the Blessed Ones, through the negation of such a view, direct [beings] to knowledge that is ultimately free from the entire net of conceptual elaboration of existence and non-existence. This is also determined by the Blessed One himself in other <s>sūtras</s>. In the <s>Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra</s> too:

body.text: "dvayaniśrito 'yaṃ mahāmate, loko yaduta astitvaniśritaśca nāstitvaniśritaśca / bhāvābhāvacchandadṛṣṭipatitaśca aniḥśaraṇe niḥśaraṇabuddhiḥ / tatra mahāmate, kathamastitvaniśrito lokaḥ? yaduta vidyamānairhetupratyayairloka utpadyate nāvidyamanaiḥ, vidyamānaṃ cotpadyamānamutpadyate nāvidyamānam / sa caivaṃ bruvan mahāmate, bhāvānāmastitvahetupratyānāṃ lokasya ca hetvastivādī bhavati / tatra mahāmate, kathaṃ nāstitvaniśrito bhavati? yaduta rāgadveṣamohābhyupagamaṃ kṛtvā punarapi rāgadveṣamohabhāvābhāvaṃ vikalpayati / yaśca mahāmate, bhāvābnāmastitvaṃ nābhyupaiti bhāvalakṣaṇaviviktatvād, yaśca buddhaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ rāgadveṣamohānnābhyupaiti bhāvalakṣaṇavinirmuktatvād vidyante neti / katamo 'tra mahāmate, vaināśiko bhavati? mahāmatirāha - ya eṣa bhagavan abhyupagamya rāgadveṣamohān na punarabhyupaiti / bhagavānāha - sādhu, sādhu mahāmate, sādhu sādhu punastvaṃ mahāmate, yastvamevaṃ prabhāṣitaḥ / kevalaṃ mahāmate, na rāgadveṣamohabhāvābhāvād vaināśiko bhavati, buddhaśrāvakapratyekabuddhavaināśiko 'pi bhavati / idaṃ ca mahāmate, sandhāyoktaṃ mayāvaraṃ khalu sumerumātrā pudgaladṛṣṭirna tveva nāstyastitvābhimānikasya śūnyatādṣṛṣṭiḥ iti /
body.translated_text: "This world, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is dependent on two [extremes], namely dependent on existence and dependent on non-existence. Fallen into views of desire for being and non-being, [the world] conceives liberation where there is no liberation. How, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the world dependent on existence? When the world arises from existent causes and conditions, not from non-existent ones, and what exists arises, not what does not exist — one who speaks thus, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, becomes an advocate of the existence of causes and conditions of entities. How, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, does one become dependent on non-existence? When, having accepted passion, hatred, and delusion, one then again conceptualizes the existence and non-existence of passion, hatred, and delusion. And one who, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, does not accept the existence of entities, because of their separation from the characteristics of entities, and one who does not accept the passion, hatred, and delusion of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, because of their being free from the characteristics of entities — do they exist or not? Which one here, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is an annihilationist? <s>Mahāmati</s> said: That one, Blessed One, who having accepted passion, hatred, and delusion does not again accept them. The Blessed One said: Well said, well said, <s>Mahāmati</s>! Well said again, <s>Mahāmati</s>, that you have spoken thus. For, <s>Mahāmati</s>, one becomes an annihilationist not merely through the existence and non-existence of passion, hatred, and delusion; one becomes an annihilationist of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> as well. And with this intention, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, I have stated: 'Better a view of self as great as Mount <s>Sumeru</s> than the view of emptiness of one conceited with non-existence.'"

body.text: ata eva bhagavatā 'vastuvādina evābhimāninaḥ' ityuktāḥ / atastatraivoktam -
body.translated_text: For this very reason, the Blessed One has called them "conceited ones who assert the reality of things." Hence in the same [text] it is stated:

children.text: abhutvā yasya utpādo bhūtva vāpi vinaśyati /
children.translated_text: He whose origination is without having [previously] existed, or who perishes after having existed,

children.text: pratyayaiḥ sadasaccāpi na te śāsane sthitāḥ //
children.translated_text: and [who asserts] both existence and non-existence through conditions — they do not stand in [the <s>Buddha</s>'s] teaching.
For whom nothing whatsoever arises and nothing whatsoever ceases,

children.text: tasyāsti nāsti nopaiti viviktaṃ paśyato jagat //
children.translated_text: for him neither 'it exists' nor 'it does not exist' applies — he sees the world as isolated [from extremes].

body.text: dvitīyapadyārthadvāreṇa svamataṃ saṃsthāpya 'parikalpitasvabhāvaviviktatvād viviktaṃ jagadityeva tāvat sūtrārthaḥ, ataśca nāsti virodhaḥ' ityabhidadhadbhiḥ kaḥ parikalpitaḥ svabhāvaḥ ityabhidhātavyam / atha pramāṇaviruddhamapi yad bālaiḥ satyamiti gṛhyate taditi cet? tadāśeṣaṃ jagat paramārthato 'nutpannamapi bālairyadutpattyādikaṃ paramārthataḥ sadityāropyate tad vakṣyamāṇapramāṇairniṣiddhatvāt saṃvṛtisvabhāvamiti kasmānna gṛhyate / yadyevaṃ nāsti? tadā yaddhi bhagavatābāhyārthāḥ parikalpitasvabhāvatvāchūnyāḥ' iti yaduktaṃ tasya paramārthato na santīti vyākhyānaṃ kasmānna kriyate? pramāṇaviruddhatvāttathā vyakhyānaṃ na karttavyamiti cet? tadā vijñānasyāpi tathā vyākhyānaṃ na kartuvyam, bāhārthavat tasyāpi pramāṇaviruddhatvāt /
body.translated_text: Having established their own view through the meaning of the second verse, those who state 'the meaning of the sūtra is simply that the world is devoid because of being devoid of the imagined nature (<s>parikalpita-svabhāva</s>), and therefore there is no contradiction' — they must explain what is the imagined nature. If [they say] it is what is grasped as true by the ignorant even though contradicted by <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid knowledge), then since the entire world, though ultimately unarisen, is superimposed by the ignorant as truly arising etc. and is refuted by the <s>pramāṇas</s> to be stated, why is it not taken as conventional nature (<s>saṃvṛti-svabhāva</s>)? If [they say] it is not thus, then why is the explanation not given that what the Blessed One said — 'external objects are empty because of being of imagined nature' — means 'they do not ultimately exist'? If [they say] such an explanation should not be given because it contradicts <s>pramāṇa</s>, then the same explanation should not be given for consciousness either, because it too contradicts <s>pramāṇa</s> just like external objects.

body.text: pramāṇai katipayairyadi vijñānaṃ vastusat sidhyati tadā dvividhameva parikalpitam, nānyaditi samyag vyākhyātaṃ bhavet, kintu tadapi naiva sidhyatīti nirdeṣṭavyam / ataśca jagadidaṃ yathoktaparikalpitasvabhāvaviviktamityasmābhirapyabhyupeyata iti nāsti sarvathā durūham / ata eva āryasandhinirmocanasūtre -
body.translated_text: If consciousness is established as substantially real by some <s>pramāṇas</s>, then it would be properly explained that the imagined is only twofold, nothing else; but rather it should be pointed out that even that is not established. Therefore, that we too accept that this world is devoid of the stated imagined nature — there is nothing at all difficult about this. For this very reason, in the <s>Āryasaṃdhinirmocanasūtra</s> —

body.text: "maitreya, paratantrapariniṣpannalakṣaṇayoḥ parikalpitasaṃkleśavyavadānalakṣaṇaṃ yaccātyantaviviktaṃ tannālambanīkriyate, sarvaśūnyatālakṣaṇatvāttasya' iti yaduktaṃ tadapyanena nirākṛtaṃ bhavati" ityuktam /
body.translated_text: It is stated: 'O <s>Maitreya</s>, that which is absolutely devoid of the imagined characteristics of defilement and purification in the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>) and perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>) characteristics — that should not be made into an object of apprehension, because it has the characteristic of complete emptiness' — this too is refuted by this [argument].

body.text: tatrāpi rāgādayo ye saṃkleśātmakasaṃvṛtisvabhāvānāṃ paratantralakṣaṇānāṃ samyaktayā saṃkliṣṭakaraṇena saṃsāre niyojanena pratipakṣe ca yathākramaṃ vidhyanabhūtābhūtatvādinā cāropyante, te teṣāṃ kṛte parikalpitalakṣaṇānyeva / yogisaṃvṛtau aviparyastapariniṣpattyā tāvat pariniṣpannalakṣaṇam / ataḥ pariniṣpannalakṣaṇayuktāni bodhipakṣānukūlavyavadānānyapi vipakṣātyantapratighātarupeṇa parinirvāṇe ca niyojanādinā samyaktayā vastudharmatāyāmāropitāni, tānyapi teṣāṃ parikalpitalakṣaṇameva / yaśca dharmadhātuḥ prakṛtiprabhāsvarastasminnasambhavaḥ paramārthataḥ saṃkleśādīnām / ataḥ parikalpitadharmatvāt tayoḥ svabhāvayoḥ saṃkleśavyavadādharmatvamasambhavameva / saṃkleśavyavadānapakṣasarvadharmāṇāṃ paramārthato 'nutpāde hi ekarasībhūtatvena nānākaraṇamayuktam / ato dvāvapi samyagrupeṇa śūnyāveva / tathyasaṃvṛtau tu dvayorapi bhāvāt saṃkleśabyadānapakṣayorabhāvādoṣo 'pi na khalu prasajyate /
body.translated_text: Therein too, passion and other [afflictions] that, through the function of causing defilement in the conventional nature of dependently-characterized entities, bind [beings] to <s>saṃsāra</s>, and through the antidote respectively, are superimposed as real or unreal etc. — these are precisely the imagined characteristics with respect to those [entities]. In the yogic conventional [truth], through the non-mistaken perfection, [there is] the perfected characteristic. Therefore, even purification [qualities] that accord with the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>), when superimposed upon the true nature of things through the function of completely counteracting the opposing factors and leading to <s>parinirvāṇa</s> etc. — these too are precisely the imagined characteristic with respect to those [qualities]. And the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), which is luminous by nature — therein, ultimately, defilement and such are impossible. Therefore, because both those natures are of imagined characteristics, their having the character of defilement and purification is entirely impossible. Since all <s>dharmas</s> of the defilement and purification sides are ultimately unarisen, being of one taste, differentiation is not proper. Therefore, both are indeed empty in their true form. But in the true conventional (<s>tathya-saṃvṛti</s>), since both exist, no fault arises from the absence of the defilement and purification sides.

body.text: āryasārdhadvisāhasrikāsūtre -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Āryasārdhadvisāhasrikāsūtra</s> —

body.text: "na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ rāgadharmi vā virāgadharmi vā, evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ rāgadharmi vā virāgadharmi vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃkāravijñānānāṃ na rāgadharmatā nāpi virāgadharmatā iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin evaṃ dveṣadharma vā adveṣadharmi vā, evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ dveṣadharmi vā adveṣadharmi vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ na dveṣadharmatā nāpi vigatadveṣadharmatā iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ mohadharmi vā vigatamohadharmi vā, evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ mohadharmi vā vigatamohadharmi vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānāṃ na mohadharmatā nāpi vigatamohadharmatā iyaṃ prajñāpāramitā / na hi suvikrāntavikrāmin rūpaṃ saṃkliśyate vā vyavadāyate vā, evaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāḥ / na vijñānaṃ saṃkliśyate vā vyavadāyate vā / yā ca rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānānām asaṃkleśatā avyavadānatā iyamucyate prajñāpāramitā" / ityuktam /
body.translated_text: It is stated: 'O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form does not have the nature of passion nor the nature of dispassion; likewise feeling, perception, and formations. Consciousness does not have the nature of passion nor the nature of dispassion. That which is the non-nature-of-passion and the non-nature-of-dispassion of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom). O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form does not have the nature of hatred nor the nature of non-hatred; likewise feeling, perception, and formations. Consciousness does not have the nature of hatred nor the nature of non-hatred. That which is the non-nature-of-hatred and the non-nature-of-non-hatred of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form does not have the nature of delusion nor the nature of non-delusion; likewise feeling, perception, and formations. Consciousness does not have the nature of delusion nor the nature of non-delusion. That which is the non-nature-of-delusion and the non-nature-of-non-delusion of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. O <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, form is neither defiled nor purified; likewise feeling, perception, and formations. Consciousness is neither defiled nor purified. That which is the non-defilement and non-purification of form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness — this is called <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.'

body.text: āryasatyadvayanirdeśasūtre 'pi -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Āryasatyadvayanirdeśasūtra</s> too —

body.text: "katamayā punarmañjuśrīḥ samatayā yāvat paramārthato yatsamaṃ vyavadānaṃ tatsamāḥ sarvadharmāḥ paramārthata iti?
body.translated_text: 'O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, by what equality is purification equal, and [by what equality] are all <s>dharmas</s> ultimately equal?'

body.text: mañjuśrīrāha - devaputra, paramārthataḥ sarvadharmānutpādasamatayā paramārthataḥ sarvadharmātyantājātisamatayā paramārthataḥ sarvadharmābhāvasamatayā paramārthataḥ samāḥ sarvadharmāḥ" ityuktam /
body.translated_text: <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: 'O Son of the Gods, by the equality of non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s> ultimately, by the equality of the absolute non-production of all <s>dharmas</s> ultimately, by the equality of the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s> ultimately — all <s>dharmas</s> are ultimately equal.'

body.text: āryasarvabuddhaviṣayāvatārajñānālokālaṅkārasūtre ca -
body.translated_text: And in the <s>Āryasarvabuddhaviṣayāvatārajñānālokālaṅkārasūtra</s> —

body.text: "saṃkṣepato hi sarve 'kuśalamanaskārāstāvat saṃkleśahetavo bhavanti, sarve ca kuśalamanaskārā vyavadānahetava iti / tatra ye cāpi saṃkleśahetavo vā vyavadānahetavo vā dharmāste sarve svabhāvataḥ śūnyāḥ, niḥsattvanirjīvaniḥpudgalanirātmakamāyāvanniḥsvalakṣaṇatvebhyaḥ / ataste antaḥśāantāḥ, ye antaḥśāntāste praśāntāḥ, ye praśāntāste tāvattatprakṛtikāḥ, ye khalu tatprakṛkāste nopalabhyante, ye nopalabhyante te naivopatiṣṭhante, ye nopatiṣṭhante ta eva tāvadākāśam, ākāśaṃ cābhyavakāśaḥ / sarvadharmān ākāśasamān vijñāyāpi saṃkleśaḥ vyavadānaṃ ceti vyavahiyete ākāśadharmatā cāpi nāpanīyate / kathamidamiti cet? mañjuśrīḥ, jātinirodhadharmavān na ko 'pi dharmo bhavati" ityuktam /
body.translated_text: It is stated: 'In brief, all unwholesome mental formations are causes of defilement, and all wholesome mental formations are causes of purification. Therein, whatever <s>dharmas</s> are causes of defilement or causes of purification — all of them are empty of own-nature, without beings, without life-force, without persons, without self, like an illusion, because they are without own-characteristics. Therefore, they are inwardly peaceful; what is inwardly peaceful is completely peaceful; what is completely peaceful has that very nature; what has that nature is not apprehended; what is not apprehended does not abide; what does not abide — that is space, and space is accommodation. Knowing all <s>dharmas</s> to be like space, defilement and purification are still conventionally spoken of, yet the space-nature is also not removed. How so? O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever has the nature of arising and cessation.'

body.text: yadi punaḥ parikalpitalakṣaṇaśūnyaḥ ko 'pi dharmaḥ syāt tadāsminneva sūtre -
body.translated_text: If, however, some <s>dharma</s> were empty only of the imagined characteristic, then in this very sūtra —

body.text: "mañjuśrīḥ, advayā, sarve dharmāḥ, arthānniḥsvalakṣaṇā advaidhīkārā anāmikā animittā amanaścittavijñāptikā anutpannā aniruddhā ahetukā asañcārā asanudācārā anakṣarā anirghoṣasvarāḥ santi" /
body.translated_text: 'O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are non-dual, without own-characteristics in meaning, not subject to bifurcation, nameless, signless, not of mind, thought, or consciousness, unarisen, unceased, without cause, not moving, not occurring, without syllables, without the sound of speech' —

body.text: iti yaduktam, api ca -
body.translated_text: what was stated, and moreover —

body.text: "mañjuśrīḥ, yacchūnyaṃ tadabhiniveśagrahaṇābhāvasyaivaitadadhivacanam, mañjuśrīḥ, nopalabhyate paramārthataḥ kaścana śūnyatākhyo dharmaḥ" /
body.translated_text: 'O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that which is empty — this is simply a designation for the absence of grasping through attachment. O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, ultimately no <s>dharma</s> called emptiness is apprehended' —

body.text: iti ca yaduktam,tad virudhyate /
body.translated_text: what was thus stated would be contradicted.

body.text: yadyevaṃ tadā āryasandhinirmocanasūtre -
body.translated_text: If so, then in the <s>Āryasaṃdhinirmocanasūtra</s> —

body.text: "abhilāpastāvannāsti asadbhūto bhāvaḥ / tatra ko hi nāma bhāva iti cet? yaḥ khalyavāryajñānena āryadarśanena cānirvacanīyatāyāmavabudhyate, sa eva tadanirvacanīyatāyāmavabuddhatvad asaṃskṛtanāmnā kevalaṃ vyavahiyate" / ityādikaṃ yaduktam, tathā bhagavatpravacaneṣu ca yadāryajñānagocaraṃ pratyātmavedanīyaṃ tad bhāvasvabhāvena saditi nirdiṣṭam, tatkathaṃ sambhavediti cet? na virodhaḥ / atrāryajñānagocarāṇāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ yo hi nairātmyalakṣaṇo dharmadhatuḥ sa eva bhāvaśabdena vivakṣayā vastvabhiniveśaśālināṃ bhayasthānaṃ parihartukāmena tathā deśitam / athavā āryajñānāni sarve ca dharmāḥ tathatāpannāḥ, ato vastuśabdāśrayapratipipādayiṣayā dharmadhātuvābhihitaḥ syāditi / bhagavadbhitrapi vineyajanāśayānurodhena tāvat sā dharmataiva vividhairupāyairupadiṣṭā /
body.translated_text: What was stated as 'There is no verbal expression of an entity that has the nature of non-existence. If asked, what then is that entity? — that which is understood through Noble non-conceptual knowledge and Noble vision in [its] inexpressibility, that very thing, because it is understood in its inexpressibility, is merely conventionally designated by the name "unconditioned"' and so forth — and also what was stated in the Blessed One's teachings that what is within the scope of Noble knowledge and individually self-cognized exists as having the nature of an entity — how is that possible? There is no contradiction. Here, the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), which has the characteristic of selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s> that are within the scope of Noble knowledge — that very thing was taught by the word 'entity,' intending to remove the source of fear for those inclined to attachment to existence. Or, all Noble knowledges and all <s>dharmas</s> have attained suchness (<s>tathatā</s>); therefore, to demonstrate the support for the word 'entity,' it was stated as <s>dharmadhātu</s>. The Blessed Ones too have taught that very <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality) through various skillful means in accordance with the dispositions of the beings to be trained.

body.text: āryalaṅkāvatārasūtre - "mahāmate, padārthānāṃ tathāgatagarbhopadeśaṃ kṛtvā tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksambuddhā bālānāṃ nairātmyasantrāsapadavivarjanārthaṃ nirvikalpanirābhāsagocaraṃ tathāgatarbhakhopadeśena deśayanti / tadyathā mahāmate, kumbhakāra ekasmānmṛtparamāṇurāśervivadhāni bhāṇḍāni karoti hastaśilpadaṇḍodakasūtraprayatnaprayogād, evameva mahāmate, tathāgatāstadeva dharmanairātyaṃ sarvavikalpalakṣaṇavinivṛttaṃ vividhaiḥ prajñopāyakauśalyayogairrgarbhopadeśena vā nairāmyopadeśena vā kumbhakāravaccitraiḥ padavyañcanaparyāyairdeśayante" /
body.translated_text: In the <s>Āryalaṅkāvatārasūtra</s>: 'O <s>Mahāmati</s>, having taught the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> for the sake of [explaining] the meanings of terms, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, teach through the teaching of <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> the domain of non-conceptual, non-appearance [knowledge], in order to remove from the ignorant the ground of terror at selflessness. O <s>Mahāmati</s>, just as a potter makes various vessels from a single mass of clay atoms through the application of skill, stick, water, thread, and effort, in the same way, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> teach that very selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>, from which all characteristics of conceptual construction have been removed, through various skills of wisdom and means — either through the teaching of <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> or through the teaching of selflessness — like a potter, with various words, expressions, and synonyms.'

body.text: tathātāpiyaṃ sarvathā vācyāpi vyavahāravaśena aśeṣasaṃskṛtadharmatā, ataḥ saṃkṛteti nāmnā vyavahiyate / utpādād vā tathāgatānāmanutpādād vā tathāgatanāṃ sarvakāleṣu sthitatvād asaṃskṛteti nāmnāpi vyapadiṣṭā / tathatā tāvat sarvasvabhāvātītalakṣaṇā, ato nāntyubhayasvabhāvāpītthamevāvabudhyate / anyathā bhavatsammatam asaṃskṛtastvapi tat kathaṃ bhavet / yato hi [bhavatā] tadasaṃskṛtaṃ vastvityapyabhidhīyate, saṃskṛtameva vastvityapi cābhidhīyate /
body.translated_text: This very <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), though in every way inexpressible, is conventionally the nature of all conditioned <s>dharmas</s>; therefore it is conventionally designated by the name 'conditioned.' Since it exists at all times regardless of whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise or not, it is also designated by the name 'unconditioned.' <s>Tathatā</s> has the characteristic of transcending all natures; therefore, it is understood as not falling into either or both extremes. Otherwise, how could what you accept as 'unconditioned entity' be [so]? For you call it both 'unconditioned entity' and say that only the conditioned is an entity.

body.text: āryaratnakarasūtre 'pyuktam -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Āryaratnakarasūtra</s> too it is said —

children.text: vadanti ye vai tathatāmasaṃkṛtāṃ tathaiva cānye kṛtakāṃ yatastām /
children.translated_text: Those who say <s>tathatā</s> is unconditioned, and likewise others who say it is produced —

children.text: notsāhavanto hyubhaye bhavanti dharmasya jñāne sugatopadiṣṭe //
children.translated_text: both are unable to know the <s>Dharma</s> taught by the <s>Sugata</s> (the Well-Gone One).

body.text: atastaditthaṃ saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtayorvastutvagrāhastāvad antagrāha iti athavā śrāvakapratyekabuddhanāṃ yad gocaraṃ tatsvalakṣaṇaṃ vastitvatyabhyupagacchātāṃ bālānāṃ kevalaṃ santrāsapadavivarjanārthameva āryajñānagocaraṃ vastusadityabhihitam / buddhabodhiattvānām atyantalokottarajñānasya viṣayastu pāramārthikaṃ vastusvalakṣaṇaṃ sarvathāsat, sarvadharmānutpādānirodhaviṣayakatvāt sadasatpakṣavirahitameva taditi / sūtre 'upuktam - "kiṃ lokottarajñānam? śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ svasāmānyalakṣaṇapatitāśayānāṃ yo hyabhiniveśaḥ / kimatyantalokottarajñānam? buddhabodhisattvānāṃ nirābhāsadharpravicayena anutpādānirodhadarśanāt sadasatyakṣavivarjitaṃ taditi /"
body.translated_text: Therefore, grasping at the reality of the conditioned or the unconditioned is extreme-grasping (<s>antagrāha</s>). Or alternatively, what is within the scope of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> — the own-characteristics that they accept as real entities — was taught as 'real entity within the scope of Noble knowledge' merely to remove the ground of terror for the ignorant. But for <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the object of the most supremely transcendent knowledge — the ultimate own-characteristic of entities — is in every way non-existent, because that knowledge has as its object the non-arising and non-cessation of all <s>dharmas</s>, and is free from the sides of existent and non-existent. In the sūtra it is stated: 'What is supramundane knowledge? — That which is the attachment of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> who have fallen into dispositions toward own and general characteristics. What is the most supremely supramundane knowledge? — That of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, who, through the analysis of <s>dharmas</s> free from appearances, see non-arising and non-cessation, free from the sides of existent and non-existent.'

body.text: śrāvakādayastāvat tathyasaṃvṛtisaṃgṛhītaṃ skandhamātraṃ svasāmānyalakṣaṇākareṇa bhāvayanti, ataḥ pudgalanairātmyamātragṛhītatvātteṣāṃ tajjñānaṃ vastuviṣayakamiti vyavahriyate, na tu paramārthatayā /
body.translated_text: <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others cultivate the mere aggregates (<s>skandhamātra</s>) included in true conventional truth (<s>tathya-saṃvṛti</s>) through the mode of own and general characteristics; therefore, because they have grasped only the selflessness of persons (<s>pudgala-nairātmya</s>), their knowledge is conventionally designated as having entities as its object, but not as [having them as its object] ultimately.

body.text: yadi buddhabodhisattvānāṃ jñānasya viṣayaḥ paramārthalakṣaṇena sahaikībhūtaṃ tadā kathaṃ tajjñānaṃ satpakṣavivarjitaṃ syāt? ata eva hi bālānāṃ santrāsapadavivarjanārtham āryajñānagocaraṃ vastusadityupadiṣṭam, na tu paramārthato vastu svalakṣaṇasaditi kathanārtham / yadyevaṃ nāsti, tadā buddhāṃ bodhisattvāśca sadvikalpasambaddhā na bhavantīti? yathā bālānāṃ santrāapadavivarjanārthamityuktam, na tu paramārthato vastusaditi pratipādanārtham, tathā bhagavatāpi sūtrāntareṣu deśitam, tathā hi āryakaṅkāvatārasūtre - "kimidaṃ bhagavan sattvānāṃ tvayā nāstyasidṛṣṭiṃ vinivārya vastusvabhāvābhiniveśena āryajñānagocaraviṣāabhiniveśānnāstitvadṛṣṭiḥ punarnāstitvadṛṣṭiḥ punarnipātyate, viviktadharmopadeśābhāvaśca kriyate āryajñānasvabhāvavastudeśanayā? bhagavānāha - na mayā mahamate, viviktadharmopadeśābhāvaḥ kriyate, na ca na cāstītvadṛṣṭirnipātyate āryavastusvabhāvanirdeśenaḥ kintu uttrāsapadavivārjanārthaṃ sattvānāṃ mahāmate, mayā anādikālabhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇābhiniviṣṭānāmāryajñānavastusvabhāvābhiniveśālakṣaṇadṛṣṭyā viviktadharmopadeśaḥ kriyate, na mayā māhamate, bhāvasvabhāvopadeśaḥ kriyate / kiṃ tu mahāmate svayamevādhigatayāthātathyaviviktadharmavihāriṇo bhaviṣyanti" - iti vistaraḥ / ato yadāryajñānagocaraviṣayo vastusvalakṣaṇatvena nirdiṣṭa nirdiṣṭaḥ sa tāvad bhagavata upāyenaiva deśanāmātram / ato bhagavato 'sandigdhaṃ pravacananayamanupādāya te mithyā [moṣadharmakaṃ] vastusvabhāvatvena vikalpayanti / te tāvābhimānino bhagavantamapi apavādya svayaṃ vinaśyanti parāṃścāpi nāśayanti / evamitthamasninneva sūtre vastusabhāvābhiniveśinaḥ ātmagrāhagṛhītatvānna muktā bhaviṣyantītyevaṃ samupadiṣṭam - "punaraparaṃ mahāmate, pramāṇatrayāvayavapratyavasthānaṃ kṛtyā āryajñānapratyātmādhigamyaṃ svabhāvadvayavinirmuktaṃ vastu svabhāvato vidyata iti vikalpayiṣyanti / na ca mahāmate, cittamano manovijñānacittaparāvṛttyāśrayāṇāṃ svacittadṛśyagrāhyagrāhakavikalpaprahīṇānāṃ tathāgatabhūmipratyātmāryajñānagatānaṃ yogināṃ bhāvābhāvasaṃjñā pravartate, sa evaiṣāmātmagrāhaḥ poṣagrāhaḥ puruṣagrāhaḥ pudgalagrāhaḥ syāt" / api ca, yadi paramārthataḥ syāt kimapi vastusat tadā tadavaśyaṃ nityaṃ vā anityaṃ vā syād, aparāyāḥ koṭerabhāvāt / tasmin vastūni nityānityatvacintayā pravṛttā yā prajñā, sā vastuno yathāsvabhāvajñānānukūlatayā samyak prajñaiva, na tu prajñāpāramiteva prativarṇikā / ata eva tathāgatena prajñāpāramitāyāṃ yaduktaṃ tenāpi virodhaḥ syāt / tathā hi - "kauśika, ye kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitāro vā yadā prajñāpāramitāmupadiśanti tadā prajñāpāramitāvadevopadiśanti / tatra te prajñāpāramiteva kurvanti / yato hi rūpamanityamityupadiśanti, tathaiva duḥkhatāṃ nirātmatāmaśucitāṃ copadiśanti / evameva vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārā vijñānaṃ skandhā dhātava āyatanāni dhyānāpramāṇārupānusmṛtisatmyakprahāṇārddhipādendriyabalabodhyaṅgāni tathāgatasya daśabalavaiśāradyapratisaṃvidāveṇīkā buddhadharmāḥ sarvākārajñatā ceti sarvaṃ duḥkhamanātmakaśucītyupadiśanti / evameva yadācaranti tadapi prajñāpāramitāyāmevācaranti / kauśika, tat prajñāpāramitāvadeva kurvanti / tatra ye prajñāpāramitāvanna kaurvanti tatkathamiti cet? te itthumupadiśantikulaputrāḥ, atrāgacchatha, prajñāpāramitābhāvanāyaṃ rūpamanityamiti mānupaśyatha, sarvākārajñatāparyantaṃ duḥkhatāṃ nirātmakatāmaśucitāṃ ca mānupapaśyatha / yatho hi rūpamitisvabhāvataḥ śūnyam, rūpasya yo 'pi svabhāvaḥ, sa [sarvathā] asan / yaccāsat saiva prajñāpāramitā / tasyāṃ nityamanityamiti nopalabhyate / yataśca yatrarūpameva nāsti tatra kuto nityamanityaṃ vāāa? sarvākārajñatāparyatantamitthameva / evaṃ ye hyupadiśanti te prajñāpāramitāvannopadiśanti /
body.translated_text: If the object of the cognition of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> were to become one with the characteristic of the ultimate, then how could that cognition be devoid of the category of existence? It is precisely for the purpose of removing the ground of fear for the childish that the object of noble cognition is taught as 'a real entity' — but not for the purpose of stating that a thing is real by its own characteristic in the ultimate. If this is not so, then <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> would not be free from connection with the concept of existence? Just as it was stated 'for the purpose of removing the ground of fear for the childish,' but not for the purpose of demonstrating that a thing is really real in the ultimate — so too the Blessed One has taught in other <s>sūtras</s>. Thus, in the <s>Ārya-Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra</s>: "O Blessed One, is it the case that, having dispelled the view of non-existence for sentient beings, you now cause the view of non-existence to fall again through attachment to the object of noble cognition and to the own-nature of entities, and effect the absence of teaching of the distinguished <s>dharma</s> through the teaching of the real nature of noble cognition?" The Blessed One said: "O <s>Mahāmati</s>, I do not effect the absence of teaching of the distinguished <s>dharma</s>, nor is the view of non-existence caused to fall through the indication of the noble real nature. Rather, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for the purpose of removing the ground of fear for sentient beings who from beginningless time have been attached to the characteristics of the own-nature of entities, I give the teaching of the distinguished <s>dharma</s> through the view characterized by attachment to the real nature of noble cognition — I do not, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, give a teaching of the own-nature of entities. Rather, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, they themselves will become dwellers in the distinguished <s>dharma</s>, having realized suchness for themselves" — thus at length. Therefore, what is indicated as the object of noble cognition in terms of the own-characteristic of a real thing — that is merely a teaching by the Blessed One's skillful means. Therefore, those who, without adopting the Blessed One's undoubted method of teaching, falsely construct [things] as having the nature of real entities — those conceited ones, having repudiated even the Blessed One, destroy themselves and destroy others as well. Thus, in this very <s>sūtra</s>, it is taught that those who are attached to the own-nature of entities, being grasped by the self-grasping, will not become liberated: "Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, having relied upon the establishment of the three means of valid cognition (<s>pramāṇatraya</s>), they will construct [the view] that the real thing, free from the two kinds of own-nature, personally realized by noble cognition, exists by its own nature. But, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for <s>yogīs</s> who have attained the stage of <s>Tathāgata</s> through personal noble cognition — whose mind, <s>manas</s>, <s>manovijñāna</s> have undergone the transformation of their basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>), who have abandoned the construction of grasped and grasper as mere appearances of their own mind — the notion of existence and non-existence of entities does not operate. That itself would be for them the grasping of self, the grasping of being, the grasping of person, the grasping of individual." Moreover, if something were to exist as a real entity in the ultimate, then it would necessarily be either permanent or impermanent, since there is no third alternative. In that case, the <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) that operates through the analysis of entities as permanent or impermanent would be correct <s>prajñā</s> itself, since it would accord with knowing the entity as it truly is — but not a counterfeit of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom). Hence there would be a contradiction with what the <s>Tathāgata</s> stated in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. For thus: "O <s>Kauśika</s>, when sons and daughters of good family teach the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, they teach the very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. There they practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself. For they teach that <s>rūpa</s> (form) is impermanent, and likewise they teach its suffering-nature, selflessness, and impurity. So too for <s>vedanā</s>, <s>saṃjñā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s>, <s>vijñāna</s>, the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, <s>dhyānas</s>, immeasurables, formless [absorptions], recollections, right efforts, bases of power, faculties, strengths, factors of awakening, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s ten powers, fearlessnesses, analytical knowledges, unique qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>, and omniscient knowledge — they teach all as suffering, selfless, and impure. Even when they practice thus, they practice in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> itself. O <s>Kauśika</s>, they practice the very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Now, how is it that some do not practice the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? They teach thus: 'O sons of good family, come here! In the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, do not view form as impermanent,' and up to omniscient knowledge, 'do not view suffering-nature, selflessness, and impurity.' For form is empty of own-nature; whatever own-nature of form — that is entirely non-existent. And that which is non-existent — that itself is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. In it, neither permanent nor impermanent is apprehended. For where form itself does not exist, how could there be permanence or impermanence? Likewise up to omniscient knowledge. Thus, those who teach in this way do not teach the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: apitvevamupadeṣṭavyam - kulaputrāḥ, atrāgacchatha, prajñāpāramitāṃ bhāvayatha mā ca kamapi dharmaṃ samatikramatha, mā ca kasmitrapi dharme tiṣṭhatha / tat kimarthamiti cet? prajñāpāramitāyāṃ nāsti ko 'ma dharmaḥ, yaḥ samatikramitavyaḥ, yatra vā sthātavyamiti / yato hi sarve dharmā svabhāvataḥ śūnyāḥ / ye svabhāvataḥ śūnyatā te 'santaḥ, saiva prajñāpāramitā / yā ca prajñāpāramitā, tasyāṃ na ko 'pi grāhyo heya utyādyo nirodhyaśceti / yadyevamupadiśanti tadā praġyāpāramitāvadevopadiśanti / ataḥ sarve vastuvādinastāvad dharmatathatāṃ viparītatayā nirdiśantyataḥ [tannirdeśaḥ] prajñāpāramitopadeśa iva prativarṇika eva / sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatāvādinastvaviparītatayā nirdiśantyataḥ sopattikā eva ta iti bhagavatā suspaṣṭaṃ nirdiṣṭam / ityevaṃ bhagavān tattatsūtre 'nekaśo 'śeṣadharman niḥsvabhāvatvenaivopadiṣṭavān / vistarabhiyā [asmābhiḥ] na bahunyapitu katapayānyevātroddhṛtāni / ata eva bhagavatā tāvadasandigdhaṃ samyakpravacananayamavadhāayitumaśaknuvatāṃ 'naiva tāvadāgamadvara sarve dharmā niḥsvabhāvatvena sādhayituṃ śakyāḥ' ityabhidadhatāṃ pratividhānamanuṣṭhitam / tatra yadyalpamatitayā evaṃvidhaṃ gambhīradharmatāṃ nādhimoktuṃ pārayanti tathāpi savikalpamātmano mandaprajñatvadosamavalokayadbhistatparityāgo naiva yujyate / ātmānaṃ vināśya pareṣāmapi mahārthavirahaṃ kṛtvā praṇāśo naiva samīcīnaḥ / evaṃ hi sati svaparadroha eva sa syāt / ataḥ prajñāvantaḥ śraddhāvantaśca gambhiradharmaparityādagṛṣṭiṃ parivarjya bhagavantaṃ pramāṇīkṛtya ātmano 'jñānadoṣakāraṇāt tadaparijñānaṃ sambhāvyata iti vicārya gambhīrasūtreṣu śraddhāmutpādya śravaṇacintābhāvanādiṣu yogaṃ kuryuḥ, parāṃścāpi samyak tadadhigantumavatārayeyuḥ, svayaṃ ca tadadhimoktuṃ praṇidadhyuriti / ata eva āryaratnakūṭasūtre proktam - "ye 'sya gambhīradharmasya gāmbhīrya prajñayā avaboddhumaśaknuvānāste tathāgatameva pramāṇaṃ kurvanti, anantā buddhobodhiriti kṛtvā / yataśca vividhādhimokṣānusāraṃ tathāgatā eva dharmopadeśe pravartante, atastathāgatā eva jānanti / nāsmādṛśairjñātuṃ śakyata iti vicārya tatparityāgo naiva yuktarūpaḥ" /
body.translated_text: Rather, one should teach thus: 'O sons of good family, come here! Cultivate the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, and do not transcend any <s>dharma</s>, nor abide in any <s>dharma</s>.' Why? In the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, there is no <s>dharma</s> that is to be transcended or in which one is to abide. For all <s>dharmas</s> are empty of own-nature. Those that are empty of own-nature are non-existent — that itself is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. And in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, nothing is to be grasped, abandoned, produced, or ceased." If one teaches thus, one teaches the very <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. Therefore, all proponents of real entities teach the <s>dharma</s>-suchness in a perverted manner, and hence their teaching is merely a counterfeit, like the counterfeit of the teaching of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. But those who teach the non-own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s> teach in a non-perverted manner, and hence they are authentic — thus the Blessed One has clearly taught. In this way, the Blessed One in this and that <s>sūtra</s> has taught all <s>dharmas</s> without exception as having no own-nature alone, in many ways. Out of fear of prolixity, we have cited here not many but only a few. Therefore, for those who, being unable to ascertain the Blessed One's undoubted method of correct teaching, declare 'it is simply not possible to establish all <s>dharmas</s> as without own-nature through scripture' — a refutation has been accomplished. If, due to their limited intelligence, they are unable to aspire to such profound <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality), even so, recognizing with discernment the fault of their own weak wisdom, they should not reject it. Destroying oneself and depriving others of great benefit and then perishing — that is simply not proper. For in that case, it would be nothing but harm to oneself and others. Therefore, those who are wise and faithful, having abandoned the view of rejecting the profound <s>dharma</s>, taking the Blessed One as authoritative, considering that their non-comprehension arises from the defect of their own ignorance, generating faith in the profound <s>sūtras</s>, should apply themselves to hearing, reflection, and meditation — and should also lead others to properly realize it, and themselves aspire to comprehend it. Hence it is stated in the <s>Ārya-Ratnakūṭa-sūtra</s>: "Those sons and daughters of good family who are unable to comprehend the profundity of this profound <s>dharma</s> by their wisdom — they should take the <s>Tathāgata</s> alone as authoritative, considering that the <s>Buddha</s>'s awakening is infinite. Since <s>Tathāgatas</s> themselves engage in the teaching of <s>dharma</s> in accordance with various aspirations, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> alone know [this]. It cannot be known by the likes of us — having considered thus, rejection [of the profound dharma] is simply not appropriate."

body.text: ityuvamāgamamukhena sarve dharmā niḥsvabhāvā eveti siddhā bhavanti /
body.translated_text: Thus, through the avenue of scripture (<s>āgama</s>), all <s>dharmas</s> are established as without own-nature.

body.text:
48
[3] ye 'pi tāvadutpattyādivibhāgaṃ dvayābhāsinā jñānenaiva kurvanti, na tu svasaṃvittimātreṇa, te dvayābhāsasya mithyātvena tadvyavasthāpitaḥ svabhāvo 'pi mithaivetyabhidadhate / tānadhikṛtyedānīmucyate -
body.translated_text: [Section 3] Now, those who make the distinction of arising and the like through cognition that appears as duality (<s>dvayābhāsin</s>) alone, and not through mere self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvitti</s>), declare that since the dual appearance is false, the own-nature established by it is also false. Addressing them, it is now stated —

body.text: yadi sarvadharmāṇāmutpādādidharmatā mithyājñānāvabhāsitatvena vyavasthāpyate, tadā kathaṃ sā paramārthasatī bhavet? dvayābhāso 'pi yadi mithyaiva tadā katajjñānarūpamavaśiṣyate yat khalu paramārthasad bhavet? anyattad vijñānaṃ grāhakākārarahitaṃ tadarvāgdarśibhiḥ nānubhavituṃ yujyate, sarveṣāṃ sarvadarśitvaprasaṅgāt / nānumānenāpi niścetuṃ śakyam, tathāvidhahetorevabhāvāt / tatra na tāvat svabhāvahetukamanumānaṃ sambhāvyate, tatsvabhāvasyaiva sādhyatvāt / na ca kāryaheturapi, yato hi kāmaṃ syāttadadvayaviruddhaṃ tathāpi tena kāryakāraṇabhāva eva na siddhaḥ, indriyānubhavātītatatvāt / na caitadvayatiriktamanyat kāryaṃ vidyate, tathā sati bhavanmatenādvayameva kāryaṃ syāt, kintu sādhyāvasthāpannatvānnaiva tat pramāṇaiḥ prasidhyati / yo hi dvayābhāsaḥ, sa tāvad śaśaśṛṅgavannaiva kāryam / ataśca pratyakṣānupalambhābhyāṃ sādhyabhūtasya kāryakāraṇabhāvasya siddhaye paramārthe 'dvayajñānena gṛhyamāṇaṃ kimapi nāsti / anupalabdherapi pratiṣedhasādhanatvānna bhavati sā sattvasiddhisādhikā / yathocyate kaiścit - yo hi yatsvabhāvaviruddhaḥ sa tatsvabhāvaviviktaḥ, yathā śītasvabhāvaviruddhamuṣṇatvaṃ śītasvabhāvaviviktam, tathā ca pratītiṣvabhāvo dharmī, dvayasvabhāvaviruddhatvāt, vyāpakaviruddhopalabdheḥ / na cāpi hetorāśrayāsiddhiḥ sāamānyasukhaduḥkhākāravedakasya dharmiṇo jñānākhyapratītisvabhāvena siddhatvāt / na ca svabhāvo 'pyasiddhaḥ, grāhyākārasya ekānekasvabhāvaviyogena asattve tadāśritaḥ parikalpito grāhakākāro 'pi niḥsvabhāva eva / na cāpi sarvābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ, kevalena kartukarmasvabhāvena kalpitatvānmithyaiva / naivātmanā ātmatvamityapi yujyate / yadi sāmānyena paramārthato dvayaviviktastvaṃ sādhayitumiṣyate tadā siddhasādhanameva, yato hi vayamapi paramārthato dvayasya mithyātvād viviktatvamevābhyupagacchāmaḥ / yadi hyabhāvasvabhāvaḥ khalu paramārthata ākāravirahitavijñānatvena sādhayitumiṣyate, tadāpi siddhasādhanameva, yato hi vayamapi paramārthataḥ sarvadharmāṇāmanutpannatvāt sarvavijñānāni tāvat paramārthato 'siddhāni dvayākārasuviyuktānītyabhyupagacchāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: If the <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality) of all <s>dharmas</s>, such as arising and the like, is established by virtue of appearing to false cognition, then how could it be real in the ultimate? If even the dual appearance is simply false, then what form of cognition remains that would be ultimately real? That other consciousness, devoid of the grasper-form, cannot be experienced by those of limited vision, since the absurd consequence would follow that everyone is omniscient. Nor can it be ascertained through inference (<s>anumāna</s>), because of the absence of a reason of that kind. In this regard, an inference based on the reason of own-nature (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>) is not possible, since the very own-nature [of that consciousness] is what is to be proved. Nor [is an inference] from the reason of effect (<s>kāryahetu</s>) [possible], for even if there were something contradictory to that duality, by that, the very causal relation would not be established, since it transcends sensory experience. Nor is there any other effect beyond this duality, for according to your position, only the non-dual would be the effect — but since it is in the state of being what is to be proved, it is simply not established by <s>pramāṇas</s> (valid means of knowledge). The dual appearance is like a hare's horn — it is simply not an effect. Therefore, through direct perception and non-apprehension, for the establishment of the causal relation of the object to be proved, nothing grasped by non-dual cognition exists in the ultimate. And since non-apprehension has the function of establishing negation, it cannot serve to establish existence. As some say: 'That which is contradictory to the own-nature of X is distinct from the own-nature of X — just as heat, being contradictory to the own-nature of cold, is distinct from the own-nature of cold. Likewise, the subject, the own-nature of cognition (<s>pratīti</s>), is [distinct] because of being contradictory to the own-nature of duality — through the apprehension of what contradicts the pervader.' Nor is there non-establishment of the basis of the reason (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>), since the subject is established as the own-nature of cognition (<s>pratīti</s>) that cognizes the general forms of pleasure and pain. Nor is the own-nature unestablished, since — when the grasped form is non-existent due to its separation from both the one and the many own-natures — the grasper-form, which is dependent upon and constructed from that, is also without own-nature. Nor is there the absurd consequence of the non-existence of everything, since [duality] is merely constructed by the own-nature of agent and action and is therefore simply false. Nor is it tenable that 'a self is not a self by itself.' If you wish to prove in general that [cognition] is free from duality in the ultimate sense, then this is merely establishing what is already established, since we too accept that, in the ultimate, duality is false and hence [everything is] free [from it]. If you wish to establish [consciousness] in the ultimate as devoid of form, having the nature of consciousness free of grasper-form — even that is merely establishing what is already established, since we too accept that, because all <s>dharmas</s> are ultimately unarisen, all consciousnesses are ultimately unestablished and free from the form of duality.

body.text: yadi vijñānākhyaṃ dharmiṇaṃ dvayaviyuktatvena vastusattvena ca sādhayitumiṣyate tadā dṛṣṭāntavayāsiddhatvādanaikāntikattvaṃ hetoḥ, bāhyārthasvabhāvānāṃ śītoṣṇīdīnāṃ samyagasiddhatvāt / ekasminneva jñāne jñānatadavabhāsayoravabhāsitatvena avirodho 'pi syādataḥ sādhyavikalaṃ dṛṣṭāntamapi syāditi / yadi vijñānaṃ dvayaviyuktaṃ sidhyati tadā tadbalena svabhāvasattvamapi sidhyatīti cet? durmatireṣā, sambandhābhāvāt / yaddhi dvayaviyuktaṃ tadavaśyaṃ samyag vastusaditi ko hyatra sambandhaḥ? yato hi yadi tannivartate tadānarthopasaṃhitaṃ pramāṇamapi nivartate / api ca, tathāvidhadṛṣṭānto 'pyasiddhaḥ / vandhyāputrādibhistena dvayena cāpyanaikāntikaḥ / tasmin dvaye nānyad dvayamapi sambhāvyate, anavasthāprasaṅgāt / śītādisparśaviyuktānāmūṣmādīnāṃ svabhāvavat dvayasvabhāvātiriktaḥ tadviyuktasvabhāvatvena siddhaḥ pratītisvabhāvabhinnastatsamānasvabhāvaḥ kaścidapi dharmī nāstyeva, dvayātmakasyaiva pratītisvabhāvatvāt / evaṃ hi anyavyaktinirapekṣaḥ san yaśca svayamevātmanābhivyajyate, sa pratītilakṣaṇaḥ / kāyabhūmiparvatanadī sāgarādayo vividhākārā ye pugato 'vabhāsamānā bāhyārthāste svayamevātmanā abhivyajyamānatvāt pratītisvabhāvātikrāntā eva pravartante /
body.translated_text: If you wish to establish the subject called 'consciousness' (<s>vijñāna</s>) as both free from duality and as a real entity — then the reason would be inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) due to the non-establishment of the example. For external objects with their own natures — cold, heat, and the like — are not properly established [in your system]. In a single cognition, since both the cognition and its appearance appear, there would be no contradiction — hence the example too would lack the property to be proved. If it is said that 'if consciousness is established as free from duality, then by its power, the real existence of its own-nature is also established' — this is poor reasoning, since there is no connection. What connection is there that whatever is free from duality must necessarily be a truly real entity? For if that [real existence] is eliminated, the <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid means of knowledge), which leads to a meaningful purpose, is also eliminated. Moreover, an example of that kind is also not established. It would be inconclusive due to the barren woman's son and the like, and also due to that duality [itself]. In that duality, no other duality can even be conceived, because of the absurd consequence of infinite regress. Just as heat and the like have an own-nature distinct from the own-nature of cold and the like [from which they are] separated — [there must be] some subject with a nature identical to [yet] different from the own-nature of cognition, established as having the nature of being distinct from duality. But no such [subject] exists at all, since the own-nature of cognition itself is of the nature of duality. For that which, independently of any other manifestation, manifests itself by itself — that has the characteristic of cognition. Bodies, grounds, mountains, rivers, oceans, and the like, which appear to people in various forms, precisely because they manifest themselves by themselves, operate as having transcended the own-nature of cognition.

body.text: evamapi ye mithyatmanā kuleṣu gṛheṣu ca pravṛttimācaranti, teṣāṃ svakāyopagūḍhadayitayā pratītisvabhāvāliṅganamiva ācaraṇād asaddvayasamāyogo 'yaṃ dūṣitatvānna viśvāsayogyaḥ / tathā ca dvayasvabhāvātmakāt priyatamād viyoge sati kimiva nānyena saha samāyogaḥ syādataḥ kevalamasyaiva dharmitvāvasthā naivopapadyate / phalataśca āśrayāsiddha evāyaṃ hetuḥ /
body.translated_text: Even so, those who conduct themselves in families and households with a false self — their conjunction with the non-existent pair is like embracing the <s>pratīti-svabhāva</s> (dependent nature) with a beloved clasped to one's own body; being vitiated, it is not worthy of trust. And when separated from the most beloved, which is of the nature of duality, what conjunction with another would there not be? Therefore, the very status of this as a property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) is simply not established. In effect, this reason is one whose basis is unestablished (<s>āśrayāsiddha</s>).

body.text: sautrāntikādayo 'pi jñānaṃ paramārthato dvayasvabhāvaṃ nāṅgikurvanti, aṃśābhāvena virodhāt / atastasyādvayasvabhāvasiddhyā kasya siddhiḥ, bāhyārthānāmapi tadaviruddhatvāt /
body.translated_text: Even the <s>Sautrāntikas</s> and others do not accept that consciousness is ultimately of dual nature, because of the contradiction due to the absence of parts. Therefore, through establishing the non-dual nature of that [consciousness], whose [existence] is established — since external objects too are not contradicted by that?

body.text: ye 'nyaiḥ pramāṇairbāhyārthā nirākriyanta iti bruvate, teṣāṃ jñānamapi kinna tathā / ye tāvat kartṛkarmabhāvāpekṣayā prajñaptatvānmithyaiveti kathayanti, tadapyanubhāvaviparītamiti /
body.translated_text: Those who say that external objects are refuted by other <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) — for them, why is consciousness not [refuted] likewise? Those who say that [objects] are merely false because they are designated in dependence on the agent-action relationship — that too contradicts experience.

body.text: bhavanto 'pi vijñānaṃ paramārthato 'dvayākāramevābhyupagacchanti / tathā sati ye nīlādivividhacittākārā bāhyārthatvena vijñāne 'vabhāsante te karmakartṛvyavahārānabhijñaiḥ kalpanādoṣavinirmukte citte spaṣṭato 'nubhūtā bhaviṣyantīti / vividhavastuviśeṣāpekṣayā ta upalakṣyanta iti cet? tasya tāvad viśeṣasya bālaparyantaṃ nāsti suspaṣṭāvabodhaḥ / yadi niyatadeśakālāvasthitasya tasyākārarāśeḥ tathāvidhaspaṣṭāvabhāsato bhinnānubhavo mithyaiveti bhavantaḥ svīrkunti tadā vimiktikāṃkṣiṇo bhavantaḥ tirobhūtadvayasvabhāvarahitātmakaṃ pratītisvabhāvaṃ viviktasvabhāvatvenābhiniviśya āsaktā eveti kimanyat / tadetadalpīyasaśchidrānnirgate 'pi vipulakāye hastini tatpucchāvarodhavaccirakālaṃ viduṣāmāścaryādbhutameveti / ataśca svatīkṣṇaprajñākhaḍgena tāmāsaktiṃ chittvā kaścana tādātmyalakṣaṇo vā tadutpattikṣaṇo vā sammbandhaḥ satyāsatyayoranyoparihārasthitalakṣaṇatvāt tādārmyavirodhaḥ asato 'pi na kutaścidapyutpattibhyupeyate / utpattau satyāmapi na yugapattādātmyenāvabhāso yujyate, kāryakāraṇayoḥ kālasvabhāvābhyāṃ bhinnatvāt / asambaddho niyatāvabhāso 'pi na yujyate, atiprasaṅgāt / ityevamavaśyaṃ kalpanābhinnasya asatsvabhāvākārāvabhāsasya svīkāraṇāt tallakṣaṇānvita evābhyupagantavyaḥ / ata ubhāvapi mithyaiva bhavataḥ / yadyevaṃ na syāt kathaṃ nāma mithyākārakalpanāsvabhāvoyostādātmyenānubhavo jāyeta / ataśca satyābhiveśapāśamutkhātamulaṃ kuruta / bhagavatāpi tāvaduktam - "yo hi dharmastathāgatenābhisambuddhaḥ, sa na satyaṃ nāpi mṛṣā" iti /
body.translated_text: You too accept that consciousness is ultimately of non-dual form alone. That being so, the various mental appearances of blue etc. that appear in consciousness as external objects — they will be clearly experienced in the mind free from the fault of conceptual construction by those who are not conversant with the conventions of agent and action. If you say: 'They are recognized with reference to the distinctions of various particular objects' — of that distinction, there is no perfectly clear understanding up to and including the childish. If you accept that the differentiated experience of that mass of appearances, established in a fixed place, time, and condition, appearing clearly in such a manner, is simply false — then, O you who desire liberation, you are merely attached, clinging to the <s>pratīti-svabhāva</s> (dependent nature) devoid of its vanished dual nature as being of an isolated nature. What else [can be said]? This is truly astonishing and wondrous to the learned for a long time — like trying to hold back the tail when even a huge elephant has emerged through a tiny hole! Therefore, cutting that attachment with the sharp sword of one's own wisdom — whether the relation is one characterized by identity (<s>tādātmya</s>) or one characterized by the moment of production (<s>tadutpattilakṣaṇa</s>) — between the true and false, since they are characterized by mutual exclusion, there is a contradiction with identity; and it is not accepted that the non-existent arises from anything whatsoever. Even when arising occurs, simultaneous appearance with identity is not justified, because cause and effect are different in time and nature. An unrelated fixed appearance is also not justified, because of over-extension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>). Thus, since the appearance of false-natured forms that are non-different from conceptual construction must necessarily be accepted, it must be accepted as endowed with that characteristic. Therefore, both [the true and the false] are simply false for you. If this were not so, how could an experience of identity arise from two things whose natures are conceptual construction of false forms? Therefore, uproot the snare of clinging to reality. The Blessed One too has stated: "Whatever <s>dharma</s> was fully awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, that is neither true nor false."

body.text: tadapi yuktibhirapi [sādhayitu] naiva śakyate / evaṃ katipayaiḥ pratyakṣaiḥ 'sarve dharmā viviktā' iti jñātumaśakyatvat / vastveva teṣāṃ viṣaya ityabhidadhānāstāvat praṣṭavyā kiṃ sarvesāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ yāni pratyakṣāṇi tāni sarvadharmanairātmyaṃ nāvaboddhauṃ samarthāni utāho ghanājñanatimiropahatamatiyanānāṃ bhavadṛśānāṃ pratyakṣāṇi nāvaboddhumiti / tatra prathamastāvat pakṣo naiva yujyate, pramāṇābhāvāt / sarveṣāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ pratyakṣāṇi na pravartanta iti niścāyakasya pramāṇasyābhāvāt /
body.translated_text: That too cannot be established even by reasoning. Since it is impossible to know through a few perceptions that 'all <s>dharmas</s> are isolated,' those who claim that entities are indeed their object should be asked: Are the perceptions of ALL persons unable to know the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, or are [only] the perceptions of those like you, whose intellects are afflicted by the darkness of dense ignorance, unable to know [it]? In that regard, the first option is simply not justified, for lack of a <s>pramāṇa</s>. Because there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> that can determine that the perceptions of all persons do not operate [to know selflessness].

body.text: svālambananivṛttimātraṃ tāvad bhrāntameva / yadi tadupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptasyānupalabdhirevāsattvena sādhyate / tadā yato hi kāraṇāt svenānupalambhaḥ, tasmin apravṛttijñānāṃ sarveṣāṃ strīpurusāṇāṃ cittasantatau pravartamānā yā cittapravṛtiḥ sā tāvānnaiva arvāgdarśināmupalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptāḥ, apareṣāṃ hi nivṛttyupalabdhirapyaniyatā / ataḥ prekṣāvatāṃ pratyakṣeṇa tajjñānaṃ naiva bhavatīti yaduktaṃ tanna yuktamiti /
body.translated_text: The mere cessation of one's own object is indeed erroneous. If non-apprehension of what has attained the characteristic of apprehension is to be established as non-existence — then, the reason from which there is non-apprehension by oneself, and the mental activity occurring in the mind-streams of all men and women who have no knowledge of non-operation regarding that [reason] — that indeed has not attained the characteristic of apprehension for those with limited vision; for others too, the non-apprehension leading to cessation is not fixed. Therefore, the statement that perceptual knowledge of that does not exist for the discerning is not justified.

body.text: atha dvitīyaḥ pakṣastadā siddhasādhanameva / vayamapi hi arvāgdarśibhistathāvidhasya tāvad gambhīradharmatattvasya pratyakṣato darśanaṃ naiva manyāmahe / yadyapi bhavādṛśāḥ khalu tathāvidhatatvāvabodhe 'samarthāstathāpi paramayoginaḥ, ye kalpairanekairaprameyapuṇyagjñānasambhārārjanaṃ kṛtvā anurūpakṛtsnopāyasamanvitāḥ bhūtārthabhāvanāprakarṣaparyantajamyajñānaprabhābhirnirastasamastāvaraṇāndhakārāsteṣaṃ pratyakṣeṇa tāvat sarvadharmanairātmyabodho bhavatyeveti kasmātra sambhavati / [viṣayam] amumadhikṛtya paścād yuktirapi pradarśayiṣyate /
