body.translated_text: If the second option [is chosen], then that is merely proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). For we too do not hold that those with limited vision can see such profound <s>dharma-tattva</s> (reality of dharmas) through direct perception. Although those like you are indeed unable to comprehend such reality, nevertheless, supreme <s>yogins</s>, who over countless eons have accumulated immeasurable stores of merit and wisdom, who are endowed with the full complement of appropriate methods, and whose darkness of all obscurations has been dispelled by the radiance of wisdom born from the culmination of the highest meditation on true meaning — for them, the knowledge of the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s> does indeed arise through direct perception. Why would this not be possible? Regarding this [very] subject, reasoning will also be demonstrated later.

body.text: vastuviṣayakāṇi pratyakṣāṇīti yaducyate naiva sidhyati / evamarvāgdarśināṃ yāni pratyakṣāṇi tāni timiropahatapratyakṣavad rupādimithyāviṣayakatvād vastusvabhāvaviṣayatvena samyagviṣayatvena vā tāvannaiva yujyante, anyathā sarveṣāṃ khalu tattvadarśitvaprasaṅgaḥ / buddhānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāyogināṃ cāpi jñānāni naiva tāvad vastuviṣayakatvena prasidhyanti, yasmānna taiḥ kaścanāpi aviparīto vastusvabhāvaḥ paridṛṣṭaḥ / āryabodhisattvasūtrapiṭake 'uyuktam -
body.translated_text: The claim that perceptions are directed toward real objects is not established. The perceptions of those with limited vision, like perception affected by an eye-disease, being directed at false objects such as form etc., are not justified as having the nature of a real entity as their object, or as having a correct object — otherwise there would be the absurd consequence that everyone is a seer of truth. The cognitions of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and great <s>yogins</s> too are not established as having real entities as their objects, since no undeluded real entity-nature whatsoever has been perceived by them. In the <s>Ārya-Bodhisattva-sūtra-piṭaka</s> it is stated:

body.text: yaduta sarve tairdharmā nisvabhāvāḥ aniruddhāḥ prakṛtyopaśāntāḥ atyantamajātāḥ atyantamabhūtāḥ atyantaparinirvṛtā eva dṛṣṭāḥ / taistāvad yena dṛṣṭaṃ tadapyanidarśanamavidarśanaṃ ca, yato hi tat samyagdarśanaṃ yathāvad yena dṛṣṭaṃ tadapyanirdarśanamavidarśanaṃ ca, yato hi tat samyagdarśanaṃ yathāvad darśanaṃ ceti / kiṃ punaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ yathāvad darśanamiti cet? tadeva yadanidarśanamiti /
body.translated_text: "All <s>dharmas</s> have been seen by them as essenceless, unceased, primordially peaceful, utterly unborn, utterly unreal, utterly and fully liberated. And what was seen by them — that too is non-demonstrable and non-observable, because that is correct seeing, seeing as it really is." What then is the seeing of all <s>dharmas</s> as they really are? It is precisely non-seeing.

body.text: āryadharmasaṅgītau nāma sūtre 'pyuktam -
body.translated_text: In the <s>sūtra</s> called <s>Ārya-Dharmasaṅgīti</s> (Noble Assembly of Dharmas) also it is stated:

body.text:
"sarvadharmāṇādarśanameva paramam darśanam" /
iti / ataḥ pratyakṣaviṣayāṇāṃ samyagvastutvaṃ na sidhyati /
body.translated_text: "Non-seeing of all <s>dharmas</s> is the supreme seeing." Therefore, the true reality of the objects of perception is not established.

body.text: yaddhi asad bhavati vastu, tanna kathamapi vijñānamutpādayituṃ kṣamamiti yaducyate, tadapi naiva yujyate / asmābhirapi tāvad śaśaśṛṅgasamebhyo 'vastubhyaḥ pratyakṣajñānotpādo naivābhyupagabhyate / tathāpi mahāyoginaḥ, ye marīcipratiśabdanibhān sarvadharmān yathāvad bhāvayanti, teṣu samyagarthabhāvanābalena prāntakoṭikadhyānāvāptito 'nuttarācintyaprabhāvasampannatayā tatpratyakṣeṣu sarvadharmanairātmyajñānaṃ bhavatyeva, aśeṣadharmanairātmsākṣātkāri suspaṣṭaṃ tāvajjñānamudetyeva / ata eva tat tattvādarśanamityabhidhīyate, na tu niṣedhyasvabhāvasyāsattvamiti /
body.translated_text: The claim that 'what is a non-existent entity cannot produce consciousness in any way' — that too is simply not justified. We too do not accept that direct perceptual knowledge arises from non-entities such as hare's horns. Nevertheless, for great <s>yogins</s> who properly meditate on all <s>dharmas</s> as similar to mirages and echoes, through the power of correct meditation on the true meaning, upon attaining the ultimate stage of meditation, being endowed with unsurpassed, inconceivable power — in their direct perception, the knowledge of the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s> does indeed arise; a perfectly clear cognition that directly realizes the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s> without exception does indeed arise. Therefore, that is called 'seeing of reality' — not [the claim] that the nature to be negated is non-existent.

body.text: atha yattāvat pratyakṣaṃ tat sasvabhāvamiti yaduktaṃ tat sarveṣāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpādaikarasatvat pratyakṣamapi paramārthato niḥsvabhāvameva, tathāpi yā saṃvṛtisatyāśritā pratyakṣavyavasthā sā sarvā tāvadavyāhayaiva / sarveṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ paramārthato niḥsvabhāvatve 'pi mādhyakāḥ sarvavyavahārāṇāṃ vyāvahārikāṇāṃ yogijñānānāmapareṣāṃ pṛthagjanajñānānām āryapudgalādīnāṃ ye hetavastātānnaiva nābhyupagacchanti, kintuṃ ye tāvat saṃvṛtito 'pyahetukāste khalu vyavahārato 'pyanutpannā eva, śaśaśṛṅgavat / yat sat tat paramārthato niḥsvabhāvamapi tāvadutpadyate, māyāpratibinbādivat / māyādīnāṃ sarveṣāṃ pratītyasamutpannatve 'pi nāsti vastutāprasaṅgaḥ, sādhakabādhakapramāṇabādhitatvāt /
body.translated_text: The claim that 'whatever is directly perceived has own-nature' — since all <s>dharmas</s> are of the single taste of non-arising, perception too is ultimately essenceless. Nevertheless, all the conventional determinations of perception remain completely uncontradicted. Even though all <s>dharmas</s> are ultimately without own-nature, the <s>Mādhyamikas</s> do not fail to accept all conventional activities — the causes of <s>yogic</s> cognitions, the cognitions of other ordinary persons, the <s>Ārya-pudgalas</s> (Noble persons), and the like. But what does not have a cause even conventionally — that indeed is unarisen even from the conventional standpoint, like a hare's horn. What exists arises even though ultimately without own-nature — like an illusion, reflection, and the like. Even though all illusions etc. are dependently arisen, there is no absurd consequence of their being real entities, because they are contradicted by <s>pramāṇas</s> that establish and negate.

body.text: tathaiva pratītyasamutpannatve 'pi sarvadharmāṇāṃ nāsti vastutāprasaṅgaḥ pramāṇabādhitatvāta / yathaiva hi mantroṣadhādiprabhāveṇa gajādivividhamāyāprādurbhāvastathaiva karmakleśādiprabhāveṇ sattvānāmutpādādayaḥ prādurbhavanti / yagināṃ tāvat svakīyapuṇyajñānasambhārasañcayavaśena yogijñānādimāyāprādurbhāvaḥ, yato hi vividhairhi pratyayaiḥ sā māyāpi vividhaivāvabhāsate /
body.translated_text: Likewise, even though all <s>dharmas</s> are dependently arisen, there is no absurd consequence of their being real entities, because they are contradicted by <s>pramāṇas</s>. Just as varied magical appearances of elephants etc. arise through the power of mantras, herbs, and the like, so too the arising etc. of beings occurs through the power of <s>karma</s> (action), <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), and the like. For <s>yogins</s>, the magical appearance of <s>yogic</s> knowledge etc. [occurs] through the power of their accumulated stores of merit and wisdom, because that illusion too appears in varied forms through various conditions.

body.text: āryaprajñāpāramitāsūtre 'uyuktamḥ "kaścichrāvakanirmitaḥ [kaścit pratyekabuddhanirmitaḥ] kaścid bodhisattvanirmitaḥ kaścit tathāganitmitaḥ kaścit karmanirmitaḥ / anena subhūte, paryāyeṇa sarvadharmā nirmitotpannā iti" /
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Prajñāpāramitā-sūtra</s> it is stated: "Some [<s>dharmas</s>] are created by <s>Śrāvakas</s>, [some by <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>,] some by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, some by <s>Tathāgatas</s>, some by <s>karma</s>. By this method, O <s>Subhūti</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are creation-arisen."

body.text: bālapṛthagjanebhyastāvad yogināmetadeva vaiśiṣṭayaṃ yatte māyākāra iva yathāvanmāyāṃ parijānanti, na ca tathaiva tasyāmabhiniviśante /
body.translated_text: The very distinction of <s>yogins</s> from childish ordinary beings is this: they understand <s>māyā</s> (illusion) as it really is, like a magician, but do not cling to it in the same way.

body.text: āryadharmasaṅgītāvapyuktamḥ
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Dharmasaṅgīti</s> also it is stated:

children.translated_text: "Just as a magician, [seeing] a creation, is intent on liberation,

children.text: na cāsya nirmite saṅgo jñātapūrvo yato 'sya saḥ //
children.translated_text: And has no attachment to that creation, because he has known it from before —
Knowing the three realms as similar to a creation, one who has crossed to awakening
Girds himself for the sake of the world, having known the world from before."

body.text: yathā bālapṛthagjanajātīyadarśakeṣu utpattyādimāyabhāso bhavati, tathaiva ye tasmin satyato 'bhiniviśante, te viparītābhiniveśavaśād "bālāḥ" ityabhidhīyante / ataḥ saṃvṛtiyogahini yogipratyakṣe tathā sthitatvātteṣāṃ śaśaśṛṅga ivātyantābhāvo naiva bhavati / ata eva pratyakṣato 'śeṣadharmanairātmajñānaṃ tāvat sadeva / avirodho 'pi tata eveti / paramārthato niḥsvabhāvatve 'pi yoginaḥ pṛthagjana iva vyavahāratayā vyavasthāpayanti /
body.translated_text: Just as the appearance of arising etc. is like an illusion for those who see with the vision of childish ordinary beings, so too those who cling to it as real — through their clinging to what is inverted, they are called 'childish.' Therefore, since [appearances] exist in that way within the <s>yogic</s> perception that accords with the conventional, their utter non-existence like a hare's horn simply does not obtain. Therefore, the knowledge of the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s> without exception through direct perception does indeed exist. Non-contradiction too [follows] from this very point. Even though ultimately without own-nature, <s>yogins</s> establish [things] conventionally, just like ordinary persons.

body.text: āryaparamārthasaṃvṛtisatyanirdeśasūtre tāvaduktamḥ
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Paramārthasaṃvṛtisatyanirdeśa-sūtra</s> (Noble Sūtra Teaching the Two Truths) it is stated:

body.text: "paramārthato 'tyantābhāvaśca saṃvṛtyā ca mārgaṃ bhāvayatīti kathanavat" 'yadarthāntaraviviktapākṣikena pratyakṣeṇa parigṛhya taditaraśūnyapratyakṣeṇa tāvadavabudhyate' - ityādikaṃ yaduktaṃ tadapi naiva yujyate, itaretaraśūnyatvādasya nayasya, na tu lakṣaṇaśūnyatvāditi / lakṣanaśūnyatve u sarve dharmāstāvat paramārthato niḥsvabhāvatvenaivābhyupagamyante, yatasteṣāṃ svasāmānyalakṣaṇāni paramārthato yathā vyavasthitāni, tebhyastacchūnyatvāt /
body.translated_text: "[One is] utterly non-existent in the ultimate, yet conventionally cultivates the path" — like such a statement. The claim that 'grasping by a partisan perception that excludes other objects, one understands through a perception that is empty of anything else' — that too is not justified, because this approach is based on mutual emptiness (<s>itaretaraśūnyatā</s>), not on emptiness of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>). In the case of emptiness of characteristics, all <s>dharmas</s> are accepted as ultimately without own-nature, because their particular and general characteristics, as they are conventionally established, are empty of that [ultimate reality].

body.text: yā hi vastūnāmitaretaraśūnyatā sā naiva paramārthaḥ, vyavahārasatyamāśritā khalu sā / ityevamanutpādarasaikatve 'pi sarvadharmāṇāṃ naiva bhedābhāvaḥ, tathāpi svapnādyavasthādivad bāleṣu parasparabhinnānyavabhāsante / ata evātra yathāprasiddhimarthāntaraviviktagrahaṇamukhena tāvaditaretaraśūnyatā vyavasthāpyate, na tu paramārthatayā / yato hi svapnamāyādisadṛśavastūnāṃ svabhāvaḥ paramārthataḥ parasparamabhinnaḥ / ata eva bhagavatābhihitam -
body.translated_text: The mutual emptiness of entities is not the ultimate; it is dependent on conventional truth. Thus, even though all <s>dharmas</s> are of the single taste of non-arising, there is no absence of differentiation. Nevertheless, like the state of dreams and the like, they appear to the childish as mutually distinct. Therefore, according to what is commonly known, mutual emptiness (<s>itaretaraśūnyatā</s>) is established through the approach of grasping objects as distinct from one another — but not as ultimate reality. Because the own-nature of entities similar to dreams, illusions, and the like is ultimately not mutually different. Therefore the Blessed One has stated:

body.text: paramārthamanāśritatveneyaṃ sarvataḥ pratikruṣṭeti parivarjanīyaiva / āryalaṅkāvatārasūtre tāvaduktam ḥ
body.translated_text: Being not dependent on the ultimate, this [mutual emptiness] is repudiated on all sides and should be abandoned. In the <s>Ārya-Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra</s> it is stated:

body.text: "evaṃ mahāmate, itaretaraśūnyatā sarvajaghanyā, sā ca tvayā parivarjayitavyā" /
body.translated_text: "Thus, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, mutual emptiness (<s>itaretaraśūnyatā</s>) is the lowest of all; it should be abandoned by you."

body.text: yā khalu sarvadharmalakṣaṇaśūnyatā, yā ca tasyāḥ svasāmānyakakṣaṇavyavasthā, sā upalabdhilakṣaṇaprāptāpi satī yogibhiḥ paramārthatayā anupalabdhākāraiva / ataḥ sarve dharmā nirābhāsajñānotpattyā jñātā bhavantīti vyavasthāpyate / ata eva ca itaretaraśūnyatā bālapṛthagjanānāṃ parikalpanāmaśrityaivābhihitā, asambadhaiva caiṣā /
body.translated_text: The emptiness of the characteristics of all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>lakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>) and the determination of its particular and general characteristics — even though attaining the characteristic of apprehension, that is perceived by <s>yogins</s> as having the form of non-apprehension from the standpoint of ultimate reality. Therefore, it is established that all <s>dharmas</s> are known through the arising of knowledge free from appearance (<s>nirābhāsa-jñāna</s>). And for this very reason, mutual emptiness is stated only in dependence on the conceptual constructions of childish ordinary beings, and is indeed unconnected [with the ultimate].

body.text: sā ca 'yogipratyakṣeṇa samyagavagamye' ti kathanaṃ naiva viduṣāṃ rucikaram / yuktyabhāvastatreti yat kathanaṃ tadapi nāsti yuktisaṅgatam, yuktīnāṃ tāvad saṃvidyamānatvāt /
body.translated_text: The claim that 'this is properly understood through <s>yogic</s> perception (<s>yogipratyakṣa</s>)' is not pleasing to the wise. The claim that there is no reasoning [to support it] — that too is not logically coherent, since reasoning indeed exists.

body.text: vidvāṃsaḥ kalpanāpoḍhamabhrāntamiti pratyakṣalakṣaṇaṃ samudīrayanti / arthābhāve 'pi bhāvanābalena arthavabhāsi suspaṣṭaṃ jñānamutpadyāte / tathāhi - yathā kāmaśokabhayonmādādyupahateṣu asakṛdabhāsabalena pramadādyavabhāsi spaṣṭaṃ jñānamupajāyate yena te tān puraḥsthitaniva dṛṣṭvā sahasā vividhaśarīrakampādibhiśceṣṭamānā dṛśyante /
body.translated_text: The learned define the characteristic of perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) as 'free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>) and non-erroneous (<s>abhrānta</s>).' Even in the absence of an [external] object, through the power of meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), a cognition arises that clearly appears as if an object — vivid and distinct. For example, just as in those afflicted by desire, grief, fear, madness, and the like, through the force of repeated [mental] appearance, a vivid cognition arises that appears as a woman and so forth, whereby they are seen suddenly behaving with various bodily trembling and the like, as if they were seeing [those objects] present before them.

body.text: ataśca yathoktatatvaṃ bhāvayatsu tajjñanamutpatsyata eveti sambhāvyate / yacca spaṣṭāvabhāsi jñānaṃ tannunaṃ nirvikalpakameva, kalpanāvāyuprakampitakāyākārasya suapaṣṭamanupapannatvāt, pradīpavat /
body.translated_text: Therefore, it is plausible that for those who meditate on the truth as described, that knowledge will indeed arise. And that cognition, which appears vividly, is certainly non-conceptual (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>), because a clear [appearance] of the form of the body shaken by the wind of conceptual construction is not tenable — like a lamp [whose flame is steady when undisturbed by wind].

body.text: prayogaḥ - ye tāvat kecinnirantaraṃ sādaraṃ bhāvanāmanutiṣṭhanti, te bhāvanāphalaṃ prakarṣaparyantajaṃ sfuṭāvabodhamanubhavantyeva, rāgādyupahataiḥ pramadādibhāvanāvat / yatra cirakālaṃ nirantaraṃ sādaraṃ sarvadharmanairātmyabhāvanaṃ svabhāvahetuḥ, tatra pramāṇopapannārthavisayakamavisaṃvādakaṃ [jñānaṃ] bhavatyeva, vyavahāreṇa dhūmādiliṅgajanitaniścayenotpannāgnyādijñānavat / yogināṃ khalu tannairātmajñānamapi pramāṇopapannārthaviṣayakamiti svabhāvahetuḥ /
body.translated_text: The formal argument: Those who continuously and earnestly practice meditation experience the fruit of meditation — vivid realization arising at the culmination of [meditative] intensity — just as those afflicted by desire and the like [experience vivid appearances] through meditation on women and so forth. Where there is continuous, earnest, long-term meditation on the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s> (<s>sarvadharma-nairātmya</s>), the reason is intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvahetu</s>); there, a cognition that is non-deceptive (<s>avisaṃvādaka</s>) and whose object is supported by valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) indeed arises — just as, conventionally, knowledge of fire and the like arises from the certainty produced by inferential marks (<s>liṅga</s>) such as smoke. That knowledge of selflessness in <s>yogins</s> too has as its object what is supported by valid means of knowledge — this is the reason of intrinsic nature.

body.text: asya pramāṇopapannatvaṃ paścāt prakāśayiṣyate / spaṣṭāvabhāsamānaṃ sad yajjñānamavisaṃvādaṇaṃ janayati tat pratyakṣaṃ pramāṇam, rupādivyavahārārthamanupahatacakṣuṣāṃ cakṣuvirjānādivat, sarvadharmanairātmyaviṣayakaṃ yogināṃ jñānamapi spaṣṭāvabhāsamānaṃ sad avisaṃvādakamiti svabhāvahetuḥ / yadyevaṃ sarvadharmanairātmyajñānaṃ yuktibhiḥ susādhyaṃ tadā kathamiva vidvāṃsastatra na pritāḥ? yadapi yogijñānaṃ tadasaditi yaducyate, tatpūrvamasmābhiḥ samyaguttaritam, sarvadharmāṇāṃ śaśaśṛṅgavadatyantābhāvasyābhāvāt / tathāpi paramārthatasteṣāmabhāva eva māyāvat / ato naivāsmābhiḥ sarve vyavahārāstāvanniṣidhyante, na ca te 'smābhirnābhyupeyanta iti yaduktaṃ tattathā /
body.translated_text: That it is supported by valid means of knowledge will be demonstrated later. A cognition that appears vividly and is existent, and which generates a non-deceptive [awareness], is perceptual valid cognition — like the visual cognition and so forth of those with unimpaired eyesight, for the purpose of conventional dealings with form and the like. The knowledge of <s>yogins</s> too, whose object is the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, appears vividly and, being existent, is non-deceptive — this is the reason of intrinsic nature. If the knowledge of the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s> is thus well-established through reasoning, how could the learned not be pleased with it? As for the statement that yogic cognition is unreal — that was properly answered by us earlier, since the absolute non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s> like a hare's horn is not the case. Nevertheless, in the ultimate, they are indeed non-existent, like a magical illusion (<s>māyā</s>). Therefore, we do not negate all conventions whatsoever, nor do we not accept them — what was said to that effect is correct.

body.text: yaistāvat "anumānenāpi sarvavastuni niḥsvabhāvatvena sādhayitumaśakyāni, kasyāpi dharmino viṣayasyāsiddhatvāt, dṛṣṭāntādīnāṃ cānutpannatāvat, sarvasāṃ yuktīnāṃ viṣayasya svabhāvasya cāsiddhatvāt" ietyavamuktam, tadapyasambaddhameva /
body.translated_text: As for the statement 'Even through inference, things cannot be established as essenceless in their entirety, since the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) is not established for any [entity], since examples and the like are unborn, and since the object and intrinsic nature of all reasons are unestablished' — that too is entirely incoherent.

body.text: itthamasmābhirniḥsvabhāvatvenābhyupete sati yadā bhavantaḥ prasaṅgamāpādayanti tadā sa prasaṅga eva nāsti /
body.translated_text: When, given that we accept essencelessness, you [opponents] raise an absurd consequence (<s>prasaṅga</s>) — that very absurd consequence does not arise.

body.text: yaiḥ khalu hetubhirasmābhirvastūnāṃ niḥsvabhāvatābhyupeyate, tatra paramārthato hetudṛṣṭāntadharmiṇāmasattvād yadyanumānānumeyādisarvavyavahārābhāvaprasaṅgo 'smāsvāpādyate, tadā sa prasaṅga eva na bhavati, iṣṭāpatteḥ / yato vayamapi anumānānumeyādisarvavyavahārādīnāṃ paramārthato 'pravṛtibhyupagacchāmaḥ / phalataḥ kathamiva tāvattadabhāvaprasaṅga āpatediti / asvīkaraṇaṃ hi nāma prāṅgalakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: By the very reasons through which we accept the essencelessness of entities, since the logical reason, example, and subject do not truly exist in the ultimate — if the absurd consequence is imposed upon us that there would be no conventional dealings of inference, the inferable, and so forth — that consequence simply does not arise, because what follows is already accepted (<s>iṣṭāpatti</s>). For we too accept that all conventional dealings such as inference, the inferable, and so forth do not operate in the ultimate. Consequently, how could the absurd consequence of their non-existence befall [us]? For non-acceptance [of what is alleged as a fault] is the very definition of a <s>prasaṅga</s> [being inapplicable].

body.text: vayaṃ tāvad bhavadbhiḥ prayuktaṃ dūṣṇamapi paramārthato 'nutpannamevābhyupagacchāmaḥ / ato nāsti ko 'pi doṣāvasaraleśaḥ / ata evācāryapādaiḥ -
body.translated_text: We accept that even the objection raised by you [against us] is, in the ultimate, simply unborn. Therefore, there is not the slightest occasion for any fault. This is precisely why the master [<s>Nāgārjuna</s>] said:

children.translated_text: "If I had any thesis whatsoever, then I would be at fault;
but since I have no thesis, I am not at fault." [<s>Vigrahavyāvartanī</s> 29]

body.text: ityaktam / yat paramārthato 'sat tad vyavahāre 'pi pravartituṃ na śakyata ityevaṃ yo hi prasaṅgaḥ, sa prasaṅga eva na bhavati, vyāptyasiddheḥ / yato hi yena kāraṇena yasyātmanivartanaṃ tena tasya vyavahāranivartanaṃ tu nāsti paramārthasvabhāvavyāptam, api tu tadviparyayavyāptamiti / vyavahārastu paramārthato 'bhāvasvabhāva eva / paramārthasvabhāvavirāhitā api svapnādayo vividhavyavahāreṣu pravartamānā dṛśyante / ataḥ sarve 'pi tāvad vyavahārā nirmāṇasvapnādivadaviruddhā eva /
body.translated_text: Thus it is said. The <s>prasaṅga</s> that 'what is non-existent in the ultimate cannot function even in convention' — that <s>prasaṅga</s> simply does not hold, because the invariable concomitance (<s>vyāpti</s>) is not established. For the cessation of something's own nature through a certain cause does not entail its cessation in convention — [convention] is not pervaded by having an ultimate intrinsic nature; rather, it is pervaded by the opposite of that. Convention itself has the nature of ultimate non-existence. Even dream [experiences], illusions, and the like, devoid of ultimate intrinsic nature, are seen to operate in various conventional dealings. Therefore, all conventions are simply non-contradictory, like magical creations, dreams, and the like.

children.translated_text: "Just as a magical creation [refutes] a magical creation, or a magical person [refutes] a person created by his own magic —
in precisely that way should this refutation be [understood]." [<s>Vaidalyaprakaraṇa</s>]

body.text: sarvatra sādhyadharmyādīnāṃ paramārthabhūtatvādeva anumānādivyavahārāḥ pravartanta iti hetoḥ paramārthato niḥsvabhāvatve sati nānumānādivyavahārāḥ pravartsyanta iti yo hi doṣa āropyate, so 'pi tāvad doṣābhāva eva / nirvivādarūpatayā saprasaṅgatvāt paramārtadharmyādibhiḥ anumānādivyavahārāḥ kutrāpi naiva siddhāḥ, tathāpi loke yathāprasiddha eva dharmiṇi vyavahārā bhavanti / yato hi pravādino hi tattvānirṇayārthameva anumānādivyavahārān prayuñjanti / yathoktam -
body.translated_text: The charge that 'the conventional dealings of inference and so forth operate only because the subject and so forth of the thesis are ultimately real' — and therefore 'if things are essenceless in the ultimate, conventional dealings of inference and so forth would not operate' — that too is not a fault at all. Since the form is beyond dispute, and since [the charge] entails a <s>prasaṅga</s>, conventional dealings of inference and the like are never established anywhere through an ultimately real subject and so forth. Even so, in the world, conventions operate regarding the subject just as it is commonly known. For debaters employ conventional dealings of inference and the like precisely for the purpose of ascertaining the truth. As it is said:

children.translated_text: "The establishment of property (<s>dharma</s>) and property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>), and whatever distinction and non-distinction [exists],
just as it is conventionally accepted in the world, without examining the ultimate meaning —
relying on that very [convention], the structure of what is to be proved and the means of proof
is constructed by the learned for the purpose of entering into the ultimate."
Furthermore: "This structure of the knowable, the means of knowing, and the result [of knowing]
is set up in accordance with observation, even though existing, for the cognitions of grasped and grasper."
"Otherwise, how could the aspects of a single entity that appears in multiple forms
be real, since the unity of that [entity] would be lost?"

body.text: idaṃ tāvad vyavahārikapramāṇalakṣaṇamityapi kathyate / pramāṇasya tāvat sarvāṇi lakṣaṇāni tattvapravṛtyarthameva bhavanti, anyathā vyarthānyeva tāni syuriti / pramāṇalakṣaṇaśāstrāṇyanadhīyānāsu gopālakāṅganāsu evamupadeśābhāve 'pi dhūmādiliṅgadarśanato 'gnyādīnāṃ jñānamutpadyata eva / ata eva vayamapi tattvapraveśāya tathatāvyavahārābhyāmanumānādipravartanād doṣarahitā eva /
body.translated_text: This much is also stated as the definition of valid cognition at the conventional level. All definitions of valid cognition serve the purpose of engaging with the truth; otherwise they would be entirely pointless. Even among cowherd women who have not studied the treatises on the definition of valid cognition, without such instruction, knowledge of fire and the like arises simply from seeing inferential marks like smoke. Therefore, we too are entirely free from fault in employing inference and the like through the conventions of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) for the purpose of entering into the truth.

body.text: api ca, ye vyavahāreṇānumānādipravṛttau yatrānityādi vastudharmaṃ satsvabhāvaṃ sādhayanti, teṣāṃ niḥsaṃśayaṃ tatra vyavahāreṇa vastubhūtadharmādayaḥ syureva, yato hi tatra tathāvidhā āśrayahīnā sādhyadisthitirnaiva siddhā /
body.translated_text: Moreover, those who, through conventional inference and the like, establish a real entity-property (<s>vastudharma</s>) with an existent intrinsic nature — for them, undoubtedly, the subject and other [elements] would indeed be real things in that convention, since for them, such a basis-less (<s>āśrayahīna</s>) establishment of the thesis and the like is simply not valid [without a real subject].

body.text: yadi tatra tathāvidha āśrayo nāsti tadā sādhyaniṣedhanād āśrayā siddhyākhyo doṣo dīyate / so 'pi yadi yathābhūtadharmiṇo nivṛttiścettadā niḥsaṃśayaṃ sādhyādidharmiṇo 'vinābhāvasya niṣedhaṃ karoti, yato hi asiddhe sati hetvasiddhayādidoṣā dīyante / svayamupakalpitānāṃ katipayadharmiṇāṃ nivṛttāvapi sādhayādeḥ kasyāpi niṣedhasyābhāvād asiddhayādidoṣā naiva yujyante, tadabhilaṣitārthasiddhau bādhābhāvāt / ye vastudharmaṃ sattsvabhāvaṃ sādhayituṃ nābhilaṣante, api tu tadāropitadharmāṇāṃ vyavacchesiddhimātraṃ vivakṣante, tebhyo 'siddhayādidoṣānāpādayituṃ vyavahāre 'pi vastubhūtadharmī naivāvaśyakaḥ, tasya taddharmābhāvāt /
body.translated_text: If such a basis does not exist there, then the fault called 'unestablished basis' (<s>āśrayāsiddhi</s>) is incurred through the negation of the thesis. If that [fault] is the withdrawal from a genuinely [real] subject, then undoubtedly it negates the invariable concomitance of the subject of the thesis and the like; for when [the basis] is unestablished, faults such as 'unestablished reason' are incurred. But when merely a few subjects constructed by oneself are withdrawn, there is no negation of the thesis or anything else — so faults such as 'unestablished [reason]' simply do not apply, since there is no obstruction to the establishment of one's desired meaning. For those who do not desire to establish a real entity-property with an existent intrinsic nature, but wish only to establish the exclusion (<s>vyavaccheda</s>) of imposed properties — for them, even in convention, a real entity-subject is by no means necessary, since it lacks that property.

body.text:
tadapekṣayāpi taddharmitā nopapadyate / tadasiddhāvapi sādhyāvinābhāvī heturabhiṣṭārthasādhakaḥ, bādhakābhāvāt / vādino 'bhīṣṭārthasiddhau prativādina upaghātakāmanayā dharmiṇaḥ sadasattvamanveṣayanti, na tu kāmacārataḥ / dharmiṇo 'sattvādicarcayāpi kim? yadi vādino 'bhiṣṭārthahānirna syāt / 'codako doṣahīnaḥ' ityapi kathanaṃ viparyayadoṣāṇuparipūrite paridhāvanamātrameva, anyatrābhāvāt / ata eva sādhyadharmaṃ tadanukūladharmiṇaṃ cāvagantuṃ pakṣalakṣaṇavelāyāmeva yuktividbhirviśeṣeṇa 'svadharma' ityabhidhīyate /
evaṃ yastāvat svakāryāṇi yugapanna sādhayati, sa na bhavatyapratihatanityaikasvabhāvaḥ, vandhyāputravat / parairiṣṭamākāśādikamapi śabdādikāryaṃ na sādhyatīti vyāpakānupalabdhi, ityabhihite 'yaṃ tāvanna viruddhaheturapītī kecit / sādhyasādhanayoriva ākāśādirnaiva vastubhūtaḥ svabhāvadharmīti sādhanabhūto 'yaṃ heturāśrayāsiddha ityapare / tatrāpi ākāśadidharmiṇāṃ vastutāyāḥ kṛte 'pyatra nirākaraṇe sādhyābhāvamātramabhyupagacchatāṃ nāsti ko 'pi doṣaḥ, hetvabhāvamātreṇa ca nasti svabhāvo 'pyasiddhaḥ, vastutāyā abhāve 'pi dharmiṇāṃ siddheḥ / ato vipratipattinirākaraṇāya svābhimatadharmyeva yadi bādhyate cettadā sādhya eva tāvanniṣedhyo bhavati, na tu dharmāntarayukto dharmītyevaṃ nirdeśakāle sveṣṭapratyakṣānumānāptaprasiddhidvārā niṣedhamavidhāya svabhāvasyaiva tāvanniṣedhaḥ svadharmī bhavatītyatra pakṣadharmatāvasthāyāmācāryeṇa svadharmī kathita iti vārtikakāraḥ / tathāhiḥ
body.translated_text:
Even in relation to that [subject], its status as subject is not tenable. Even when that [subject] is unestablished, a reason that is invariably concomitant (<s>avinābhāvin</s>) with the thesis proves the desired meaning, since there is no invalidating cognition (<s>bādhaka</s>). When the proponent's desired meaning is established, the opponent seeks to investigate the existence or non-existence of the subject through a strategy of undermining — not arbitrarily. And what [good] is the discussion about the non-existence of the subject if the proponent's desired meaning is not undermined? The statement 'the objector is free from fault' too is merely a running about over faults of inversion that have not been thoroughly examined — since it is absent elsewhere. Therefore, in order to understand the property to be proved and the subject conforming to it, those skilled in reasoning specifically designate it as '<s>svadharma</s>' (own-property) at the stage of defining the thesis.
Thus, [the argument:] 'That which does not simultaneously produce its own effects is not of unobstructed, permanent, unitary intrinsic nature — like the son of a barren woman. Space and the like, as imagined by others, do not produce effects such as sound' — this is the non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>). When this is stated, some say: 'This is indeed not a contradictory reason.' [Others say:] 'Since space and the like are not a real-entity subject of intrinsic nature, like the thesis and what proves it, this reason as a means of proof is [faulty due to] unestablished basis.' In that case too, for those who accept merely the absence of what is to be proved when the reality of subjects like space and the like is negated — there is no fault whatsoever, and the intrinsic nature is not unestablished merely through the absence of the reason, since subjects are established even in the absence of reality. Therefore, to remove disagreement, if one's own accepted subject itself is invalidated, then it is precisely the thesis that is negated — not the subject qualified by some other property. Thus, at the time of specification, without making a negation through one's own accepted perception, inference, or reliable testimony, the negation of intrinsic nature itself becomes the 'own-property subject' — at this stage of the thesis-property, the master [<s>Dharmakīrti</s>] stated 'own-property subject.' This [is explained by] the <s>Vārttikakāra</s> (sub-commentator). For thus:

children.translated_text: "Everywhere, the property that the proponent desires as his own thesis —
invalidation would apply to the subject having that property, not through some other property of the subject."

body.text: anyathāsyoparodhaḥ ko bādhite 'nyatra dharmiṇi /
body.translated_text: "Otherwise, what impediment [would there be] when the subject is invalidated elsewhere?"

body.text: iti vastaraḥ / vipratipattinirākaraṇārthaṃ coktamḥ
body.translated_text: Thus [it is explained] in detail. And for the purpose of removing disagreement, it is said:

children.translated_text: "Just as, by others, [it is argued:] space and the like are not of a previously non-existent form,
since they are not causes of sound, etc. [produced] all at once — thus the objector states:"
"Likewise, [if you say] space and the like, not being real-entity intrinsic nature, are not the subject —"
"there is no invalidation whatsoever of the desired thesis [in this way]."
"For when both [subject and property] are to be proved, whatever invalidation opposes the property of the thesis,
that is described by this [verse] as 'invalidation of the subject.'"

body.text: avaśyaṃ caitadavagantavyam / anyathā kramayaugapadyābhyāmabhivyaktena arthakriyāsāmarthyaviyogena paraparikalpitaḥ padārthāḥ kathamiva niṣeddhuṃ śakṣyante / sadvastunastānnaiva kathamapi niṣedhaḥ kartuṃ pāryate / āśrayāsiddhadoṣeṇa yadi asato 'pi naiva kartuṃ pāryate tadā niṣedha eva kasyāpi kathamapi kartuṃ naiva śakyate / ata eva yogācāraistāvaduktam -
body.translated_text: This must necessarily be understood. Otherwise, how could the entities imagined by opponents — lacking the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsāmarthya</s>) as pervaded by the absence [of such capacity] manifested through succession and simultaneity — be negated? A negation of a real existing entity cannot be accomplished in any way. If, through the fault of 'unestablished basis,' [negation] of what is non-existent too cannot be accomplished, then no negation of anything could ever be accomplished. Hence, the <s>Yogācāras</s> have stated:

children.translated_text: "Object-ness does not exist in one [thing], nor does it exist in many atoms;

children.text: nāsti tat kṣaṇikaṃ vāpi saccāpi na hi vidyate /
children.translated_text: nor is that momentary; and even if existent, it is not found —
for [manifesting causal efficacy] successively and simultaneously would be contradictory."

body.text: ityādibhirbāhyādiniṣedhaḥ kathamiva karttuṃ śakyaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: Through such [arguments] and the like, how could the negation of external [objects] and the rest be accomplished?

body.text: tairthikaiḥparikalpiteṣu dravyaguṇakarmasāmānyādiṣu niṣeddhumiṣyamāṇeṣvapi kathaṃ tatra āśrayāsiddhādayo doṣā naiva pravartsyante? yadi prasaṅgasādhanamātreṇaiva niṣedhanātra pravartsyanta ityevaṃ brūyāttadā apramāṇaṃ hi tatra prasaṅgasādhanam / phalata ekāntenaiṣāmabhāvo vyavahāre kathaṃ siddhaḥ syāt, pramāṇāpekṣitātvāttasya /
body.translated_text: When it is desired to negate the categories imagined by the non-Buddhists (<s>Tīrthikas</s>) — substance (<s>dravya</s>), quality (<s>guṇa</s>), action (<s>karma</s>), universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), and the like — how would faults such as 'unestablished basis' not arise there? If one says that negation there proceeds merely through <s>prasaṅga</s>-proof alone, then the <s>prasaṅga</s>-proof there is not a [valid] means of knowledge. Consequently, how would the non-existence of these [categories] be definitively established in convention, since that [establishment] requires valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>)?

body.text: atha pramāṇameva prasaṅgasādhanamiti cettadā kimiva tatra āśrayāsiddhādayo doṣā na pravartante? yukttibalena āgantuśīleṣu doṣeṣu prekṣāvadbhiḥ svataḥ [svapakṣataḥ] siddhirnaiva yuktimatī atha bāhyārthādīn niṣeddhukāmānāṃ vidyata eva vastubhūto buddhilakṣaṇo dharmī, yatastenaiva bāhyārtheṣu pradhānādiṣu cotpattiniṣedhaḥ sādhayate, ataḥ āśrayāsiddhādayo doṣāstatra na pravartanta iti cettadā ekānekasvabhāvaviyuktatvakramayaupadyavyāptārthakriyāsāmarthyavirahitatvādo hetavastadā aprasiddhataddharmatvadharmiṇi abhīṣṭasādhyadharmaṃ sādhayiṣyantyeva /
body.translated_text: Now, if [one says] that <s>prasaṅga</s>-proof is itself valid cognition, then how do faults such as 'unestablished basis' not arise there? Through the force of reasoning, the discerning do not reasonably accept establishment from one's own side alone [without valid support] regarding adventitious faults. But if those who wish to negate external objects and the like do have a real-entity subject characterized as cognition (<s>buddhi</s>), whereby they prove the negation of arising for external objects such as <s>Pradhāna</s> and the like — and therefore faults like 'unestablished basis' do not arise there — then the reasons [such as] 'lacking a unitary or manifold intrinsic nature,' 'lacking the capacity for causal efficacy pervaded by succession and simultaneity,' and the like would indeed prove the desired property of the thesis regarding a subject whose possession of that property is not established.

body.text: apakṣadharmatve 'pi sādhyāvinābhāvamātrahetuḥ sādhyasādhane 'samarthaḥ / yadyevaṃ syāttadā cākṣuṣatvamapi śabdadharmaṇi kathamanityatvasādhane 'śaktam? yadi te tatprasiddhatvamabhyupagacchanti tadā bāhyapradhānādivat buddhireva śaktatvaikānekatvavyāptadharmaviyuktatvanniḥsvabhāvaiva tāvat setsyati, teṣāṃ taddharmatvāt / anye 'pi dharmā nānyasiddhāṃ bhavanti / sāmarthyādivirāhitaṃ vastu tāvadasiddhameva /
body.translated_text: Even when [a reason] is not a property of the thesis, a reason that is merely inseparable from what is to be proved is incapable with respect to proof and what is to be proved. If it were so, then how would being visible be incapable of proving impermanence in the case of the property of sound? If they accept the well-known status of that, then, just like external <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and such, cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) itself will be established as essenceless, because it is devoid of the pervasion-property of capacity, one-or-many nature. Other properties too are not established for others. An entity devoid of capacity and the like is simply unestablished.

body.text: anyathā [yadyevaṃ na syāttadā] tato bahyapradhānādayo na niḥsvabhāvāḥ setyanti / niḥsvabhāvatve khalu siddhe āśrayāsiddhadidoṣāṇāṃ tādavasthye 'pi nāsti svapakṣahāniprasaṅgaḥ / buddhau tāvat siddhe 'pi bāhyapradhānādibhirutpattiniṣedhe pradhānādīnāṃ parikalpitasvabhāvaniṣedhastu asiddha eva, ākārāntaratvāttasya / yadyasiddha eva saḥ, tadā parakalpitāḥ pradhānādayo 'santa eva / evaṃvidhe tāvad dharmiṇi kathamasadvyavahāro 'pi pravarteta / na khalvanyeṣu anyavyavahārapravṛttiryajyate /
body.translated_text: Otherwise, external <s>Pradhāna</s> and such would not be established as essenceless. When essencelessness is indeed established, even though faults such as unestablished locus (<s>āśrayāsiddha</s>) remain the same, there is no absurd consequence of loss to one's own position. Even when cognition is established, in denying the arising [of things] from external <s>Pradhāna</s> and such, the denial of the imagined nature (<s>parikalpita-svabhāva</s>) of <s>Pradhāna</s> etc. is itself unestablished, because it has a different form. If it is indeed unestablished, then the imagined <s>Pradhāna</s> etc. are simply non-existent. How would even the convention of 'non-existent' apply to such a subject (<s>dharmin</s>)? For the application of one convention to others is not possible.

body.text: kecana tāvadajñāninastriṣu pratisaṃkhyānirodhāsaṃskṛteṣu kasyāpyutpattimattvābhāvaṃ paramārthavasturupeṇa parikalpayanti / tanniṣeghasādhane ca buddhestāvat kathaṃ nāma viṣayibhāvo bhaviṣyati, yato hyanye [vādinaḥ] teṣu tayā utpattimattvābhāvadharmaṃ nābhyupayanti / ato tanniṣeghastāvanna kathamapi sādhayituṃ śakyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Some ignorant people imagine the absence of any production in the three [types of] analytical cessation (<s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s>) and the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) as an ultimate real entity. How could cognition be the object in proving their denial, since other [opponents] do not accept the property of absence-of-production in those [categories] through that [cognition]? Therefore, their denial cannot be established in any way.

body.text: atha anādikālinasvabījaparipākapariniṣpannabālānāṃ buddhau vidyamāno bāhyavastuvikalpa eva dharmī, tadādhāreṇa pradhānādīnāṃ niṣedhyamānatvāt / sa paramārthataḥ svabhāvavirahito 'pi bhrāntyā bāhyamiva pradhānādyabhinnamiva sarvasāmarthyaśūnyaṃ ca sarvadharmasamavetamiva kalpayati / tatra pradhānādisvarūpaniṣedhe pradhānādisvarūpaniṣedhastāvat sādhyasādhanaviṣayakaḥ sidhyati, yato hi sa bālairbāhyapadhānādyupagṛhītavādiprativādibhirapi taimirikairdvicandradarśanamiva tadabhinnatayaiva vyavahriyate /
body.translated_text: Rather, the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) is the very conceptualization of external objects present in the cognition of the ignorant, whose [dispositions] have been perfected through the ripening of beginningless seeds — because <s>Pradhāna</s> and such are denied on that basis. Though that [conceptualization] is ultimately devoid of own-nature, through error it imagines [things] as if external, as if identical with <s>Pradhāna</s> etc., as if devoid of all capacity, and as if conjoined with all <s>dharmas</s>. Therein, the denial of the nature of <s>Pradhāna</s> etc. is established as the object of proof and means of proof, because even the opponents — both proponents and counter-proponents who accept external <s>Pradh��na</s> and such — operate with it as identical, just as those with visual distortion [operate with] the perception of a double moon.

body.text: sa hi yadyapi [sarvathā] buddhayā parikalpitamātra eva, tathāpi tadākāratayā buddhirityevamupacaryate vastuto 'yaṃ nāsti [kathamapi] buddhisvabhāvaḥ, tadvilakṣaṇasvabhāvenāvavabhāsamānatvāttasya / ataḥ siddhe 'pi tasya niḥsvabhāvatve buddhiniḥ svabhāvatāyā nāsti prasaṅgaḥ, yato hi bāhyapradhānādīnāṃ tāvanniṣedhastu pramāṇaiḥ sādhyate, na tu [kadācit] tattvaniṣedhāya hetavaḥ prayujyante /
body.translated_text: Although it is entirely merely imagined by cognition, it is figuratively called 'cognition' because it has that form. In reality, this is not at all the nature of cognition, because it appears with a nature different from its own. Therefore, even when its essencelessness is established, there is no absurd consequence of the essencelessness of cognition, because the denial of external <s>Pradhāna</s> etc. is established by <s>pramāṇas</s>, but reasons are never applied for denying reality [itself].

body.text: vastusatāṃ śabdādibāhyadharmiṇām anityādidharmasiddhaye [te] bāhyaśabdādayastabhinnāśca buddhistha upacāradharmiṇyevāśrayante, yato hi te deśakālādibhīnnāvasthāniyatā bāhyaśabdādayo vādiprativādināṃ buddhau svasvabhāvena naiva pratyakṣībhavanti / sādhyasādhanādiviśeṣāṇāmapyasambhavaḥ, niraṃśatvāt / ato 'numānāmeyādayaḥ sarve vyavahārā buddhistha eva dharmiṇyāśritāḥ pravartante, prakārāntarāsambhavat / yadyevaṃ tadā paramārthato niḥsvabhāvatve parikalpitadharmiṇaṃ niḥśritya niṣedhādisiddhayartham āśrayāsiddhādidoṣāṇāmapravṛttavapi kāmaṃ balenāsmāsu apālambhāḥ kriyante /
body.translated_text: For proving properties like impermanence in the case of substantially real external subjects like sound and other [things], [the opponents] too rely on external sounds etc. that are indistinct from cognition, in the subject that is figuratively [treated as the] locus — because external sounds etc. that are determined by conditions of place, time, and state never appear directly with their own nature in the cognition of proponents and opponents. The particular features of proof, means of proof, etc. are also impossible, because [cognition] is partless. Therefore, all conventions such as 'to be inferred by inference' etc. operate by depending only on the subject that is in cognition, because no other mode is possible. If so, then even when others, using force, level charges against us through the door of unestablished locus etc. for establishing denials etc. by depending on the imagined subject, [those charges are groundless] even when essencelessness is ultimately [accepted].

body.text: yathā hi paramārthapravṛttyarthaṃ bhavantaḥ pradhānādiniṣedhye parikalpitadharmiṇyeva sādhyasādhanādīn manasikurvanti, tathaiva vayamapi prasiddheṣu rūpaśabdādiṣu ye tāvat sadasadādisvabhāvā āropyante, tanniṣedhāya bālebhyastān māyāmarīcisvapnapratībimbādisamān nirdiśāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: Just as you, for the purpose of establishing the ultimate, attend to proof and means of proof etc. in the imagined subject for the denial of <s>Pradhāna</s> and such — in the same way, we too, regarding well-known forms, sounds, and such, declare to the ignorant that the natures of existent, non-existent, etc. that are superimposed upon them are like illusion, mirage, dream, and reflection, in order to deny those [superimpositions].

body.text: tatra yathā āropite dharmiṇi vastutvāropaṇaniṣedhae 'pi vādiprativādiṣu pratībhāsamānatvād asadādidoṣā na pravartante, tathaiva rupādayo 'pi tāvadāgoālaṅganānāmavabhāsante, tatkathaṃ nāma te 'siddhā bhaviṣyantīti / avabhāso hi tatkāraṇanivṛttyā jāyamānena satyasvabhāvena tāvannasti vyāptaḥ, alīkasyāpyavabhāsamānatvāt / yadyevaṃ no cettadā sarve puruṣāstadarśinaḥ syuḥ, kevalasya tattvasyaivāvabhāsamānatvāt /
body.translated_text: Therein, just as faults of non-existence etc. do not arise when denying the superimposition of reality upon the superimposed subject, because it appears to both proponents and opponents — in the same way, forms etc. also appear even to cowherd women, so how could they be unestablished? For appearance is not pervaded by a true nature arising from the cessation of its cause, because even what is false can appear. If this were not so, then all persons would be seers of that [reality], because only truth alone would appear.

body.text: yathaiva hi tasmin parikalpitadharmiṇi sāmarthyaśūnyatvavyāptyupanyāsena niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ prasādhya pradhānādayaḥ sādhyante, tathaivāsmābhirapi parikalpitavastuni tat [niḥsvabhāvatvaṃ] samyaktāa sādhayituṃ yathoktaḥ sāmarthyābhāvādiḥ kathaṃ na siddhaḥ syāt / prekṣāvadbhistu svīkaraṇaṃ vicārārham, bhāvātmakatāyā nirṇayasyāyuktatvāt, vicarāvasthāyāṃ tu nāstyeva / atatstannirṇayo na kṛtaḥ vicāro 'pi nirṇayārthaka eva / yataḥ pramāṇādvārā siddhāntanirṇayakāle ko 'pi siddhānto nābhyupagato bhavatītyatastasmin kāle kasmin āśrayāsiddhimukhena dharmyasiddhayādidoṣaḥ pradātuṃ śakyate / atha vādī pramāṇaistattvanirṇayaṃ kṛtvā parebhyastatpratipādayituṃ pravṛtaḥ, ataḥ sa siddhāntābhyupagamāt pūrvavartīti manyate, tadāpi tāvanna ujyate / svapratītikāle siddhānto nābhyupagamyata iti /
body.translated_text: Just as in that imagined subject, by presenting the pervasion of being devoid of capacity, essencelessness is established and <s>Pradhāna</s> etc. are thereby proved — in the same way, for us too, how would the stated absence of capacity etc. not be established for properly proving that [essencelessness] in imagined entities? For those of discernment, acceptance [of any view] is subject to investigation, because the determination of the nature of an entity is not valid; in the state of investigation, [that determination] simply does not exist. Therefore, since that determination has not been made, investigation too is for the purpose of determination. Because at the time of determining a position through <s>pramāṇa</s>, no position whatsoever has been accepted, at that time to whom can the fault of unestablished locus in the subject be attributed? If it is thought that the proponent, having determined the truth through <s>pramāṇas</s>, proceeds to demonstrate it to others, and therefore he is subsequent to accepting a position — that too is not valid, because at the time of one's own realization, no position was accepted.

body.text: pūrvata eva siddhāntamanabhyupagacchanto vādinaḥ svayaṃ pramāṇatastattvajñānaṃ kurvanti, taireva cāparānapi bodhayantīti kathaṃ siddhanto 'bhyupagataḥ syāt / pūrvaṃ svayaṃ pramāṇaistattvaściyaṃ kṛvā siddhāntena aparebhyo 'vabodhanamapi nāsti siddham / apare 'pi prekṣāvantastāvat tacchabdamātreṇaiva pramāṇairanupapanne 'rthe naiva viśvasanti / ataḥ svamirṇayavad aparebhyo 'pi nirdeśasamaye tādavasthyāt sarvatra pramāṇaireva tattvanirṇayaḥ kriyate / ataḥ siddhānto nābhyupagato bhavatīti / ata eva kathaṃ tena dharmiṇastāvadasiddhādayaḥ pratīpādyante / samyakpramāṇabalena vādināmabhīṣṭasādhyasiddhāvapi 'siddhāntābhyupagamāt tebhyo doṣā jāyante' iti ye vadanti kiṃ teṣāṃ yuktyantaramiti / vastutastattvavimarśāvasare siddhāntaprasiddhe dharmiṇi na ke 'pyāśrayante / tathāvidhasya dharmiṇiḥ kutrāpi vādiprativādiṣvasiddhatvādeva / yathā bauddheṣu śabdādayo bhautikā ityabhyupagamyante, na tathā vaiśeṣikādiṣu, ākāśaguṇatvena tasyābhyupagamāt / yadi tathāvidho dharmi siddho na syāttadā na ko 'pi kutrāpi tatsādhanārthaṃ pratvarteta / yadi tathāvidho siddhastadā taddharmoṃ 'pi ubhayasammataḥ siddha eva / ato nāsti vivādāvasaraḥ / ata eva sarve tattvajijñāsavaḥ siddhāntaviśeṣasiddhaṃ dharmiṇamapahāya āgopālaprasiddhameva tamāśritya sādhyasādhanaviṣayakaṃ cintanaṃ parivardhayanti / ataḥ siddhāntāśrayaṇaṃ kṛtyā āśrayāsiddhādivacanamasambaddhameva /
body.translated_text: Proponents who do not accept a position beforehand generate knowledge of truth themselves through <s>pramāṇa</s>, and with those very [<s>pramāṇas</s>] they also awaken others — so how would a position be accepted? Even the notion that one first determines the truth through <s>pramāṇas</s> and then informs others through a [doctrinal] position is not established. Others who are discerning also do not trust an unjustified meaning merely on the basis of words alone. Therefore, just as in one's own determination, at the time of instructing others too, since the situation is the same, the determination of truth is made everywhere only through <s>pramāṇas</s>. Therefore, no position is accepted. How then can unestablished subjects be demonstrated through that? Those who say 'faults arise for them from accepting a position' even when the proponents' desired thesis is established by the force of correct <s>pramāṇa</s> — what reasoning do they have? In reality, at the occasion of investigating truth, no one relies on a subject established [merely] in a doctrinal position, because such a subject is unestablished everywhere for both proponents and opponents. Just as for Buddhists, sounds etc. are accepted as material elements, this is not so for <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> and others, since they accept those as qualities of space. If such a subject were not established, then no one would ever undertake to prove it anywhere. If such [a subject] is established, then its property too, being accepted by both, is already established. Therefore, there is no occasion for dispute. For this very reason, all those who seek to know the truth, setting aside the subject established by a particular doctrine, relying instead on that which is well-known even to cowherds, develop their investigation regarding proof and what is to be proved. Therefore, the statement about the fault of unestablished locus based on relying on a doctrinal position is entirely irrelevant.

body.text: vyavahāre ye 'prasiddhā dharmiṇasteṣu codanamidaṃ samucitameva / asmāsu rupādayastāvad vyavahāre 'pi nāprasiddhāḥ /
body.translated_text: This objection is appropriate for those whose subjects are unestablished in convention. For us, however, forms etc. are not unestablished even in convention.

body.text: "yatkhalu paraprasiddhapramāṇaiḥ svapakṣaḥ sādhanīyaḥ" iti yaducyate tad dūṣaṇameva tāvanna bhavati, anabhyupagamāt / ato vyavahāre vayam ubhayasiddhairhetvādibhiḥ sādhyaṃ sādhayāma ityevaṃ paścānnirdekṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: The statement that 'one must prove one's own position with <s>pramāṇas</s> established by the opponent' — that is not a refutation at all, because it is not accepted [by us]. Therefore, we establish what is to be proved through reasons etc. established for both parties in conventional [usage] — this we shall explain later.

body.text: "sarve dharmā viviktāḥ, na kenāpi samyagliṅgenāliṅgitā atiparokṣatvād" iti yaduktaṃ tadapi tāvannaiva yujyate, siddhe 'pi sādhyarmiṇi sādhyadharmasamyagliṅgayoḥ parasparāvinābhūtasya sādhyasādhanabhāvasyāpravartanāt, vivādābhāvācca tatra / tathāpi katipayeṣu dharmisu sa siddhaḥ, katipayeṣu ca sandigdha iti / ataḥ avinābhāvaniyamanirdeśena sāmānyadharmiṇi sādhyadharmaṃ sādhayeyuriti kathanaṃ yujyata eva /
body.translated_text: The statement that 'all <s>dharmas</s> are isolated; they cannot be indicated by any correct logical mark, because they are extremely beyond [direct] perception' — that too is not valid, because even when the subject to be proved is established, the proof-relation of inseparability between the correct mark and the property to be proved does not [simply] cease to operate, and there is no dispute there. Nevertheless, in some <s>dharmas</s> that [relation] is established, and in some it is doubtful. Therefore, the statement that by indicating the invariable concomitance, one can prove the property to be proved in the general subject is entirely appropriate.

body.text: tadvadatrāpi māyāmaricisvapnagandharvanagarādisadṛśeṣu katipayeṣveva dharmiṣu sa sidhyatītyataḥ paramārthato niḥsvabhāvatvād ekānekasvabhāvādidharmeṣu vyāptiḥ siddhaiva / api ca, asmābhiranyatra savivādeṣu rupādiṣu vyāptidharmopadarśanena sādhitatvānnāsti doṣa iti /
body.translated_text: Likewise here too, in some subjects such as those resembling illusion, mirage, dream, and <s>Gandharva</s> cities, that [essencelessness] is established. Therefore, the pervasion through properties like being of one-or-many nature is already established, since [the subject] is ultimately essenceless. Moreover, since this has been established by us elsewhere through demonstrating the pervasion-property in disputed forms etc., there is no fault.

body.text: ye kecana - "kāryasvabhāvābhyāṃ hetubhyāṃ naiva sarve dharmā niḥsvabhāvā iti sādhayituṃ śakyante, vastusādhanatvāttayoḥ" iti yat kathayanti, tadapi naiva yujyate, paramārthato bhāvasvabhāvasādhanāvetāviti kutrāpyanullikhitatvāt /
body.translated_text: What some say — that 'all <s>dharmas</s> cannot be proved to be essenceless through the reasons of effect-nature (<s>kārya-svabhāva</s>) and own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), because those two establish real entities' — that too is not valid, because it is nowhere recorded that these two establish the nature of existence ultimately.

body.text: yadā sādhanasvarupāntaḥpraviṣṭatvādimau vastusādhanāvityucyete tadā niḥsvabhāvatāyāmapi prayogaviśeṣavaśena sādhanasvabhāvāveva / atastatsādhyāmānāyāṃ kathaṃ na tau [hetū] sambhavataḥ? svabhāvahetureva kāryādihetubhyaḥ prayogabhedena vividhākāreṣu prapañcitaḥ / ata eva vidvadbhiḥ "pakṣadharmastadaṃśena vyāpto hetuḥ" iti sāmānyena hetulakṣaṇaṃ nirdiṣṭam / ato 'trāpi prayogabhedena svabhāvādayaḥ aucityavaśānna virudhyante / paścādapyevaṃ nirdekṣyāmaḥ /
body.translated_text: When these two are called 'proofs of real entities' because they fall within the form of proof, then in [establishing] essencelessness too, through a particular formulation, they are indeed of the nature of proof. Therefore, how are those two [reasons] not applicable when that [essencelessness] is being proved? The <s>svabhāva-hetu</s> (own-nature reason) itself is elaborated into various forms through differences in formulation from the effect and other reasons. For this very reason, the wise have stated the definition of a reason in general as 'a property of the thesis that is pervaded by that [probandum] as its part.' Therefore, here too, through differences in formulation, the own-nature and other [reasons] are not contradicted by propriety. This too we shall explain later.

body.text: tatra sarve dharmā paramārthato 'nutpannā niḥsvabhāvāśca, tathāpi imau dvāvapi teṣu vyavahārasatyatvena vidyete eva / ataḥ kathaṃ tāvekasminna sambhavataḥ / "kevalaṃ samyak kāryamātreṇa svabhāvamātreṇa vā hetunā bhavitavyam" iti yaduktam, tasyāpi kimapi kāraṇaṃ nāsti, yato hi pratibimbaphalamapyunumānameva svahetutayālambanīkaroti / "ādarśadigataḥ pratibimbo hi tāvadanyadekaṃ rūpam" iti yaduktam, tadapi na yucyate, sapratighatvasya ekasminneva viṣaye 'nupapannatvāt / "tadeva rūpaṃ tathaivālambyate" idamapi kathanaṃ naiva samīcīnam, tathāvidhaviṣayākārasambabaddhasvabhāvena virahitatvāt /
body.translated_text: Therein, all <s>dharmas</s> are ultimately unarisen and essenceless; nevertheless, these two [reasons] exist in them as conventional truth. Therefore, how can the two not occur in the same [subject]? The statement 'there must be a reason consisting merely of correct effect or merely of own-nature' — there is no basis for that either, because even a reflection is a type of inference that takes as its object its own cause. The statement 'a reflection in a mirror is simply another form' is also not valid, because impenetrability (<s>sapratighatva</s>) is not possible in a single object. The statement 'that very form is apprehended as such' is also not correct, because it lacks the nature connected with the object-aspect of that kind.

body.text: yadyapi pratibimbādaya ādarśadyāśrayāśritā bhavanti, tathāpi yadi viṣayākārādibhedānurūpatayā ālambyeran, tadā tadrūpaṃ tathāvidhaṃ sthirasvabhāvaṃ nāstyeva / anyākāragrahanamapi tāvannaiva yujyate, atiprasaṅgāt / 'vijñānasyaiva pratibimbākāratayā pratibhāsanādasti sa [ākāraḥ] vijñāsvabhāvena vastusan' idi yaduktaṃ tadapi na yuktiyuktam, yato hi amūrtaṃ nīlādivijñānaṃ niraṃśatayā sthitaṃ vividhākārarahitameva bhavatītyucyate / pratibimbavastu tadvilakṣaṇatayā pratibhāsata ityataḥ kathaṃ sa [ākāraḥ] tatsvabhāvena san syāt / yathoktaṃ bhavatāpi triṃśikāyāṃ pudgalaniḥsvabhāvataṃ pratipādayatā yad yo hi parikalpitaḥ svabhāvaḥ sa sarvathā nithyaiva, vandhyāputrādivat /
body.translated_text: Although reflections and such are supported by a mirror and other bases, if they were apprehended in conformity with the difference of object-aspect etc., then such a form of stable own-nature simply does not exist. The apprehension of another aspect too is not valid, because of over-extension (<s>atiprasaṅga</s>). The statement 'since consciousness itself appears in the form of a reflection, that [aspect] exists as substantially real with the nature of consciousness' — that too is not supported by reason, because it is said that immaterial cognition of blue etc., being partless, exists as devoid of various aspects. Since the reflection-thing appears as different from it, how could that [aspect] exist as having its nature? As you yourself have stated in the <s>Triṃśikā</s> (Thirty Verses), while demonstrating the essencelessness of persons (<s>pudgala</s>): the imagined nature (<s>parikalpita-svabhāva</s>) is in every way simply non-existent, like a barren woman's son.

body.text: ātmādayaḥ parikalpitasvabhāvā evetyādibhiḥ prayogaiḥ svabhāvaheturevocyate / tathaivānye 'pi paraparikalpitadharmā naivālambitā bhavantīti kathaṃ nocyate / yathācāryairnirdiṣṭaṃ tathā sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvatāsādhanāyāṃ vyāpyānupalabdhikṣaṇā dharmāḥ kathaṃ noktāḥ / tathā paścānnirdekṣyāmaḥ / yatkhalu svabhāvānupalabdhirasambhavetyuktaṃ tattāvat pūrvaṃ kṛtottaramiti / nayo 'yamanyo 'nyaśūnyatāyā ityapyaśakyasādhanaḥ / tadā kimiti praśne lakṣaṇaśūnyateyamiti /
body.translated_text: Through formulations such as 'the self and others are of imagined nature' — this is precisely the <s>svabhāva-hetu</s> (own-nature reason). Likewise, why is it not said that other dharmas imagined by others are also not objects of apprehension? And as the teachers have indicated, for proving the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, how are the <s>dharmas</s> that are instances of non-apprehension of the pervaded (<s>vyāpyānupalabdhi</s>) not stated? This we shall explain later. As for the statement that 'non-apprehension of own-nature is impossible' — that has already been answered earlier. The claim that 'this is a different approach of mutual emptiness (<s>anyonyaśūnyatā</s>)' is also impossible to establish. If asked 'what is it then?' — this is emptiness of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>).

body.text: viruddhopalabdhyādayo 'sambhavā iti yaduktaṃ tā atyasambaddhā eveti / yato hi sarve dharmā viviktāḥ katipaye ca sahaviruddhā iti na sidhyanti, tathāpi māyākhapuṣpādayaśca sāmānyatayā niḥsvabhāvāḥ sahaviruddhāśceti sidhyantyeva /
body.translated_text: As for the statement that apprehension of contradictories (<s>viruddhopalabdhi</s>) and the like are impossible — that is entirely incoherent. For although all <s>dharmas</s> are isolated [from intrinsic nature] and it is not established that some are mutually contradictory, nevertheless, illusions, sky-flowers, and the like, being without own-nature in general, are indeed established as mutually contradictory.

body.text: yadyevaṃ nāsti tadā katham bhavadbhiḥ paraparikalpitā īśvarādayo niḥsvabhāvatvena sādhayituṃ śakyante / ataḥ sāmānyena niḥsvabhāvatāmātreṇa yadi vyavahāre viruddhādayaḥ sidhyanti, tataḥ sarveṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ paramārthataḥ sattvābhyupagame virusśādharmādīnupadarśaya niḥsvabhāvatvena teṣāṃ samyak sādhanāt kimatra tāvad virodha / tadviruddhādīnāṃ vastutāyāṃ prasaṅgo na yuktarūpaḥ, yato hi paramārthato niḥsvabhāveṣu dharmeṣu bhūtarupābhivyaktistu, kutrāpi samyagbhāvasvabhāve notpatiṣṭhati / yadi tiṣṭhettadā viruddhādayo na sidhyeyuḥ /
body.translated_text: If this is so [and nothing exists], then how can those imagined by others, such as <s>Īśvara</s> and the like, be established by you as being without own-nature? Therefore, if contradictories and the like are established in convention merely through the general [characteristic of] essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatā</s>), then when the existence of all <s>dharmas</s> in the ultimate sense is accepted, by demonstrating properties of contradiction and the like and correctly establishing their essencelessness — what contradiction is there in that?

body.text: ato yadi sarve dharmā niḥsvabhāvāḥsahānavasthānaviruddhāśca sidhyantyatastadviruddheṣu vastutāprasaṅga iti na vaktavyam, viruddhādīnāṃ vyavahārasiddhatvāt, na tu paramārthataḥ / evameva dīpakādau adṛḍhalakṣaṇe vastuni paricchinne sati dṛḍhākāraviviktataiva tāvat paricchidyate, yato na vyavahāre vyavacchedaḥ, ataḥparicchedānupapattireva tatra / yo yathā parichidyate, yatra ca tathā paricchedo nāsti, sa abhāva eva tāavat parasparaparihārasthitalakṣaṇo viradho vyavasthāpyate / sadasatoḥ kramākramayośca virodhayorapi tathaiva draṣṭavyam / nāstyāsanne deśe 'gni, avikalaśīlasparśadityādisthaleṣu sa virodhadhastāvat sahānavasthānalakṣaṇo vyavasthāpyate /
body.translated_text: Therefore, if all <s>dharmas</s> are without own-nature and contradictory as mutually non-co-existent, one should not say that there is the unwanted consequence of reality in their contradictories — since contradictories and the like are established in convention, not ultimately. Just so, when a thing of unstable character such as a lamp is ascertained, what is ascertained is precisely its separation from the stable form, since there is no exclusion in convention. Therefore there is simply the impossibility of ascertainment there. Contradiction, whose characteristic is mutual exclusion in [their] abiding, is established with respect to what is ascertained in a certain way and where such ascertainment does not hold — that indeed is non-existence. The contradiction between existence and non-existence, and between sequence and simultaneity, should be viewed similarly. In cases where fire is absent in a nearby place, or where there is contact of unimpaired sense-faculties, etc. — that contradiction whose characteristic is mutual non-co-existence is established.

body.text: prasiddhe 'pi tasmin virodhe dīpakādayo hi vasturupeṇātyantamanupapannāḥ, māyādimithyāvastuṣvapi jātivināśayoravabhāsamānatvāt ata eva ācāryaiḥ paramārthapravṛttyarthaṃ yathā dīpakādiṣu nityānityādivirodho 'vabhāsate, tathaiva vyavasthā kṛtā / dīpakādayo bāhyārthatvena vijñānarūpatvena vā paramārthato 'siddhāḥ, ubhayoḥ svabhāvayostaireva nirākṛtatvāt / paramārthavastusvabhāvena sahānavasthānalakṣaṇavirodhasya sākṣātkāri jñānaṃ paramārthavastusvabhāve na kathañcit pravartate, arvāgdarśināṃ darśanamārge 'pravṛtatvāt / sahānavasthānalakṣaṇo
body.translated_text: Even though that contradiction is well-known, lamps and the like are utterly untenable as real things, since even in false things such as illusions, [the characteristics of] origination and destruction appear. For this very reason, the masters (<s>ācāryas</s>), for the purpose of engaging with ultimate [reality], have made the arrangement just as the contradiction of permanence, impermanence, and the like appears in lamps and similar things. Lamps and the like, whether as external objects or as having the nature of consciousness, do not ultimately [exist].

body.text: virodhastāvat sāṃvṛtika eva, vastūnāṃ svayameva vinaśyamānatvānnānyakāraṇaiḥ / yadi pratyayāntarairvināśa iti tadā na vināśahetubhistatra kimapyupakriyate / pratyayāntaraiḥ kriyamāṇe 'pi vināśe sa svahetubhireva kriyate, nānyakāraṇairiti /
body.translated_text: Contradiction is merely conventional, since things perish by themselves and not through other causes. If destruction [occurs] through other conditions, then those causes of destruction contribute nothing at all there. Even when destruction is brought about through other conditions, it is brought about by its own causes alone, not by other causes.

body.text: yadyavastutvād vināśasya tattvena anyatvena vā tasya vijñaptirna yujyata iti cintyate tadā ātyantikatayā sa vināśakāraṇairna kriyate, niḥsvabhāvatvāt / ato 'kiñcitkarā agnyādayo hi kathaṃ nāma paramārthato viruddhāḥ setsyanti / tathāpyagnyādayaḥ śītādīn kramaśo niḥsāmarthalakṣaṇān anityān prakarṣatamān utpādayantyata eva te hyagnyādayo viruddhā iti kevalaṃ vyavahriyanta eva / ata ācāryairvirodhanayo 'yamityukto na tu virodha evetyuktaḥ / ataśca virodho 'yaṃ vyavahāramātrāśrita evokto na tu paramārthāśritaḥ agniśītādayaśca na paramārthato bāhyārthasvabhāvāḥ sidhyanti, teṣāṃ tāvajjñānākārasvabhāvo 'pi ca kalpita eva / ekasmin jñāne śītoṣṇayoravabhāsaḥ sambhavati / anekāni sajātīyavijñānāni yugapannaiva sambhavanti, ataḥ śītādayaḥ svapnādinmithyāvabhāsa eva, ato nāsti teṣu paramārthato virodhaḥ /
body.translated_text: If one thinks that because destruction is unreal, its cognition as identical or different is not tenable — then absolutely, that destruction is not produced by causes of destruction, because of [its] essencelessness. Hence, how can fire and the like, being utterly inefficacious, be ultimately contradictory? Nevertheless, fire and the like, progressively rendering cold and similar things into the characteristic of powerlessness — [being] impermanent — intensify [their destruction].

body.text: vṛkṣaśiṃśapādīni vyāpyavyāpakavastūnyapi vyavahāramāśritya parikalpitasāmāanyaviśeṣavyavasthayā vyavasthāpyante, yato hi vṛkṣādayo vyāpakāḥ vastutaḥ sāmānyātmakāḥ / paramārthatastvetat kimapi nāstyeva /
body.translated_text: Things standing in the relation of pervaded and pervader (<s>vyāpya-vyāpaka</s>), such as tree and <s>śiṃśapā</s> (a type of tree), are also established by relying on convention, through the arrangement of imagined universals and particulars. For trees and the like, being pervaders, have the nature of universals in reality. But ultimately, none of this exists at all.

body.text: viśeṣādayastāvanna bāhyārthasvabhāvāḥ, jñānākārā api paramārthatayāsiddhatvāt / tathāpyukṣitatattvarthā vidvāṃso gajāvalokanamiva svapnadṛṣṭakhadirādivividhamithyāviṣayāṇāmanubhūtivad vṛkṣādivastūnāṃ mṛṣātvamevāśritya tathatāyāṃ pravṛttyarthaṃ paramārthānukūlatayā vyāpyavyāpakādivyavasthāṃ kurvate / tathaiva bījāṅkurādīni kāraṇakāryādīnyapi saṃvṛtyāśrayeṇaiva vyavahriyante, na tu paramārthasattayā, bījādīnāṃ paramārthato 'siddhatvād bitathānāmapi svapnādīnāṃ tathaivāvabhāsamānatvācca /
body.translated_text: Particulars and the like are not of the nature of external objects, since even the aspects of cognition are not established as ultimately real. Nevertheless, the wise ones who have examined the truth of reality, relying on the falsity of things like trees — just as in the experience of various false objects such as a <s>khadira</s> tree seen in a dream or the viewing of an elephant — make the arrangement of pervaded, pervader, and the like in a manner favorable to the ultimate, for the purpose of engaging with <s>tathatā</s> (suchness).

body.text: jāgradavasthāyāṃ māyākāryakāraṇādīni vitathānyapyupalabhyanta eva / atastāni vyāvahārikeṇa kāryakāraṇabhāvena vastusvabhāvatvena vyāptāni bhavanti / kintu tāvatā tāni paramārthasvabhāvatayā na samavatiṣṭhante / yato hi vyāpake vidyamāne 'pi sati vyāpyasya siddhirna niyatā / tathāpi vastusvabhāvatvena suvyāptāni kāryakāranavastūni yadi nivatante, tadā māyādivat paramārthataḥ parikalpito vastusvabhāva eva nivartate / ataḥ virodhādisarvā vyavasthāstattvapravṛtau samarthā bhavanti / ataḥ eva vidvadbhistathatāyā nirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ / tairthikaparikalpitatāni pramāṇādīnī tathātāyā ananukūlatvāt parītyājyānītī sanyakpramāṇalakṣaṇapratipādakasya śāstrasya praṇayanaṃ kṛtamiti /
body.translated_text: Even in the waking state, false things such as the products and causes of illusions are indeed apprehended. Hence, they are pervaded by being of the nature of things through the conventional relation of cause and effect. But for that reason, they do not abide as being of the nature of ultimate reality. For even when the pervader exists, the establishment of the pervaded is not certain. Nevertheless, being of the nature of things [conventionally],

body.text: itthaṃ katipaye tairthikāḥ piṇḍātmādikaṃ mithyāvastutattvaṃ sisādhayiṣayā sarvajñatāvirāgitākarmaphalasambandhādīnāṃ sāṃvṛtikīṃ vyavasthāṃ nirākartuṃ pramāṇānāṃ viparītalakṣaṇāni kurvanti / ataḥ sudhiyastāvattanniṣidhya pudgaladharmanairātmyatathatāyāṃ praveśānukūlāṃ sāṃvṛtikīṃ karmaphalasambandhādivyāvasthāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayituṃ pratyakṣādīnāṃ viśuddhāni pramāṇalakṣaṇāni viracitavantaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, certain non-Buddhist thinkers, wishing to establish the false reality of aggregate-selves and the like, make the characteristics of the means of valid knowledge perverted in order to deny the conventional arrangement of the connection of actions and their results, omniscience, dispassion, and the like. Therefore, the wise, having refuted that, [establish] the conventional arrangement of the connection of actions and their results and the like, which is favorable to entry into the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the selflessness of persons and <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: tānyapi bhagavatā [tathāgatena] anujñātānyeva / ato vayaṃ paramārthānukulāni viśuddhapramāṇalakṣaṇānyeva tāvanmanyāmahe / ato virodhādivyavahārāṇāṃ svīkṛtiātreṇa yo hi bhāvasvabhāvābhyupagamaprasaṅgaḥ, sa tāvadanaikāntika eva, tadabhyupagame 'pi bhāasvabhāvasyāsiddheḥ /
body.translated_text: These too have been approved by the Blessed One [the <s>Tathāgata</s>] himself. Therefore, we consider only those characteristics of pure means of valid knowledge that are favorable to the ultimate. Hence, by the mere acceptance of conventional practices such as contradiction, the unwanted consequence of accepting the reality of things is simply inconclusive, since even with that acceptance, the reality of things is not established.

body.text: nanvevamanumānena saha sambandhaprasidhyarthaṃ pratyakṣapramāṇaṃ yadyabhyupagamyate tadā vastunastāvat siddhireva, kalpanāpoḍhatvādabhrāntatvācca pratyakṣapramāṇasya / abhrāntajñānenādhyavasitaḥ khalu vastusvabhāvaḥ kathaṃ nāmānumānena nirākartuṃ śakyate? yadi nirakriyate tadā pratyakṣameva tāvad bādhitaṃ syāt / yadi tad bādhitaṃ syāttadānumānameva tāvanna syāt sisthitam / pratyakṣasambaddhenāpyunumānena pratyakṣaṃ bādhyata iti kathanato naivācitamanyat / yadi pratyakṣasiddho 'rtho 'numānena naiva bādhyate tadā prāpyasya prāptyā susthita eva tāvad vastuvādīti kathanamapi samyaṅnirākṛtameveti /
body.translated_text: Now, if perceptual valid knowledge (<s>pratyakṣa-pramāṇa</s>) is accepted for the purpose of establishing the connection with inference (<s>anumāna</s>), then the thing is certainly established — since perceptual valid knowledge is free from conceptual construction (<s>kalpanāpoḍha</s>) and non-erroneous (<s>abhrānta</s>). How could the nature of a thing determined by non-erroneous cognition be negated by inference? If it is negated, then perception itself would

body.text: ityamācāryaistāvatpratyakṣasya dvaividhyamabhihitam - yagipratyakṣaṃ sāmānyapratyakṣaṃ ca / tatra yaddhi sādharaṇaṃ pratyakṣaṃ tat paramārthamadhikṛtya nāstyabhrāntam / anyathā sarvaṃ yogipratyakṣameva syānna ca syuḥ kecanāpyarvāgdarśinaḥ / yogipratyakṣātiriktaṃ sāmānya pratyakṣaṃ yadyapi [abhrāntaṃ] nāsti tathāpi vyavahāre svapnādivad yathāprasiddhenārthena sahāvisaṃvādāttadabhrāntamucyate / śrāvakīyāṇi yogipratyakṣāṇi pudgalanairātmyamātrasākṣātkārīṇītyatastadavisaṃvādena pratyakṣapramānāni, na tu sarvākāragocaratveneti / kevalaṃ bhagavata eva pratyakṣaṃ sarvākāratattvagocaram, atastadeva tāvadaviparītamavisaṃvādakam / phalato yadeva sarvākāratattvamadhikṛtyābhrāntaṃ tadeva sarvākāratattvāvisaṃvādād yathārthamabhrāntamiti / ata eva bhagavadbhireva tāvat sarvadharmalakṣaṇarahitatā parijñātā /
body.translated_text: be [refuted]. Thus the masters have stated a twofold [classification of] perception: yogic perception (<s>yogi-pratyakṣa</s>) and ordinary perception (<s>sāmānya-pratyakṣa</s>). Among these, ordinary perception, with reference to the ultimate, is not non-erroneous. Otherwise, all [perception] would be yogic perception, and there would be no ordinary beings at all. Ordinary perception, apart from yogic perception, even though [it may appear] non-erroneous,

body.text: tasya sarvākārajñānasya nāsti vastutāprasaṅgo 'pi, sarvadharmasaṃgṛhīitatvāttasya / atastena lakṣaṇābhāvatāyāmabhisaṃbudhyate / āryaprajñāpāramitāyāmapi - "yaduta pratyakṣalakṣaṇaṃ sarvākārajñānam, alakṣaṇe abhisambuddhatvāttathāgatānām" - iti yaduktaṃ tattathaiva /
body.translated_text: for that omniscient knowledge (<s>sarvākārajñāna</s>), there is no unwanted consequence of being a real thing, since it encompasses all <s>dharmas</s>. Hence, through it, one awakens to the absence of characteristics. In the <s>Ārya-Prajñāpāramitā</s> too: "Namely, omniscient knowledge is characterized by direct perception, because the <s>Tathāgatas</s> have fully awakened to what is without characteristics" — what is stated there is precisely so.

body.text: vyavahārārthastāvat pratyakṣagocarārthaḥ mithyābhāsitasvapnādivat / sa yadā bālairvastutaḥ paramārthatveropyate, tadā sa anumānabādhito bhavati, na tu darśanādivyavahārārthaḥ [bādhyate] / ato yadabhrāntaṃ tat pratyakṣam, na cānumānabāghitamiti / yaśca paramārthatvenāropaḥ sa eva bādhyate, tadabhrāntatvābhāvāt / ato nāstyanena pratyakṣāpavādaprasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: The object of conventional usage, being the object of perception, is like a falsely appearing dream and the like. When the childish superimpose upon it the status of a real, ultimately existing thing — then it becomes contradicted by inference; but the conventional function of seeing and the like is not [contradicted]. Hence, that which is non-erroneous is perception, and it is not contradicted by inference. And the superimposition of being ultimately real — that alone is what is contradicted; that non-erroneous [perception]

body.text: arvāgdarśinastāvadanumānena pratyakṣasambaddhatve 'pi na paramārthatvaprāptā bhavanti, apitu kevalaṃ saṃvṛtāveva [tiṣṭhanti] / yato hi arvāgdarśibhirvāstavikaḥ paramārśasvabhāvaḥ pratyakṣatayā pṛthak pṛthak nānubhūyate / ato naiva vastusvabhāvaḥ saṃvṛtimapi bādhate kintu yo hi tatra satyākāratvāropastannirākṛtireva sādhyate / phalano vastuvādino arthābhāve 'pi arthābhiniveśinaste kathaṃ susthitā iti /
body.translated_text: ordinary beings, even though they have perception connected with inference, do not attain the status of being ultimate, but remain merely in convention. For ordinary beings do not individually experience the real ultimate nature through perception. Hence, the nature of things does not even contradict convention; rather, what is superimposed there as having the character of reality —

body.text: ekato 'numānaṃ vyavahāreṇa pratyakṣasambaddhaṃ sat sthitiṃ pratnoti, aparataśca pratyakṣaṃ kāṣṭhadvayagharṣaṇajatitāgniriva tadbādhāṃ karotīti bādhitameva taditi cennaitāvatāsmāsvaniṣṭāpattiriti / yathā sarve jāgatikadharmā yathāvatpravicayāgnerindhanāni bhavanti, sa ca mithyendhanāni bhasmīkṛtya svayamapyupaśāntaḥ praśāntavikalpalakṣaṇamuttamaṃ nirvāṇamavabodhayatīti / yaduta -
body.translated_text: on the one hand, inference, being conventionally connected with perception, maintains its standing; on the other hand, perception, like fire born from the friction of two sticks, performs its refutation — so if [one says] it is refuted, that much does not amount to an undesired consequence for us. Just as all worldly <s>dharmas</s> become the fuel for the fire of thorough investigation, and that [fire], having burned up the false fuel, itself

body.text: vijñānāgnerjaddharmāḥ sarva evandhanaṃ matāḥ / tān yathāvatyravicayya jvālairdagdhvopaśāmyati // ato yadi tattvajñānamutyadyate tadānumānalakṣṇā kalpanā nivṛttā satī nirāśrayāpi nānabhyupagatā [bhavatī] / ata eva bhagavatā ratnakūṭe savikalpāpi sampratyavekṣaṇā nirvikalpajñānaphalotpatteḥ kāraṇamiti [matvā] mahāphalābhinirvṛttaye kāṣṭhadvayagharṣaṇajanitāgnerdṛṣṭāntena nirdiṣṭā /
body.translated_text: All inert <s>dharmas</s> are indeed considered the fuel for the fire of consciousness; having investigated them as they are and burned [them] with its flames, it subsides. Therefore, if the knowledge of reality arises, then conceptual construction, which has the characteristic of inference, having ceased, even though without support, is not [thereby] unaccepted. For this very reason, the Blessed One stated in the <s>Ratnakūṭa</s> that even conceptual investigation is a cause, since the fruit of non-conceptual knowledge (<s>nirvikalpa-jñāna</s>) arises [from it].

body.text: api ca, sarvadharmāṇāṃ niḥsvabhāvatvasādhane yadyeko hetubhūto dharmo nīrdiśyate tadā nivṛtisādhakaḥ sa dharmo viruddho jāyate /
body.translated_text: Moreover, if a single <s>dharma</s> serving as a reason is indicated for establishing the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, then that <s>dharma</s> which establishes cessation becomes contradictory.

body.text: yadyasan sa dharmastadā asato 'bhāvenāsambaddhatvāt kathaṃ hi sa [abhāvaṃ] sādhayediti /
body.translated_text: If that <s>dharma</s> is non-existent, then since non-existence, being non-entity, is unconnected, how could it establish [non-existence]?
