body.text: sataḥ kāryasya tāvat [kvacidapi] apekṣā naiva yujyate, sarvātmanā siddhatvāttasya / ato nākāṅkṣata eva sarvānapi / itthaṃ nitye tāvat kramaśo 'rthakriyā na yujyate, nāpi ca yugapadapi, yato hi tasya tathāvidhārthakriyāyā vinaṣṭasvabhāvamanusṛtya kāryotpattirvā tadviyogo vā na yujyate / yadi tatsāmarthyasvabhāvaṃ paścatkāle 'pi anusarati tadāpi tena sarvāṇi kāryāṇi yāni pūrvotpannani tāni naiva punarutpādayituṃ śakyante, pūrvotpannatvādeva /
body.translated_text: For an effect that already exists, there is no need for dependence [on anything], since it is already fully accomplished in every respect. Hence it does not expect anything at all. Thus, for a permanent [cause], efficacious activity is not tenable either sequentially or simultaneously, for the effect must follow the perishable nature of such efficacious activity.

body.text: yadanyat tatsadṛśaṃ tatkathaṃ notpadyata iti virodhaparīkṣāpi tāvannaiva yujyate,tena tadutpādayitumaśakyatvāt / sāmarthye sati pūrvotpannameva syāditi cet? naiva tāvattad yujyate / tata utpādyasya kāryasya anutpattāvapi tadutpattisāmarthyasvabhāvānusaraṇaṃ pratihataṃ syāt / yo yadā yadutpādayati tadā tasmin apratihatasāmarthyaṃ bhavatīti kathanaṃ naiva yuktimattaram / tasmādayaṃ pūrvamapi paścātkāla iva anutpādaka eva syāt, anutpādakāvasthāto 'bhinnatvāt / tataśca paścātkāle 'pi pūrvavad utpādaka eva syāt / yadyevaṃ nāsti tadā viruddhadharmayogād asmaikatvahāniḥ syāt / ataḥ sa yugapadarśakriyāmapi tāvannaiva karoti /
body.translated_text: As for [the question] why something else similar to it does not arise — even the examination of contradiction is not tenable, since it is incapable of producing that. If [one says] that given its capacity, it would have arisen before — even that is not tenable. For even without the arising of the effect to be produced, the continuity of the nature of the capacity to produce it

body.text: kramayaugapadyābhyāṃ vyatiricya anyastāvat prakāro 'rthakriyākārī nāstyeva / parasparaparicchittyā vyavacchedābhāvāt, [ataḥ] asanneva saḥ / ato parasparaparihārasthitalakṣaṇo virodhāntaro na sidhyatīti cet? asanneva tadā sa iti / ataḥ parato nityādutpattistāvannaiva yujyate /
body.translated_text: There is no other mode of efficacious activity apart from sequence and simultaneity. Since there is no exclusion through mutual ascertainment, it is simply non-existent. Hence, if [one says] that the other kind of contradiction, whose characteristic is mutual exclusion in abiding, is not established — even then it is simply non-existent. Therefore, origination from a permanent other [cause]

body.text: nāpyanityāt, kṣaṇasthitidharmitvāttasyānityasya / ataḥ kalpakalpāntareṣu aviśeṣatayā sthitatvāt pūrvavat paścādapi tasya vināśo naiva yujyate / kāryotpattistāvadatītād [hetoḥ] bhavatīti vaibhāṣikāḥ, yathā te atītādapi vipākahetoḥ kāryotpattiṃ varṇayanti, anāgatāṃ vā, yathā tata eva anāgatajāterutpādaḥ / evaṃvidha upacāro vā vartamānakriyākramo vā atītāddhetorbhavatīti vādo naiva sarvathā yuktaḥ, atītasyāsattvāt / yadi tata utpattiraṅgīkriyate tadā ahetuta eva syāt /
body.translated_text: Nor from an impermanent [cause], since that impermanent [thing] has the property of existing for only a moment. Hence, remaining without difference across aeons, its destruction later is not tenable, just as before. The <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s> [hold that] the arising of the effect occurs from a past [cause]. As they describe the arising of an effect even from a past ripening cause (<s>vipākahetu</s>) —

body.text: ko hi nāmātītaḥ? kimupahatasvabhāvo 'tīta iti / yadyevaṃ nāsti tadā vartamāna iva anupahatasvabhāvātmakatvāt kathaṃ hi sa atīta iti / yaścopahatasvabhāvaḥ sa tāvadasatsvabhāvatvāt kathaṃ kāryamutpādayiṣyati / arthakriyā hi svasvabhāvamevāpekṣate / yadi kriyāvināśena atīta ityucyate, na tu svabhāvaparihāṇyetyucyate, evaṃ sati vinaṣṭāyāḥ kriyātaḥ kāryotpattirnaiva yujyate / evaṃ na bhavati / kathaṃ hi kāryotpattau kriyamāṇāyāṃ kriyāvināśa iti / ekasvabhāvātmake vastuni kriyāvanti akriyāvanti ca kāryāṇi na yujyate, bhinnatāyāḥ prasaṅgāt, niraṃśatvāddhi tasya /
body.translated_text: What indeed is the past (<s>atīta</s>)? Is the past that whose nature is impaired? If so [i.e., if it does not exist], then being of the nature of unimpaired nature like the present, how is it past? And that whose nature is impaired, being of the nature of non-existence, how could it produce an effect? For efficacious activity depends on its own nature. And

body.text: ākṣepamātrā hi kriyā, na cānādhāyikā, abhinnatvāt sa ākṣepakāla evādhānaṃ kariṣyati / anyathā pūrvavat paścādapi sā tathā bhavituṃ na śaktā syāt /
body.translated_text: Impulsion (<s>ākṣepa</s>) is indeed an action, and it is not non-conferring; being non-different [from the cause], it will confer [the result] at the very time of impulsion. Otherwise, just as before, it would not be capable of being so afterwards either.

body.text: api ca, kriyā nāma sā kiṃ samarthasvabhāvā yaduta karmasvabhāvā? yadi tat svabhāvadvayaṃ vastunaḥ sakāśād bhinnaṃ tadā kathaṃ nāma tad [vastu] vinaṣṭamityabhidhātuṃ śakyate / yadi tadupahatasvabhāvaṃ tadā samastavastuno nityasattāvādasya hāniḥ prasajyate / arthāntaravināśe satyapi vastuno hyacalasvabhāvasya vināśo naiva sidhyati / yathā mṛte 'pi devadatte yajñadattasya anupahatasvabhāvātmakatvānmṛta sa iti vaktuṃ na śakyate /
body.translated_text: Moreover, is this action called [impulsion] of the nature of capacity or of the nature of the object? If that dual nature is different from the thing, then how can that [thing] be said to have perished? If it is of impaired nature, then the unwanted consequence of the loss of the eternalist position regarding the constant existence of all things would follow.

body.text: yadi kriyāntaravināśāttasya vināśaḥsvīkriyate, tadaitannaiva yujyate, anavasthānāt, yato hi kriyāyāṃ kriyāntarasadbhāvo nāstyet / tasyāmapi tulya eva virodhaḥ parīkṣā ca / phalataḥ kasyāpi vināśo naiva sidhyet / anyārthatve sati kriyāyāḥ vastu tāvad ahetukameva syāt, kevalaṃ kriyāta eva kāryasyotpādāt / ato vastunastāvadasattvaprasaṅgaḥ / arthakriyāsāmarthyalakṣaṇatvād vastunaḥ / anyārthakriyāntarobhayasvabhāvātmakatvād yadi vastuna utpattirabhyupagamyate tadā kriyā yadā vastuna utpattirabhyupagamyate tadā kriyā yadā svabhāvata evotpādayati tadā vastvapi tathaivotpādakaṃ syāt / phalato 'nyārthapratītyā kim? arthāntarasya pakṣatve anyārthakalpanāyām anavasthādoṣānnaiva [kadāpi] hetutvaṃ sidhyet / vastūpakārābhāvād 'asyeyaṃ kriyā' - iti sambandha eva na siddhaḥ syād, upakārasāpekṣatvāt sambandhasyeti /
body.translated_text: If its destruction is accepted through another action's destruction, then this is simply not tenable, because of infinite regress — since in the action, the existence of another action does not hold. In that [other action] too, the same contradiction and examination [apply]. In consequence, no destruction of anything would ever be established. If the action serves another purpose, then the entity would be without cause, since the effect arises merely from the action. Therefore, the absurd consequence of the non-existence of the entity [follows], since the entity is characterized by the capacity for causal efficacy (<s>arthakriyāsāmarthya</s>). If the arising of the entity is accepted as having a nature that is both other-purpose and action-combined, then when the action produces by its own nature, the entity too would produce in just the same way. What, then, is the need for dependence on another purpose? If the other purpose is the thesis, then, due to the fault of infinite regress in constructing another purpose, the status of being a cause would never be established. Due to the absence of benefit to the entity, the very connection 'this is its action' would not be established, since connection depends on benefit.

body.text: upakārakatvameva yadi vastutvenāṅgīkriyate tadā kriyātmakatvād vastunaḥ, kriyāmupakarotīti cettadā kāryamapi kathaṃ na tathaivopakaroti? kena tāvat kāraṇena kriyāntaratvenopakalpyate? yadi kriyā hi sanmātravastusāpekṣaiva tadā avikalahetutvāt sadā talsamīpavartinī eva, ato vināśo 'pi tāvannaiva sidhyati / yadi sā arthantarabhūtā tadā sambandhastāvadasiddha eva / kriyāṇāmeva parasparayogād vastu tāavad gauṇameva sthāsyapi / kṣaṇikasya [vastunaḥ] utpādasamanantarameva asthāyitvāt [tasya kasyāmapi] kriyāyāṃ karmasvabhāvatvaṃ naiva yujyate ye tāvadakṣaṇikāste sadā ekasvabhāvatvenāvasthitvānnaiva kriyāvanta ākāśavat / ataḥ keṣvapi 'karma kriyate' iti na sidhyati / ata eva sāmarthyakriyādiśabdena vastusvabhāvo 'bhidhīyate, nānyasminnarthe /
body.translated_text: If benefiting itself is accepted as entity-nature, then, since the entity would be of the nature of action — and if [one says] 'it benefits the action' — then why would the effect not similarly benefit? For what reason is it constructed as another action? If the action is dependent merely on an existent entity, then, since the cause is complete, it would always be proximate to it — and therefore destruction too would not be established. If it is something different, then the connection is simply not established. Due to the mutual conjunction of actions alone, the entity would remain merely secondary. Since a momentary [entity], due to its non-endurance immediately upon arising, [cannot be] the object-nature in any action — this is simply not tenable. Those that are non-momentary, since they abide always in a single nature, would have no action at all, like space. Therefore, in no [entities] is 'action is performed' established. Hence, by the word 'capacity,' 'action,' and the like, the own-nature of the entity is denoted, not anything else.

body.text: kriyā, yā vastvabhinnatvenobhayasvabhāvā, sā vinaśya yadi svasvabhāvopahatalakṣaṇā [bhavati], tadā vastvapi tadabhinnatayā svasvabhāvohatameva bhavati / ataḥ kathamatītasya sattvaṃ setsyatītī? vastunaḥ svasvabhāva iva kriyāyā api avināśaprasaṅge sati kriyāyā naiva [kadāpi] vināśaḥ sidhyati / saiva kriyā punaryadi anyatve 'nabhidheyeti sati kriyāyā naiva [kadāpi] vināśaḥ sidhyati / saiva kriyā punaryadi anyatve 'nabhidheyeti kalpyate tadā prajñaptisattvāt sā avastveva / phalatastadbalena trikālavyavasthāpi naiva samīcīnā syāt / vastusataḥ kenāpa prakāreṇa anabhidheyatvaṃ nopapadyate / tathā sati sarvasyāpyanābhidheyatvaprasaṅgaḥ / ato 'tītasya avastutvānnaiva tena kāryasyotpattiriti /
body.translated_text: If the action — which, being non-different from the entity, has both natures — when it perishes, has its characteristic impaired by its own nature, then the entity too, being non-different from it, would have its own nature impaired. Therefore, how would the existence of the past be established? Just as there would be the absurd consequence of non-destruction of the action like the own-nature of the entity —

body.text: nāpyanāgatāt / atīta iva tasyāpyasattvāt / evamasattvād ākāśakamalasadṛśād anāgatādapi kāryotpattirnaiva yujyate / yadi aprāptakriyastāvadanāgata ityucyate tadā tadānīṃ tasmādapi kāryotpattiḥ ātyantikatayā naiva yuktimatī, aprāptakriyatvādeva / yadi vastu sarvadā vidyamānaṃ tadā tasyāḥ prāpteravikalakāraṇānāṃ sadbhāve 'pi kimiva kriyā naiva prāpyate / nāpi kriyā vastunaḥ sakāśādarthāntarabhūteti pūrvameva nirdiṣṭatvāt / yadi nāsti arthāntarabhūtā tadā kriyāvat svabhāvo 'pi naiva aprāptaḥ syādabhinnatvāt / ataḥ anāgatāstitvaṃ naiva sidhyati / vastunaḥ svabhāva iva tadabhinnā kriyāpi sarvadā sadeva, ataḥ sā aprāptetyapi naiva sidhyati / ataḥ anāgatānnāsti kāryotpattiḥ tasyāsattvādeva /
body.translated_text: Nor [can an effect arise] from the future, since, like the past, it too is non-existent. Thus, from a future [cause] resembling a sky-flower, which is non-existent, the arising of an effect is simply not tenable. If the future is defined as 'that which has not attained action,' then at that time, the arising of an effect from it is absolutely untenable, precisely because it has not attained action. If —

body.text: vartamāna ityapi pakṣo na sambhavati / yadi tataḥ [vartamanāt] kāryaṃ samutpadyate tadā samakālaṃ vā samutpadyatām,. viṣamakālaṃ [bhinnakālaṃ] vā samutpadyatām / na tāvat kadācit samakālam / kāryotpattitaḥ pūrvaṃ śaśaśṛṅganibhād asatkāraṇād utpādo naiva yuktaḥ / yasmin kāle ca hetorātmabhāvaḥ [kāryotpadane] samarthastasmin kāle kāryasyāpi samakālaṃ sattvāt siddhameva tat [kāryam] iti / atastasmin [karye] sa hetuḥ kamapi vyāpāraṃ naiva karoti / hetuvyavahāro 'pi tāvat [tasmin] naiva yuktarūpaḥ, yathā phalābhimato naiva heturiti / yadyevaṃ na syāttadā kāryakāraṇabhāvasyaiva bhaṅgaḥ syāditi / viṣama [bhinna] kālamiti pakṣo 'pi naiva sambhavati evameva yadi kāryaṃ [utpādāt] pūrvameva sat syāt tadānāgatotpādaḥ syāt / ayamapi tāvat [pakṣaḥ] naiva yujyata ityuktapūrvamasmābhiḥ /
body.translated_text: The thesis 'from the present' is also not possible. If the effect arises from that [present cause], does it arise simultaneously or at a different time? Never simultaneously — arising from a non-existent cause, resembling a hare's horn, prior to the arising of the effect, is not [possible] —

body.text: yadi [kāryaṃ] kṣaṇāntaravyavadhānenotpadyate tadā tadatītādevotpadyata iti naiva yuktamityuktapūrvam / yadyavyavahitatayā [utpādaḥ], tadā sarvātmanāvyāvahitatvāt samakālikatāprasaṅgaḥ / athāpi syāt, yadyapi avyavahitatvena kāryasyotpādastathāpi nāsti samakālikatāprasaṅgaḥ, dvitīye kṣaṇe kāryasattāyā abhyupagamāditi / tadāpi kṣaṇikatvānnasti hetoḥ sthitiḥ / atra bhagavatāpi - "asmin satīdaṃ bhavati" iti kāryakaraṇabhāvasya nirdeśāt kalpanātrayaṃ vivarjya caturthī svīkriyate / tāḥ kalpanāḥ punaḥ - kāraṇat pūrvaṃ kāryaṃ vā, samakālike kāryakāraṇe vā, kṣaṇāntaravyavahitatvaṃ vā, avyavahitatve sati dvitīyakṣaṇe 'vasthānaṃ vā - ityevaṃvidhāḥ syuḥ /
body.translated_text: If [the effect] arises with the intervening of another moment, then it would arise from what has become past — which has been said to be untenable. If [it arises] without interval, then, since there is no interval whatsoever, the absurd consequence of simultaneity [follows]. Moreover, even if the arising of the effect is without interval —

body.text: tatra yattavat pūrvameva sthitaṃ bhavati na tad hetau sati jāyate, pūrvameva niṣpannatvāttasya / samakāle 'pi hetuto naivotpatsyate [kāryam], tasmin kāle tasya [kāryasya] api satvāt / ityevaṃ samakālikakāryābhāvāt kāraṇasyāpyasattvam / kāraṇasattve kāryesyāpi sattvam / tṛtīyakṣaṇabhāvi kāryamapio hetuto notpadyate, dvitīyasattve kāryasyāpi sattvam / tṛtīyakṣaṇabhāvi kāryamapi hetuto notpadyate, dvitīyakṣaṇa eva vināśāt kāraṇaṃ tāvadasadeva / ityaṃ dvitīyakṣaṇe vidyamānaṃ kāryameva hetoḥ samutpadyate, prāthamakṣaṇikasya hetoḥ svakāle sattvādeva / tato 'vyavahite dvitīye kṣaṇe kāryasattāyā anubhavārtham - "asmin satīdaṃ bhavatī" tyuktam / na ca kāryakāle kāeanasattāyāḥ prasaṅgaḥ, kṣaṇikatvāttadā tasyāsattvāt / nāpi vinaṣṭāt kāraṇāt kāryotpattiprasaṅgaḥ, prathame kṣaṇe kāraṇasya avinaṣṭātvāt tadavyavadhānenaiva ca kāryasyotpādāt / tṛtīye kṣaṇe tāvat kāryotpādo 'sviti cet? naitadapi yujyate, [kāryakāraṇayo] madhye nāstyevaṃvidham aṇumātramapi kālāntarāstitvam / vidyamānaṃ kāraṇaṃ kālāntarāvyavahitaṃ ca kāryaṃ yadyabhyupagamyate, naiva tatkāryaṃ tadā svanirbharam / [evaṃ ca sati] samakālikatvaprasaṅgaḥ syānnaveti vicāraṇīyatāmarhati / niraṃśe tāvad vastuni kālāntareṇāvyavahite ca sati samakālikatvaṃ muktvā nānyā gatiḥ sambhavati, tayoḥsarvātmanā avyavahitatvāt / yadi nāsti madhye kālāntarāstitvaṃ tadā avaśyaṃ pūrvāparatoḥ kṣaṇayoḥ saṃsparśaḥ syāt / tathā ca sati sarveṣāṃ [kṣaṇānāṃ] ekasminneva kṣaṇe samanupraveśaḥ syāt / [phalataḥ] yathā paramāṇoḥ sarvātmanā saṃyoge piṇḍasya aṇumātratāprasaṅgaḥ, tathaiva kalpasyāpi kṣaṇamātratāprasaṅga iti /
body.translated_text: That which already existed before — that does not arise when the cause is present, since it had already been accomplished. Even simultaneously, the effect will not arise from the cause, since at that time the [effect] too exists. Thus, due to the absence of a simultaneous effect, the cause too is non-existent. If the cause were existent —

body.text:
yathā khalu deśakramaḥ pramāṇairavabhāsamānatvāt saṃvṛtau svīkriyata tathā kālakramo 'pio tatsadṛśa eva, svapnādau kalpādīnāmapyavabhāsamānatvāt / tatra prayogaḥ - ye sarvātmanā kālāntareṇāvyavahitāsteṣu pūrvāparakālabhedo na sambhavati, dakṣiṇavāmaśṛṅgavat kāryakāraṇayorapi sarvātmanā kālāntareṇāvyavadhānamiti, svabhāvahetuḥ /
athaikadeśenāvyavahitatvam, naiva sarvātmaneti cet? tadā kṣaṇasyāpi sāvayavatvaprasaṅgaḥ / phalataḥ antimakālalakṣaṇasya kṣaṇasyāpi [svarūpatā]hāniḥ syāt /
athāpi kāryotpattikāle hetorabhāvād, abhāvena ca saha sarvātmanā vā ekadeśena vā avyavahitatvamiti cintā na pravartata iti cet? tadapi naiva yujyate, tayormadhye kasyā api kālāntarasadbhāvasambhāvanāyā abhāvānnaiva tadā hetvabhāvayogaḥ sambhavati /
body.translated_text: Just as spatial sequence is accepted in the conventional, because it appears to <s>pramāṇas</s> (valid means of knowledge), so too temporal sequence is of the same kind, since even <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages) and the like appear in dreams. The argument there is: for those that are completely without interval by another time, the distinction of earlier and later time is not possible, [just as] right and left —

body.text: punaśca, kāryotpattikāle yadi kāraṇaṃ nāsti, tadā kāryamahetukameva syāt / vinaṣṭāt kāraṇāt yadi kāryamabhyupagamyate, na tu vartamānāt [vartamānasya tadānīm] asattvāt, tadā tasya vartamānamayuktam, yadi tad vartamānaṃ tadā [tasya] asattven saha virodha āpadyate / yadi tat sadityabhyupeyate tadā avyavahitatvadicintā kathaṃ na pravṛtā syāt / yadi punaḥ kāryotpattikāle kāraṇaṃ vidyamānameva, kintu kāryasattākāle tadasaditi hetoḥ avyavahitatvādicintā naiva kāryeti cet? naitadapi yujyate, sattāto 'nanyārthakatvādutpatteḥ / itthaṃ tu bhavantaḥ kāraṇasya nirantaratve satkāryasyotpattiṃ varṇayanti / ye tāvannirantaratvena sattvādityabhidadhānāste 'pi kathañcidapyavahitatvamabhyupagacchantyeva / anthayā nirantaraśabdasya ko 'rthaḥ syāt / nirantaratvam avyavahitvaṃ saṃspṛṣṭatvamityādīnāmabhinnārthakatvāt tadabhyupagamasāmarthyena kāryakāraṇaikatvamapyabhyupagataṃ syāt / kālāntareṇāvyavahitasya sato nānyāvasthā sambhavinī /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, if the cause does not exist at the time the effect arises, then the effect would be without a cause. If the effect is accepted from a destroyed cause, but not from a present [one] — since [the present cause is] non-existent [at the time of the effect] — then calling it 'present' would be unjustified. If it were present, there would be a contradiction with its non-existence —

body.text: api ca, vinaṣṭahetoḥ kāryotpattiprasaṅgasya ayujyamānatvād bhavantastaṃ [pakṣaṃ] parityajya vartamānahetoravyavadhānena kāryotpattimabhyupagacchanti / tatra tāvat kiṃ sarvātmanā kāryotpattiṃ svīkurvanti yaduta ekadeśeneti cintā pravṛttaiva syāt, prakārāntarasyāsambhavāt / ataḥ kāraṇaṃ tāvat kāryakṣaṇāvyavahitameva / tatra ca ye nāpyekadeśena na ca sarvātmaneti bruvanti, tena taiḥ kimucyata iti vicāryamāṇe avyavahitamapi nāpyavyavahitamiti kathanaṃ paryavasyet / evaṃvidhaṃ subhāṣitaṃ ko 'nyaḥ kathayituṃ pārayati /
body.translated_text: Moreover, since the absurd consequence of an effect arising from a destroyed cause is untenable, you abandon that position and accept the arising of an effect from a present cause without interval. There, the question arises whether you accept the arising of the effect in every respect or only partially — the inquiry has indeed proceeded [above] —

body.text: api ca, yadi vidyamānakāryakāle kāraṇaṃ nāstyeva, tadā 'avinaṣṭāt kāraṇāt kāryamutpadyata' iti naiva kathanīyam, tasmin kāle kasyāpyavinaṣṭakāraṇasyāsadbhāvāt / yasmin kāle kāraṇam avinaṣṭaṃ tasmin kāle kāryamapi nāsti, atastat [kāryaṃ] avinaṣṭāt kathamutpadyate /
body.translated_text: Moreover, if at the time the effect exists the cause simply does not exist, then it should not be stated that 'the effect arises from an undestroyed cause,' since at that time no undestroyed cause exists. At the time when the cause is undestroyed, the effect too does not exist — therefore, how would that [effect arise] from what is undestroyed?

body.text: evaṃ cintyate - svayaṃ vināśavyavahite 'pi vastuni nāsti samakālikatvam, yathācchāyātayoḥ pūrvāparatvābhāve 'pi udakadhārāyāṃ caikadeśatvaṃ nāsti, tathaivātrāpi kāryakāranayorasamīcīnarūpatve 'pi samakālikatvaṃ nāstītyayaṃ vicāraprakāro na yujyate, virodhāt tulyaparīkṣaṇīyatvācca /
body.translated_text: It is considered thus: even in an entity separated by its own destruction, there is no simultaneity — just as, [in the case of] a shadow and [its object], even when there is no before-and-after, there is no one-placedness in a stream of water — similarly here too, even though the cause and effect do not have a proper form [simultaneously], there is no simultaneity. This mode of examination is not tenable —

body.text: evaṃ tatra sadasadbhāve yadyekadeśenāvyavahitatvaṃ tadā avayavisadbhāvaprasaṅgaḥ / yadi sarvātmanā tadā samakālikatvameva / tathaiva chāyātapayorudakadharāyāṃ cāpi yadi sarvātmanāvyavahitatvaṃ tadaikadeśatvameva syāt / yadyekadeśenāvyavahitatvaṃ tadāvayavisādbhāvaprasaṅgaḥ / asmākaṃ tu [mate] sarva evāyaṃ sadasadbhāvaḥ paramārthato 'siddhaḥ, tasya sadasadbhāvādisarvaprapañcajālavirahitatvāt / avyavahitatvādisamudbhūto 'sadbhāva iti nāsti kaścana vyavahārastathāpi dvipīye kṣaṇe vastūni svasvabhāvanirodhamātraṃ prajñapayanti / nāsti kiñcinnirantaratvamiti, asanmātratvāt /
body.translated_text: Thus, regarding the state of existent and non-existent: if non-interruption is partial, there would be the absurd consequence of the part-possessor being existent. If total, then it is simply simultaneity. Likewise, in the cases of shadow-and-sunlight and water-stream: if non-interruption is total, it would simply be partial identity. If non-interruption is partial, there would be the absurd consequence of the part-possessor being non-existent. For us, however, this entire state of existent-and-non-existent is ultimately unestablished, because it is free from the entire net of conceptual elaboration including the states of existent and non-existent. There is no convention called 'non-existent state arising from non-interruption etc.' — nevertheless, in the second moment, things are designated as merely the cessation of their own nature. There is nothing that is continuous, because it is merely non-existent.

body.text: nirodhamātraṃ tāvanna kiñcit, atastena saha paramārthato 'vyavahitatvādicintanaṃ naiva pravartate / kāryakāraṇayostu paramārthataḥ sattvabhyupagamād ekadeśenāvyavahitatvādicintā tāvat pravartata eva / āryaśālistambasūtre yo hi bhagavatā tulādaṇḍopamayā avyavahitatvena kāryakāraṇabhāvo 'bhihitaḥ, sa tāvaducchedadṛṣṭiparhārārthaṃ sāṃvṛtikakāryakāraṇabhāvatvena draṣṭavyaḥ, na tu paramārthataḥ, tulādaṇḍasya paramārthatvenāsiddhatvāt / yadi tulādaṇḍasvabhāva eko 'vayavī dṛṣṭāntatvena pradaśryate, tadā sa khallavasiddha eva / parasparaviruddhayorunnāmāvanāmādikṛtyayorekasmin yugapadbhāvo naiva samīcīnaḥ / paramāṇusañcayātmako 'pi sa [tulādaṇdaḥ] arthato 'siddha eva, niravayavatvena sañcayasyāyujyamānatvādeva / yadi sa avayavīti tadā tasyābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ / yadi vijñānāvabhāsisvabhāvatvena tulādaṇḍastāvannirdiśayate, tadā parikalpitasvabhāvatvena mithyaiva saḥ / kathamiva tasya vastusattvaṃ syāt / amūrttatvād vijñānasya nordhvādhogamanam / ata eva chāyātapodakadhārādinottaritam /
body.translated_text: Mere cessation is nothing at all; therefore, thinking about non-interruption etc. in relation to it does not operate ultimately. But since the existence of cause and effect is accepted ultimately [by others], thinking about partial non-interruption etc. does indeed operate. The cause-effect relation stated by the Blessed One in the <s>Āryaśālistambasūtra</s> through the simile of a balance-beam as non-interrupted should be understood as conventional cause-effect relation, for the purpose of removing the view of annihilationism, and not ultimately — because the balance-beam is unestablished as an ultimate [reality]. If a balance-beam with a single part-possessor nature is presented as an example, then it is simply unestablished. The simultaneous presence in one [thing] of mutually contradictory functions such as rising and falling is not at all proper. Even as an aggregate of atoms, that [balance-beam] is factually unestablished, because an aggregate is impossible in what is partless. If it is a part-possessor, there would be the absurd consequence of its non-existence. If the balance-beam is indicated as having the nature of what appears in consciousness, then it is simply false as having an imagined nature. How could it have substantial reality? Because consciousness is immaterial, it does not move upward or downward. For this very reason, the examples of shadow-and-sunlight, water-stream, etc. are also surpassed.

body.text: laṅkāvatārādisūtreṣu bhagavatā kāryakāraṇabhāvaniṣedhastāvat sāṃvṛtakāryakāraṇeṣvevāvagantavyaḥ yadapi bhagavatā 'asmin satīdaṃ bhavati' ityuktaṃ tena vikalpatrayaṃ parihatya caturthaṃ eva vikalpo 'bhyupagamyata iti yaduktaṃ tad vakṣyate kiṃ 'asmin satīdaṃ bhavati' iti vacanena vikalpatrayaṃ niṣidhya caturthavikalpābhyupagam āgamena nirdiṣṭo yaduta yuktyā? āgameneti cet, tannaiva yujyate / yato hi yau chāyāṅkurau dīpaprakāśau vā samakālavidyamānau tāvapi dīpe sati prakāśo bhavatīti na vyavahāraviruddhau / evameva vidyamānakāryaṃ vidyamānakāraṇasāpekṣamiti śabdamātreṇa nirdiśyate, na tu vidyamānakāryakāle kāraṇaṃ nāsaditi / yadi hi vastutvaṃ pramāṇāntaraiḥ paramārthataḥ kṣaṇikatvena sādhyate tadā tadapi parikalpitamātrameva, na tvāgamena [siddhaḥ] / itthaṃ tu loke 'pi samakālikaṃ chāyāṅkurādikamapi kāryakāraṇabhāvena jñāyata eva /
body.translated_text: The denial of cause-effect relation by the Blessed One in the <s>Laṅkāvatārasūtra</s> and other sūtras should be understood as applying to conventional cause-effect [relations]. As for the Blessed One's statement 'when this exists, that arises' — the claim that by this, three alternatives are rejected and only the fourth alternative is accepted — we ask: is this fourth alternative indicated by scripture or by reasoning? If by scripture — that is not valid. For shadow and sprout, or lamp and light, which exist simultaneously — even they can be expressed as 'when the lamp exists, light arises,' and this does not contradict convention. In the same way, it is indicated merely by words that an existing effect depends on an existing cause, but it does not [mean] that the cause does not become non-existent at the time when the effect exists. If the fact of real existence is established as momentary through other <s>pramāṇas</s> ultimately, then that too is merely imagined, not [established] by scripture. In this way, even in the world, shadow, sprout, and such things that are simultaneous are known as having a cause-effect relation.

body.text: atha yuktyeti pakṣaḥ, tadā bhagavato vacanāni [pramāṇatvena] naivoddhartavyāni, tāni etadarthaṃ naiva pramāṇam / atha kevalayā yuktyaivaikayā kathanīyamiti cet? etadapi naiva vaktuṃ śakyate, yato hi yathā yuktyā vikalpatrayaṃ na sambhavati tathā caturtho 'pi vikalpaḥ paramārthato naiva sambhavatīti [pūrvaṃ] vistarena nirdiṣṭam /
body.translated_text: If the position is [that this is established] by reasoning, then the Blessed One's words should not be cited [as authoritative], since they are not <s>pramāṇa</s> for this purpose. If it is said that it should be stated by reasoning alone — this too cannot be said, because just as three alternatives are not possible through reasoning, the fourth alternative too is ultimately not possible — as has been explained in detail [previously].

body.text: lokaprasiddhimatikramya nityatvadravyatva svātantryādiguṇopetamātmānamabhyupetamātmānamabhyupetya karmafāsambandhādisaṃvṛtiṃ nirākurvatāṃ dṛṣṭiparihārārthaṃ bhagavaduktena idampratyayatāmātreṇevāvasthiteṣu saṃvṛtimāśritya asmin satīdaṃ bhavatītyuktam, na tvāgamena vikalpatrayaṃ parihatya caturthavikalpāśrayaṇaṃ kalpanīyam / ataḥ parata utpattirnaiva yuktimatī / phalataśca sarveṣāṃ vastūnāṃ māyeva prajñāptyā utpādādibhya eva santuṣyatām , mithyātvāt /
body.translated_text: For the purpose of removing the view of those who, transgressing common knowledge, accept a self endowed with qualities such as eternality, substantiality, and independence, and who deny the convention of the relation between action and its fruit, etc. — the Blessed One stated 'when this exists, that arises,' relying on convention, in matters that are established merely through conditionality (<s>idaṃpratyayatā</s>). But one should not imagine that by scripture three alternatives are rejected and the fourth alternative is relied upon. Therefore, arising from an other is not supported by reasoning. Consequently, let one be satisfied with the designation of arising etc. for all things as if they were illusion, because of their falsity.

children.translated_text: The arising of an effect from a perished cause is not valid,
nor is the arising from an unperished [cause] accepted by you as being like a dream.
Whether from a ceased or an unceased seed, the arising of a sprout —
all arising is declared by you to be like a magical illusion. [17-18]

body.text: ato ye ācāryāḥ "na paramārthata adhyātmikānyāyatanāni praratyayataḥ samutpadyante, paratvāt" ityādyabhidadhate, [teṣāmapi] te hetavo naiva sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttikāḥ, vipakṣe bādhakapramāṇasambhavāt / ato 'nityatāsiddhivattāvat sattvasiddhiḥ / jaḍatādisiddhau parato vipakṣe bādhakapramāṇābhāvāt teṣvanaikāntikatā / utpādanirodha eva tāvat sādhanīyaḥ, na tu vipakṣe badhakapramāṇasadbhāvaḥ / vyavahāre parataḥ siddhatvānnastyasiddhatvaṃ pramāṇasyāpi [bhavanmate paramārthataḥ] samyagvastutvāddhetvādīnāṃ na vyavahāraḥ kutrāpi sidhyatīti nirdiṣṭaṃ pūrvam / ata eteṣāmanaikāntikatvāsiddhatvapratipādanaṃ nāma asambaddhamettaitat /
body.translated_text: Therefore, when the teachers state 'the internal sense-bases do not ultimately arise from conditions, because of being other' and so forth — their reasons do not have uncertain exclusion from the counter-thesis (<s>vipakṣa</s>), because there is the possibility of a contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s> in the counter-thesis. Therefore, the establishment of existence is like the establishment of impermanence. In [proving] inertness etc., because there is no contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s> in the counter-thesis, there is inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntika</s>) in those [cases]. It is the arising and cessation itself that is to be proved, not the presence of a contradicting <s>pramāṇa</s> in the counter-thesis. Since it is established conventionally as from another, the <s>pramāṇa</s> is not unestablished. [In your view], since ultimately the reasons etc. are truly real, it has been stated earlier that no convention is established anywhere. Therefore, the demonstration of their inconclusiveness and unestablishedness is entirely irrelevant.

body.text: tairthikāḥ ye hi parādivyavahāravaśāt parādīni santīti kathayanti tān ācārya āha -
body.translated_text: The teacher addresses those <s>Tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist philosophers) who, on the basis of conventional usage of 'from another' etc., say that 'other' etc. exist —

body.text: "na hi svabhāvo bhāvānāṃ pratyayādiṣu vidyate"
body.translated_text: 'The own-nature of entities is not found in conditions etc.'

body.text: ityādinā dūṣayatītyucyate / ataḥ śāstraistāvadasiddhatvāt parata utpattirnāstīti nirdiṣṭam / parādayaḥ śabdā ye tāvatprajñāptigocarāstānapi paramparayā vastusaṃsargiṇa ityabhidadhatāṃ teṣāṃ 'vastusabhāvaḥ pratyayeṣvastītyutpadyate' ityumamabhiprāyamādāya dūṣaṇaṃ pradattam, pratyayādiṣu sattve paramārthato vastusvabhāvasyānutpādāditi vistareṇa khalvabhihitam /
body.translated_text: — refuting [them] with this and similar [statements]. Therefore, it is stated in the treatises that since [other-nature] is unestablished, arising from another does not exist. The words 'other' etc. are objects of designation; those who say they are ultimately connected with real entities — their statement 'the own-nature of a real entity exists in conditions' was taken as the intended meaning and a refutation was given, because when own-nature exists in conditions etc., the own-nature of the real entity is ultimately unarisen — as has been stated in detail.

body.text: ato yadā sarveṣāṃ vastūnāṃ paramārthataḥ parata utpādo naivopapadyate tadā pratyayādibhyo 'pi anutpādādasiddha eva / ato nāstyeva paramārthataḥ śabdasaṃsargi kimapi vastu / phalato 'siddhe 'pyevaṃvidhe vyavahāre vastu tāvadabādhitameveti yaduktaṃ tanna yujyate /
body.translated_text: Therefore, when the arising from another of all things is ultimately untenable, then because of non-arising even from conditions etc., [other-nature] is simply unestablished. Therefore, there is no real entity whatsoever that is ultimately connected with words. Consequently, the statement that 'even though such a convention is unestablished, the entity is uncontradicted' is not valid.

body.text: ye sāṃkhyādayaḥ pradhāneśvarādikaṃ manvānāḥ pradhāneśvarādibhyo vastūnāmutpādamabhyupagacchanti, teṣāmapi mataṃ svato vā parato vā utpādapakṣe pṛthakpṛtham doṣābhidhānānnaiva yuktarūpamiti /
body.translated_text: Those <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> and others who, conceiving of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), <s>Īśvara</s> (God), and such, accept the arising of things from <s>Pradhāna</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, etc. — their view too is not proper, because faults have been separately stated for each of the positions of arising from self or from another.

body.text: anye ye kadācit svātantryena ubhayata utpattiṃ varṇayanti , te 'pyubhayapakṣīya [svaparapakṣīya] doṣairdūṣitatvānnirākṛtā eva / apare ca ye tāvat - 'ubhayātmakasya vastunaḥ pramāṇaviruddhatvānna ko 'pi tadabhyupagacchatīti hetoḥ ubhayata utpattiṃ dūṣayitvā bhavantaḥ kevalamātmānameva mohayanti, tattu [bhavatāṃ] śabdamātrameva" iti kathayanti / te tāvad vidvāṃsaḥ svayaṃ śāstrāṇāmaparijñānāt śabdārthayośca samyaganavagamāt [kevalaṃ] śabdaśa upahasanti / kecana tāvat kaṇṭakāditīkṣṇatādṛṣṭāntena sarvāṇi vastūni paramārthato 'hetuta utpadyanta iti kathayanti, tatra vastūnāṃ paramārthato 'hetuta utpattiṃ sādhayatāṃ teṣāṃ dṛṣṭāntastāvannaiva siddhaḥ, paramārthato 'nutpannatvāt sarvadharmāṇām / saṃvṛtau suddha iti cenna, tatrāpyasiddha eva, kaṇṭādīnāṃ svabījata utpādaḥ pratyakṣato niścitatvāt / anenaiva teṣāṃ taikṣṇyādīnāmapi niścitatvānna ko 'pi [dharmaḥ] ahetuta utpadyate / evaṃ kādācitkatvāt sarveṣāmeteṣāṃ vastūnāṃ sāpekṣatvaṃ niścitameva anapekṣitasya tu sadā aviśeṣāttasya kādācitkatvaṃ nopapadyata eveti /
body.translated_text: Others who sometimes describe arising from both [self and other] independently — they too are refuted, because they are vitiated by the faults of both positions. And still others who say 'since an entity of both natures is contradicted by <s>pramāṇa</s>, no one accepts it; therefore, having refuted arising from both because of the reason [that no one accepts it], you merely delude yourselves — but that is just empty words' — those learned ones, due to their own lack of full understanding of the treatises and improper comprehension of the relation between word and meaning, merely mock [us] on the basis of words. Some describe, using the example of the sharpness of thorns etc., that all things ultimately arise without a cause. In proving the causeless arising of things ultimately, their example is simply not established, because all <s>dharmas</s> are ultimately unarisen. If [they say the example is established] conventionally — it is not established even there, because the arising of thorns etc. from their own seeds is determined through direct perception. By this very [fact], since the sharpness etc. of those [things] is also determined, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever arises without a cause. Thus, because of occasional occurrence, the dependence of all these things is certainly established. For what is independent, since there would be no difference at all times, its occasional occurrence is simply untenable.

body.text: yatteṣāṃ sāpekṣatvaṃ tadeva hetuḥ, anupakāriṇi apekṣāyā anupapannatvāt / tatra yadupakārakatvena prasiddhaḥ, sa eva tasya heturiti sidhyati / ahetukatve sati sarvatra abhinnatvāt kaṇkādiṣvapi tīkṣṇatāyā nirdhāraṇaṃ na syāt / phalataḥ sarve sarvātmakāḥ syuḥ / ye bījādayaste loke kāryakāraṇātmakatvena pratyakṣataḥ siddhāḥ / ataḥ pratijñā tāvat pratyakṣabādhitaiva / api ca, hetutaḥ sādyasya sādhanāvasare anyataḥ [hetataḥ] utpatteḥ [siddheḥ, bhavadbhiḥ] avaśyaṃ svīkārāt svavacanavirodho 'pi / anyathā hetuprayoga eva tāvannirarthakaḥ syāt / naiva pratijñāmātreṇa tāvadiṣṭārthasiddhiḥ, tathā sati sarvataḥ sarvasiddhiprasaṅgaḥ / ato 'hetuvādī khalu vyavahāre pratyakṣādibhirbādhitatvād vidvadbhiḥ sāvadhānatayā pariharttavya eva /
body.translated_text: That very dependence of those [things] is the cause, because dependence on what does not assist is untenable. Therein, what is well-known as assisting — that very thing is established as its cause. If there were no cause, then because of non-difference everywhere, the determination of sharpness even in thorns and such would not be possible. Consequently, everything would be of every nature. Seeds and such are established in the world through direct perception as having the nature of cause and effect. Therefore, the thesis is contradicted by perception itself. Moreover, since you necessarily accept that a proof arises from something else [i.e., from a cause] in the course of proving what is to be proved by a reason, there is also a contradiction with your own words. Otherwise, the very application of a reason would be purposeless. A desired meaning is not established merely by assertion; if it were, there would be the absurd consequence of everything being established from everything. Therefore, the proponent of causelessness, being contradicted in convention by perception and other [<s>pramāṇas</s>], should indeed be carefully avoided by the wise.

body.text: hetvādayastāvanmāyādivat siddhāḥ, te yathā avicāraramaṇīyatvena prasiddhāstathā teṣāmaniṣedhād anutpattirityucyate, pratyakṣāditaścāpi sāṃ naiva bādhitā / dharmyasiddhatvādayastāvad doṣāḥ pūrvameva nirākṛtāḥ / sapakṣe sattvānnāsti heturapyasiddho viruddhaścāpi / ākāśapuṣpādayastvanutpanna eva, na te sasvabhāvatvenānubhūyante / atasteṣu vyāpterutpatteḥ samyaṅ nivṛttyā tasyāpi [sasvabhāvatvasya] nivṛttiḥ / ato nāstyanaikāntikatvamapi / teṣūtpatteḥ pravṛttirniścayena sādhayituṃ naiva śakyate, svapnādiṣvasatputrādīnāmapyutpattidarśanāt / sā khalu [utpattiḥ] tadvijñāne tathaivāvabhāsata ityapi kathanamyuktam, kathanamayuktam, tatrāpi paramārthatastathākāro naiva sambhavīti pūrvaṃ nirdiṣṭam / anyasya anyākāreṇāvabhāsanamapyayuktameva tattvānyatvayoḥ parasparaviruddhatvāt?
body.translated_text: Reasons etc. are established like illusion etc. — just as they are well-known as being delightful without investigation, their non-arising is stated because of not denying them, and it is not contradicted even by perception etc. The faults of unestablished subject etc. have already been refuted earlier. Because [the reason] is present in the similar class (<s>sapakṣa</s>), the reason is not unestablished nor contradictory. Sky-flowers etc. are simply unarisen; they are not experienced as having own-nature. Therefore, through the correct exclusion of arising in those [sky-flowers etc.], there is also the exclusion of that [own-nature]. Therefore, there is no inconclusiveness either. The occurrence of arising in those [things] cannot be established with certainty, because even non-existent sons etc. are seen to arise in dreams and such. The statement 'that [arising] appears just so in their consciousness, therefore it exists as substantially real with the nature of consciousness' — is also not valid, because it has been stated earlier that ultimately such an aspect is not possible even there. Is not the appearance of one thing in the aspect of another also not valid, because identity and difference are mutually contradictory?

body.text: tadutpattyā sasvabhāvatvādīnāṃ vyaptatve 'pi utpattau satyāṃ samyaksvabhāvo naiva niyatarūpeṇa sidhyati, vyāpakasāmīpye sarvavyāpyāṇāṃ sāmīpyaṃ navaśyaṃbhāvīti niścitamityuktameva pūrvam / ataḥ sādhāraṇamevaitad / paramarthato na kasminnapyutpattiḥ pravartata iti sādhitameva /
body.translated_text: Even if [the concepts of] own-nature etc. are pervaded by its arising, when arising is present, a correct own-nature is not established in a determinate form — because it has been stated earlier that when the pervader is nearby, the nearness of all the pervaded is not necessarily the case. Therefore, this is entirely common. It has been established that ultimately arising does not operate in anything whatsoever.

body.text: yanna kaiścidapi pratyayaiḥ samutpadyate tad vastu kutaḥ prādurbhavatīti kathayadbhirabhivyaktimātrameva ato 'naikāntika eva heturiti cet tatasyāpi pūrvaṃ nirākṛtatvāt tyājyamevaitaditi / atha pratyayairvastu abhivyajyata eveti cettadā ki sā abhivyaktiḥ svalakṣaṇopacayasvabhāvā vā tadāvaraṇasaṃkṣayātmiokā vā indriyaiḥ sukṛtā vā tadviṣayakavijñānotpattilakṣaṇā veti vicāraḥ samupajāyante /
body.translated_text: If those who say 'from where does an entity that is not produced by any conditions whatsoever come into being' [answer that] it is mere manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>) — and therefore the reason is inconclusive — since that too has been previously refuted, it should be abandoned. If [they say] an entity is indeed manifested by conditions, then what is that manifestation? Various investigations arise: is it of the nature of an increase in own-characteristics, or of the nature of destruction of its covering, or is it produced by the senses, or does it have the characteristic of the arising of a cognition of that object?

body.text: tatra naiva tāvat prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ kathamapi yujyate, nityatāyā hāniprasaṅgat /
body.translated_text: The first position is not valid in any way, because there would be the absurd consequence of the loss of eternality.

body.text: yadā anupacayasvabhāvaḥ svato vinaśya abhivyañcakapratyayairutpadyate tadā ekasyāparasyānupacayasvabhāvasyotpādavaśāt svalakṣaṇopacayo bhavatīti cet? na, tatpūrvasvabhāvo yadi na nirudhyeta tadā dvau parasparāvirudhau upacayāpacayasvabhāvau niryuktitayā ekasminneva svīkāryau syātām / yadyapūrvaḥ kaścana svabhāvo notpadyate tadā abhivyañcakāḥ pratyayāstāvannirarthakaḥ syuḥ / upacayamanirākṛtya vastūnāmutpattirapi na yujyate / tacca naiva tāvadāvaraṇasaṃkṣayātmakam, asatsvabhāvatvena parairakāryatvāt /
body.translated_text: If [they say] that what has the nature of non-increase, having perished of its own accord, arises through manifesting conditions, and thus through the arising of another [thing] that has the nature of non-increase, there is an increase in own-characteristics — no. If the previous nature does not cease, then two mutually contradictory natures — increase and non-increase — would have to be unreasonably accepted in a single [thing]. If no new nature arises at all, then the manifesting conditions would be purposeless. Without refuting increase, the arising of things is also not valid. And that [manifestation] is certainly not of the nature of destruction of covering, because according to others, what has a non-existent nature is not a cause.

body.text: vatusvabhāve kriyānirākaraṇaṃ tāvat pūrvameva kṛtam / yadyasti ekā kriyā, tadā sarve te pratyayā ye yadā arthamabhivyañcinti tadā ananyārthabhūtā kriyā tatra naiva sambhavati, pūrvata eva tasyāvidyamānatvāt / nityasya bhāvasya tvāvaraṇaṃ tadviśeṣāṇāmavināśād anutpādācca kadāpi na yujyate, atiprasañgāt / tadviṣayakavijñānaotpattau vighnakaraṇādapyāvaranaṃ niva yujyate, svaviṣayakajñānotpattau samarthatvāt, vidyamāne svavijñāmavijñeyasvabhāve 'vikalavijñānaṃ tāvat kenāpi vighnayitumaśaktvācca / yadi nāsti sa samartho vā svavijñānavijñeyo vā tadā svahetuvikalatayā tadvijñānotpattireva na syāt / atastadviṣakavijñānotpattau vighnakārakatvād āvaraṇaṃ tāvannaiva yujyate /
body.translated_text: The refutation of action with respect to the nature of an entity has already been made previously. If there is a single action, then all those <s>pratyayas</s> (conditions) that manifest an object — at that time, an action that is non-different in nature from them is simply not possible, since it was non-existent from the very beginning. Moreover, <s>āvaraṇa</s> (obscuration) of a <s>nitya</s> (permanent) entity is never tenable, since its particular properties neither perish nor arise — and because of the absurd consequence of over-extension. Nor is <s>āvaraṇa</s> (obscuration) tenable through obstructing the arising of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) pertaining to that object, since [the permanent entity] has the <s>sāmarthya</s> (capacity) to produce cognition of its own object, and since, when its own nature as cognizable by its own consciousness exists, the unimpaired <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) cannot be obstructed by anything whatsoever. If it lacks that capacity, or if it lacks the nature of being cognizable by its own consciousness, then due to the incompleteness of its own causes, the arising of that consciousness would simply not occur. Therefore, <s>āvaraṇa</s> (obscuration) is simply not tenable on the grounds of obstructing the arising of consciousness pertaining to that object.

body.text: yathā āvaraṇasaṃkṣaye tathā vijñānotpattāvapi avighnāpādanasvabhāvo 'pi kriyāyāṃ naiva yujyate / asāmarthyāt tadvijñānavijñeyasvabhāvābhāvācca abhivyañjakaiḥ pratyayairāvaraṇaṃ kriyata ityasyāpi nirākaraṇaṃ kṛtameva [pūrvam] / tathātve 'pi tadviṣayakavijñānotpattirayuktaiva / yadi sāmarthayamabhyupagamyate tadā āvaraṇakārake satyapi avikalahetoḥ sadbhāvāt sadaiva vijñānotpattisambhavād vyañjakānāṃ bhāvānāṃ kriyā nirarthikaiva syāt / ato nityasya tāvadakiñcikaratvāt kathamapyāvaraṇaṃ na yujyate / anityatā tu kadāpi kenāpi hetuviśeṣeṇa vijñānānutpādakasyānyasya kṣaṇasyotpādād āvriyata eva /
body.translated_text: Just as in the case of the removal of <s>āvaraṇa</s> (obscuration), so too in the arising of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) — even the nature of not producing obstruction is not tenable as an action, due to the lack of <s>sāmarthya</s> (capacity) and the absence of the nature of being cognizable by that consciousness. The refutation of the claim that <s>āvaraṇa</s> (obscuration) is produced by <s>abhivyañjaka</s> (manifesting) conditions has also already been made previously. Even if that were the case, the arising of consciousness pertaining to that object would still be untenable. If <s>sāmarthya</s> (capacity) is accepted, then even when the obscuration-producer is present, since the complete cause exists, the arising of consciousness would always be possible — and therefore the action of the <s>abhivyañjaka</s> (manifesting) entities would be entirely purposeless. Thus, since a <s>nitya</s> (permanent) entity is incapable of any action whatsoever, <s>āvaraṇa</s> (obscuration) is in no way tenable for it. But for the <s>anitya</s> (impermanent), obscuration is indeed possible at some time through some particular cause, due to the arising of another <s>kṣaṇa</s> (moment) that does not produce consciousness.

body.text: indriyaiḥ sukṛtatvapakṣo 'pi tāvannaiva [yujyate] / yadi tatsukṛtvaṃ [vastu]svabhāvabhūtaṃ tadā anityātāyāḥ prasaṅgaḥ, pūrvasadṛśatvāttasya / yadi tadanyārthabhūtaṃ tadā sukṛtatvaṃ naiva yuktiyuktam, akiñcikaratvāttasya / yadyevaṃ nāsti tadātiprasaṅgaḥ / kasminnapi vastuni kenāpi kimapi karaṇaṃ tāvannaiva sambhavamiti [pūrvaṃ] nirdiṣṭam / indriyaiḥ sukṛtatve 'pi yadi abhivyañcakairbhāvaiḥ tadindriyavijñānotpādāsāmarthyam athavā tadvijñānavijñeyasvabhāvāsattvaṃ tadā tadvijñānotpattirasambhavinī, ato nirarthakameva tāvat sukṛtatvamiti prasaṅgaḥ /
body.translated_text: The thesis that [the object] is well-fashioned by the <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties) is also not tenable. If that well-fashioned quality belongs to the intrinsic nature [of the entity], then impermanence would follow, since it is similar to what was discussed before. If it is something different from the entity, then the well-fashioned quality is not logically justified, since it would be inefficacious. If it does not exist in that way either, then there is the absurd consequence of over-extension — it has been stated previously that no action whatsoever by anything upon any entity is possible. Even granting the well-fashioned quality produced by the <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties), if the <s>abhivyañjaka</s> (manifesting) entities lack the capacity to produce cognition through those sense faculties, or if the nature of being cognizable by that consciousness is absent, then the arising of that consciousness would be impossible — and therefore the absurd consequence follows that the well-fashioned quality is entirely purposeless.

body.text: yadi vidyata eva sāmarthyaṃ tadvijñeyasvabhāvo vā tadā indriyaiḥ sukṛtakatvataḥ pūrvameva tasmin [viṣaye] vijñānotpādasya prasañgaḥ syāt, tadā sukṛtakatvamapi nirarthakameva syat / atastamin viṣaye vijñānotpādalakṣaṇamapi na saṅgataṃ syāt / yato hyevaṃ tad vyaṅgyaṃ vastvapi yadi asamarthaṃ vā tadvijñānavijñeyavabhāvaṃ vāpi nāsti tadā vijñānotpāde 'pi na pad [vastu] tasya [vijñānasya] viṣayaḥ syāt / yadi [tad vastu] samarthaṃ vā tadvijñānavijñeyasvabhāvaṃ vā syāt tadā svasvabhāvavat sāmīpyāt tatsattāmatreṇaiva vijñānasya samutpādo bhaviṣyatītyato na tena vyañjakavijñānotpādaḥ kriyata iti [sidhyati] /
body.translated_text: If the <s>sāmarthya</s> (capacity) or the nature of being cognizable by that consciousness does indeed exist, then the arising of consciousness regarding that object would follow even prior to its being well-fashioned by the <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties), and in that case the well-fashioned quality too would be entirely purposeless. Therefore, even the characteristic of the arising of consciousness regarding that object would not be coherent. For if that manifest entity is either incapable or lacks the nature of being cognizable by its own consciousness, then even when consciousness arises, the entity would not be its object. If [that entity] is capable or possesses the nature of being cognizable by that consciousness, then, just like its own nature, merely by virtue of proximity and its mere existence, consciousness would arise — and therefore it is established that the arising of <s>abhivyañjaka</s> (manifesting) consciousness is not produced by it.

body.text: api ca, bhavatāṃ tāvanmate sarvesāṃ vastūnāṃ jāyataḥ sadaivāvatiṣṭhanta iti hetostatra [vastuṣu] vyaṅgyavyañjakādīnāmapi sadā avasthitatvāt / [nityatvāt] vyaṅgyavyañjakādivyavasthā naiva [samīcīnatayā sarvathā] yujyate, [teṣāṃ] vyaṅgyavyañjakādīnāmakiñcitkaratvāt / sadaivābhīvyaktiprasaṅgo 'pi sarvavastūnāṃ dūrnivāra eva, sarvadā avikalasamagrīkatvāt / api ca, vyaktasya tāvannityatvena parikalpitatvāt, nityasya ca sarvasāmarthyavirahiotatvānnaiva hi vastutvaṃ kathamapyupapadyate / ataḥ kathaṃ tenānaikāntikahetutvamapi / ityevaṃ yadi sarvasāmarthyaśūnyaṃ tasya abhāvarūpatvameva, yathā - vandhyāputra iti / ye tāvadīśvarādayaḥ [paraiḥ] abhyupagamyante, te 'pi tathaiva / te 'pi kramayogapadyābhyāmarthakriyāvirodhāt sarvasāmarthyaśūnyā eveti pūrvamapi [bahudhā] nirdiṣṭam / samakṣe siddhatvānnāyaṃ heturasiddhaḥ, nāpi viruddhaḥ, vandhyāputrādiṣu vastutvaprasaṅgānnāpyanaikāntiko 'pi / itthaṃ tāvadaśeṣasāmarthyaśūnyatvameva abhāvalakṣaṇam /
body.translated_text: Moreover, according to your own doctrine, since all entities, being born, always persist — and therefore the manifest, the manifester, and so forth also always abide in those entities [due to their permanence] — the distinction between the manifest, the manifester, and so forth is simply not tenable [in any proper way whatsoever], since those — the manifest, the manifester, and the rest — are entirely inefficacious. The absurd consequence that all entities are always manifest is also quite unavoidable, since the complete aggregate [of conditions] is always present. Furthermore, since the manifest is conceived as <s>nitya</s> (permanent), and since a permanent thing is devoid of all <s>sāmarthya</s> (capacity), its entityness is not established in any way whatsoever. Therefore, how can it even serve as a non-exclusive reason? Thus, if it is devoid of all capacity, it has the very nature of non-existence, like a son of a barren woman. Those entities such as <s>Īśvara</s> (God) and the like that are accepted by others are also just the same. They too, because of the contradiction with causal efficacy through both succession and simultaneity, are devoid of all capacity — as has been stated previously in many ways. Since [this] is established through direct perception, this reason is not unestablished, nor is it contradictory, and since entityness would absurdly follow for the son of a barren woman and the like, it is not non-exclusive either. Thus, being devoid of all capacity whatsoever is indeed the defining characteristic of non-existence.

body.text: asaṃskṛteṣvapi tathātvāt kathaṃ tāni vastūnīti? ityevaṃ pratisaṃkhyānirodhādayo ye sarvasāmarthyaśūnyāsteṣāṃ vandhyāputrādyabhinnatve 'pi ye khalu tān vastutvena parikalpayanti , teṣām kalpaneyaṃ naiva yuktimatī, hetorevābhāvāt /
body.translated_text: If one asks: since the <s>asaṃskṛtas</s> (unconditioned phenomena) are also of that nature, how can they be entities? — Indeed, regarding <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (analytical cessation) and the like, which are devoid of all capacity, even though they are no different from a son of a barren woman and the rest, those who conceive of them as entities — their conception is simply not rational, since there is no cause [to support it].

body.text: pratisaṃkhyānirodhādayo yadi kasyāpi jñānasya viṣayāstadā avaśyaṃ te hetutvenaṅgīkaraṇīyāḥ, ahetorviṣayatvānabhyupagamāt / hetuviśeṣasya svākārarpaṇamātreṇa vijñānopakārād viṣayatvamityaṅgīkriyate / yadyevaṃ tarhi tasya nityatāyā hāniprasaṅgaḥ, vyavahāre 'pi tasya kramayaugapadyābhyām arthakriyākāritvānupapannatvāt / anupakāritve 'pi yadi vijñānena vijñeyasvabhāvasya abhāvād viṣayatvaṃ kalpyate, tathā sati yadi vijñānaṃ vijñeyasvabhāvamanusaratīti tadā tadvijñānasyāpi tadanusaraṇena nityatāyāḥ prasaṅgaḥ / yadi nānusarati tadā tannityatāyā hāniprasaṅgaḥ / yadi sarvajñajñānaṃ taditi na kasyāpi vastunaḥ sāmīpyamiti kalpyate, tadāpi prekṣāvadbhistasmin vastusattāyā vyavahāro nopapadyate, vijñaptyarthaṃ taddhetujñānasyābhāvāt /
body.translated_text: If <s>pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (analytical cessation) and the like are objects of some cognition, then they must necessarily be accepted as causes, since it is not accepted that a non-cause can be an object. It is accepted that objecthood consists merely in the imprinting of its own form upon consciousness, through which a particular cause aids <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). If so, then the absurd consequence would be the loss of its permanence, since even in conventional usage, its capacity to produce causal efficacy through either succession or simultaneity is untenable. Even if objecthood is posited despite the absence of any aid, on the grounds that the nature of being cognizable by consciousness is absent — in that case, if consciousness conforms to the nature of its cognizable [object], then the absurd consequence would be that consciousness too becomes permanent through conforming to it. If it does not conform, then the absurd consequence would be the loss of its [the object's] permanence. If it is held that the cognition of an omniscient being is such, and that no entity has proximity [to it], even then the convention of asserting the existence of that entity cannot be maintained by the discerning, since there is no cognition caused by it that could serve as the basis for communication.

body.text: yena kāraṇena tato vibhaktaṃ śaśaśṛṅgādiṃ ye jñeyatvenopacaranti, teṣāṃ sameṣāṃ svabhāvarāhityāda viśeṣo 'bhidhātavyaḥ, abhāvād
body.translated_text: Those who designate as cognizable the hare's horn and the like, which are separated from that [reality] — for all of them, a distinction must be stated on account of the absence of intrinsic nature, due to non-existence —

body.text: vibhaktasya rāhityasvabhāvasya vastūtvena jñānāsambhavāt / tatra svabhāvatvena gṛhītalakṣaṇaviśeṣasyātmanaḥ sattvābhidhānamayuktam, asadvastunyapi sarvasāmarthyaviyogasvabhāvasya grahaṇāt / vandhyāputrādisadṛśe tadabhitnne 'pi yadi vastviti nāma prajñapyate, tadā nāsti vivādaḥ, kintuṃ kathaṃ vandhyāputrādayo 'hetukā iti nocyata ityucyate / ityevam asaṃskṛtānāṃ sattvābhidhānaṃ naiva samīcīnam /
body.translated_text: since cognition is impossible if what is separated, whose nature is the absence [of intrinsic nature], is taken as an entity. It is unjustified to declare the existence of a particular defining characteristic apprehended as having intrinsic nature, since even in the case of a non-existent entity, the nature of being devoid of all capacity is grasped. Even though [the unconditioned] is no different from a son of a barren woman and the like, if it is designated as an 'entity,' then there is no dispute — but the question is: how can one not say that the son of a barren woman and the like are without cause? Thus, the assertion of the existence of <s>asaṃskṛtas</s> (unconditioned phenomena) is simply not proper.

body.text: ata evoktaṃ laṅkāvatārasūtreḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore it is stated in the <s>Laṅkāvatārasūtra</s>:

body.text: asadbhāvasamāropaḥ punarmahāmate, yaduta ākāśanirodhanirvāṇākṛtakābhiniveśasamāropaḥ /
body.translated_text: The superimposition of non-existent entities, <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the superimposition [arising from] attachment to <s>ākāśa</s> (space), <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and the unconditioned.

body.text: ye tāvannityānityābhyāmanabhidheyatvena pudgalādināmubhayathāpi siddhiranaikāntikīti pratipādayanti, tanna yujyate, sadvastuni kathamapi anabhidheyatvāsambhavāt / evameva nityānityāni tāvat parasparaparihārasthitalakṣaṇāni / yadi tāni kramaśa ekasiddhinisedhāmyām aparaniṣedhasiddhibhāñji na syustadā asadeva syuḥ / phalata ekasya niṣedha evāparasya siddhiriti hetoḥ kathaṃ tāvadanabhidheyaṃ vastvityabhidhīyate /
body.translated_text: Now, those who maintain that the establishment of <s>pudgala</s> (person) and the like through being inexpressible as either permanent or impermanent is non-exclusive in both ways — that is not tenable, since inexpressibility is in no way possible for an existent entity. For permanence and impermanence are characterized by being established through mutual exclusion. If they, through the negation of one and the establishment of [the other], were not to entail the establishment and negation of the other, then [the entity] would simply be non-existent. Consequently, since the negation of one is itself the establishment of the other, how can an entity be said to be inexpressible?

body.text: anyathā [yadyevaṃ nāsti tadā] anabhidheyatvāt sarvāṇyeva vastunyanabhidheyāni syuḥ / phalataḥ svaparoditānām aśeṣavastuviśeṣāṇāṃ vilopasambhavād mahātmabhirvajrakaṇādiyukticatuṣṭayasyābhidhād ebhyo mārgebhyo
body.translated_text: Otherwise, [if it is not so,] then due to inexpressibility, all entities whatsoever would be inexpressible. Consequently, since the destruction of all particular entities — both one's own and others' — would be possible, the great ones have propounded the fourfold reasoning of the <s>Vajrakaṇa</s> (diamond splinters). From these paths,

body.text: naiva viruddham / yathoktam -
body.translated_text: there is no contradiction at all. As it has been stated:

children.text: na svato nāpi parato na dvābhyāṃ nāpyahetutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Not from itself, not from another, not from both, nor without a cause —

children.text: utpannā jātu vidyante bhāvāḥ kvacana kecana //
children.translated_text: nowhere do any entities whatsoever arise at any time.

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: ityevaṃ sarve dharmā nirātmāna iti sādhyante / ata eva bhagavatā prajñāpāramitāsūtre vastuṣu nityānityagrāhasya tāvanniṣedhaḥ kṛtaḥ / anyasūtrāṇāṃ strotāṃsi pūrvameva nirdiṣṭāni / ato ye rūpaṃ nityamityudīrayanti, te tāvannaiva prajñāpāramitāmācaranti / kathamiti cet? yadā tad rūpaṃ sadeva nāsti tadā tannityābhidhānasya tu kathaiva kā? ityuktam / sarvākārajñatāparyantaṃ [sarvadharmeṣu] evameva prayoktavyamiti /
body.translated_text: In this way, it is established that all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are without self. For this very reason, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) has made the prohibition of grasping at permanence and impermanence with regard to entities in the <s>Prajñāpāramitāsūtra</s> (Perfection of Wisdom Sūtra). The streams of other <s>sūtras</s> have been indicated previously. Therefore, those who proclaim that form is permanent are simply not practicing the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom). How so? When that form simply does not exist, then what possibility is there for declaring it permanent? — so it has been stated. This same [reasoning] should be applied up to and including <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience in all aspects) [with respect to all dharmas].

body.text: ata evātrāpi parataḥ kāryotpāde tāvat ko virodhaḥ, kathaṃ hi tato 'pi [parato 'pi] kāryotpādaniṣedhaḥ kriyate? nātra [kānicit] bādhakapramāṇānyapītyādi yaduktam, etat sarvaṃ pūrvaṃ kṛtottarameva /
body.translated_text: For this very reason, regarding what was said here — 'What objection is there to the arising of an effect from another? How can the negation of the arising of an effect from another also [be maintained]? There are no invalidating <s>pramāṇas</s> (valid means of knowledge) here' and so forth — all of that has already been answered previously.

body.text: satkāryotpādaniṣedhāryamapi bhavatāṃ savidhe nāsti ubhayasiddho heturdṛṣṭāntaścetyādi yaduktam, tāpi naiva yujyate / tathā hi - kiṃ tat yat sadityucyate? aṃśaistāvanniraṃśasya siddhirasambhavinīti yasya svabhāvaḥ sarvātmanā niṣpannaḥ, yaśca niṣpannasvabhāva iti tasya paraiḥ[hetupratyayaiḥ] apūrva ityākhyaṃ bhedaṃ kartuṃ naiva śakyate / yasyāpūrvamiti bhedaṃ naiva śakyate kartum, sa kadāpi kenāpyutpādayituṃ naiva śakyate, yathā - ākāśakusumādīni / yastāvattasya sattābhiniveśaḥ, so 'pi tadvadeveti tasyāpi hetvādayo 'sambhavina eveti /
body.translated_text: As for what was stated — 'Even in refuting the arising of an existent effect, you do not have a reason or example established for both parties' and so forth — that too is not tenable. For consider: what is it that is called 'existent'? Since a partless [entity] cannot be established through parts, that whose <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature) is fully accomplished in every respect, and which is of accomplished nature — it is simply not possible for external [causes and conditions] to produce in it a modification called 'novel.' That which cannot have a modification called 'novel' produced in it — that can never be produced by anything whatsoever, just like a flower in the sky and the like. And that attachment to the existence of such [an entity] is of the very same kind — therefore causes and the rest are simply impossible for it as well.

body.text: vicchinnamātre sādhye tathaiva ca hetornideśe na te abhūtadharmito viruddhāḥ / yathā sati naiva āśrasiddhādidoṣāḥ, pūrvameva tannirdiṣṭatvāt / sādhyasādhanayoḥ sapakṣe 'nugamānnaiva viruddhakhyo 'pi hetudoṣaḥ / vyavahārena bhinnatvād utpattau vyāpakaḥ / phalato vyāpakanivṛttyā nāsti vyāpyo 'pi sambhavī / ato nāstyanaikāntiko 'pi hetuḥ / yasya kenāpi bhavati bhedaḥ, sa tasya prakṛtiḥ / ato yastāvadanyaḥ, sa kathaṃ tasyeti? yaśca svabhāvataḥ pūrvameva sthitaḥ, sa hetusannidhānāt pūrvamapi tathaiva bhāvāt kathaṃ 'hetubhirutpannaḥ' iti kathayituṃ śakyate? ato nāstyanaikāntikatvamiti /
body.translated_text: When what is to be proven is mere discontinuity, and when the reason is indicated in just that way, these are not contradictory as having a non-existent subject. Just as when [the subject] exists there are no faults such as unestablished basis and the like — since that has been indicated previously. Since the reason and what is to be proven are concomitant in the <s>sapakṣa</s> (concordant instance), there is no fault of the reason called 'contradictory' either. Since [existence and non-existence] are distinct through convention, [non-arising] pervades arising. Consequently, through the cessation of the pervader, the pervaded too does not exist. Therefore, there is no non-exclusive reason either. That which undergoes modification through something is the <s>prakṛti</s> (nature) of that [modifier]. Therefore, that which is other — how can it belong to that [entity]? And that which already existed by its own nature previously — since it existed in just the same way even before the proximity of causes, how can it be said to have been 'produced by causes'? Therefore, there is no non-exclusiveness [of the reason].

body.text: bhedayogyatvādutpattau vyāpakatvamityato 'sadutpadyata iti ced? vyavahāramātreṇaivaitat syāt, paramārthato 'sattvāt / evameva yadi savabhāvato 'bhāva ekaprakṛtika eva, tadā paścādapi kathaṃ sa satsvabhāvaḥ syāt, sadasatoḥ parasparaviruddhātvāt / yaśca parasparaparihārasthitalakṣaṇo dharmaḥ sa tadviruddhadharmiṇi kathaṃ nāma yuktaḥ syāt, yathā amūrtadhārmāntarbhūtaṃ tāvadākāśaṃ kathaṃ nāma mūrtaṃ syāditi / utpattyākhyo hi prasiddhaḥ satsvabhāvastāvad asatsvabhāvaparihārasthitalakṣaṇatvāt kathaṃ hi nāma paramārthato 'bhāvena samprayuktaḥ syāt /
body.translated_text: If one objects that arising pervades [non-existence] because of the susceptibility to modification, and therefore 'the non-existent arises' — this would hold only in mere convention, since in the ultimate sense it is non-existent. Likewise, if in terms of intrinsic nature non-existence is of a single nature, then how could it subsequently become existent in nature, since existence and non-existence are mutually contradictory? And how could a <s>dharma</s> (property) characterized by being established through mutual exclusion be justified in a <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer) possessing the contradictory property — just as how could <s>ākāśa</s> (space), which belongs among incorporeal properties, ever be corporeal? For the well-known existent nature called 'arising,' since it is characterized by being established through the exclusion of non-existent nature, how could it in the ultimate sense be conjoined with non-existence?

body.text: evaṃ vicāryamāṇe yadsat, tasya utpattikriyāvatyāmutpatau kimapyupadeśanaṃ nāma nāsti / pṛthaksāmarthyavataḥ kasyāpi bhāvātmakasya hetoranantaraṃ prādurbhāvasya sampratibhāsābhāvāt taddhetorasadutpadyata iti loke utpattiviśeṣaviṣayikāyāḥ kalpanāyāḥ abhidhānasya ca vyavahāraḥ pravartate / vyavahāramātreṇa tu vastusattve bādhāleśo 'pi naiva sambhavati / asadvastuni sadākhyadharmasya tāvat sattāleśo 'pyasmābhirnābhyupeyate / yadi tat sat, tadā naiva tadasat / yo hi paścādapi utpattisvabhāvaḥ, sa tāvadanya eva / yaścānyaḥ, sa na tasyetyabhidhātuṃ śakyate / ataḥ 'asadutpadyate' iti yadktaṃ tadabhāvato bhāvasiddhiriti naiva yujyate / yato hyatra bhāvasvabhāvaparīkṣāyā evāvasaraḥ / ataḥ kriyānirodhamātraṃ vaktuṃ neṣṭamiti /
body.translated_text: When examined in this way, there is simply nothing to be taught regarding the arising of what is existent through an arising that possesses the activity of origination. Since there is no appearance of a manifest emergence immediately following any cause that is an entity possessing its own distinct capacity, the convention of the designation and the conceptual construction regarding a particular kind of arising operates in the world [only as] 'the non-existent arises.' But through mere convention, not even the slightest invalidation of the entityhood of a thing is possible. We do not accept even the slightest existence of a property called 'existent' in a non-existent entity. If it is existent, then it is simply not non-existent. For that which is of the nature of arising even subsequently is altogether different. And what is different cannot be predicated of that [original entity]. Therefore, what was stated — 'the non-existent arises' — as establishing existence from non-existence, is simply not tenable. For here this is precisely the occasion for examining the nature of existence. Therefore, it is not intended to state merely the cessation of activity.

body.text: yadyetad vastu hetoḥ sāmīpyāt pūrvamudbhūtaṃ nāsti, tadā tasya kaḥ svabhāva ityabhidheyam / yadi tadā kiñcidapi nāsti tadā tat kadācid vastutvenābhidhāsyata iticintā naiva yujyate / yadi nāsti vastunaḥ kimapi bhāvātmakamastitvaṃ tadā tasya svabhāvo 'sadeveti suspaṣtamabhidhāsyate / anyathā kimiti tasyāsattvamityucyate / evaṃ yo hi pūrvamasan, sa paścādbhāvī kaścana bhāvasvabhāva eva /
body.translated_text: If this thing does not exist prior [to its production], being close to the cause, then what is to be said of its nature? If nothing whatsoever exists then, then the thought that it will sometime be designated as a real thing is not at all tenable. If there is no positive being whatsoever of the thing, then its nature will clearly be stated as simply non-existent. Otherwise, why is its non-existence stated? Thus, what was previously non-existent and later comes into being is of the very nature of a positive entity.

body.text: so 'pi kathaṃ nāmāpūrvasvabhāvātiriktaḥ prajñaptuṃ śakyate / pūrvaṃ nāsīdityasadutpattervyavahārasyāpi hetupratyayābhāsāḥ kathaṃ samyagityabhidhātuṃ śakyāḥ? evamabhūtasya bhūtasiddhistāvadasataḥ satsiddhireva syāt / yato hi yadi nāstyanyastadā abhūtādanyo bhūto nāsti satsamīpavarttyapi / asatyapyanye abhūtādanyasyotpādābhidhānasambaddhameva / phalato 'pūrvavastūnāṃ papaścāt sattvābhidhanaṃ tāvat tadviruddhadharmānvitasyaivābhyupagamaḥ /
body.translated_text: How can that too be designated as beyond an unprecedented nature? Even the conventional usage of production from non-existence, [expressed as] 'it did not exist before' — how can the appearances of causes and conditions be said to be correct? Thus, the establishment of the becoming of what has not [previously] been is simply the establishment of the existent from the non-existent. For if there is no other [thing], then apart from what has not been, there is no other that has come into being, even though it exists in proximity. Even when speaking of the origination of something other than what has not been, [the expression] is connected with non-existence. As a result, saying that unprecedented things later exist amounts to accepting what is endowed with contradictory properties.

body.text: viruddhadharmānvitaḥ svabhāvo 'pi tāvadanupapanna eva / tathā sati sarvasya sarvasvabhāvatāprasaṅgaḥ / ekasmin krameṇa sattvāsattve aviruddheityabhidhānamapi naiva yujyate / tathā sati samakāle 'pyaviruddhatvaprasaṅgaḥ / yadi samakāle te aviruddhe tadā krameṇāpi kathaṃ te na tathā, abhinnatvāditi /
body.translated_text: A nature endowed with contradictory properties is itself simply untenable. In that case, the unwanted consequence of everything having the nature of everything [would follow]. The statement that existence and non-existence in a single [thing] sequentially is not contradictory is also not tenable. In that case, the unwanted consequence of non-contradiction even simultaneously [would follow].

body.text: bhinnadharmiṇi viruddhalakṣaṇasyāviruddhatve 'pi ekasmin dharmiṇi naiva krameṇāpi tad bhavituṃ śakroti / yathā yugapadanekaviruddhadharmānvitatvād ekatvahāniprasaṅgaḥ, tathaiva krameṇāpi tadanvitatvāt tatpravṛttiriti / anyathā parairapi pradhānādīnāṃ kramaśo mahadādigaṇe parivartanam abhivyaktim vā upakalpayatāṃ vyaktāvyaktādidharmavirodhaḥ kathamabhidhīyate / krameṇa vastūnāmutpādakeṣu īśvarādiṣu kathaṃ nāma samarthāsamarthādivirodhodbhāvanaṃ yujyate / ye kecana parvatakāyavajrādīn dṛḍhasvabhāvān teṣāṃ śītoṣmādyavasthābhedena kramaśo bhedaṃ vyavasthāpayanti, te 'pi teṣāṃ kṣaṇikatvaṃ sisādhayiṣavaḥ kathaṃ krameṇa prādurbhavatsu teṣu śītoṣmādiviruddhatvamabhidhātuṃ śaknuvanti / yadi vastūni tāvad abhūtvā utpadyante, bhūtvā cābhāvatvenāvabhāsanta iti vicāraṇād ekasmin kramaśaḥ sadasattvaviruddhatvena vyavasthāpayituṃ śakyata iti kathayantīti cennedaṃ yujyate / yato hi tāmrādiṣvevaṃ dāḍharyamārdavaśaityauṣṇyādīni krameṇa dṛśyanta eva / atastatrāpi aviruddhatvaprasaṅgaḥ syāt / atastena adṛḍhatayā ye svabhāvatvena sādhayanti, tannaivopapadyate /
body.translated_text: Even though contradictory characteristics may not be contradictory in different subjects, in a single subject they cannot be so even sequentially. Just as the unwanted consequence of the loss of unity arises from being endowed with many contradictory properties simultaneously, so too even sequentially, from being endowed with them,

body.text: api ca, asmābhirapyetādṛśī dṛṣṭirnaiva parityajyate / yato hi māyāsvapnādisamā alīkā api [padārthāḥ] abhūtvā bhavanti, bhūtvā ca vinaśyamānāḥ pratibhāsante / kintu svabhāvataḥ sadasatostu krameṇāpi tayoḥ sadasatorvirodha eva / tadyathā -
body.translated_text: Moreover, we too do not at all abandon such a view. For even things that are illusory like illusions and dreams — false though they are — come into being without having existed, and appear as perishing after having existed. But in terms of [their] own nature, the sequential [change] of existence and non-existence

children.translated_text: If existence were by nature, then its non-existence would not occur;
for the becoming-otherwise of [one's own] nature is never tenable.

body.text: yathoktaṃ kārikāyāmḥ -
body.translated_text: As stated in the verse:

children.translated_text: That [thing], being non-existent by nature — how could it, being non-entity, come to be through other conditions?
What other reason that is essenceless has been stated by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>?

body.text: āryakaṅkāvatārasūtre 'pi pūrvaṃ rāgādīn sattvenābhyupagamya punarasattvenāṅgīkaraṇaṃ vaināśikataiva / kāryakāraṇabhāvo yadi paramārthata syāttadā evamabhidadhānānāṃ [sā] dṛṣṭistāvat samyag mārgānusaraṇād muktimārgānukūlaiva strānnatvananukūlā / ato laṅkāvatārasūtre yaduktaṃ tadapyaviruddhamevaṃ, tathā hi -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra</s> too, having first accepted passion and the like as existent, then accepting them as non-existent is indeed annihilationism (<s>vaināśikatā</s>). If the cause-effect relation existed ultimately, then the view of those who state thus would follow the correct path

children.translated_text: All non-Buddhist thinkers are deluded by the wrong view of cause and effect;
therefore there is no liberation for them, who advocate positions of existence and non-existence.

body.text: punaśca,
body.translated_text: And again:

children.text: abhūtvā yasya cotpādo bhūtvā cāpi vinaśyati /
children.translated_text: For him whose origination is without having [previously] existed, and who also perishes after having existed,

children.text: pratyayaiḥ sadasaccāpi na te me śāsane sthitāḥ //
children.translated_text: [who asserts] both existence and non-existence through conditions — they do not stand in my teaching.

body.text: hetupratyayasāmarthyaniścaye 'pi paramārthato 'sata utpattirnaiva yujyate, svabhāvāntaraṃ kartumaśakyatvat / pratiniyatasāmarthyato viruddhamapi svabhāvaṃ kartuṃ naiva pāryate, tathā sati śaśaśṛṃṅgādīnāmapyutpādaprasaṅgaḥ syāditi vidvāṃso bruvanti / ato hetūnāṃ niyatasāmarthyena vyavasthāpi niyatā bhavedityabhidhānamapi tāvadasambaddhameva / saṃvṛtāvapi khalvasata utpattiḥ kathaṃ na vitudhyata iti vicāraṇāpi tāvannaiva yujyate, vastunyeva virodhasya vyavasthāpannānmithyāvastuni [avastuni] tadvyavasthānamasambaddhameva / anyathā paramārthaivaiṣā utpattiḥ syānnatu saṃvṛtau /
body.translated_text: Even when the capacity of causes and conditions is ascertained, production from what is ultimately non-existent is not at all tenable, since it is incapable of making another nature. Through specifically determined capacity, it is not at all possible to make even a contradictory nature; in that case, even hare's horns and the like

body.text: api ca, yā khalu vastūnāmutpattiḥ saṃvṛtimāyāvadavasthitā, saivaropyāsmābhirvirodhivacanairmithyātvena sādhyate, nānyatveneti paścād vistareṇa nirdekṣyate / evaṃ vastūnāṃ paramārthasadutpattirnopapadyate, na santi ca tāni [vastūni] asadbhūtānyapi / eteṣāmutpattirmāyāvanmithyaiva pradarśyate / ata eva sarvāṇi khalu vastūni māyāvadeva vyavasthitāni / ataśca bhagavatā - mahāmate, sato 'sataścānutpannatvāt sarve dharmā anutpannā evetyanekadhā sadasatorniṣedhaṃ kṛtvā anutpāda eva nirdiṣṭaḥ /
body.translated_text: Moreover, the origination of things that is established as conventional, like illusion — that very [origination] is what we establish as false through statements of contradiction, not as something other — this will be explained at length later. Thus, the ultimately real origination of things is not tenable.

body.text: bhagavata 'pi parikalpisvabhāvamabhipretya sadasatorutpattivirodho vyavasthāpitaḥ na tu tattvata ityevaṃ yeṣāṃ kathanaṃ tadapyagre 'bhidhāsyate / yo hi vastvātmā paramārthato 'nupanna so 'pi tattvata utpanna ityevaṃbhūto yo parikalpitaḥ svabhāvastamapi ye parikalpitasvabhāvatvenābhyupagacchanti, tadā tannaiva yuktarūpam / vastūnāmasya svabhāvasya paramārthato 'nutpannatve 'pi grāhyagrāhakārasvabhāvenānuppannatvāt sa parikalpitasvabhāva iti cintyate tadā parikalpitātmakayoḥ sadastoryathā utpattivirodhastathaiva paramārthātmakasyāpi kathaṃ notpattivirodhaḥ / tattvatastu utpatteḥ sadasadākārātirikttvena anyākāratayānutpannatvāt sādhāraṇameva taditi /
body.translated_text: The statement by some that even the Blessed One established the contradiction of origination from existence and non-existence with reference to the imagined nature (<s>parikalpita-svabhāva</s>), not in terms of reality — that too will be addressed later. For the very essence of the thing that is ultimately non-arisen, that too in truth

body.text: ato yaḥ pratītyasamutpannaḥ sa paramārthataḥ śūnyaḥ, māyādivaditi / nāstyayaṃ heturanaikāntiko 'pi yadi viparyayastadā yathoktadoṣadūṣitāni pramāṇānyapi sambhaveyuḥ / yo hi hetupratyayānapekṣya samutpadyate tasya kṛtaka eva svabhāvaḥ, na tu pāramārthikaḥ / akṛtakasya parāpekṣā naivopapadyate / ya eva kṛtakastasya naiva prakṛtyā svabhāvo yujyate, prakṛteravikārāt / ko 'pi tāṃ [prakṛtiṃ] parivartayituṃ naiva kṣamaḥ / ato yo hi pāramārthikaḥ svabhāvaḥ, yaścābhūtvā bhavati, bhūtvā ca vigaccati tau [svabhāvau] parasparaviruddhatvādasambaddhāviti pūrvaṃ nirdiṣṭameva / ato nāstyanaikāntikatvamiti / tathā hiḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore, that which is dependently arisen (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>) is empty (<s>śūnya</s>) in the ultimate sense, like an illusion and the like. This reason is not inconclusive; if there were a reversal, then the means of valid knowledge, vitiated by the stated faults, would also be possible. For that which arises without depending on causes and conditions

children.translated_text: "The origination of own-nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) through conditions and causes is not tenable;
an own-nature arisen through causes and conditions would be fabricated (<s>kṛtaka</s>).

children.text: svabhāvaḥ kṛtako nāma bhaviṣyati punaḥ katham /
children.translated_text: How can what is called a fabricated own-nature come to be?

children.text: akṛtrimaḥ svabhāvo hi nirapekṣaḥ paratra ca //"
children.translated_text: For own-nature is by definition unfabricated and independent of other [things]."

body.text: nityānityasvabhāvayorupakalpitatvād vastūnām antadvayadarśane prasaṅgamāpādayitum uttam āryaśrīmālāsūtre -
body.translated_text: To show that the unwanted consequence of the view of two extremes follows from the fabricated nature of permanence and impermanence for things, it is stated in the <s>Ārya-Śrīmālā-sūtra</s>:

body.text:
"bhagavan, dvayorantayo paśyatītyucyate / yaduta ucchedaśāścatadarśanam /
'anityāḥ saṃkārā iti ced bhagavan paśyet sāsya syāducchedadṛṣṭiḥ sāsya syānna samyagdṛṣṭiḥ / nityaṃ nirvāṇamiti ced bhagavan paśyet sāsya syācchaśvatadṛṣṭiḥ, sāsya syānna samyagdṛṣṭiḥ /"
