body.text: ataḥ pṛthivyādīnāṃ kalpitasvabhāvatvāt tatsvabhāvasaṃgṛhītāstāvadagnidhūmādayo 'pi kalpitasvabhāvā eva / ato 'gnidhūmādīnāṃ kalpanākalpitasvabhāvatvena nirdeśaḥ saṃvṛtimatrātmaka eva, na tu paramārthātmakaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, since earth and the like are of a constructed own-nature, fire, smoke, and the like — which are comprised within that own-nature — are also of a constructed own-nature alone. Therefore, the teaching of fire, smoke, and the like as having an own-nature constructed by conceptual construction pertains to convention alone, not to the ultimate.

body.text: abhidharmādau yaḥ khalu hetupratyayādīnāṃ nirdeśaḥ, so 'pi saṃvṛtireva, na tu pāramārthikaḥ / paramārthastu yadā na kasyacanotpādastadāhetukatvaṃ tāvadanupapannameveti pūrvameva nirdiṣṭam / yatāvat skandhādīnāṃ nirdeśaḥ, so 'pi vyavahārasatyāśrita evetyapi pūrvameva nirdiṣṭam /
body.translated_text: The teaching of causes, conditions, and the like in the <s>Abhidharma</s> and elsewhere — that too is merely convention, not ultimate. But in the ultimate, since there is no origination of anything whatsoever, causality is simply untenable — as has already been stated. And the teaching of <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and the like — that too is dependent on conventional truth alone — as has also already been stated.

body.text: āryadharmasaṃgītau tavaduktam - bodhisattvena tathāgatārhatsamyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ yo vyāvahārikatvena nirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ, sa khalu daśādha boditavyaḥ / kathaṃ daśadhā? tadyathāskandhanirdeśaḥ dhātunirdeśaḥ, āyatananirdeśaḥ, sattvanirdeśaḥ karmanirdeśaḥ, jātinirdeśaḥ, jarānirdeśaḥ, maraṇanirdeśaḥ pratisandhinirdeśastathaivaiteṣāmupaśamārthaṃ nirvāṇanirdeśa iti / sarva 'pīme vyavahāramātratvena nirdiṣṭā iti tatroktam / svaparamatasthitaistattvārthatvenopakalpitānāṃ skandhādīnāṃ paramārthato 'nutpannatvena sādhanāt siddhasādhanameva /
body.translated_text: In the <s>Ārya-Dharmasaṅgīti</s> it is said: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> should understand in ten ways the teaching that was given by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones, as conventional. How ten? Namely: the teaching of <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), the teaching of <s>dhātus</s> (elements), the teaching of <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), the teaching of beings, the teaching of <s>karma</s> (action), the teaching of birth, the teaching of old age, the teaching of death, the teaching of rebirth-connection, and likewise the teaching of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> for the purpose of their pacification. It is stated therein that all these are taught merely as convention. Since those <s>skandhas</s> and the like — posited as having the nature of reality by those adhering to their own and others' doctrines — are proved to be unoriginated in the ultimate, this is simply proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>).

body.text: yacca tadā vastveva svīkṛtaṃ syādityuktaṃ tatpūrvaṃ kṛtottarameva /
body.translated_text: The statement that 'then a real entity would simply be accepted' — the answer to that was already given earlier.

body.text: kā nāma saṃvṛtiryadi sarvamevāsaditi yaduktaṃ tadapi naiva yuktisaṃṅgatam, parasparavirodhāt / saṃvṛtirhi nāsti śaśaśṛṅgavadabhāvasvabhāvā / tadā kathamiti cet? yacca samyaṅ niḥsvabhāvaṃ vastu tasya tannivṛttakāre yā samāropikā bhrāntabuddhiḥ, saiva saṃvṛtiriti / athavā yayā tattvamāvriyate [yayā vā tattvabodhaḥ] bādhyate, sā saṃvṛtiriti / sūtre 'pi tavadutam -
body.translated_text: The statement that 'what then is convention if everything is simply non-existent?' — that too is not logically coherent, because of mutual contradiction. For convention is not of a nature of non-existence like a hare's horn. Then what is it? That superimposing deluded cognition which, with respect to a thing that is properly essenceless, [operates] in the domain of the cessation of that [essencelessness] — that itself is convention. Or alternatively, that by which reality is concealed, [by which] the understanding of reality is obstructed — that is convention. It is also said in the <s>sūtra</s>:

children.text: bhāvā vidyanti saṃvṛtyā paramārthe na bhāvakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Entities exist in convention; in the ultimate, they are not entities.
That delusion regarding what is without own-nature — that truth is convention.

body.text: tannirvṛtatvāttadupadarśitaṃ sarvaṃ khalu vastu saṃvṛtimātramevetyuktam / sāpyanādikalīnabhrāntavāsanāparipākajarūpaiva / tayā sarveṣu sattveṣu pāramarthikavastusvabhāva ivopadarśyate, atastadbuddhayadhikārena sarvaṃ hi mithyāvastu saṃvṛtisanmātrameveti / tacca naiva paramārthato vastusvabhāvam, yathābhāsamanavasthitatvāt / naiva ca śaśaśṛṅgavat tadatyantābhāvasvabhāvamapi, avicārato ramaṇīyatvenāvabhāsamānatvāt / yathoktā saṃvṛtistāvannaiva vastusvabhāvāpi, viparītākāropagrāheṇābhāsitatvāt / tattvānyatvayostāvat parasparaparihārasthitalakṣaṇatvāt tattvānyatvavirodha iti pūrvameva nirdiṣṭam /
body.translated_text: Because it arises from that, it has been demonstrated that all entities are indeed merely <s>saṃvṛti</s> (convention). And that [convention] is of a form born solely from the ripening of deluded <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) that have been dormant since beginningless time. Through it, in all beings, [things] appear as if possessing an ultimate entity own-nature; therefore, with respect to that cognition, all false entities are merely conventionally existent. And that is not an entity own-nature in the ultimate, because it does not abide as it appears. Nor is it of the nature of absolute non-existence like a hare's horn, because without investigation it appears as something delightful. The convention as described is indeed not of the nature of real entities, because it appears through the apprehension of an inverted form. Since identity and difference have the characteristic of being established through mutual exclusion, the contradiction between identity and difference has already been pointed out earlier.

body.text: na ca te atyantamabhāvasvabhāve, avabhāsamānatvāt / ataḥ sarvaṃ khalu vastu sadasatsvabhāvātītam / ato bhāvamabhāvaṃ vā svabhāvamāśrita yattāvaccodyaṃ tatsarvaṃ nirādhārameva / vastunyeva tāvad vidhirvā pratiṣedho vā sambhavī / vidhipratiṣedhābhāve tvasadeva / ata ubhayaṃ khallasatsvabhāvaviruddham, naiva tadasadvastuni [sambhavati] /
body.translated_text: Nor are they of the nature of absolute non-existence, because they do appear. Therefore, all entities indeed transcend the own-nature of both existent and non-existent. Thus, whatever objection is based on the own-nature of existence or non-existence — all of that is simply groundless. Affirmation or negation is possible only with respect to a [real] entity. In the absence of affirmation and negation, [the thing] is simply non-existent. Therefore, both [affirmation and negation] are contradictory to what is of non-existent own-nature; they simply do not [occur] in a non-existent entity.

body.text: kasyacidekasyāpi svabhāvasya tatrāsiddheḥ ubhayāsatsvabhāvatvena vyavasthāpyate / ato nāstyubhayāsatsvabhāve kaścana virodhaḥ / apekṣāviśeṣeṇa sāmarthyāsāmarthyadivirodho 'pi naiva sambhavī, asāmarthādināṃ paramārthasatyāśritatvena sāmarthyādīnāṃ ca saṃvṛtisatyāśritatvena vyavasthīyamānatvāt /
body.translated_text: Since not even a single own-nature is established therein, it is determined as having a both-non-existent own-nature. Therefore there is no contradiction whatsoever in what is of both-non-existent own-nature. The contradiction of capacity and incapacity and so on is also not possible with respect to specific dependence, because incapacity and the like are determined as depending on <s>paramārthasatya</s> (ultimate truth), while capacity and the like are determined as depending on <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s> (conventional truth).

body.text: māyāpuruṣādivat sarvavastuṣu bhrāntābhrāntajñānābhyāṃ vyavasthāpanāt krmaśaḥ satyadvayabhedo vyavasthāpyate / māyāpuruṣādau bhrāntairyathā vyavasthīyate, tathā sarvavastuṣu mithyākārena jñānena yadāropitaṃ tat saṃvṛtisatyamiti vyavahriyate / māyāpuruṣādau abhrāntairyathā vyavasthīyate tathaiva sarvavastuṣu yaḥ svabhāvaḥ samyakpramāṇaiḥ sampratipādyate, sa paramārthasatyam / ato māyādivyavahāra ivāpekṣāviśeṣena satyadvayaśritā ime sarvavyavahārā aviruddhā evetyavaśyamabhyupetavyam /
body.translated_text: Just as with illusory persons and the like, since all entities are determined through deluded and non-deluded cognitions, the distinction of the two truths (<s>satyadvaya</s>) is established sequentially. Just as [things] are determined by the deluded with respect to illusory persons and the like, so too in all entities, what is superimposed by cognition of a false form is designated as <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s> (conventional truth). Just as [things] are determined by the non-deluded with respect to illusory persons and the like, so too in all entities, whatever own-nature is established through correct valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) — that is <s>paramārthasatya</s> (ultimate truth). Therefore, just as in the convention of illusions and the like, it must necessarily be accepted that all these conventions, depending on the two truths with respect to specific dependence, are indeed non-contradictory.

body.text: yadyevaṃ nāsti tadā taimirikādyālambiteṣu keśādiṣu vijñānavādināṃ ca dvayābhāseṣu kimivemāni codyāni na syuḥ / itthaṃ yadīme keśādayaḥ paramārthato 'santa eva tadā kathamiva te sadrūpeṇāvabhāsante, kathamiva ca deśakālāvasthānāṃ pṛthaṅ niścayaḥ parigṛhyate / utpādānutpādādayaḥ sadasatī ca parasparamekasmin naiva yujyate, yato hi tatra yathā keśādiṣu dvayābhāseṣu ca bhrāntābhrāntajñānābhyāṃ vyavasthitasvabhāvasya saṃvṛtiparamārthasatyamāśritya saṃvṛtau sattvaṃ paramārthe cāsattvaṃ vyavasthāpyate, yathā ca tatrāpekṣāviśeṣastāvadaviruddha eva, tathaiva sarvavastūnāṃ sādṛśyena nedaṃ codyaṃ yujyata eva /
body.translated_text: If [things] do not exist in this way, then would not these same objections also apply to the hairs and the like perceived by those with eye-disease (<s>timira</s>) and to the dual appearances [maintained by] the <s>Vijñānavādins</s>? Thus, if these hairs and the like are indeed ultimately non-existent, then how do they appear in the form of what is existent, and how is a separate determination of place, time, and states apprehended? Origination and non-origination and the like, as well as existent and non-existent, are not tenable simultaneously in one [thing]; because therein, just as in the case of hairs and dual appearances, the own-nature determined through deluded and non-deluded cognitions — depending on conventional and ultimate truth — is established as existence in convention and non-existence in the ultimate, and just as the specific dependence there is indeed non-contradictory, so too by analogy with all entities, this objection is simply untenable.

body.text: ye ca saṃvṛtāvutpāda ityabhidadhate, teṣāmayamāśayaḥ - yena hetunā yathoktabhrāntanāṃ saṃvṛtasvabhāvānāṃ vastūnāṃ naiva samyagutpādo jāyate tathāpyutpattisādṛśyamupadṛśyate, atasteṣāṃ buddhimadhikṛtya saṃvṛtāvutpādo bhavatītyabhidhīyate / ata eva bhagavatā cāpyuktam - "bhāvā vidyanti saṃvṛtyā" iti /
body.translated_text: Those who state 'origination exists in convention' — their intent is this: although true origination does not occur for entities that are of conventional own-nature, being deluded as described, still a semblance of origination is observed; therefore, with respect to their cognition, it is stated that origination occurs in convention. For this very reason, the Blessed One too has said: 'Entities exist conventionally.'

body.text: paramārthato 'nutpannatvādikaṃ yaduktaṃ tasyāyamarthaḥ samyak śravaṇacintanabhāvanotpannāni sarvajñānānyaviparyastaviṣayitvātparamāni, teṣāmarthaḥ paramārtha iti / pratyakṣeṇa va paramparayā vā kṛta bhedā api santi / tābhyāṃ sarvāṇi vastūni anutpannatvenaiva jñāyante / itthaṃ paramārthato 'nutpada iti samyagjñānena asiddhotpāda ityeva vakṣyate / ata ubhe api na sto 'sambaddhābhidhāne yadyevaṃ nāsti tadā bhavadbhirapi 'sarvāṇi vastūni paramārthato 'nutpannāni' ityādīnāmarthaḥ kathamupanīyate, kathaṃ vā bhavatāṃ satyadvayāśrito vyavahāraḥ pravartate / yadi niyataṃ śabdārthamatiricya mithyaiva pare dūṣyante tadā spaṣṭamasambaddhāmevābhidhānaṃ parilakṣyate /
body.translated_text: The meaning of the statement 'unoriginated in the ultimate and so on' is this: all cognitions born from correct hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>), reflection (<s>cintana</s>), and meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) are supreme because they have non-inverted objects; their object is the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>). There are also distinctions made through direct perception or through tradition. Through both of these, all entities are cognized as unoriginated. Thus, 'unoriginated in the ultimate' means precisely 'origination not established through correct knowledge.' Therefore, neither [objection] amounts to an incoherent statement. If [you say] this is not so, then how do you too convey the meaning of statements like 'all entities are unoriginated in the ultimate'? And how does your convention, based on the two truths, proceed? If others are merely falsely refuted going beyond the meaning of words, then the statement is clearly observed to be incoherent itself.

body.text: aparīkṣyaiva avikalpamātramityādi yaduktaṃ tadapyasambaddameva, yato hi cintanotpannasya prajñātattvasyāviparītatvena niyatacintanagatasamyakpramāṇabalotpannaṃ tathaiva bhāvanābalotpannamapi kalpitamevocyate, yato hi tattvārthapratyakṣastāvat samyagvicārahetukastanniṣyandabhūtaśca bhavati /
body.translated_text: The statement 'merely non-conceptual' and so on, made without examination — that too is simply incoherent, because that which is born through the power of correct valid cognition (<s>pramāṇa</s>) arising from determined reflection, being non-inverted in the reality of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) born from reflection — and likewise that which is born through the power of meditation — is called merely 'conceptual construction,' since direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) of the meaning of reality is caused by correct investigation and is its natural outflow.

body.text: yāni khalu tattvarthaparāṅmukhani mithyākāropagṛhītāni jñānāni, tāni sarvāṇi tadviparītatvād akalpitānītyucyante, tāni naiva nirvikalpāni, naiva va kalpanāmātrarahitāni / atastatprasiddhasvabhāvatvāt sarvāṇi mithyākārasvabhāvāni vastūni saṃvṛtirityabhidhīyante / phalato 'kalpitatve 'pi na tāvannirvikalpajñānam, na cānumānaprasiddhārthasya parihāraḥ, naiva ca vastutattvasvīkāraḥ / naivātra tāvadasanniṣedhābhilāṣo 'pi / itthaṃ dūṣaṇamidaṃ sarvabālapṛthagjanān saṃkleśayituṃ śabdaprayogamātrameva / ato naiva tad viduṣāṃ santoṣakaramiti /
body.translated_text: Indeed, those cognitions that turn away from the meaning of reality and are grasped in a false form — all of them, being the opposite of that [correct knowledge], are called 'non-constructed'; but they are neither non-conceptual nor devoid of mere conceptual construction. Therefore, because of their well-known nature, all entities of false-form own-nature are called <s>saṃvṛti</s> (convention). Even though they are 'non-constructed' in terms of result, there is neither non-conceptual knowledge (<s>nirvikalpajñāna</s>), nor the avoidance of what is established through inference, nor the acceptance of the reality of entities. Nor is there even a desire to negate the non-existent herein. Thus, this refutation is merely an exercise in words to confuse all childish ordinary beings (<s>bālapṛthagjana</s>). Therefore, it does not bring satisfaction to the learned.

body.text: 'saṃvṛtirlokaprasiddhā' ityādikaṃ yaduktaṃ tacca doṣarahitameva, sarveṣāṃ lokaprasidhārthānāṃ saṃvṛtitvenābhyupagamāt / nāpi sarve 'rthāḥ sarvendriyagocarāḥ, kenacit kasyacideva grahaṇāt / ataḥ karmaphalādīnāṃ pṛthakśo niyatavyavasthā yā atyantaparokṣā, sā sarvathā sarvajñajñānasyaiva gocarā, na tu sāmānyajñānaviṣayā / kecana śāstraracayitāraḥ prasiddhimatītya kalpanādisvabhāvatvenipakalpitaṃ vastu mithyāsaṃvṛtisaditi kathayanti, tattu prasiddhāvapyasaditi / yattu pratītyasamutpadānukūlatvena parikalpitaṃ tattu" nāstīha sattva ātmā vā dharmāstvete sahetukāḥ" ityataḥ saṃvṛtisadevetyuktam / ato vastūnamanekatve 'pi praṇetṛbhiryadyapyanekasvabhavatvena kalpitāni, tathāpi teṣāṃ svabhāve naiva parasparavirodhaḥ / [66] yacca 'māyārthaḥ saṃvṛtyarthaḥ' ityuktaṃ tadapyasatyārthe māyārthasya svīkārād doṣahitameva, atyantābhāvasvabhāvābhāvāt / ato nāstyasmin pūrvokto doṣo 'pi / nāpi cātra saṃkleśvyavadānāpavādadoṣo 'pi, tasya pūrvaṃ nirākṛtatvāt /
body.translated_text: The statement 'convention is what is well-known to the world' and so on — that is entirely free from fault, because all worldly well-known things are accepted as being of the nature of convention. Nor are all objects within the range of all senses, because each [object] is apprehended only by a particular [sense]. Therefore, the separate determinate arrangement of <s>karma</s>, its fruits, and the like, which is extremely remote [from ordinary perception], is entirely within the range of omniscient knowledge alone, and not an object of ordinary knowledge. Some authors of treatises say that an entity fabricated by the nature of conceptual construction and the like, going beyond what is well-known, is falsely conventionally existent, but that it is non-existent even in what is well-known. But what is constructed in conformity with <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) — since 'there is no being or self here, but these <s>dharmas</s> are with causes' — is said to be conventionally existent. Therefore, even though entities are manifold and authors have constructed them with manifold own-natures, still there is no mutual contradiction in their own-nature. [66] The statement 'the meaning of illusion is the meaning of convention' — that too is free from fault, because the meaning of illusion is accepted as the meaning of the unreal, since there is no own-nature of absolute non-existence. Therefore there is no previously stated fault in this. Nor is there the fault of denying affliction (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>), since that has been refuted previously.

body.text: māyārthasya mithyājñānārthasve jñānavastuni naiva prasaṅgaḥ, mithyākāropagṛhītatvenāvabhāsanāt, satyāsatyayoḥ parasparaviruddhatvācca / mithyāsvarūpasyāpi satyatvenāvabhāse sati naiva jñānaṃ bhrāntaṃ syāt, tasminnekasvabhāvo 'pi naiva yukturūpaḥ, ekasminnekasvabhāvasya viruddhatvāt / asatyasvabhāvasya mithyātvād bhrānte sati naiva jñānaṃ syāt, tayoḥ sarvātmanā parasparaviruddhatvāt, ekasminnavayavāvayavibhāvasyāsambhavācca / ato mithyāsvabhāvatvājjñānasvarūpe 'ntarjñeyavādināṃ mate mahān viśeṣo [bhedaḥ] jāyate /
body.translated_text: There is no undesired consequence that the object of illusion, being the object of false cognition, [applies to] the entity of knowledge, because it appears through being grasped in a false form, and because the true and the false are mutually contradictory. If even what is of false own-nature were to appear as true, then cognition would not be erroneous; and in that [case], even one own-nature would not be proper, because of the contradiction of one own-nature in one [thing]. If what is of unreal own-nature, being false, is erroneous, then there would be no [valid] cognition, because the two are mutually contradictory in every respect, and because the relation of part and whole is impossible in one [thing]. Therefore, because of being of false own-nature, a great distinction arises in the own-form of cognition, according to the view of the <s>antarjñeyavādins</s> (proponents of internally cognizable objects).

body.text: saṃvṛtiḥ śabdamātrātmiketyādi yaduktaṃ tadapi pūrvapakṣarūpeṇa svamatopakalpitmeva / atastannaiva yujyate / sugatamateṣvapi jagadidaṃ śabdamātramevetyuktam / yathoktam sūtre -
body.translated_text: The statement 'convention is of the nature of mere words' and so on — that too is merely fabricated by one's own position in the form of a prior objection. Therefore that is not tenable. Even in the doctrines of the <s>Sugata</s> (Buddha), it is said that this world is merely words. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:

children.translated_text: "In <s>sūtra</s> after <s>sūtra</s>, conceptual construction is spoken of, and also through the alternative of designations and names;
what is to be expressed (<s>abhidheya</s>), freed from expression (<s>abhidhāna</s>), is not perceived."

body.text: ye tāvadabhidhānaṃ vastubhūtam, abhidheyaṃ ca tadatiriktamiti kalpayanti, teṣāmevaṃ kalpayatāṃ mataniṣedhāryamevābhidheyaṃ kalpanāyāṃ pratiṣṭhitamityupadarśitaṃ saṃjñāmātre pratiṣṭhitamityādinā / saṃjñā tāvadatra kalpanāmātrātmikaiva, tasyāmavabhāsyamānaṃ nāmaivābhidhānam, arthastvabhidheyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Those who conceive that expression is a real entity and that what is to be expressed (<s>abhidheya</s>) is something other than it — for those who conceive thus, it is demonstrated that what is to be expressed, worthy of having their view refuted, is established in conceptual construction; this is shown by the [statement] 'established in mere designation' and so on. Here, designation (<s>saṃjñā</s>) is of the nature of mere conceptual construction, and what appears in it — namely, the name — is the expression (<s>abhidhāna</s>), while the object is what is to be expressed.

body.text: ato 'bhidhānādatiriktabhidheyaṃ nāstītyuktam /
body.translated_text: Therefore it is said that what is to be expressed (<s>abhidheya</s>), apart from the expression (<s>abhidhāna</s>), does not exist.

body.text: kalpanājñāne 'vabhāsyamānamabhidhānamatra nāmaśabdenābhipretaṃ, na tu śrotravijñānavijñeyaḥ śabdaḥ tasyābhidhānatvābhāvāt / etāvanmātratve sati rūpadīnāṃ sarve vividhābhāsā na setsyanti, na ca skandhādīnāṃ vyavasthāpi setsyati / sūtre 'pi paramārthasatyanirdeśasāmarthyena sarveṣāṃ jñānajñeyābhidhānādīnāṃ saṃvṛtisatyatvena nirdiṣṭatvānnaiva te śabdamātratvena nirdiṣṭā iti / āryasatyadvayanirdeśasūtre 'pyuktam -
body.translated_text: The expression that appears in conceptual cognition is here intended by the word 'name,' not the sound that is cognizable by auditory consciousness, since that is not an expression. If that alone were the case, all the various appearances of form (<s>rūpa</s>) and the like would not be established, nor would the arrangement of the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) and the like be established. Even in the <s>sūtra</s>, since all cognitions, cognizables, expressions, and the like are designated as <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s> (conventional truth) by the force of the teaching on <s>paramārthasatya</s> (ultimate truth), they are not designated as being of mere words. As is also stated in the <s>Āryasatyadvayanirdeśasūtra</s>:

body.text: "yaduta devaputra, paramārthastāvat sarvavyavahārātītaḥ, yato hi nirviśeṣaḥ anutpannaḥ aniruddhaḥ abhidhānābhidheyajñānajñeyādirahitaḥ sa iti /"
body.translated_text: "O son of the gods (<s>devaputra</s>), the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>) transcends all convention, because it is without distinction, unoriginated, unceased, and devoid of expression, what is to be expressed, cognition, what is to be cognized, and the like."

body.text: etatsāmarthyena jñānajñeyābhidhānadayaḥ sarve saṃvṛtisatyatvenopadarśitāḥ 'saṃvṛtisatyasya paramārthasvabhāvanivṛttatvāt / ata evāryākṣayamatinirdeśasūtre 'pyuktam -
body.translated_text: By the force of this [statement], cognition, cognizables, expressions, and all the rest are shown as being of <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s> (conventional truth), since conventional truth is free from the own-nature of the ultimate. For this very reason, it is also stated in the <s>Āryākṣayamatinirdeśasūtra</s>:

body.text: "etadānukūlyena lokavyavahārastāvajjñānajñeyātmakaḥ akṣaraśabdairnirdiṣṭo 'bhidhānātmaka eva saṃvṛtisatyamiti veditavyam, na tu abhidhānābidheyamātrātmakamiti" / anyathā yatra cittasya pravṛttirapi nāsti, evaṃvidhaḥ paramārthaḥ saṃvṛtisatyanivṛttasvabhāva iti nirdeśo 'pi kathamupapannaḥ syāt / tatra paramārthatvena nirdiṣṭānāmārthānamavastubhūtānāṃ subhāṣitādivibhāgo 'pi naiva suśaka iti codyaṃ tāvat siddhasādhanameva / sarve dharmāstathātātvenaikarasā eva / tathātāyāṃ nāsti kaścanapi vibhāgaḥ / ataḥ subhāṣitadurbhāṣitatvena yadi tathatāsvabhāvo naiva vibhāgārhastadā naivāyaṃ kaścanāpi doṣa iti /
body.translated_text: "In conformity with this, worldly convention, being of the nature of cognition and cognizable, designated by syllables and words, and of the nature of expression, should be understood as <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s> (conventional truth) — but not as being of the nature of mere expression and what is to be expressed." Otherwise, how would the teaching that the <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate), where there is no activity of mind whatsoever, has a nature free from conventional truth, be tenable? The objection that the distinction between well-spoken (<s>subhāṣita</s>) and so on is not possible for objects designated as ultimate that are non-entities — that amounts to proving what is already established. All <s>dharmas</s> are of one taste by virtue of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). In <s>tathatā</s> there is no distinction whatsoever. Therefore, if the own-nature of <s>tathatā</s> does not admit of distinction in terms of well-spoken and ill-spoken, then this is no fault at all.

body.text: ityevaṃ ye tāthāgatāgamāḥ pratyakṣaparokṣatayā paramārtathābhidhāyakā dehavatāṃ ca hitasukhajanakāste subhāṣitānītyucyante, tadviparītāni na subhāṣitānīti teṣāṃ bhedaḥ sidhyati / bhavanmatānusāraṃ tavannāmnaḥ parikalpitasvabhāvatayopādānāt subhāṣitāsubhāṣitarupeṇa kathaṃ vyavasthā kriyate? asmin bhavatāṃ yaduttaram, asmākamapi tathaiveti gauṇamevaitat / yattāvacchabdārthetyādikamuktam, tadapi naiva yujyate, śabdārthayoḥ saṃvṛtimātratvābhāvāt /
body.translated_text: Thus, those <s>Tāthāgata</s> scriptures (<s>āgama</s>) that declare the ultimate through the direct and the indirect, and that produce benefit and happiness for embodied beings — they are called 'well-spoken' (<s>subhāṣita</s>). Those that are the opposite are not well-spoken — thus their distinction is established. Following your position, since names are adopted as being of fabricated own-nature, how is the determination made in the form of well-spoken and ill-spoken? Whatever answer you give to this, for us too it is just the same — this is merely figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>). The statement 'regarding the word and its meaning' and so on — that too is not tenable, because word and meaning are not of the nature of mere convention.

body.text:
śabdārtho 'pyastīti nirdiśyate, yato hi abhidheyādisamastavastūni paramārthato niḥsvabhāvatvena māyādivat parikalpitasvabhāvāni / yathā aneke puruṣāḥ puruṣetiśabdārthasāmānyākārasvabhāvena vyavasthāpyante, tathaiva paramārthato niḥsvabhāvāni vastūni kathaṃ na vyavasthāpayituṃ śakyante? viśeṣataḥ kevalaṃ vastusvabhāva eva śabdārthasāmānyasvarūpo bhavatīti yaduktaṃ tatra kimapi kāraṇaṃ naiva paśyāmaḥ / anādīti yad viśeṣaṇaṃ nāsti vastubhūtaṃ tasyāpyasaditi sāmānyavyavahāro dṛśyate / sukhādīni svasaṃvedyāṃ - nittyādikaṃ yaduktaṃ tadapi naiva yujyate, teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ sukhādīnāṃ saṃvṛtyantargatatvāditi pūrvaṃ kṛta eva nirdeśaḥ / vastūni kevalamanidarśanasvabhāvāni eva bhaviṣyantīti yaduktaṃ tatrāpi nāsti kācana yuktiḥ, keśoṇḍukadvicandrādimithyāsvabhāvānāmapyanirvacanīyasvabhāvena dṛśyamānatvāt / sūtre 'pyabhidhānābhidheyādayaḥ saṃvṛtikāḥ, na tu satsvabhāvā nirdiṣṭā iti pūrvamuktameva /
asya strotobhūtaṃ sūtraṃ pūrvaṃ nirdiṣṭameva /
ye kecana paramārthaṃ yadyapi prasajyamātramityabhidadhate, [kintu] sa tathā prasajyamātro na bhavati / aniścitameva tasya lakṣaṇam / yatāvat paramārthe hyāropitasvabhāvaḥ sa saṃvṛtireva sa [paramārthastu] sarvaprapañcātītaḥ / sūtre 'pyuktam - "mañjuśrīḥ, kiṃ tāvat paramārthasatyam? mañjuśrī - rāhadevaputra, yadi paramārthataḥ paramārthasatyaṃ kāyavākcittaniṣedhamātrasvabhāvaḥ syāttadā sa paramārthasatyamiti saṃkhyāṃ na gacchet, tadā sa saṃvṛtireva syāt / api ca, devaputra, paramārthataḥ paramarthasatyaṃ sarvavyavahārātītamiti" /
body.translated_text: It is indicated that the meaning of words also exists. Since all entities (<s>vastu</s>) such as the expressible (<s>abhidheya</s>) and so forth are, in the ultimate sense (<s>paramārthatas</s>), without intrinsic nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>) and possess a nature that is conceptually constructed (<s>parikalpitasvabhāva</s>) like illusions (<s>māyā</s>) and so on — just as many persons are established through the universal form (<s>sāmānyākāra</s>) that is the meaning of the word 'person,' in exactly the same way, how can entities that are ultimately without intrinsic nature not be established? In particular, as for the statement that the nature of an entity (<s>vastusvabhāva</s>) alone constitutes the universal form of word-meaning, we do not see any reason whatsoever for that. As for the qualifier 'beginningless' (<s>anādi</s>) — even for that which does not exist as a real entity (<s>vastubhūta</s>), the conventional usage of 'non-existent' is observed. As for the statement regarding pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and such being self-cognized (<s>svasaṃvedya</s>), permanence (<s>nitya</s>) and the like — that too is not tenable, since all those pleasures and such are included within <s>saṃvṛti</s> (convention), as has already been indicated previously. As for the statement that entities would simply be of a nature that cannot be demonstrated (<s>anidarśanasvabhāva</s>) — there too there is no logic, since even false natures such as hair-nets (<s>keśoṇḍuka</s>), double moons (<s>dvicandra</s>) and the like are seen as having an inexpressible nature (<s>anirvacanīyasvabhāva</s>). It has already been stated previously that in the <s>sūtra</s>s, designation (<s>abhidhāna</s>), the designated (<s>abhidheya</s>), and so forth are conventional (<s>saṃvṛtika</s>), and are not indicated as having a real nature (<s>satsvabhāva</s>). The <s>sūtra</s> that is the source of this has already been cited previously. As for those who maintain that the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>) is merely a negative consequence (<s>prasajyamātra</s>), [however] it is not merely a negative consequence in that way. Its definition is entirely indeterminate. Whatever nature is superimposed (<s>āropitasvabhāva</s>) upon the ultimate is simply <s>saṃvṛti</s> (convention); [the ultimate] transcends all conceptual proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>). As stated in the <s>sūtra</s> as well: "<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, what then is ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>)? <s>Mañjuśrī</s> [replied]: <s>Rāhadevaputra</s>, if ultimate truth were ultimately of the nature of mere negation of body, speech, and mind, then it would not be reckoned as ultimate truth; it would then be merely <s>saṃvṛti</s> (convention). Moreover, <s>Devaputra</s>, ultimate truth ultimately transcends all conventional usage (<s>vyavahāra</s>)."

body.text: teṣu vastuvāsanāyā api pūrvaṃ kṛtaniṣedhāt kevalaṃ saṃvṛtyantargatābyeva tānyoto 'nyataḥ pūrtirnaivāvaśyakī / yadi pramāṇairabhāvo naiva māyādibhirbhinnastathāpi paramārthataḥ svataḥ saditi nāma kriyate tadā saharṣaṃ kriyatāṃ svairamutsavo 'pyanubhūyatām, kintu svamatānakūlyena kṛtāṃ vyavasthāṃ vastūni naivānuvidadhate / pratītyasamutpannatā svasaṃvedyatā ca naiva vastūno heturbhavati, māyākeśoṇḍukādīnāṃ bhrāntatvāt kutrāpi sambandhasyāsiddhatvācca / yadyapratītyasamutpannatve vastūni naiva dṛśyate tadā tadadarśanamanyatrāpi tathaiva syāditi kathanasambaddhameva, satyapi vyāpake vṛkṣe śiṃśāpāsattvasyānanirvāryatvāt / ataḥ sukhādīni tāvadaviparīttatvenāsiddhatvānnaiva nirvivādabhūtāni /
body.translated_text: Since the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) of entities has already been negated previously among those, they are simply included within <s>saṃvṛti</s> (convention), and therefore fulfillment from anything else is not at all necessary. If non-existence as established by <s>pramāṇa</s>s (valid cognitions) is not different from illusions (<s>māyā</s>) and such, yet one still claims it is ultimately real of its own accord, then let one do so with delight, let one freely enjoy the celebration! However, entities do not conform to an arrangement made contrary to one's own doctrine. Neither dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpannatā</s>) nor self-cognizability (<s>svasaṃvedyatā</s>) serves as a cause for an entity, since illusions, hair-nets (<s>keśoṇḍuka</s>), and such are erroneous (<s>bhrānta</s>), and because the connection is unestablished in any case. If entities are not seen in the absence of dependent origination, then the statement that such non-perception would apply elsewhere as well is merely connected [to the argument] — for even when the pervader (<s>vyāpaka</s>), the tree, is present, the non-existence of the <s>śiṃśapā</s> (rosewood) cannot be precluded. Therefore, pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and such, to begin with, are not beyond dispute, since they are unestablished as non-erroneous (<s>aviparīta</s>).

body.text: kṣaṇamātrātiriktatvenāsthitatvādityādikaṃ yaduktaṃ tadapi nāstyasvīkāryam, svabhāvato 'nityatvasyānupapannatvāt / vastūnāṃ yadi samyaktvaṃ tadā sthitatvāsthitatvatoḥ parasparavirodho 'pyanupapanna eveti pūrvaṃ kṛtanirdeśāditi / ataścalasvabhāvatvād vastūni tāvanniḥsvabhāvatvena pradarśyante, ata eva ca tāni saṃvṛtisvabhāvānyucyante /
body.translated_text: As for the statement that there is no permanence because of not enduring beyond a single moment (<s>kṣaṇamātra</s>) — that too need not be accepted, since momentariness (<s>anityatva</s>) by intrinsic nature is untenable. If entities have correctness (<s>samyaktva</s>), then the mutual contradiction between permanence and impermanence is also untenable — as has already been indicated previously. Therefore, because of having a transient nature (<s>calasvabhāva</s>), entities are shown to be without intrinsic nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>), and for this very reason they are said to have a conventional nature (<s>saṃvṛtisvabhāva</s>).

body.text: yadi calasvabhāvārthaḥ saṃvṛtyarthastadā nāstyaniṣṭāpattiḥ / tāni sarvāṇi calasvabhāvāni vastūni māyādivat prakṛtyā niḥsvabhāvalakṣaṇarahitāni, paramārthasvabhāvāni ceti / so 'pi [svabhāva] tathāgataḥ syānnavā syāt sarvadā sthitatvānnityaḥ, ato nāsti siddhasādhanam /
body.translated_text: If <s>saṃvṛti</s> (convention) means 'having a transient nature' (<s>calasvabhāva</s>), then there is no undesired consequence (<s>aniṣṭāpatti</s>). All those entities of transient nature, like illusions (<s>māyā</s>) and such, are by their very nature devoid of the characteristic of intrinsic nature (<s>niḥsvabhāvalakṣaṇa</s>), and [are also said to have] an ultimate nature (<s>paramārthasvabhāva</s>). That [nature] too — the <s>Tathāgata</s> — may or may not exist; since it abides permanently, it is eternal (<s>nitya</s>). Therefore, this is [the fallacy of] proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>).

body.text: yadapi asatyārthetyādikamuktaṃ tadapi satyaśabdasyārthānabhijñatayaivoktam, bhrāntabuddhitvāt saṃvṛteriti pūrvaṃ nirdeśāt / mithyākāratayopagṛhītatvena sa asatya ityuktaḥ / samyaktayā asatye 'pi tasmin,satya iva prasiddhatvāt taccintanādhikareṇa satyeti nāmnā vyavahriyate / yadā sarvāṇi jñānajñeyādīni saṃvṛtiricyucyante, tadāpi lokaprassiddhayaiva satyānītyabhidhīyante, na tu samyagjñānādhikāreṇa, śabdamātrasya apekṣāviśeṣavaśena prayuktatvāt satyāsatyayoḥ parasparavirodhābhāvāt /
body.translated_text: As for the statement beginning with 'in an unreal sense' (<s>asatyārtha</s>) — that too is said merely out of unfamiliarity with the meaning of the word 'true' (<s>satya</s>), since it has been previously indicated that <s>saṃvṛti</s> (convention) is of the nature of erroneous cognition (<s>bhrāntabuddhi</s>). It is called 'untrue' (<s>asatya</s>) because it is apprehended in a false form (<s>mithyākāra</s>). Even though it is untrue when correctly [examined], since it is well-known as if true, it is conventionally designated by the name 'truth' (<s>satya</s>) in the context of investigating it. When all cognitions (<s>jñāna</s>), objects of cognition (<s>jñeya</s>), and so forth are called <s>saṃvṛti</s> (convention), even then they are called 'true' only by worldly convention (<s>lokaprasiddhi</s>), not in the domain of correct knowledge (<s>samyagjñāna</s>), because mere words are employed depending on specific contextual requirements, and because there is no mutual contradiction between 'true' and 'untrue.'

body.text: viparītākāreṇāvabhāsitastvāt saṃvṛtistāvad vastutvena naivābhyupeyate, anyatvābhāvāditi pūrvamevāveditam / tayā vyavasthitaṃ jagat tadadhikāreṇa yataḥ satyamityucyate, ataḥ saṃvṛtiravaśyaṃ vastutayā svīkartavyeti yaduktaṃ tasyāpyayuktatvāt pratijñā naiva hāpayituṃ śakyā /
body.translated_text: Since <s>saṃvṛti</s> (convention) appears in a distorted form (<s>viparītākāra</s>), it is not accepted as having the status of a real entity (<s>vastu</s>), because there is no otherness — this has been made known previously. Since the world is established through it and is called 'true' in that context, therefore the assertion that <s>saṃvṛti</s> must necessarily be accepted as a real entity — since that too is unreasonable, the thesis cannot be undermined.

body.text: saṃvṛtiḥ pramāṇam apramāṇaṃ vā? yadi pramāṇaṃ tadā kathaṃ sā saṃvṛtiḥ? yadyapramāṇaṃ tadā kathaṃ tayā nairātmyaṃ sādhayituṃ śakyam? - iti yaduktaṃ tadapi naiva yuktam / yato hi yathā anumānajñānasya mithyākāragrahaṇapravṛtatvāt saṃvṛtisvabhāvatve 'pi abhīṣṭarthakriyāprāpakatvāt pramāṇatvamabhyupaganyate tathaiva saṃvṛtisvabhāvasya mithyātve 'pi yathānurūpaśravaṇamananādihetuparamparāgatatvāllokikalokottarāthaiḥ sahāvisaṃvādāt pramāṇatvamabhīdhīyate, tadviparītatve tvapramāṇam / pramāṇādisarvavyāvasthāstavad vyavahāreṇaiveti pūrvaṃ prasādhitameva, atastā gauṇā eva /
body.translated_text: Is <s>saṃvṛti</s> (convention) a <s>pramāṇa</s> (valid cognition) or not a <s>pramāṇa</s>? If it is a <s>pramāṇa</s>, then how is it <s>saṃvṛti</s>? If it is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>, then how can selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) be established through it? — this objection too is not tenable. For just as inferential cognition (<s>anumānajñāna</s>), despite being of the nature of <s>saṃvṛti</s> because it operates by apprehending false forms (<s>mithyākāra</s>), is accepted as a <s>pramāṇa</s> because it leads to the accomplishment of the desired purposeful activity (<s>arthakriyā</s>) — in exactly the same way, even though the nature of <s>saṃvṛti</s> is false (<s>mithyā</s>), it is called a <s>pramāṇa</s> because it has arisen through the succession of causes such as appropriate hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>), reflection (<s>manana</s>), and so forth, and because it is non-discordant (<s>avisaṃvāda</s>) with both worldly (<s>laukika</s>) and supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>) aims; when the opposite obtains, it is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>. It has already been established that all determinations such as <s>pramāṇa</s> and so forth are merely by way of convention (<s>vyavahāra</s>); therefore they are only figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>).

body.text: yāni vijñānādīni saṃvṛtibījāni tāni paramārthato 'ṅgīkarttavyānīti yaduktaṃ tanna yaktiyuktam / yadīmāni kāraṇamātrāṇīti sādhyante tadā siddhasādhanameva, yato hyeteṣāṃ svānurūpahetavastāvadanādisaṃvṛtirūpā iti svīkriyanta eva, nemānyahetukatvena pratijñāyante /
body.translated_text: As for the statement that consciousnesses (<s>vijñāna</s>) and such, which are the seeds (<s>bīja</s>) of <s>saṃvṛti</s> (convention), must be accepted as ultimately real — that is not logically sound. If these are established as mere causes, then it is [the fallacy of] proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>), since their causes in accordance with their own nature are accepted as being of the form of beginningless <s>saṃvṛti</s> (convention); they are not asserted as being without a cause (<s>ahetuka</s>).

body.text: yadi tad bījaṃ paramārthasiddhamekaṃ ceti tadā kutrāpi tadanvayābhāvādanaikāntikameva / vṛkṣādyaśeṣasaṃvṛtioināṃ yadyuttaropādānahetvānukūlyaṃ na parikṣiṣyante tadā ramaṇīyatāmātrameva dṛṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ syāt / nāpi viruddho hetuḥ, yakṣānurūpabaleḥ sadbhāvāt sarvāstāḥ saṃvṛtayo 'satsvabhāvāḥ prasādhitā eva / anyathā [yadyevaṃ na syāt] katha tāḥ saṃvṛtaya iti / yadyasatsvabhāvāstadā vījānyapi tadanurūpāvastubhūtanyeva, na te vastubhūtāni, tadviruddhatvād asiddhatvāt pramāṇabādhitatvācceti tā gauṇā eva /
body.translated_text: If that seed (<s>bīja</s>) is one that is ultimately established, then since its invariable concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>) is not found anywhere, [the reason] is merely inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). If the favorableness of subsequent material causes (<s>upādānahetu</s>) for all conventional entities such as trees and the rest is not examined, then what is seen would merely be seen as pleasantness alone. Nor is the reason contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>), since offerings appropriate to <s>Yakṣa</s>s do exist; all those conventional entities (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) have been established as being without real nature (<s>asatsvabhāva</s>). Otherwise [if it were not so], how could they be <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventions)? If they are without real nature, then the seeds too, conforming to that, are merely non-entities (<s>avastubhūta</s>), not real entities — because of being contradicted by that, because of being unestablished, and because of being invalidated by <s>pramāṇa</s>s (valid cognitions). Therefore, they are merely figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>).

body.text: vastusvabhāvastāvat svīkriyata iti yaduktaṃ tattu yena kāraṇena vastusvabhāvaḥ svīkriyate tena satyadvayabhedānudhānaṃ kutrāpi naiva sidhyati / asatyapi vastusvabhāve aparīkṣyamāṇāni rūpadīni siddhānyeva / teṣu ye utpādādayaḥ samāropyante te saṃvṛtisatyatvena vyāvasthāpyante / pramāṇaiḥ samyaṅ nirupya anāropitā ye tāvadanutpādādayaste paramārthasatyatayā vyāhriyante / ataḥ paramārthato 'satyapi vastusvabhāve satyadvayaṃ vyāvasthāpyata eveti gauṇā eva /
body.translated_text: As for the statement that the intrinsic nature of entities (<s>vastusvabhāva</s>) is accepted — by the very reason for which the intrinsic nature of entities is accepted, the investigation of the division into two truths (<s>satyadvaya</s>) is not at all established anywhere. Even without the intrinsic nature of entities being real, form (<s>rūpa</s>) and so forth, when not subjected to analysis, are established as they are. Among those, the arising (<s>utpāda</s>) and so forth that are superimposed upon them are established as conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>). Those such as non-arising (<s>anutpāda</s>) and so forth that are not superimposed, being correctly ascertained through <s>pramāṇa</s>s (valid cognitions), are expressed as ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>). Therefore, even without the intrinsic nature of entities being ultimately real, the two truths (<s>satyadvaya</s>) are indeed established. Thus they are merely figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>).

body.text: yattāvadidaṃ gauṇāṃ paramārthamityuktaṃ tadapyasambaddhameva, dharmapudgalanairātmyalakṣaṇāyāstathātāyā yuktisaṅgatatvāt / paramo 'pi sā, āvaraṇaparihārārthibhirarthyatvādartho 'pi sā / aviparītasya jñānasya artha iti viṣaya iti kṛtvā sā paramārtha ityucyate / yatkhalu viṣayi lokottaraṃ jñānaṃ tadanyaśbdārthaprayogairapi vyavahriyate / śravaṇamananabhāvanopajātāyāḥ prajñāyā anukūlatvād vyavahāreṇaiva sā evamabhidhīyate /
body.translated_text: As for the statement that the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>) is figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>) — that too is incoherent, since <s>tathatā</s> (suchness/thusness), characterized by the selflessness of phenomena and persons (<s>dharma-pudgala-nairātmya</s>), is logically consistent. It is also 'supreme' (<s>parama</s>), since it is sought (<s>arthya</s>) by those who desire the removal of obscurations (<s>āvaraṇa</s>); it is also a 'meaning/object' (<s>artha</s>). Being the object — that is, the domain — of non-erroneous cognition, it is called <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate reality). Indeed, the supramundane cognition (<s>lokottarajñāna</s>) that is its subject (<s>viṣayin</s>) is also expressed through other terminological usages. Because it is conducive to the <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) born of hearing (<s>śravaṇa</s>), reflection (<s>manana</s>), and meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>), it is designated thus merely by convention.

body.text: tatra yena kāraṇena paramārthatattvalakṣaṇabhāvanayā yogibhiraśeṣasaṃkleśān parihatya uttarottaraprajñādiviśeguṇāṃścadhigamya mahārthatvaṃ prasādhyate, tena 'parama' śbdaprayogaḥ sarvathā yujyata eva / tadapi lokottaraṃ paramaṃ jñānaṃ sarvakalpanāvigatatvāt sarvadharmanirābhāsatvācca svasaṃvedyamanupalambhātmakaṃ ca, na tūpalambhasvarūpam / yathoktam -
body.translated_text: In that regard, since by meditating on the characteristic of ultimate reality (<s>paramārthatattva</s>), <s>yogin</s>s remove all afflictions (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) without remainder and, having attained progressively higher special qualities such as wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and so forth, accomplish the state of great purpose (<s>mahārthatva</s>) — for this reason, the use of the word 'supreme' (<s>parama</s>) is entirely appropriate. Moreover, that supreme supramundane cognition (<s>lokottarajñāna</s>), being free from all conceptual construction (<s>kalpanā</s>) and being without the appearance of any <s>dharma</s>, is self-cognized (<s>svasaṃvedya</s>) and of the nature of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>), not of the nature of apprehension (<s>upalambha</s>). As stated:

body.text: 'devaputra, paramārthasatyaṃ tāvat sarvākāraparamagocarasarvajñastāpyatītam /"
body.translated_text: "<s>Devaputra</s>, ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>) transcends even the domain of omniscient knowledge (<s>sarvajñajñāna</s>) in all its aspects."

body.text: anena vastuviṣayataḥ samyagatītatvena nirdeśādālambanadarśanasya niṣedha eva kṛtaḥ / paramārthalakṣaṇe yajjñānātmakamityuktaṃ tadapyaśeṣasampadādhārabhūtameva / ato mahārthasādhakatvāt paramārthastāvannāsti gauṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: By this indication that [ultimate truth] has completely transcended the domain of entities (<s>vastu</s>), the negation of apprehending an object of support (<s>ālambanadarśana</s>) has indeed been made. As for the statement that the definition of the ultimate (<s>paramārthalakṣaṇa</s>) is of the nature of cognition (<s>jñānātmaka</s>) — that too is indeed the basis of all accomplishments (<s>sampad</s>) without exception. Therefore, since it accomplishes the great purpose (<s>mahārtha</s>), the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>) is not figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>).

body.text: api ca, yadyasti tāvadekaḥ tāvadekaḥ kaścana gauṇaḥ paramārthastadā nirvāṇaṃ tāvat kīdṛśaḥ paramārthaḥ? tatra kasyāpi vastunaḥ samyaktayā arthasvabhāvasambhavābhāvāt tadapi kathamebhiścodyairanavamardanīyaṃ syāt / atastatra yad bhavatāmuttaraṃ tadasmākamapi samānameva / paramārthe vastūni tāvanna santīti yaduktaṃ tadapi paramārthamadhikṛtya jñānātmakatvaṃ samyagaviparītatvenāsadevetyuktam / ekena khalu prakāreṇa paramārthastāvadasanniti yaduktaṃ tattattvato vicāreṇāsadevetyarthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, if there is indeed some figurative (<s>gauṇa</s>) ultimate, then what kind of ultimate would <s>nirvāṇa</s> be? In that case, since no entity whatsoever can genuinely possess a real nature (<s>arthasvabhāva</s>), how could it too be immune to these objections? Therefore, whatever answer you give there is the same as ours. As for the statement that entities do not exist in the ultimate — that too has been said regarding the ultimate with respect to its being of the nature of cognition (<s>jñānātmaka</s>): it is correctly and non-erroneously non-existent. When it is said in one way that the ultimate is non-existent, the meaning is that upon investigation into reality (<s>tattvatas</s>), it is indeed non-existent.

body.text: saṃvṛtiparamārthayorekatvamiti yaduktaṃ tatra bhagavān paramārthalakṣaṇaṃ saṃskāralakṣaṇena saha tattvato nānyaṃ nānanyamiti svayamevoktavān / yathoktamāryasandhinirmocanasūtre -
body.translated_text: As for the statement of the identity of <s>saṃvṛti</s> (convention) and <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate reality) — there the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavān</s>) himself has stated that the characteristic of the ultimate (<s>paramārthalakṣaṇa</s>) is, in reality, neither identical with nor different from the characteristic of conditioned phenomena (<s>saṃskāralakṣaṇa</s>). As stated in the <s>Āryasandhinirmocanasūtra</s> (Noble Sutra of the Explanation of the Profound Intention):

body.text: "yaduta yadi paramārthalakṣaṇam saṃskārebhyo nānyaṃ [abhinna] syāttadā sarve bālapṛthagjanāḥ satyadarśinaḥ syuḥ / tataśca sarve prāptanirvāṇāḥ sarvajñāśca bhaveyuḥ / yathā ca saṃskārāḥ saṃkleśalakṣaṇāstathaiva paramārtho 'pi saṃkleśalakṣaṇaḥ syāt / tathā ca yathā paramārthaḥ sarvasaṃskāreṣvabhinnastathā saṃskāralakṣaṇanyapi[abhinnāni] syuḥ, kintu saṃskāralakṣaṇāni bhinnāni, phalataḥ paramārtho naivānanyaḥ / bhūtārthaprāpteranantaraṃ yogibhiḥ paramārthagaveṣaṇaṃ naiva yujyata iti paramārthastāvat saṃskārebhyo nāstyanyo nānyo 'pīti / anyathā satyadarśināṃ saṃskāranimittamanabhibhūtameva syāt / saṃskāranimittasyānabhibhāvād yoginastāvannaiva nimittabandhanānmuktāḥ syuḥ / nimittabandhanairamuktatvānna ca te doṣṭhulyabandhanādapi muktāḥ syuḥ / tasmādamuktatvānnaiva syāt nirvāṇasaddhirna vānuttarasukhānubhūtirapi / api ca, paramārthalakṣaṇaṃ yadi saṃskāralakṣaṇebhyo bhinnaṃ syāttadā na syāt paramārthaḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇam na ca paramārthalakṣaṇaṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ nairātmyaṃ niḥsvabhāvatā vā syāt, nāpi saṃkleśavyavadānayoḥ pṛthaglakṣaṇaṃ sidhyet / phalataḥ śakhasyaṃ śuklatvamiva paramārthalakṣaṇam saṃskārebhyastattvānyatvabhyāmanirvacanīyameveti" /
body.translated_text: "If the characteristic of the ultimate (<s>paramārthalakṣaṇa</s>) were not different from [i.e., identical with] conditioned phenomena (<s>saṃskāra</s>), then all foolish ordinary beings (<s>bālapṛthagjana</s>) would be seers of truth. In that case, all would have attained <s>nirvāṇa</s> and would be omniscient (<s>sarvajña</s>). And just as conditioned phenomena have the characteristic of affliction (<s>saṃkleśa</s>), so too the ultimate would have the characteristic of affliction. And just as the ultimate is undifferentiated in all conditioned phenomena, so too would the characteristics of conditioned phenomena be undifferentiated; but since the characteristics of conditioned phenomena are differentiated, consequently the ultimate is not identical [with them]. After the attainment of true reality (<s>bhūtārtha</s>), the search for the ultimate by <s>yogin</s>s would not be tenable — therefore the ultimate is neither different from nor identical with conditioned phenomena. Otherwise, the sign (<s>nimitta</s>) of conditioned phenomena would remain unconquered for the seers of truth. Since the sign of conditioned phenomena would not be overcome, <s>yogin</s>s would not be freed from the bondage of signs (<s>nimittabandhana</s>). Not being freed from the bondage of signs, they would not be freed from the bondage of latent defilements (<s>dauṣṭhulyabandhana</s>) either. Therefore, being not freed, there would be neither the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> nor the experience of unsurpassed bliss. Moreover, if the characteristic of the ultimate were different from the characteristics of conditioned phenomena, then the ultimate would not be the general characteristic (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>) of conditioned phenomena, nor would the characteristic of the ultimate be the selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) or essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatā</s>) of conditioned phenomena, nor would the separate characteristics of affliction (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>) be established. Consequently, just as whiteness of a conch shell, the characteristic of the ultimate is inexpressible (<s>anirvacanīya</s>) as either identical with or different from conditioned phenomena."

body.text: vastutāyāmeva tāvattattvānyatvakalpanaṃ sambhavati / paramārthalakṣaṇe tu niḥsvabhāvatvena tattvānyatvābhyaṃ vastu nābhidhātuṃ śakyate / vastusattve hi tattvānyatvabodhasya sambhavānna tu niḥsvabhāve vastuni tatsambhavaḥ, ato nāsti virodhaḥ / jñānātmakaparamartho 'pi saṃvṛtyā saha tathatālakṣaṇe paramārthākāre ekatvena svīkriyata eva / yathoktamāryaprajñāpāramitāyām -
body.translated_text: The conceptual construction of identity and difference is possible only with respect to real entityhood (<s>vastutā</s>). But regarding the characteristic of the ultimate (<s>paramārthalakṣaṇa</s>), because of its essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatva</s>), an entity cannot be designated through either identity or difference. For the cognition of identity and difference is possible when an entity exists, but not when the entity is without intrinsic nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>); therefore there is no contradiction. The ultimate that is of the nature of cognition (<s>jñānātmakaparamārtha</s>) too is conventionally accepted as identical with <s>saṃvṛti</s> (convention) in the ultimate aspect of the characteristic of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). As stated in the <s>Āryaprajñāpāramitā</s> (Noble Perfection of Wisdom):

body.text: 'kiṃ bhagavan, asti lokasaṃvṛtiranyā, paramārtho 'pyanyaḥ? bhagavānāhasubhūte, naiva lokasaṃvṛtiranyā, paramārtho 'pyanyaḥ / yattāvallokasaṃvṛtestattvaṃ tadeva paramārthasyāpi tattvamiti" / jñānātmakastu paramārtho māyādibhirabhinnatvāt samyaksaṃvṛtisvabhāvaśca tattvāvabodhānukūlatvāt paramārthasvabhāvaśca / ato 'pekṣāviśeṣavaśena ekasminnubhayasvabhāvo naiva viruddhaḥ /
body.translated_text: "O Blessed One, is <s>lokasaṃvṛti</s> (worldly convention) one thing and <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate reality) another?" The Blessed One said: "<s>Subhūti</s>, <s>lokasaṃvṛti</s> is not one thing and <s>paramārtha</s> another. The very reality of <s>lokasaṃvṛti</s> is the reality of <s>paramārtha</s> as well." The ultimate, being of the nature of knowledge (<s>jñānātmaka</s>), because of being non-different from illusions and the like, has the nature of correct convention (<s>samyaksaṃvṛti</s>); and because of being favorable to the realization of reality, it also has the nature of the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>). Therefore, by virtue of the relative distinction, having both natures in one is not at all contradictory.

body.text: yattavad bhavadbhiḥ puṇyajñānasambhārapāripūrirduṣkaretyādikamuktaṃ tadapi naiva yujyate, anenaiva tāvad darśanena sambhāraparipūrṇatāyā yujyamānatvāt / itthaṃ samyagdṛṣṭisamutthitā eva dānādayaḥ parisuddahetusamutthitatvādiṣṭaphalaṃ viśeṣaphalaṃ cābhinirharanti, na tu viparītasamutthitāḥ, mithyādṛṣṭisamutthitaśīlāṅgādivat /
body.translated_text: As for what you have said — that the fulfillment of the accumulations of merit and knowledge is difficult, and so on — that too is not at all valid, since through this very view the fulfillment of the accumulations is accomplished. Thus, acts of generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and the like, arising from right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>) alone, produce desired fruits and special fruits through being arisen from pure causes, but not those arising from the contrary — like moral components and the like arising from wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>).

body.text: paramārthato dānādivastūnāmabhāvāt tadupalambho viparīta eva, marīcyādiṣu jalopalambhavat / atastatsamutthitapāramitānaṃ sarvo 'pi prayāso mithyātmātmīyasamutthitadānādivad aviśuddhahetusamutthitatvenātyantaṃ nirbala eva / upalabdhilakṣanaprāptānāṃ dānādīnāmanupalabdhistāvat samyagarthatvena marīcyādiṣu jalānupalambhaivāviparītaiva / atastatsamutthitadānādayo mahāphalāḥ, sūpacitahetusamutthitatvena svasthabījābhinirhatāṅkura iva / ato 'nupalambhasamāśritesu dānādiṣu samyadṛṣṭisamutthitatayā vidvajjaneṣu śraddhaivotpadyate, na tvanyeṣu / yena kāraṇena dānādiṣvapravṛteḥ puṇyābhāvastāni dātavyādīni naivātyantamasadbhūtāni, saṃvṛtau teṣāṃ sadbhāvāt / naiva ca sarvadānupalambha eva, asamāhitāvasthāyāṃ māyādivat teṣāmupalambho 'pi / tadādhimuktisamudbhūtānupalabdhu tāni vyavasthāpyanta eva / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā
body.translated_text: From the ultimate standpoint, since things such as generosity (<s>dāna</s>) do not exist, perceiving them is erroneous indeed, like perceiving water in mirages. Therefore all effort of the <s>pāramitās</s> arising from that is entirely weak, like generosity arising from false notions of self and mine, being arisen from impure causes. The non-perception of generosity and the like that have the characteristics of perception is correct in the proper sense, like the non-perception of water in mirages — and that is not erroneous. Therefore generosity and the like arising from that [non-perception] are great-fruited, like sprouts arising from well-planted seeds in healthy ground. Therefore, in generosity and the like based on non-perception, arising from right view, faith arises among the wise, but not in others. Since there is no merit from not engaging in giving and the like, those objects of giving are not absolutely non-existent, because they exist in convention. Nor is it always non-perception alone; in the non-meditative state, like illusions, their perception also occurs. They are established through conviction-born non-perception. As the Blessed One has said:

body.text: kathaṃ bhagavan, upākuśalā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā dānaṃ datvā prajñāpāramitāṃ parisampadayanti? bhagavānāha - subhūte, bodhisattvā mahāsattvā dānaṃ datvā parityajanti tadā māyābuddhireva ṭeṣāṃ dāne sūpatiṣṭhatīti" vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: "How, O Blessed One, do <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> who are skilled, having given gifts, perfect the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>? The Blessed One said: <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>, having given gifts, relinquish them; then the illusion-like understanding establishes itself well regarding their giving." ...and so on in detail.

body.text: ata eva bhagavan ye bodhisattvā bhavanti, māyādivadadhimuktyā arthijanebhyaḥ putrādīnāṃ parityāgo rocate / samāpattyavasthāyaṃ tu dānādīnāmatyantamanupalambha eva / tadā te tatpravṛttiṃ naivāśrayante, samāhitāvasthāyāṃ dānādīnāmupekṣyamāṇatvāt / kintu pṛṣṭhalabdhāvasthāyāṃ tāvat te pravartanta eva / āryaratnakūṭasūtre 'pyuktam -
body.translated_text: For this very reason, O Blessed One, those who are <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — with conviction like illusions and the like — find it pleasing to give away sons and the like to those who seek objects. But in the state of meditative absorption (<s>samāpatti</s>), there is absolute non-perception of generosity and the like. Then they do not rely on that activity, since generosity and the like are disregarded in the meditative state. However, in the post-attainment state (<s>pṛṣṭhalabdha</s>), they do indeed engage [in them]. As stated in the <s>Āryaratnakūṭasūtra</s> as well:

body.text: "bhikṣavaḥ, bodhisattvairdānādīnāṃ svabhāvopalambho naiva karttavyaḥ, adānamapi naivācaritavyam" iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: "O monks, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should not perceive the own-nature of generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and the like, nor should they practice non-giving." ...and so on in detail.

body.text: ata eva prajñāpāramitādiṣvapi śūnyatādhimuktasya anupalambhāśritāni dānādīni bṛhatphalāni paripūrṇāni cetyuktāni / yathoktaṃ tatraiva -
body.translated_text: For this very reason, even in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and the like, it is said that for one who has conviction in emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), generosity and the like based on non-perception are great-fruited and complete. As stated therein:

body.text: "tatkiṃ manyate subhūte, sukaraṃ pūrvasyāṃ diśi ākāśasya pramāṇamudgṛhītum? subhūtirāha no hīdaṃ bhagavan / evameva subhūte, yo bodhisattvo 'pratiṣṭhito dānaṃ dadāti, tasya subhūte, puṇyaskandhasya na sukaraṃ pramāṇamudgṛhītum /"
body.translated_text: "What do you think, <s>Subhūti</s> — is it easy to take the measure of space in the eastern direction? <s>Subhūti</s> said: No indeed, O Blessed One. Just so, <s>Subhūti</s>, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who gives without abiding [in any notion], it is not easy to take the measure of that heap of merit, <s>Subhūti</s>."

body.text: dānaśabdo 'tra ṣaṭpāramitāvācakaḥ, ṣaṭdānapāramitā ityuktatvāt / āryaratnākarasūtre 'pyuktam - "bodhyarthamanutiṣṭhadbhiḥ sarve dharmā niḥsvabhāvā jñeyāḥ / tatra dānamapi niḥsvabhāvatvena jñāyate / upādātā ca niḥsvabhāvatvena jñeya, deyamapi niḥsvabhāvamiti jñeyam, pariṇāmanāpi niḥsvabhāveti jñeyā, yasya khalu pariṇāmanā kriyate, tadapi niḥsvabhāvatvena jñeyam / yadarthaṃ hi pariṇāmanā vidhīyate tadapi niḥsvabhāvatvenaiva jñeyam / tat kimartham? dānaṃ tāvad dānasvabhāvena śūnyam / tathaiva upādātā deyaṃ dānaphalaṃ pariṇāmanā bodhiśceti tattasvabhāvena śūnyā iti yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / evaṃ hi śūnyatādhimuktasyāprameyaiścintanairdānapāramitā pariśuddhā bhavati, tad dānaṃ ca dānapāramiteti saṃjñāṃ pratilabhate, na tu kadāpi malinā bhaviṣyati" iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: The word '<s>dāna</s>' (generosity) here denotes the six <s>pāramitās</s>, since 'the six <s>dāna-pāramitās</s>' has been stated. In the <s>Āryaratnākarasūtra</s> too it is said: "Those who practice for the sake of awakening should know all <s>dharmas</s> as essenceless (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>). Therein, generosity too should be known as essenceless. The receiver too should be known as essenceless, the gift too as essenceless, the dedication too as essenceless, that for whose sake the dedication is made should also be known as essenceless. For what purpose? Generosity is empty of the own-nature of generosity. Likewise the receiver, the gift, the fruit of generosity, the dedication, and awakening — these are empty of their respective own-natures; thus the practice should be carried out. For one who has conviction in emptiness, through immeasurable contemplations, the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) becomes purified; that generosity obtains the designation '<s>dānapāramitā</s>' and will never be defiled." ...and so on in detail.

body.text: ityevamanupalambhasamāśritāni dānādīni bṛhatphalāni viśuddhāni ca bhānti / tataśca anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhistāvat karatalasthiteva bhavati, upalambhāvakāśo 'pi dūrata eva sthitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Thus, generosity and the like based on non-perception are great-fruited and pure. Therefore, unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s>) is as if placed in the palm of the hand, while even the scope for perception stands far away.

body.text: sarve dharmā niḥsvabhāvā iti yaducyate, tasya tāvatko 'rthaḥ? yadyātmanāsattvānniḥsvabhāvāstadā siddhasādhanameveti yaduktaṃ tadapi yadyātmanā 'sattvānni' svabhāvatvena vyavastāpyate tadā na ca viruddhatvaṃ nāpi siddhasādhanamiti / yato hi yadi vastunaḥ svabhāvo 'vipoarītatadā parāpekṣayā tatsattvam tatsattvam āditaścāsattvaṃ naivopapadyate, ekasmin sadasattvayoḥ krameṇāpi virodhāt / phalatastāvadimāni vastūni paramārthataḥ svabhāvena parāpekṣitānītyato niḥsvabhāvanyeva / na hi svabhāvasya kṛtakatvaṃ nāma yujyata iti pūrvaṃ kṛtanirdeśāt / na caisāṃ paramārthataḥ parāpekṣayāpi sattvamiti pūrvameva prasādhitam / ataḥ kathamiva siddhasādhanam / vyavahāre tāvadimāni paramāśritya pravartante, ato nityasattvādīnāmapi nasti prasaṅgaḥ / evameva yadi vastvādīni prakṛtitaḥ sasvabhāvāni tadā svātmanāsattvaṃ svabhāvena ca sattvaṃ naivopapadyate, viruddhatvāt / ekasmin vatūni sattvāsattvasthitāsthiotatvādayaḥ parasparaviruddhadharmā naiva yujyate / ataḥ svātmanāsattvān svabhāvataścāsthitatvāttāni [vastūni] niḥsvabhāvatvenaiva suspaṣṭatayābhivyajyante / phalataḥ kathamiva siddhasādhanaṃ syāt / parikalpitātmanā svabhāvato 'sattvaṃ tadā naiva siddhasādhanamiti pūrvameva prasādhitam, pramānabādhitatvāt parikalpitasvabhāvasyeti /
body.translated_text: As for the statement 'all <s>dharmas</s> are essenceless (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>)' — what is its meaning? If [one objects that] they are essenceless because of being non-existent by their own nature, then this is merely proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>) — that too, if essencelessness is established by [their] non-existence by their own nature, then there is neither contradiction nor proving what is already established. For if the own-nature of an entity is non-inverted, then its existence relative to others, [while maintaining] its existence from the beginning and its non-existence — this is simply untenable, due to the contradiction of existence and non-existence even in succession in one thing. In effect, these entities are essenceless precisely because they are ultimately dependent on others for their own-nature — for it is not proper for own-nature to be produced, as was previously demonstrated. Nor is their existence even relatively in the ultimate established — this was already proven before. Therefore how could this be proving what is already established? In conventional usage, these things operate dependently, so there is no absurd consequence of eternal existence and the like either. Likewise, if things like pots were inherently endowed with own-nature, then their non-existence by their own nature and their existence by own-nature would be untenable, due to contradiction. In one entity, mutually contradictory properties such as existence and non-existence, stability and instability, are not tenable. Therefore, because of non-existence by their own nature and non-stability by own-nature, those [entities] are clearly expressed as essenceless alone. In effect, how could there be proving what is already established? The non-existence of the imagined self by own-nature — that is not proving what is already established, as was already demonstrated, because the imagined own-nature is invalidated by valid cognition.

body.text: vastūnāmutpattirapi paramārthataḥ pramāṇabādhitaiva / sā ca saṃvṛtya yujyate, na tu grahyagrāhakasvabhāvatayā / yaccāryāṇāṃ paramajñānagocaraṃ vastūnāmaviparītaṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ tadapi naiva saditi yuktyagamābhyāṃ pūrvaṃ pratipaditameva / yā ca saṃkleśavyavadānavyavsthā, sāpi naivāviparītasvalakṣaṇasamāśritā / bhagavatāpi vyavahārasatyāśritatvenaivāsyāḥ vyavasthāyā nirdiṣṭatvādityapi pūrvamevāveditam /
body.translated_text: The origination of entities is also invalidated in the ultimate by valid cognition. That [origination] is tenable conventionally, but not as having the nature of the graspable and the grasper. And the non-inverted own-characteristic of entities that is the domain of the supreme knowledge of the noble ones — that too does not exist, as was demonstrated previously through reasoning and scripture. And the structure of affliction (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>) is also not based on the non-inverted own-characteristic. It has already been indicated that the Blessed One taught this structure as being based on conventional truth (<s>vyavahārasatya</s>) alone.

body.text: sarvāṇi tāvad vastūnyādita ev notpannānityato 'nupannānīti yaduktaṃ tatra naiva siddhasādhanādayo doṣāḥ pravartante, yato hi sarve dharmāḥ paramārthato 'nādikāladeva praśāntatvādanutpannā ityabhyupagamyante, na tu saṃsārasyānādimātratayā, na cāpi pūrvaniruddhasya anutpattikatayā / api ca, bhagavatā bālapṛthagjanānāṃ santrāsaparivarjanārthamebhirapi prakārairvastūnāmanutpattiḥ sandarśitā, na tu iyanmātreṇaivetyavadhāryate, svaparādibhiranutpādasya pūrvameva nirdiṣṭatvāditi /
body.translated_text: In [the statement] that 'all entities have been unarisen from the very beginning, and are therefore unarisen' — the faults of proving what is already established and the like do not apply, because all <s>dharmas</s> are accepted as unarisen by virtue of being pacified from beginningless time in the ultimate — but not merely because <s>saṃsāra</s> is beginningless, nor because of the non-arising of what has previously ceased. Moreover, the Blessed One showed the non-arising of entities in these ways in order to avoid frightening childish ordinary beings (<s>bālapṛthagjana</s>), but it is not determined by this measure alone, since non-arising from self, other, and so on has already been demonstrated earlier.

body.text: parikalpitātmanā svātmanā vanutpāde 'pi naiva siddhasādhanamiti nirdiśyate / māyādivad vyavahāratayotpatterabhyupagamo 'pi sarvathānutpannatvena, naivānutpatterabhyupagamo na vā paramārthato 'nutpaterabhyupagamaḥ / ato nāsti darśanādivirodho 'pi / sarve tāvad dharmā dharmadhātulakṣaṇāyāṃ niḥsvabhāvatāyāṃ samarasatvena tathātākāratayā naiva viśeṣotpattirityato 'nutpattirabhyupagamyate, tathāpi naiva tatra siddhasādhanamiti / lokaprasiddhamapi svabhāvamālocya viśeṣotpattirnāstityapi naivocyate, ato nāsti darśanādivirodho 'pi / yadyapyutpattikriyālakṣaṇarahitatvād īśvarādito 'nutpannātvād vānutpattiḥ svīkriyante, tathāpi naiva tanmātratayaiveti, api tu yathā pūrvamuktaṃ tathātvenaivāsvīkriyante / ye tāvadanekasūtravirodha iti kathayanti, tebhyaḥ pūrvameva dattamutaram /
body.translated_text: Even regarding non-arising in terms of the imagined self, it is indicated that there is no proving what is already established. Even with the acceptance of arising conventionally like illusions and the like, because of non-arising in every respect, there is neither acceptance of non-arising [in the ultimate] nor acceptance of arising in the ultimate. Therefore there is no contradiction with perception and the like either. All <s>dharmas</s>, in the essencelessness that has the characteristic of <s>dharmadhātu</s>, being of one taste (<s>samarasa</s>) in the form of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), have no specific arising — therefore non-arising is accepted; yet even there, there is no proving what is already established. Nor is it said that there is no specific arising even with respect to the commonly acknowledged own-nature; therefore there is no contradiction with perception and the like. Even though non-arising is accepted because of lacking the characteristic of arising-activity or because of not arising from <s>Īśvara</s> (God) and the like, it is not accepted in that manner alone, but rather as was stated previously. Those who say there is contradiction with many <s>sūtras</s> — the answer to them has already been given.

body.text: triyānasādhanam
body.translated_text: Proof of the three vehicles

body.text: yadapi sādhanaviśeṇa yānatrayasiddhayanumānaṃ śraddhāviśeṣeṇa ca gotraviśeṣānumānaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ tenāpi yanatrayaṃ sādhayituṃ na śakyate / anena tāvadaparimitā yānabhedāḥ syuḥ / punaścanena yānatrayasādhanānumitasya gotratrayasyāpi niścitāvabodho naiva kartuṃ śakyaḥ, aparimitagotrabhedāvabodhāt / sūtre 'pi - "evaṃ hi sati aparimitasya yānabhedasya yanabhedasyaprasaṅgaḥ syāt" - ityukyam /
body.translated_text: As for the inference proving the three vehicles (<s>yānatraya</s>) through specific means and the inference of specific lineages (<s>gotra</s>) through specific faith — even by these, the three vehicles cannot be established. By this reasoning, there would be unlimited vehicle-divisions. Furthermore, through this, even definite ascertainment of the three lineages inferred by the three-vehicle proof cannot be accomplished, because of the comprehension of unlimited lineage-divisions. It is also stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: "In such a case, there would be the absurd consequence of unlimited vehicle-divisions."

body.text: yena khalu kāraṇena sattveṣu gotrabhedānumānasya niyatā siddhiḥ niyataśca śraddhabhedābodhaḥ pratīyate, te 'pyakalyāṇamitrasaṃsargeṇa akāraṇameva paraduḥkhamabhinandanto dṛśyante / evameva ye 'kāraṇameva paraduḥkhamabhinandanārthāmālambante, te 'pi kalyāṇamitrasamparkādinā kevalaṃ parahitacintane pravartamānā avalokyante / ye kalyāṇamitrasamparkādinā kevalaṃ parahitacintane pravartamānā avalokyante / ye khalvalpamātrake svasukhe hite cāsajyamānāḥ pareṣu daurmanasyaṃ dhārayanti, te 'pi pareṣu daurmanasyaviparītatvenāpyavalokyante / ye tāvat bhavasukhabhilāṣeṇa puṇyāni sampādayanti, te 'pi bhavasukhecchaviparīttvena samyakkāryāṇyanutiṣṭhamānā api dṛśyante / itthaṃ sādhanānāmaniyatatvāvabodhāt śraddhāyā anaiyatyamanumīyate / phalatatastatrānumānena gotrabhedasyāpyaniyatasvabhāvo 'vabudhyate / ato gotrabhedasyāpyaniyatatayā kathaṃ tāvad yānatrayaniścayaḥ sādhayituṃ śakyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Even those for whom a definite proof of lineage-division inference among beings and a definite comprehension of faith-division seem to be perceived — they too are seen, through association with bad spiritual friends, rejoicing in others' suffering without cause. Likewise, those who embrace purposeless rejoicing in others' suffering — they too are observed, through association with good spiritual friends and the like, engaging solely in concern for others' welfare. Those who, without attachment to even a small amount of their own happiness and benefit, bear ill-will toward others — they too are observed as being the opposite regarding ill-will toward others. Those who accumulate merit out of desire for worldly happiness — they too are observed carrying out correct actions, being the opposite of desire for worldly happiness. Thus, from the comprehension of the uncertainty of the means, the uncertainty of faith is inferred. Consequently, through that inference, the uncertain nature of lineage-division too is comprehended. Therefore, given the uncertainty of lineage-division, how can the certainty of the three vehicles be established?

body.text: sattvanāṃ vivuidhāśayavaśenāpi gotrabhedo niścetuṃ na śakyate / yāni tāvat pañcābhisamayagotrāṇi tānyapi ekaniścayābhiprāyeṇaiva nirdiṣṭāni, na tvātyantikatāyā / tasminneva hi sūtre gotrāṇyanātyantikatayaiva nirdiṣṭāni / tathā hi -
body.translated_text: Even through the various dispositions of beings, lineage-division cannot be ascertained. The five <s>abhisamaya</s>-lineages are also taught with the intention of a single definitive [truth], not with ultimate finality. In that very <s>sūtra</s>, the lineages are taught as not being ultimately final. Thus:

body.text: 'sarvakuśalamūlotsargecchantiko hi mahāmate, punarapi tathāgatādhiṣṭhānāt kadācit karhicit kuśalamūlān vyutthāpayati / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta aparityaktā hi mahāmate, tathāgatānāṃ sarvasattvāḥ" iti /
body.translated_text: "O <s>Mahāmate</s>, an <s>icchantika</s> (one who has cut off all roots of virtue) — even he, through the sustaining power (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, at some time, somewhere, gives rise to roots of virtue (<s>kuśalamūla</s>). For what reason? Because, O <s>Mahāmate</s>, all beings have not been abandoned by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>."

body.text: phalatastathāgatādhṣṭhānena tāvadapare 'pyanuttarabodhau praṇidadhata iti jñātavyam / yastāvad akṣayamatinirdeśasūtre yāntrayanirdeśaḥ, so 'pi naivādhārabhūtaḥ, yato hi tathāgatā lokasya vividhāśayavaśena vividhāni yānāni nirdiśanto dharmopadeśe pravartante, na tu yanatrayamātratayā / evameva āryagaṇḍavyūhesūtre 'pyuktam -
body.translated_text: Consequently, it should be known that through the sustaining power of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, even others aspire to unsurpassed awakening (<s>anuttarabodhi</s>). The teaching of the three vehicles in the <s>Akṣayamatinirdeśasūtra</s> is also not a foundation [for the three-vehicle theory], because the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, in accordance with the various dispositions of the world, teach various vehicles in their <s>Dharma</s> instruction, but not as merely three vehicles. Likewise, it is stated in the <s>Āryagaṇḍavyūhasūtra</s> as well:

body.text: "śrīvairocanakhye lokadhātau tathāatasamantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketurājena abhisambodhiradhigatā, tadanantadameva tena aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ śrāvakabhūmau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ niryāṇāyāṃ bhūmau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ indriyapariśuddhiprabhāvanāniryaṇāyaṃ baudhau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ vimalaparākramadhvajāyāṃ bodhau paripācitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ buddhabhūmau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ balasamatāsamudācārānugamaniryāṇāyāṃ baudhau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ sarvatrānutaddharyabhisambhinnanayayānaniryāṇāyāṃ baudhau pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ caryāprayogasamavasaraṇanayaniryāṇāyāṃ baudhau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / apremeyaḥ sattvāḥ samādhiprasthānanayaniryānāyāṃ baudhau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ sarvārambaṇaviṣayapariśuddhimaṇḍalanayaniryāṇāyāṃ baudhau pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ bodhisattvabaudhau cittamutpāditāḥ / aprameyāḥ sattvāḥ bodhisattvamārge pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ" iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: "In the world-realm called <s>Śrīvairocana</s>, enlightenment was attained by <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Samantajñānaratnārciśrīguṇaketarāja</s>, and immediately thereafter by him innumerable beings were established on the <s>Śrāvaka</s> stage. Innumerable beings were established on the stage of deliverance. Innumerable beings were established in the awakening of the deliverance through the cultivation of purification of faculties. Innumerable beings were matured in the awakening of the Stainless Valor Banner. Innumerable beings were established on the <s>Buddha</s> stage. Innumerable beings were established in the awakening of the deliverance of following the practice of equality of powers. Innumerable beings were established in the awakening of the deliverance of the method of penetrating all vehicles everywhere. Innumerable beings were established in the awakening of the deliverance of the method of converging practice and application. Innumerable beings were established in the awakening of the deliverance of the method of proceeding through <s>samādhi</s>. Innumerable beings were established in the awakening of the deliverance of the method of the maṇḍala of purification of the domain of all objects. Innumerable beings generated the mind [of awakening] toward <s>Bodhisattva</s> awakening. Innumerable beings were established on the <s>Bodhisattva</s> path." Thus in detail.

body.text: bhagavatāpi bālajanapraveśārthaṃ yānabhedo vyavasthāpitaḥ, na tu nītārthatayā nidiṣṭaḥ / ata eva aryalaṅkāvatāre 'pyuktam -
body.translated_text: Even by the Blessed One, the division of vehicles was established for the purpose of entry by foolish persons, but it was not taught as definitive meaning (<s>nītārtha</s>). Therefore, in the <s>Āryalaṅkāvatāra</s> too it is said —

children.translated_text: "The divine vehicle, the <s>Brahma</s> vehicle, and likewise the <s>Śrāvaka</s> [vehicle],
the <s>Tathāgata</s> [vehicle] and the <s>Pratyeka</s> [vehicle] — these vehicles I proclaim.

children.text: yānānāṃ nāsti vai niṣṭhā yāvaccittaṃ pravartate /
children.translated_text: There is no finality of vehicles as long as the mind operates.

children.text: citte tu vai parāvṛtte na yānaṃ na ca yāninaḥ /
children.translated_text: But when the mind is turned around, there is neither vehicle nor traveler.
The establishment of vehicles does not truly exist; I proclaim the division of vehicles
for the purpose of attracting the foolish — I proclaim the division of vehicles."

body.text: ata eva āryasaddharmapuṇḍarīkasūtrādau ekayānanirdeśo naiva neyārtha iti pratipāditam tathā hi -
body.translated_text: For this very reason, it has been demonstrated that in the <s>Āryasaddharmapuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> and the like, the teaching of one vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>) is indeed not of provisional meaning (<s>neyārtha</s>). For thus —

body.text: "evaṃ rūpeṣu śāriputra, kalpasaṃkṣobhakaṣāyeṣu bahusattveṣu lubdheṣvalpakuśalamūleṣu tadā śāriputar, tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāṃ upāyajauśalyena tadaivaikaṃ buddhayanaṃ triyānanirdeśena nirdiśanti" /
body.translated_text: "In such forms, <s>Śāriputra</s>, when the aeons are disturbed by defilements, when beings are numerous, greedy, and of meager wholesome roots — then, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones, through skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), teach the one <s>Buddhayāna</s> (Buddha vehicle) through the exposition of three vehicles."

body.text: punaśca
body.translated_text: And furthermore:

body.text: "imeṣu buddhadharmeṣu śraddadhādhvaṃ me śāriputra, pattīyatāvakalpayata / na hi śāriputra, tathāgatānāṃ mṛṣāvādaḥ saṃvidyate / ekamevedaṃ śāriputra, yānaṃ yadidaṃ buddhāyānam" /
