body.translated_text: "Have faith in these <s>Buddha</s> teachings, <s>Śāriputra</s>! Trust and do not doubt! For, <s>Śāriputra</s>, there is no false speech found among the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. There is only this one vehicle, namely the <s>Buddhayāna</s> (Buddha vehicle)."

body.text: punaśca
body.translated_text: And furthermore:

children.text: ye bhunti hīnābhiratā avidvasū acīrṇacaryā bahubuddhakoṭiṣu /
children.translated_text: Those who are delighted in the inferior, unwise, who have not practiced conduct among many <s>Buddha</s> <s>koṭis</s> (billions),
who are attached to <s>saṃsāra</s> and greatly suffering — to them I show <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.

children.text: upāyametaṃ kurute svayambhū bauddhasya jñānasya prabodhanārtham /
children.translated_text: The Self-born One employs this as a skillful means for the awakening of <s>Buddha</s> knowledge.

children.text: na cāpi teṣāṃ pravade kadācid yuṣme 'pi buddhā iha loki bheṣyatha //
children.translated_text: Yet he never tells them: 'You too shall become <s>Buddhas</s> here in this world.'

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ kālamavekṣya tāyī kṣaṇaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā tatu paśca bhāṣate /
children.translated_text: For what reason? The Protector watches the time and, having seen the [right] moment, speaks afterwards.

children.text: so 'yaṃ kṣaṇo adya kathañci labdho vadāmi yeneha ca bhūtaścayam //
children.translated_text: This moment is now somehow obtained; I shall speak the true account here.

children.text: bauddhasya jñānasya prakāśanārthaṃ loke samutpadyati lokanāthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the illumination of <s>Buddha</s> knowledge, the Lord of the World arises in the world.

children.text: ekaṃ hi yānaṃ dvitiyaṃ na vidyate na hīnayānena nayanti buddhāḥ //
children.translated_text: There is indeed one vehicle; a second does not exist. <s>Buddhas</s> do not guide [beings] by an inferior vehicle.

children.text: pratoṣṭhito yatra svayaṃ svayambhūryaccaiva buddhaṃ yatha yādṛśaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Where the Self-born One himself abides, and whatever the <s>Buddha</s> [state] is like and of what kind,

children.text: balāśca ye dhyānavimokṣa indriyāstatraiva sattvā pi pratiṣṭhāpeti //
children.translated_text: the powers, <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, and faculties — in that very [state] he establishes beings.

body.text: mārtsaryadoṣo hi bhaveta mahyaṃ spṛśitva bodhiṃ virajāṃ viśiṣṭām /
body.translated_text: The fault of miserliness would be mine, having touched the stainless, supreme awakening,

body.text: yadi hīnayānasmi pratiṣṭhapeyamekaṃ pi sattva na mametu sādhu //
body.translated_text: if I were to establish [beings] in an inferior vehicle — even for a single being, this would not be good for me.

children.text: ekaṃ hi yānaṃ dvitiyaṃ na vidyate tṛtīyaṃ hi naivāsti kadāci loke /
children.translated_text: There is indeed one vehicle; a second does not exist; a third never exists anywhere in the world.
It is through other skillful means that the supreme persons display a diversity of vehicles.

body.text: tatra prajvalitagṛhāntaḥsthitān bālajanān bahirniṣkāsayitumupāyabhūtasya vāhanaviśeṣasya dṛṣṭāntadvārā, tadvadeva ratnadvīpasthitaṃ nāyakapuruṣaṃ nivartayitumupāyabhūtasya madhye 'raṇyaṃ nagaranirmāṇasya ca dṛṣṭāntadvārā bhagavān upāyabhūtāni yāni trīṇi yānānyupadiṣṭavān, sa tāvanneyārtha eva / āryabodhisattvagocaropāyaviṣayavikurvaṇanirdeśe nāma mahāyānasūtre 'pyuktam -
body.translated_text: Therein, through the illustration of various special conveyances [offered] to lure the foolish persons situated inside a burning house to come outside, and likewise through the illustration of creating an illusory city in the middle [of a wilderness] as a skillful means to turn back a caravan leader situated on a jewel island, the Blessed One taught the three vehicles as skillful means. That is indeed of provisional meaning. In the <s>Āryabodhisattvagocaropāyaviṣayavikurvaṇanirdeśa</s>, a <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtra, it is also said —

body.text: "mañjuśrīḥ, tasmin buddhakṣetre yānenaikena niryāstīti tad yānaṃ tāvat sāravat syāditi / nāsmāsu śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānavyavasthā / kathamiti cet? tathāgatā hi nānātvasaṃjñāvirāhitā iti hetoḥ /
body.translated_text: "<s>Mañjuśrī</s>, in that <s>Buddha</s>-field there is deliverance by a single vehicle — would that vehicle then be substantial? Among us there is no establishment of <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles. Why? Because the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are free from the notion of diversity.

body.text: yadi mañjuśrīḥ, tathāgatāḥ kasmaicinmayānaṃ nirdiśeyuḥ, kasmaicit pratyekabuddhayānam, kasmaicicca śrāvakayānaṃ nirdiśeyustadā tathāgatasya tāvaccittam apariśuddhamabhiniveśajuṣṭaṃ ca syāt / prādeśikī ca tasya mahākaruṇā syānnānātvasaṃjñā ca / dharmamuṣṭiścācāryasya syāt / api ca, mañjuśīḥ, yebhyaśca sattvebhyo 'haṃ dharmamupadiśāmi te sarve bodhiniyatā mahāyānaparāyaṇāḥ sarvajñatābhinirhatāḥ pakṣaikaniṣṭhāśca bhavanti / taditthaṃ sarvajñatamanuprāpnuvantīti / ato nāsmāsu yānavyavastheti / mañjuśrīḥ, yā hi yānavyavasthābhidhīyate, tayā sarvajñena bhūmervyavasthā kṛtā, pudgalānāṃ vyavasthā kṛtā, alpasattvasamūhasya aprameyasattvasamūhasya ca vyavasthā kṛtā / dharmadhātorasambhedād yānabhedo 'pi tāvannāsti / anena hi prasthānadvāraṃ pradarśitam / prasthānanirdeśo 'pi tāvat saṃvṛtireva, na tu paramārthaḥ / ata ekameva yānam, na dvitīyamiti /"
body.translated_text: If, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> were to teach the <s>Mahāyāna</s> to some, the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle to some, and the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle to some — then the mind of the <s>Tathāgata</s> would be impure and possessed of attachment. His great compassion would be partial, and there would be the notion of diversity. There would be a teacher's closed fist. Moreover, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, those beings to whom I teach the <s>Dharma</s> are all destined for awakening, directed toward the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, oriented toward omniscience, and standing on one side [of awakening]. They thus attain omniscience. Therefore, among us there is no establishment of vehicles. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, what is called the establishment of vehicles — by that the Omniscient One has made the establishment of stages, the establishment of individuals, the establishment of the group of few beings and the immeasurable group of beings. Because of the indivisibility of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), there is no division of vehicles. For this is the gateway of setting forth that has been shown. The exposition of setting forth is merely conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), not ultimate. Therefore, there is only one vehicle, not a second."

body.text: āryaśrīmālāsūtre 'pyuktam -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Āryaśrīmālāsūtra</s> too it is said —

body.text: "yacca parinirvāṇaṃ yāni ca trīṇi yānānyupadiṣṭāni tatsarvaṃ tathāgatānāmupāyamātram, ekayānāvabodhena anuttarasamyaksaṃbodheradhigamāt /" ata eva ekayānanirdeśastāvadābhiprāyika iti vacanasya dharmadhātulakṣaṇe sarvayānānāṃ samatvādekayānamiti kathanaṃ tāvannāstyāryasaddharmapuṇḍarīkādyanukūlamiti niyataṃ vidvadbhiravadhāryam, naiva tadabhiprāyavaśāduktamiti jñeyam / āryadaśadharmādau yānatrayanirdeśastu upāyasvarūpatvād vineyajanebhyaḥ sa ekayānanirdeśābhiprāyeṇaiva vihita ityeva niśceyam / ato yānatrayanirdeśastāvad buddhanāmupāyamātram, na tu vāstavika ityato vineyajanā naiva teṣu pravartante / mahāyānasūtrākaṅkāre hi - ekasya yānasya ca yā hi deśanā tadānukūlyena prayojanena sā / iti yaduktaṃ tacchrāvakāṇāṃ yadyanuśayasamucchedo jāyeta tadā jāterapi sarvathopacchedād anekajanmaparamparāsamudāgataṃ buddhātvaṃ kathaṃ nāma sādhyaṃ syāditi kathanaṃ tu teṣāṃ jāteḥ sarvathopacchedasyāsiddhatvānnaiva yuktam / āryaśrīmālāsiṃhanādasūtre coktam -
body.translated_text: "Whatever <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> and whatever three vehicles have been taught — all of that is merely the skillful means of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, [established] through the understanding of one vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>), from the attainment of <s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s> (supreme perfect awakening)." Therefore, the teaching of one vehicle is indeed intentional (<s>ābhiprāyika</s>) — the statement expressing this as 'because of the equality of all vehicles with respect to the characteristic of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, it is called one vehicle' is certainly not in accord with the <s>Āryasaddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> and the like. It should be firmly understood by the learned that it is not stated from that intention. The teaching of three vehicles in the <s>Āryadaśadharma</s> and the like, being of the nature of skillful means, was prescribed for trainable beings with precisely the intention of the one vehicle teaching. Therefore, the teaching of three vehicles is merely a skillful means of the <s>Buddhas</s>, not actual. Since it is not actual, trainable beings should not engage in those [three vehicles]. In the <s>Mahāyānasūtrālaṅkāra</s> —: 'And the teaching of the one vehicle, by what purpose and in accordance with that —' Thus what was stated, regarding <s>Śrāvakas</s>, if the complete eradication of latent tendencies were to occur, then since birth itself would be completely cut off in every way, how could <s>Buddhahood</s> accumulated over many successive lifetimes be achieved? — this statement, however, is not valid because the complete cutting off of their birth in every way is unestablished. In the <s>Āryaśrīmālāsiṃhanādasūtra</s> it is also said —

body.text: "arhato 'pi vināśasadbhāvāttatsaṃtrāsena tāvadarhantaḥ pratyekabuddhā api bhagavataḥ śaraṇaṃ pratipadyante, sopadhiśeṣadharmitvād bhagavan śrāvakārhatāṃ pratyekabuddhānām, janmakṣayābhāvācca bhagavan, teṣām / ato bhavatyeva teṣāṃ janma / bhavantyeva te sopadhipeṣāḥ, naiva janmatā, apitu karmaṇāṃ pāripūrerabhāvād bahukaraṇīyāvaśeṣācca / yadi naiva te teṣāṃ parihāraṃ kurvīran tadā santyaneke nirvāṇadhātorapasārakāsteṣu prahātavyadharmā..." iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: "Because even for the <s>Arhat</s> there is destruction and existence, the <s>Arhats</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> too, terrified by that, take refuge in the Blessed One, being of the nature of possessing residue (<s>sopadhiśeṣa</s>). Blessed One, since there is no exhaustion of birth for the <s>Śrāvaka</s> <s>Arhats</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, there is indeed birth for them. They are indeed possessed of residue — not [residue] from birth, but because there is the incompleteness of the fulfillment of actions and much remaining to be done. If they were not to make provision for that, then there would indeed be many who fall away from the realm of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, and among them there would be defilements to be abandoned..." and so on in detail.

body.text: yaśca jātikṣaya ityādinā kṣayānutpādajñānayoḥ samudbhavastasya neyārthatvaṃ tu taminneva sūtre nirdiṣṭam / tathā hi -
body.translated_text: The provisional meaning (<s>neyārthatva</s>) of the statement 'destruction of birth' and the like, referring to the arising of the knowledge of destruction and non-arising, has been indicated in that very sūtra. For thus —

body.text: "bhagavan, arhantāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ vimuktiṃ yāvad yat pratyekṣaṇājñānaṃ yāścāśvāsādhāyikāścatastro 'nusmṛtayastat sarvamābhiprāyikam, yānānāṃ neyārthatvena vibhāgaṃ kṛtvā vyākaraṇāt / bhagavat, tatkimarthamiti cet? dvidhā bhavati cyutiḥsamucchedikā ca acityapariṇāminī ceti / tatra samucchedikā ca acintyapariṇāminī ceti / tatrasamucchedikā tāvaccyutiḥ pratisandadhatāṃ sattvānāmeva / bhagavan, arhatāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ vaśitāprāptabodhisattvānāṃ ca manomayakāyasya cyutistu bodhimaṇḍaparyantam acintyapariṇāminyeva bhavati / bhagavan, anayordayoścyutyoḥ samucchedacyuteradhikāre tāvadarhatāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ jātikṣayo jāyata iti pratīyate........ iti' vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: "Blessed One, what is called the direct knowledge and the four recollections that serve as the basis of confidence (<s>āśvāsādhāyikā</s>) up to the liberation of the <s>Arhats</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> — all of that is intentional (<s>ābhiprāyika</s>), since it has been explained through the analysis of vehicles as being of provisional meaning (<s>neyārtha</s>). Blessed One, if asked why — there are two kinds of passing away: one that is annihilative and one that is inconceivably transformative. Therein, the annihilative passing away pertains only to beings who take rebirth. Blessed One, the passing away of the mental body (<s>manomayakāya</s>) of <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have attained mastery is inconceivably transformative, extending to the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>). Blessed One, of these two kinds of passing away, it is under the scope of annihilative passing away that it appears that the destruction of birth occurs for <s>Arhats</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>..." and so on in detail.

body.text: anayostāvaccyutyoravidyāvāsabhūmipratyayairanāstravakarmahetubhiḥ samudbhūtā jātistu bhavatyeveti nirdiṣṭam / tathā hi -
body.translated_text: Of these two kinds of passing away, the birth that arises through causes consisting of uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>) karma, conditioned by the ground of the latent impressions of ignorance (<s>avidyāvāsabhūmi</s>), does indeed exist — as has been stated. For thus —

body.text: "bhagavan, yaduta upādānapratyayāḥ sāstravakarmahetukāstrayo bhavāḥ sambhavanti / evameva bhagavan, avidyāvāsabhūmipratyayā anāstravakarmahetukā arhatāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ vaśitāprāptānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ ca manomayāstrayaḥ kāyāḥ sambhavanti.....iti" vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: "Blessed One, just as the three states of existence arise conditioned by attachment and caused by contaminated karma — in exactly the same way, Blessed One, conditioned by the ground of the latent impressions of ignorance and caused by uncontaminated karma, three mental bodies arise for <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have attained mastery..." and so on in detail.

body.text: āryalaṅkāvatārasūtre cāpi nirdiṣṭaṃ yad dhātutrayātikrānta api te 'nāstravadhātau avasthitā bhavanti / atastathāgatādhiṣṭhānena jātivaśitāṃ prāpya sambhāradvayaṃ ca paripūrya te buddhatvamavāpnuvantīti / tathā hi -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Āryalaṅkāvatārasūtra</s> too it has been taught that even though they have transcended the three realms, they abide in the uncontaminated realm (<s>anāsravadhātu</s>). Therefore, through the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having attained mastery over birth and having completed the two accumulations, they attain <s>Buddhahood</s>. For thus —

body.text: "prahīṇā bhavanti dharmanairātmyāvabodhāt, tadā te vāsanādoṣasamādhimadābhāvādanāstravadhātau prativibudhyante / punarapi lokottarānāstravadhātuparyāpannān sambhārān paripūrya acintyadharmakāyavaśavartītāṃ pratilapsyante /
body.translated_text: "Their [defilements] are abandoned through the realization of the selflessness of phenomena (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>); then, because of the absence of the intoxication of <s>samādhi</s> and the faults of latent impressions, they awaken in the uncontaminated realm. Furthermore, having completed the accumulations that pertain to the supramundane uncontaminated realm, they will attain mastery over the inconceivable <s>Dharmakāya</s>.

children.translated_text: Just as a piece of wood is carried away by the waves of the ocean,

children.text: tathā hi śravako mūḍho lakṣaṇena pravāhyate //
children.translated_text: so too the <s>Śrāvaka</s>, deluded, is carried away by [clinging to] characteristics.
Bound by the latent impressions of afflictions, freed from active afflictions,
intoxicated by the intoxication of <s>samādhi</s>, they abide in the uncontaminated realm.

children.text: niṣṭhāgatirna tasyāsti na ca bhūyo nirvartate /
children.translated_text: There is no final destination for that one, nor does one arise again;
having attained the body of <s>samādhi</s>, one does not awaken for an entire aeon.
Just as an intoxicated person awakens when the intoxication subsides,

children.text: tathā te buddhadharmākhyaṃ kāyaṃ prāpsyanti māmakam //
children.translated_text: so too they will attain my body, called the <s>Buddhadharma</s>."

body.text: atra khalu kāṣṭhodadhyupamayā bhavasāgare pravahamānatvaṃ nirdiṣṭam / taraṅgopamayā tāvad dharmalakṣaṇaṃ prati abhiniveśavaśāt parinirvāṇaṃ na prāpyata iti saṅketitam / 'vāsanākleśasambaddhāḥ' ityādinā tu avidyāvāsanābhūmibandhanenāvimuktāḥ, kleśaparyatthānaiśca visaṃyuktā iti / 'niṣṭhāgatirna tasyāsti' ityādinā tāvannirvāṇanagare 'praviṣṭāstathā bhavasāgare 'pi na bhramantīti / anāstravasamādhisamprayuktatvād anekakalpaparyantamanāstravadhātau sthitiḥ, tadantaraṃ tato vyatthāya sambhārān paripūrya buddhatvāvāptirityādikaṃ spaṣṭatayā nirdiṣṭam /
body.translated_text: Here, through the simile of wood and the ocean, being carried along in the ocean of existence is indicated. Through the simile of the waves, it is signified that due to attachment to the characteristics of <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Parinirvāṇa</s> is not attained. By 'bound by the latent impressions of afflictions' and so forth, [it means they are] not freed from bondage to the ground of the latent impressions of ignorance (<s>avidyāvāsanābhūmi</s>), yet freed from the active afflictions. By 'there is no final destination for that one' and so forth, [it means] they have not entered the city of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, nor do they wander in the ocean of existence. Due to being conjoined with the uncontaminated <s>samādhi</s>, their abiding in the uncontaminated realm for the duration of many aeons, and then arising from that and completing the accumulations and attaining <s>Buddhahood</s> — all this has been clearly taught.

body.text: yaccāpyāryalaṅkāvatārādisūtreṣu nirmitaśrāvakānadhikṛtya śrāvakavyākaranaṃ kṛtaṃ taddhīnādhimuktasattvānāṃ bhayaparihārārthaṃ yānatrayanirdeśopāyapradarśanārthaṃ ceti jñātavyam / avaivartacakrasūtre 'pyuktam -
body.translated_text: The fact that in the <s>Āryalaṅkāvatāra</s> and other sūtras, the prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) of <s>Śrāvakas</s> was given with reference to emanated <s>Śrāvakas</s> — this should be understood as being for the purpose of removing the fear of beings of inferior aspiration and for demonstrating the skillful means of the teaching of three vehicles. In the <s>Avaivartacakrasūtra</s> too it is said —

body.text: "sarveṣu lokadhātuṣu sarvabuddhānāṃ dharmopadeśastāvadavaivartacakrasamānatayā samāna iti / martyalokadhātusattvāstu pañcakaṣāyakāle samutpadyamānā hīnādhimuktā eva / ataste ekayānoddeśyaṃ naiva paripālayanti, na ca tasminnadhimucyante / ato 'nayā yuktyā te sattvā buddhatvaṃ pratyabhimukhīkriyanta iti /"
body.translated_text: "In all world-realms, the <s>Dharma</s> teaching of all <s>Buddhas</s> is the same, in the manner of the irreversible wheel. But the beings in the world-realm of mortals, arising in the age of the five defilements, are of inferior aspiration. Therefore they do not preserve the instruction of one vehicle, nor do they have faith in it. Therefore, by this reasoning, those beings are turned to face <s>Buddhahood</s>."

body.text: āstravāṇāṃ kṣayādarhanto yadi na pratisandadhate, ato 'nekajanmaparamaparāsādhyaṃ buddhatvaṃ na pratilabhanta iti tadā bodhipariṇāmitānāmapyarhatāṃ na pratisandhirna ca teṣu buddhātvādhigama iti / yadi praṇidhānabalena tathāgatādhiṣṭhānena ca teṣāṃ pratisandhirabhyupagamyate, tadā kathaṃ nāpareṣvapi tathā? yathoktamāryaprajñāpāramitāyām -
body.translated_text: If <s>Arhats</s>, due to the exhaustion of defilements (<s>āsrava</s>), do not take rebirth at all, and therefore cannot attain <s>Buddhahood</s> which requires many successive lifetimes — then even <s>Arhats</s> whose [merit] has been dedicated to awakening should not take rebirth, and there should be no attainment of <s>Buddhahood</s> for them either. If their rebirth is accepted through the power of aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) and the sustaining power of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, then how not for others as well? As stated in the <s>Āryaprajñāpāramitā</s>:

body.text: "api ca, yadi te 'nuttarasamyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayanti, tadā anumodayiṣyāmi, nāhaṃ teṣāṃ kuśalamūlanāṃ vighnaṃ kariṣyāmi / śuddhadharmaviśeṣaiḥ śuddhadharmaviśeṣādhyupālambhaḥ karaṇīya iti /"
body.translated_text: "Moreover, if they generate the mind toward unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarasamyaksaṃbodhi</s>), then I shall rejoice; I shall not create any obstacle to their roots of virtue. One should make the effort to apprehend pure special qualities through pure special qualities."

body.text: yadi te sarveṇa sarvamanuttarasamyaksaṃbodheye abhavyā iti tadā kathaṃ nāhaṃ teṣāṃ kuśalamūlānāṃ vighnaṃ na kariṣyāmītyuktam / atyantābhāveṣu naiva vidhnasambhavaḥ / avasthāviśeṣābhiprāyeṇaiva śāntasyaikāyanasya kathanaṃ niyatam, na tu sarvadaiva niyatābhiprāyeṇeti jñeyam / āryasaddharmapuṇḍarīkasūtre 'yuktam -
body.translated_text: If they are in every way incapable of unsurpassed perfect awakening, then why was it said 'I shall not create any obstacle to their roots of virtue'? For in things that are absolutely non-existent, there is no possibility of obstruction. The teaching of one vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>) as pacified should be understood as certainly stated with the intention of a specific stage, not as stated with a definitive intention in every case. In the <s>Āryasaddharmapuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> it is stated:

body.text: "bhikṣurvā bhikṣuṇī vārhattvaṃ pratijānīyādanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhānaṃ parigṛhyocchinno 'smi buddhāyānāditi vadedetāvanme samucchrayasya paścimakaṃ parinirvāṇaṃ vadedābhimānikaṃ taṃ śāriputra, pratijānīyāḥ /"
body.translated_text: "If a monk or a nun should claim <s>Arhatship</s> and say, while having taken up the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening, 'I am cut off from the <s>Buddhayāna</s> (Buddha vehicle),' and should say 'this is my final <s>Parinirvāṇa</s>, the summit of my existence' — you should recognize that one as arrogant (<s>abhimānika</s>), <s>Śāriputra</s>."

body.text: arhantastāvat kleśakṣayahetoḥ sarvathā naiva pratisandadhate, tathātvāt / ye khalu satyadarśinaḥ śrāvakāḥ, ye ca kāmadhāturāgarahitā anāgāminaste buddhagotrakā iti / dvividhā api te 'nuttarasamyaksaṃbodhau vyākṛtāḥ acintyapariṇāminyā jātyā yuktatvātteṣāmiti yat kathanaṃ tadapyāryaśrīmālāsiṃhanādaāryaprajñāpārimitāāryadaśadharmakasūtrādiviruddham / teṣu kevalamarhata eva pratisamdhirupadiṣṭā, na tvanāgāmināmiti / tatrāryamālāsiṃhanādasūtraṃ tu pūrvamevoddhṛtam / āryaprajñāpāramitāśutre coktam -
body.translated_text: <s>Arhats</s>, due to the exhaustion of afflictions, do not take rebirth at all, being such by nature. The statement that those <s>Śrāvakas</s> who see the truths, and those <s>Anāgāmins</s> (non-returners) free from desire-realm attachment, are of <s>Buddhagotra</s> (Buddha-lineage) — and that both types have been predicted for unsurpassed perfect awakening because they are endowed with an inconceivably transformative birth — this too contradicts the <s>Āryaśrīmālāsiṃhanāda</s>, <s>Āryaprajñāpāramitā</s>, <s>Āryadadaśadharmakasūtra</s>, and the like. In those, only the rebirth of <s>Arhats</s> is taught, not that of <s>Anāgāmins</s>. The <s>Āryaśrīmālāsiṃhanādasūtra</s> was already cited earlier. In the <s>Āryaprajñāpāramitāsūtra</s> it is said:

body.text: "arhattvaṃ samadhigamya yadi sa samyaksaṃbodhimabhilaṣate tadā kathaṃ nāma ajātiṃ labdhuṃ śaknoti, parijanatā khalu bhagavatā tasya jātervyākṛtatvāt / bhagavānāha - maitreya, nāhaṃ karmakleśavaśājjātiṃ prajñapayāmi, apitu acityaparinirvāṇe pariṇāmanayā tasya jātiṃ prajñapayāmiti" /
body.translated_text: "Having attained <s>Arhatship</s>, if one aspires to perfect awakening, then how can one obtain the unborn [state]? For the Blessed One has predicted that one's birth [will occur] through full understanding. The Blessed One said: <s>Maitreya</s>, I do not prescribe birth through the force of <s>karma</s> and afflictions; rather, I prescribe that one's birth [occurs] through inconceivable transformative dedication (<s>acintyapariṇāmanā</s>)."

body.text: āryadaśadharmakasūtre 'pyuktam -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Āryadadaśadharmakasūtra</s> too it is said:

body.text: "bhagavan, śrāvakāḥ kṣīṇāstravāḥ, parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanagotrakāstathāpi kathaṃ te 'nuttarasamyaksambodhimabhisamboddhuṃ śakṣyante? bhagavānaha - śṛṇu kulaputra, tasya dṛṣṭāntam / tathaivāsti yathā kulapuitra, kṣatriyakule 'bhiṣikaḥ kaścana rājakumāro yadi sarvāsāṃ śilpavidyānāmadhyayanaṃ karoti / sa nāsti tīkṣṇendriyo 'pi tu mandendriyaḥ san paścādadhyeyasya pāṭhayasya prathamam, pūrvamadhyeyasya pāṭhayasya paścādadhyayanaṃ karoti, tadā kiṃ vicārayasi kulaputra, kimetāvatā sa nāsti rājakumāra iti kathayiṣyate? avocat - naiva bhagavan, naiva sugata, rājakumāra eva sa kathayiṣyate / bhagavānāhakulaputra, tathaiva bodhisattvagotrakā api ye mandendriyāste pūrvaṃ bhāvanāmārgeṇa kleśakṣayaṃ kṛtvā paścādanuttarasamyaksaṃbodhau abhisambuddhā bhaviṣyantīti /" vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: "Blessed One, <s>Śrāvakas</s> whose defilements are exhausted, whose lineage of bonds to existence is completely destroyed — how then can they attain unsurpassed perfect awakening? The Blessed One said: Listen, O son of good family, to an illustration for this. It is like this, O son of good family: a certain prince anointed in a <s>Kṣatriya</s> family, if he undertakes the study of all arts and sciences — he may not be of sharp faculties but being of dull faculties, he studies later what should have been studied first, and first what should have been studied later. Then what do you think, son of good family — would he be called 'not a prince' for that reason? He said: No, Blessed One, no, <s>Sugata</s>, he would still be called a prince. The Blessed One said: Son of good family, just so, even those who are of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-lineage but of dull faculties — having first destroyed afflictions through the path of cultivation, they will later attain unsurpassed perfect awakening." ...and so on in detail.

body.text: yacca "sārvagatikā buddhā bhaviṣyanti" ityuktam, tadarthastāvat sarveṣāṃ buddhatvasāmīpyāpekṣābhiprāyeṇeti - yaduktaṃ tadapi svecchāmātropakalpitatvādayuktameva / sārvagatikānāṃ bhavyatāṃ dṛṣṭvā tathoktamityatra ko virodhaḥ / tathaiva cāryaratnameghādisūtreṣvapi bhagavataḥ śākyamunernāmaśravaṇamātreṇa avaivartikabījāropaṇād abhedena sarve sattvā avaivartikatve vyākriyante, na tu sāmīpyāpekṣayā / ato yena śrāvaṇaṃ yena vā śravaṇaṃ yaśca śrotā teṣavapi avaivartikabījāni vidyanta eva, yato hi bhavatāṃ mate 'pi malānāmāgantukatvāccittaṃ prakṛtyā prabhāsvaramabhyupagamyate / ataḥ sārvagatikāstadarśaṃ bhavyā eva / astadabhiprāyeṇa tathābhidhānaṃ yujyata eva /
body.translated_text: As for the statement 'all beings will universally become <s>Buddhas</s>' — the interpretation that this is stated with the intention of the proximity of all beings to <s>Buddhahood</s> is improper, being fabricated by mere wish alone. Having seen the universal potential of all beings, it was so stated — what contradiction is there in this? Likewise, in the <s>Āryaratnameghā</s> and other <s>sūtras</s>, through merely hearing the name of the Blessed <s>Śākyamuni</s>, seeds of irreversibility (<s>avaivartika</s>) are planted without distinction in all beings — and this prediction of all beings as irreversible is not made with the intention of proximity. Therefore, whether [one considers] that which is heard, or the hearing itself, or the hearer — in all of them seeds of irreversibility do indeed exist, since even in your view the mind is accepted as naturally luminous (<s>prakṛtyā prabhāsvara</s>) because defilements are adventitious (<s>āgantuka</s>). Therefore, all beings are universally capable in this way. With precisely that intention, such a statement is indeed proper.

body.text: sarve sattvāstathāgatagarbhā iti yaduktaṃ tena sarve 'pyanuttarasamyaksaṃbodhipadaprāptiyogyā evopadarśitāḥ, yato hi tathāgataśbdo dharmadhātuḥ pudgaladharmanairātmyalakṣaṇaḥ prakṛtyā prabhāsvaraścetyeteṣvartheṣvabhyupagamyate / tathā ca nirdeśena sarve 'nuttarasamyaksaṃbodhisvabhāvā eva nirdiṣṭāḥ /
body.translated_text: The statement 'all beings possess <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s>' indicates that all are indeed fit for attaining the stage of unsurpassed perfect awakening, since the word '<s>Tathāgata</s>' is accepted in these meanings: the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality), characterized by the selflessness of persons and <s>dharmas</s> (<s>pudgala-dharma-nairātmya</s>), and naturally luminous. Thus, by this teaching, all are indicated as having the very nature of unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: api ca, 'yānam' iti yaduktaṃ tadapi nirvāṇagaraprāpako jñānātmako mārga evetyuktam, yāyate 'neneti kṛtvā / tattvajñānādeva hi mokṣamadhigantuṃ śakyate, nānyasmāt / tattvamapyekameva, anyathānavasthāprasaṅgaḥ / dṛṣṭibhede 'pi vastutattvaṃ nānekarūpeṣu vibhājayituṃ śakyate / ekasvabhāvatvāttattvasya, tadviṣayi jñānamapyekasvabhāvameva / adhigatatattvanāṃ buddhabodhisattvānāṃ yajjñānaṃ tadapi tattvaviṣayakābhijñānasvarūpameva, sarvasaṃkleśapratipakṣatvāttasya / na hi prādeśikairjñānaistattvabodho 'tiprasaṅgāt / tathā sati sarve tattvadarśinaḥ syuḥ / ato yattāvat pudgaladharmanairātmyatattvasākṣātkāri jñānaṃ tadeva nirvāṇaprāpakaḥ samyaṅ mārgo nānyaḥ / ata ekameva yānamiti /
body.translated_text: Moreover, the word '<s>yāna</s>' (vehicle), as stated, refers to the path having the nature of knowledge that leads to the city of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — because 'one travels by means of it.' For liberation can be attained only through the knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>), not from anything else. Reality too is one only; otherwise there would be an infinite regress. Even when views differ, the reality of things cannot be divided into multiple forms. Since reality is of one nature, the knowledge pertaining to it is also of one nature alone. The knowledge of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have realized reality is also of the nature of complete cognition directed at reality, since it is the antidote to all afflictions. For realization of reality cannot occur through partial knowledge, as that would lead to absurd consequences — in such a case, all would be seers of reality. Therefore, only that knowledge which directly realizes the reality of the selflessness of persons and <s>dharmas</s> is the correct path leading to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, and nothing else. Hence there is only one vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>).

body.text: eta eva bhagavatā nānyena tāvanmārgeṇa mokṣa iti nirdiṣṭam / āryalaṅkāvatārasūtre coktam -
body.translated_text: For this very reason, the Blessed One taught: 'There is no liberation by any other path.' In the <s>Āryalaṅkāvatārasūtra</s> too it is said:

body.text: "yaduta anye punarmahāmate, kāraṇādhinān sarvadharmān dṛṣṭvā nirvāṇagatibuddhayo bhavanti, dharmanairātmyadarśnābhāvānnāsti mokṣo mahāmate / eṣā mahāmate, śrāvakayānābhisamayagotrakasyāniryaṇaniryāṇabuddhiḥ / atra te mahāmate, kudṛṣṭivyāvṛttyarthaṃ yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ" iti /
body.translated_text: "Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmate</s>, those who, having seen all <s>dharmas</s> as dependent on causes, develop the notion of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as the goal — because of their failure to see the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>), there is no liberation, O <s>Mahāmate</s>. This, O <s>Mahāmate</s>, is the notion of non-definitive emergence pertaining to the lineage of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> realization. Therein, O <s>Mahāmate</s>, effort should be made for the purpose of averting wrong views."

body.text: āryaprajñāpāramitāsūtre 'pi bhagavatā proktam -
body.translated_text: In the <s>Āryaprajñāpāramitāsūtra</s> too the Blessed One said:

body.text: "yad dvayaṃ tad vastu, advayaṃ tu avastu / avocat - bhagavan, kiṃ tāvad dvayam? bhagavānāha - sūbhūte, rūpasaṃjñaiva dvayam, tathaiva skandhadhātusparśavedanādhātuṣaṭkapratītyasamutpādadhyānārūpyaduḥkhanairātmyasukhasattvādīnāṃ saṃjñā" iti / ityādikaṃ vistareṇa tāvannirdiśya -
body.translated_text: "What is duality is substance; what is non-duality is non-substance. He said: Blessed One, what then is duality? The Blessed One said: <s>Subhūti</s>, the very perception of form is duality; likewise the perception of aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), contact (<s>sparśa</s>), feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), the six sense-bases (<s>dhātuṣaṭka</s>), dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), <s>dhyāna</s>, formless [attainments], suffering, selflessness, happiness, beings, and the like." And so on, teaching in detail:

body.text: "yāvaddhi saṃjñā tāvad dvayam / yāvad dvayaṃ tāvad vastu / yāvad vastu tāvat saṃsāraḥ / yavācca saṃsārastāvannāsti sattvānāṃ mokṣaḥ" iti /
body.translated_text: "As long as there is perception, so long there is duality. As long as there is duality, so long there is substance. As long as there is substance, so long there is <s>saṃsāra</s>. And as long as there is <s>saṃsāra</s>, there is no liberation for beings."

body.text: ityanena prakrāreṇa dvayasaṃjñānukūlā kṣāntirapi tāvadasattvena jñānavyeti prakaṭitam / āryasatyadvayāvatārasūtre 'pi prajñaptaṃ yat sarvakleśānāṃ mūlaṃ bhāvābhiniveśa eva / ata eva sarvadharmaniḥsvabhāvabhāvanayaiva tāvat kleśāḥ parihartuṃ śakyante, nānyena kenacinmārgeṇeti kṛto nirdeśaḥ / tathā hi -
body.translated_text: In this way, it has been revealed that even patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) favorable to the perception of duality is extinguished by the knowledge of non-being. In the <s>Āryasatyadvayāvatārasūtra</s> too it is taught that the root of all afflictions is clinging to existence (<s>bhāvābhiniveśa</s>) alone. Therefore, the teaching was made that afflictions can be overcome only through the meditation on the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s>, and by no other path. Thus:

body.text: "kathaṃ mañjuśrīḥ, kleśā vinayaṃ gacchanti, kathaṃ kleśāḥ parijñātā bhavanti? mañjuśrīrāhaparamārthato 'tyāntājātānutpannābhāveṣu sarvadharmeṣu saṃvṛtyāsadviparyāsaḥ / tasmād asadaviparyāsāt saṃkalpavikalpaḥ / tasmāt saṃkalpavikalpād ayoniśomanasikārāad ātmasamāropaḥ / tasmād ātmasamāropād dṛṣṭipatyutthānam / tasmād dṛṣṭiparyutthānāt kleśāḥ pravartante / yaḥ punardevaputra, paramārthato 'tyantājātānutpannābhāvān sarvadharmān prajānāti, sa paramārthato 'viparyastaḥ / yaśca paramārthato 'viryastaḥ so 'vikalpaḥ / yaścavikalpaḥ sa yoniśaḥ prayuktaḥ / yaśca yoniśaḥ prayuktaḥ, tasyātmasamāropo na bhavati / yasyātmasamāropo na bhavati tasya dṛṣṭiparyutthānaṃ na bhavanti / yāvat paramārthato nirvāṇadṛṣṭisarvadṛṣṭiparyutthānamapi na bhavanti / tasyaivam anutpādavihāriṇaḥ kleśā atyantaṃṃ vinītā draṣṭavyā / ayamucyate kleśavinayaḥ / yadā devaputra, kleśān nirābhāsena jñānena paramārthato 'tyantaśūnyān atyantābhāvān atyantanirnimittān prajānāti, tadā devaputra, kleśāḥ parijñātā bhavanti / tatra yathāpi nāma devaputra, ya āśīviṣasya gotraṃ prajānāti , sa tasyāśīviṣayasya viṣaṃ śamayati / evameva devaputra, yaḥ kleśānāṃ gotraṃ prajānāti, tasya kleśāḥ praśāmyanti / devaputra āhakataman mañjuśrīḥ, kleśānāṃ gotram? āha - yāvadeṣā paramārthato 'tyantājātānutpannābhāveṣu sarvadharmeṣu kalpanā, idaṃ kleśānāṃ gotram" iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: "How, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, do afflictions become subdued? How are afflictions fully understood?" <s>Mañjuśrī</s> said: "In all <s>dharmas</s> that are ultimately absolutely unborn and unarisen and non-existent, there is conventionally a false inversion (<s>viparyāsa</s>). From that false inversion arises conceptual discrimination (<s>saṃkalpavikalpa</s>). From that conceptual discrimination, through incorrect mental engagement (<s>ayoniśomanasikāra</s>), there is the superimposition of self (<s>ātmasamāropa</s>). From that superimposition of self arise the eruptions of views (<s>dṛṣṭiparyutthāna</s>). From those eruptions of views, afflictions proceed. But he, O son of the gods, who knows all <s>dharmas</s> as ultimately absolutely unborn, unarisen, and non-existent — he is ultimately non-inverted. And he who is ultimately non-inverted is free from conceptual discrimination. And he who is free from conceptual discrimination is correctly engaged. And for him who is correctly engaged, there is no superimposition of self. For him in whom there is no superimposition of self, there are no eruptions of views — including even the eruption of the view of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> and all [other] views in the ultimate. For one who thus abides in non-arising, afflictions should be seen as ultimately subdued. This is called the subduing of afflictions. When, O son of the gods, one knows afflictions through appearanceless knowledge (<s>nirābhāsa-jñāna</s>) as ultimately completely empty, completely non-existent, and completely signless (<s>nimitta</s>) — then, O son of the gods, afflictions are fully understood. Therein, just as, O son of the gods, one who knows the lineage of a venomous snake pacifies the poison of that snake — just so, O son of the gods, one who knows the lineage of afflictions, for him afflictions are pacified. The son of the gods said: <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, what is the lineage of afflictions? He said: Whatever conceptualization exists regarding all <s>dharmas</s> that are ultimately absolutely unborn, unarisen, and non-existent — this is the lineage of afflictions." ...and so on in detail.

body.text: phalataḥ sarvadharmaśūnyatābhāvanayaiva tāvanniḥśreyasanagarapraveśaḥ / atastadarthino ye kalyāṇamicchanti, taiḥ kumārgavicārān dūrata eva parityajya mahātmabhiryo hi yuktyāgamapradīpaḥ prakāśīkṛtaḥ sadbhiśca puruṣaiḥ [yaḥ] muhurmuhurāveditaḥ sa sādaraṃ nirantaraṃ ca sadā sevanīyaḥ / ataśca ekameva yānam, sarve ca dharmāḥ paramārthato niḥ svābhāvā iti sidhyati /
body.translated_text: In effect, entry into the city of the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>) is through the meditation on the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> alone. Therefore, those who desire that and wish for welfare should, having far abandoned the wanderings on wrong paths, constantly and respectfully always follow the lamp of reasoning and scripture that has been illuminated by great souls and repeatedly pointed out by good people. Thus it is established that there is only one vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>), and all <s>dharmas</s> are ultimately essenceless (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>).

body.text: // ācāryakamalaśīlapraṇītaṃ madhyamālokākhyaṃ śāstraṃ samāptam //
body.translated_text: The treatise called <s>Madhyamakāloka</s> (Illumination of the Middle Way), composed by <s>Ācārya</s> <s>Kamalaśīla</s>, is complete.

body.text: bhāratīyopādhyāśīlendrabodhinā bhoṭadeśīyānuvādakena dpala brcegas mahābhāgena cānūditam /
body.translated_text: Translated by the Indian preceptor <s>Śīlendrabodhi</s> and the Tibetan translator <s>dPal brTsegs</s>, a most distinguished [translator].

body.text: śubhamastu
body.translated_text: May there be well-being (<s>śubham astu</s>).
